aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.analyzer_configuration.internal_access_c: The AWS account IDs to include in the internal access analysis rule, defining the set of accounts whose access to resources is analyzed by the internal access analyzer.
The list of resource ARNs that define the inclusion scope for the internal access analysis rule, restricting the Access Analyzer's internal access analysis to the specified resources.

The list of AWS resource types (such as AWS::S3::Bucket or AWS::IAM::Role) that are explicitly included in the internal access analysis rule, meaning that the internal access analyzer will only analyze these resources for access within your security perimeter.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.analyzer_configuration.unused_access_con: The list of AWS account IDs that this exclusion applies to, excluding those accounts' resources from being analyzed by the unused access analysis rule.
Specifies a list of resource tag key-value pairs that identify AWS resources to exclude from unused access analysis when the exclusion type is set to resource_tag.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.archive_rules: Archive rules that automatically archive new findings matching the specified filter criteria before they are listed in the analyzer's active findings.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.archive_rules.filter: Defines the filter conditions for an archive rule, specifying which findings to automatically archive by matching criteria such as resource, principal, or other finding attributes.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.archive_rules.filter.contains: Specifies a list of strings that the criterion's value must contain for a finding to match the archive rule and be archived.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.archive_rules.filter.eq: In an archive rule filter, the eq field contains a list of string values that the rule's chosen property (e.g., the principal ARN or resource ID) must exactly match for a finding to be archived.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.archive_rules.filter.exists: Indicates whether the archive rule filter matches when the specified criterion exists (true) or does not exist (false) on the analyzed resource, used to automatically archive findings based on presence or absence of a property.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.archive_rules.filter.neq: Specifies a list of values that the filter criterion must not match, causing findings where the specified property does not equal any of these values to be archived under this archive rule.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.archive_rules.filter.property: The name of the resource property the archive rule filter applies to, such as 'aws.accountId', 'aws.region', or 'error', used to match against findings in AWS Access Analyzer.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.archive_rules.rule_name: The name of an archive rule in IAM Access Analyzer, which identifies a rule that automatically archives findings matching its defined criteria.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Access Analyzer analyzer, used as the name of the key-value metadata pair for organizing or identifying the resource.
aws_access_analyzer_analyzer.tags.value: The value component of a tag attached to the AWS Access Analyzer analyzer, allowing you to associate arbitrary metadata such as ownership or environment with the analyzer.

aws_account_access_application.identity_source: The computed identity source object that describes how the access application determines identities, including the source type and the associated IAM Identity Center instance ARN when applicable.
aws_account_access_application.identity_source.identity_center: Specifies the AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) instance to be used as the identity source for the access application, including the required Identity Center ARN.

aws_account_access_entitlement.entitlement.principal_role: Defines the IAM role principal, including its role name and optional organizational unit, that is granted the access entitlement to the specified target accounts.
aws_account_access_entitlement.entitlement.principal_role.principal: The IAM user, role, or AWS account that is granted the account access entitlement and assumes the specified principal role in the target AWS account.
aws_account_access_entitlement.entitlement.principal_role.principal.ide: Specifies the AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) user or group that acts as the principal for the access entitlement, granting that identity access to the target account.

aws_acmpca_certificate.api_passthrough.extensions.certificate_p: Specifies the certificate policies extension to include in the issued certificate, where each object contains a policy OID and optional policy qualifiers under the API passthrough extensions.
The object identifier (OID) of a certificate policy, as used in the CertificatePolicies X.509 extension (RFC 5280), which identifies the policy under which the certificate is issued.
A list of policy qualifiers that provide additional information, such as a certification practice statement (CPS) URI, for each certificate policy extension in the certificate.
The OID identifying the type of certificate policy qualifier (id-qt-cps for a CPS pointer or id-qt-unotice for a user notice).
For a certificate policy qualifier, the Qualifier object carries the CPS URI (a Uniform Resource Identifier pointing to the Certification Practice Statement) as required by RFC 5280.
The URI of the Certification Practice Statement (CPS) for the certificate policy qualifier, specifying where the CA's practices are published.
aws_acmpca_certificate.api_passthrough.extensions.custom_extens: Indicates whether the custom extension is marked as critical in the X.509 certificate, as defined by RFC 5280.
The object identifier (OID) for the custom X.509 extension, which is included in the certificate's extensions when using API passthrough in AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority.
The string value of the custom X.509 extension, containing the extension's data (often ASN.1 encoded) to be placed in the certificate.
aws_acmpca_certificate.api_passthrough.extensions.extended_key_: Sets the ExtendedKeyUsage extension in the certificate's X.509 extensions (as pass-through to ACM Private CA), listing permitted usages such as server authentication, client authentication, code signing, or custom OID-based purposes.
Specifies a custom object identifier (OID) for the ExtendedKeyUsage extension, allowing a non-standard extended key usage value instead of a predefined ExtendedKeyUsageType.

Specifies a standard extended key usage type (such as SERVER_AUTH, CLIENT_AUTH, CODE_SIGNING, or EMAIL_PROTECTION) to include in the certificate's ExtendedKeyUsage extension via the api_passthrough structure.
aws_acmpca_certificate.api_passthrough.extensions.subject_alter: Specifies one or more subject alternative names (SANs) to include in the certificate's subjectAltName extension, such as DNS names, IP addresses, or email addresses.

This field specifies a directory name (a distinguished name) to be included as a subject alternative name in the certificate, representing the ASN.1 `directoryName` general name type in the SubjectAlternativeNames extension via the ACM PCA API passthrough.

The Common Name (CN) component of a directory name (X.500 distinguished name) used as a subject alternative name in the certificate's X.509 extensions, passed through to the ACM Private CA API via the ApiPassthrough structure.
The two-letter ISO 3166 country code in the directoryName form of the SubjectAlternativeName extension when passing X.509 extensions through the ACM Private CA certificate API.
A list of custom attribute (OID/value) pairs that further qualify the X.500 directory name in the subject alternative names extension of the certificate, passed through to the private CA.
The dotted decimal object identifier (OID) that identifies the attribute type in a custom DirectoryName attribute within a subject alternative name extension of an AWS Private CA certificate.
The value of a custom attribute within an X.500 distinguished name (DN) that is used as a subject alternative name (DirectoryName) in the certificate's API passthrough extensions.

Specifies the distinguished name qualifier (DNQ) to include in the directoryName entry of the Subject Alternative Name extension for the certificate, an optional X.520 attribute that helps disambiguate otherwise identical distinguished names.
Specifies the generation qualifier (e.g., Jr., III) for a DirectoryName subject alternative name in the API passthrough configuration for an AWS Private CA certificate.
Specifies the given name (first name) attribute of the X.500 distinguished name used as a directory-name subject alternative name in the certificate issued by the private CA.
Specifies the initials attribute of an X.500 distinguished name used in the directoryName entry of a SubjectAlternativeNames extension in the certificate's ApiPassthrough configuration.
Specifies the locality (L) attribute of a directory name in the subject alternative names extension, indicating the city or place for that certificate subject.
The organization (O) attribute of a directory name used as a subject alternative name, specifying the organization to which the certificate subject belongs.
Specifies the organizational unit (OU) component of the X.500 directory name in a subject alternative name extension, used to identify the entity associated with the certificate.

Specifies the pseudonym attribute (an X.520 name component) of an X.509 directory name used as a subject alternative name, passed through to ACM Private CA's certificate API as part of the extensions.

The serial number attribute of the X.500 distinguished name in a directoryName subject alternative name, used to identify the subject within the directory namespace (not the certificate's serial number).
The state or province attribute of the directory name (DN) in a subject alternative name extension for the certificate, as provided via the API passthrough.
Specifies the surname (family name) component of the distinguished name used as a directoryName entry in the subject alternative names extension of the certificate.
Specifies the title attribute (e.g., 'Dr.', 'Esq.') of the X.500 directory name used as a subject alternative name in the certificate.
The DNS name to include in the Subject Alternative Name extension of the certificate, passed through via the API passthrough.

Configures an EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) party name to be included as an entry in the certificate's Subject Alternative Name extension, with fields for the party name and the optional name assigner (the organization that assigned it).

Specifies the name assigner element of an EDI party name included in the Subject Alternative Name extension, identifying the organization that assigned the EDI party name, passed through to the private CA for certificate issuance.

Specifies the name of the EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) party, typically an organization or individual, used in the subject alternative name extension of the certificate to identify the certificate holder for EDI messaging purposes.
The IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) to include as a subject alternative name extension in the certificate issued by the private CA.
Specifies an otherName subject alternative name, which consists of an object identifier (type_id) and a string-encoded value, for the certificate's Subject Alternative Name extension.
Specifies the object identifier (OID) that defines the type of the 'other name' in a SubjectAlternativeName extension within the certificate's ApiPassthrough, as per RFC 5280.
The value of the OtherName subject alternative name, carrying the actual data (such as a user principal name or a custom string) for the name type identified by the corresponding TypeId OID.

Holds the object identifier (OID) string for a subject alternative name of type REGISTERED_ID, which can be included in the certificate's Subject Alternative Name extension to specify a custom registered identifier.
The RFC 822 email address to include as a subject alternative name on the certificate.
Specifies a uniform resource identifier (URI) to include as a subject alternative name (SAN) in the certificate's subjectAlternativeName extension.
aws_acmpca_certificate.api_passthrough.subject.custom_attribute: The object identifier (OID) of the custom attribute to include in the certificate subject.

The value of a custom X.509 subject attribute (such as an organizational unit or domain component) that is passed through from the original API request to the certificate's subject in AWS ACM Private CA.
aws_acmpca_certificate.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the issued certificate, uniquely identifying it within the AWS account and region.
aws_acmpca_certificate.certificate: The PEM-encoded certificate issued by the private CA for the requested certificate signing request.
aws_acmpca_certificate.certificate_authority_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the private certificate authority (CA) that issues the certificate.
aws_acmpca_certificate.template_arn: Specifies the ARN of the certificate template that determines the certificate type (such as end-entity or subordinate CA) and its extensions for the issued certificate.

aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the certificate authority within AWS.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.crlsign: Indicates whether the certificate authority's certificate key can be used to sign certificate revocation lists (CRLs).
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.data_encipherme: Specifies whether the DataEncipherment key usage bit is set in the certificate authority's CSR, indicating that the certificate's public key can be used to directly encrypt user data.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.decipher_only: Indicates whether the CA's private key is intended to be used only for deciphering data, as specified in the KeyUsage extension of the certificate signing request.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.digital_signatu: Specifies whether the CA certificate's key usage extension includes the digitalSignature bit, allowing the CA's key to be used for verifying digital signatures (e.g., on certificates and CRLs).
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.encipher_only: When true, sets the encipherOnly flag in the key usage extension of the certificate authority's CSR, indicating the key may be used only for enciphering data.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.key_agreement: Indicates whether the certificate key can be used for key agreement (e.g., Diffie-Hellman key exchange) in the KeyUsage extension of the CSR.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.key_cert_sign: Specifies whether the key can be used to sign certificates (keyCertSign), a critical usage for a CA certificate.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.key_enciphermen: When true, the key usage extension of the CA's certificate signing request includes the KeyEncipherment usage, indicating the CA's public key may be used for key encipherment.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.key_usage.non_repudiation: Whether the CA certificate's KeyUsage extension sets the nonRepudiation bit, which indicates the key may be used to verify signatures that provide non-repudiation.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.csr_extensions.subject_information_acces: Specifies the GeneralName (such as a URI, DNS name, or IP address) that provides the access location for a Subject Information Access method, for example the URL of an OCSP responder.
Specifies the X.500 distinguished name of the access location for the Subject Information Access extension in the certificate authority's certificate signing request (CSR).

Specifies the common name (CN) component of the X.500 distinguished name that identifies the directory name in the access location for a subject information access (SIA) extension of the private CA certificate.

Specifies the two-letter country code (C attribute) of the X.500 distinguished name used as the access location for the Subject Information Access (SIA) extension in the certificate authority's certificate signing request.

Specifies a list of custom attribute objects (each containing an object identifier and value) to include in the X.500 directory name used for the subject information access access location in the CA certificate signing request.

The object identifier (OID) that identifies the attribute type of a custom attribute within the distinguished name (directoryName) used as the access location for a subject information access extension in the certificate signing request for the private CA certificate.

The value of a custom attribute (such as an organization name or email address) within the X.500 directory name used in the subject information access extension of the certificate authority's certificate signing request.

Specifies the distinguished name qualifier (DNQ) component of the X.500 directory name used as the access location for the subject information access (SIA) extension in the certificate signing request (CSR) for the certificate authority.

Specifies the generation qualifier (e.g., 'Jr.', 'Sr.') component of the X.500 distinguished name for the directory name that serves as an access location in the Subject Information Access CSR extension of an ACM Private CA certificate authority.
Specifies the given name (first name) component of the distinguished name used as the access location in the subject information access extension of the private CA's CSR.

The subject's initials, used as part of the X.500 distinguished name when a directory name is specified as the access location in the subject information access extension of the certificate authority's certificate signing request.
The locality component (such as city) of the X.500 distinguished name used in the access location for the Subject Information Access (SIA) extension in the certificate authority's CSR.
Specifies the organization (O) attribute of the X.500 distinguished name used as the directory name access location in the Subject Information Access extension of the certificate signing request.

The organizational unit (OU) attribute of the X.500 distinguished name used as the directory name for an access location in the Subject Information Access (SIA) extension of the certificate authority's certificate signing request.

Sets the pseudonym attribute (X.500 distinguished name component) of the directory name used as the access location in a Subject Information Access extension within the certificate authority's CSR extensions.
Sets the serialNumber attribute of the X.500 distinguished name used as the directoryName access location in the Subject Information Access extension of the certificate authority's CSR.

Specifies the state or province component of the X.500 distinguished name used in the directory name for an access location in the Subject Information Access extension of the certificate authority's CSR.
Specifies the surname (SN) attribute of an X.500 directory name in the access location of the Subject Information Access (SIA) extension for the private CA certificate.

The Title attribute in the directory name of a subject information access entry, specifying the job title of the entity identified by that X.509 distinguished name within the CSR's SubjectInformationAccess extension.

The DNS name of the GeneralName structure that specifies the access location in a Subject Information Access extension, indicating the host where information about the issuing certificate authority can be retrieved.

Specifies the EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) party name within an access location for the Subject Information Access extension of the certificate authority's CSR, containing the NameAssigner and PartyName fields.

Specifies the name assigner for the EDI party name in the subject information access extension of the certificate authority's certificate signing request (CSR), identifying the entity that assigned the party name.

The party name component of the EDI party name access location in the Subject Information Access (SIA) extension of the certificate signing request, identifying the EDI party associated with the subject.
The IP address of the access location (GeneralName) for the Subject Information Access extension in the certificate signing request, specified in dotted decimal notation (e.g., 192.168.0.1).

Specifies the OtherName variant of the GeneralName for the access location, which consists of an object identifier (OID) and a string value, as used in the Subject Information Access extension of the certificate authority's CSR.
Specifies the object identifier (OID) that identifies the type of name in the otherName field of the access location used in the subject information access extension of the CSR.

The value of the otherName object in the Subject Information Access extension, which holds the actual string data (such as a URI or identifier) associated with the given TypeOid for the certificate authority's CSR.

Specifies the registered ID (object identifier) that serves as the access location in a subject information access entry, enabling the CSR extension to reference an OID-based general name for the certificate authority.

The RFC 822 email address used as the access location in a Subject Information Access extension for the certificate authority's certificate signing request, indicating where to find additional subject information.

Specifies the uniform resource identifier (URI) that identifies the network location of the access information, such as an OCSP responder or CA issuer endpoint, for the subject information access extension in the CA's certificate request.

Specifies the access method (a predefined type such as CA_REPOSITORY or a custom object identifier) that is included in a Subject Information Access extension entry in the certificate authority's CSR.

Specifies the predefined access method type for an entry in the Subject Information Access (SIA) extension of the CA certificate, which can be one of CA_REPOSITORY, RESOURCE_PKI_MANIFEST, or RESOURCE_PKI_CRL.
Specifies a custom object identifier (OID) in dotted-decimal notation that identifies the access method for the Subject Information Access extension in the certificate authority's CSR.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.revocation_configuration.crl_configurati: Determines whether the CRL distribution point extension is omitted from certificates issued by this certificate authority, with true meaning the extension is not included.

Specifies the type of certificate revocation list (CRL) to generate: COMPLETE for a single CRL covering all unexpired certificates, or PARTITIONED for multiple CRLs partitioned by serial number range.
Specifies the custom CNAME (fully qualified domain name) that overrides the default S3 URL in the CRL distribution point included in certificates issued by this private CA.
Specifies the file path in the S3 bucket where the certificate revocation list (CRL) is published, beginning with a slash (e.g., '/crl') and limited to 512 characters.
Specifies whether a certificate revocation list (CRL) is enabled for the certificate authority.
The number of days before the certificate revocation list (CRL) expires, after which AWS Private CA generates a new CRL.
The name of the S3 bucket where the certificate revocation list (CRL) is published or stored for the private certificate authority.

This field specifies the canned access control list (ACL) that AWS Private CA applies to the certificate revocation list (CRL) object when it writes the CRL to the configured S3 bucket, commonly set to PUBLIC_READ or BUCKET_OWNER_FULL_CONTROL.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.revocation_configuration.ocsp_configurat: Enables or disables the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responder for the certificate authority, allowing clients to query the OCSP endpoint for real-time certificate revocation status.
Specifies a custom CNAME (fully qualified domain name) that ACM Private CA uses for the OCSP responder URL, overriding the default responder endpoint.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.common_name: The common name (CN) to include in the subject distinguished name of the certificate authority's CA certificate.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.country: The two-letter ISO country code to include in the certificate authority's subject distinguished name.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.custom_attributes.object_identif: Specifies the object identifier (OID) of a custom attribute to include in the certificate authority's subject when configuring custom subject fields.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.custom_attributes.value: The value string for a custom subject attribute (identified by its OID) included in the X.509 subject distinguished name of the certificate authority.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.distinguished_name_qualifier: Adds a qualifier to the subject distinguished name of the certificate authority to disambiguate entities with similar names.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.generation_qualifier: Specifies the generation qualifier (e.g., 'Jr.', 'Sr.', 'III') for the certificate authority's subject distinguished name (DN).
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.given_name: The given name (first name) of the certificate subject, which becomes part of the X.509 Subject field in certificates issued by this certificate authority.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.initials: Specifies the subject's initials as a component of the X.500 distinguished name embedded in the private CA certificate.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.locality: Specifies the locality (such as a city) of the certificate subject when creating a private CA certificate.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.organization: The organization (O) attribute of the certificate subject's distinguished name, identifying the legal entity that owns the certificate.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.organizational_unit: The organizational unit (OU) component of the X.509 subject distinguished name for the certificate authority.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.pseudonym: Specifies the subject's pseudonym, an X.520 distinguished name attribute that appears in the certificate authority's subject name.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.serial_number: The serial number attribute of the certificate authority's subject distinguished name, which forms part of the X.500 identity for the CA.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.state: The state or province of the certificate subject, used as part of the distinguished name in the certificate authority's subject.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.surname: The surname or family name of the certificate subject, included as a component of the X.509 Subject Distinguished Name.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.subject.title: The title attribute of the certificate authority's X.509 subject distinguished name, representing the holder's position or job title (for example, 'Director').
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.tags.key: The key part of a tag that you can attach to an AWS Private CA certificate authority to help identify and organize the resource.
aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.tags.value: The value part of a key-value tag attached to the certificate authority, used to categorize, organize, or control access to the resource (paired with the corresponding tag key).

aws_agent_registry_registry.discovery_configuration.authorizer_confi: Specifies the expected value that the custom JWT claim must equal in order for the custom JWT authorizer to authorize a request, as part of the authorizing claim match value configuration.
The name of the claim in the incoming JWT token that the custom authorizer extracts to evaluate as a custom claim for access control decisions.

aws_agent_registry_registry_record.descriptors.a2a_agent_card.source.from_u: The object that specifies which credential provider to use and its configuration (such as the provider type and provider-specific settings) for securely obtaining the authentication credentials needed to fetch the agent card from the given source URL.
Configuration for an IAM-based credential provider used to authenticate requests to the source URL from which the A2A agent card is fetched, specifying the IAM role or access keys to use.
The AWS Region used by the IAM credential provider when authenticating requests to fetch the agent card from the specified URL.
The ARN of the IAM role that the IAM credential provider assumes to authenticate and access the source URL.
The OAuth 2.0 grant type used by this credential provider to obtain an access token when fetching from the source URL, such as client_credentials.
Defines the list of OAuth 2.0 scopes to request when the OAuth credential provider obtains an access token to access the external URL source.
Selects the authentication protocol (such as basic authentication, OAuth, or API key) used by the credential provider configuration to fetch the agent card from the remote URL in the source.
aws_agent_registry_registry_record.descriptors.mcp_server.source.from_url.c: Specifies the IAM credential provider settings, including the IAM role to assume, for authenticating to an MCP server accessed via its URL in the registry record's descriptor.
Specifies the AWS region used by the IAM credential provider when authenticating requests to fetch the MCP server definition from the source URL.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the service assumes to generate temporary credentials for authenticating to the MCP server endpoint when using the IAM credential provider in the URL source.
The AWS service name used by the IAM credential provider to sign requests when authenticating to the MCP server accessed via the URL.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0-based credential provider configuration used to authenticate when connecting to the MCP server sourced from a URL.
Specifies a dynamic map of additional custom parameters to be included in the OAuth token request made by the credential provider for the MCP server sourced from a URL.

Specifies the OAuth 2.0 grant type (e.g., client_credentials or authorization_code) used by the credential provider to obtain an access token when establishing a connection to the MCP server specified by the source URL.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 scopes to request from the MCP server's authentication endpoint, defining the specific permissions the agent will be granted when connecting via the configured URL.

aws_aiops_investigation_group.chatbot_notification_channels.chat_confi: The ARNs of the AWS Chatbot configurations that serve as notification channels for the investigation group, enabling alerts to be delivered to configured chat services such as Slack or Microsoft Teams.
aws_aiops_investigation_group.chatbot_notification_channels.snstopic_a: The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that serves as a chatbot notification channel for the investigation group, receiving event notifications and alerts.
aws_aiops_investigation_group.cross_account_configurations.source_role: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role in the source account that the investigation group assumes to access data across accounts.
aws_aiops_investigation_group.encryption_config: Specifies the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the investigation group's data, enabling customer-managed encryption for the AWS AIOps resource.
aws_aiops_investigation_group.encryption_config.kms_key_id: The ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the data associated with the investigation group, as specified in its encryption configuration.
aws_aiops_investigation_group.tag_key_boundaries: This list of tag keys defines the boundaries of the investigation group, so that resources sharing the same values for all specified tag keys are grouped together for investigation.
aws_aiops_investigation_group.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AWS AIOps investigation group, used for resource identification and organization.
aws_aiops_investigation_group.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the AWS AIOps investigation group, used to organize and manage the group within AWS.

aws_amazon_mq_broker.amqp_endpoints: The list of AMQP protocol connection endpoints (host:port) for the Amazon MQ RabbitMQ broker instances, used by clients to connect.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon MQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.authentication_strategy: Defines the authentication strategy for the broker, where SIMPLE uses built-in username/password authentication and LDAP integrates with an external LDAP server for ActiveMQ brokers.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.auto_minor_version_upgrade: Indicates whether the broker automatically upgrades to new minor versions of the Amazon MQ engine as they are released by AWS.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.broker_name: A user-defined name for the broker that must be unique within your AWS account and region, used to identify the Amazon MQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.configuration: Specifies the ID and revision of the Amazon MQ broker configuration that defines the broker's engine settings and other configuration parameters.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.configuration.id: The unique identifier of the Amazon MQ configuration that defines the broker's engine settings and parameters.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.configuration.revision: The revision number of the Amazon MQ broker configuration that identifies a specific version of the configuration to apply, required when specifying a configuration for the broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.console_urls: Provides the list of console URLs for accessing the ActiveMQ web console of each broker instance in the Amazon MQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.data_replication_mode: Specifies the data replication mode for the Amazon MQ broker, allowing either 'NONE' to disable replication or 'CRDR' to enable continuous data replication to a secondary broker in another region.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.deployment_mode: Determines whether the broker runs as a single instance or as an active/standby pair across multiple Availability Zones.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.encryption_options: Specifies the encryption configuration for the broker, including the KMS key ID to use and whether to use an AWS-owned key for encrypting data at rest.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.encryption_options.use_aws_owned_key: Indicates whether to use an AWS-owned key for encrypting data at rest on the broker; when set to false, you must supply a customer-managed KMS key ID in the `KmsKeyId` field.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.engine_type: The type of broker engine to provision, such as ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ, which determines the broker's messaging protocol and features.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.host_instance_type: The Amazon MQ broker instance type (e.g., mq.t3.micro, mq.m5.large) that determines the compute and memory capacity of the broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.id: The unique broker identifier assigned by Amazon MQ, which serves as the Terraform resource ID.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ip_addresses: Computed list of IP addresses assigned to the broker, with one entry per broker instance (for example, two for active/standby deployments).
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata: Defines the LDAP server connection and search parameters (such as hosts, service account credentials, and user/role search criteria) used by the broker to authenticate and authorize users when the broker's authentication strategy is set to LDAP.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.hosts: Specifies the list of fully qualified domain names (FQDN) of the LDAP servers used for authentication in the Amazon MQ broker's LDAP server metadata.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.role_base: Specifies the LDAP distinguished name (DN) of the base object for role (group) searches, used to authenticate and authorize user roles in the Amazon MQ broker's LDAP server metadata.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.role_name: Specifies the LDAP attribute name that contains the role name for role-based access control when using LDAP authentication for the Amazon MQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.role_search_matchin: The LDAP search filter (e.g., `(memberOf=cn=myrole,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com)`) used to locate role (group) entries in the directory when mapping users to roles for the Amazon MQ broker's LDAP authentication.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.role_search_subtree: Specifies whether the LDAP role search should recursively search the entire subtree beneath the role base (true) or only a single level (false).
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.service_account_pas: The password for the service account that Amazon MQ uses to authenticate to the LDAP server when LDAP-based user authentication and authorization is configured.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.service_account_use: The username of the LDAP service account that Amazon MQ uses to authenticate and bind to the LDAP server for user and group queries.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.user_base: Specifies the Distinguished Name (DN) of the base directory entry in the LDAP server that contains the user accounts used for authentication and authorization for the Amazon MQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.user_role_name: Specifies the name of the LDAP role that is associated with the user for the Amazon MQ broker, defining the user's permissions in the LDAP directory.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.user_search_matchin: Provides the LDAP search filter, using `%s` as a placeholder for the username, that Amazon MQ uses to locate the user entry during authentication.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.ldap_server_metadata.user_search_subtree: This boolean specifies whether the LDAP search for users is performed across the entire directory subtree (true) or only at the base context (false).
aws_amazon_mq_broker.logs: Specifies the logging configuration for the Amazon MQ broker, including whether general and audit logs are enabled.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.logs.audit: Specifies whether to enable audit logging for the broker, which publishes audit log entries to the configured CloudWatch Logs log group.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.logs.general: Whether to enable general logging for the Amazon MQ broker, which publishes broker activity logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.maintenance_window_start_time: Specifies the preferred maintenance window start time (day of week, time of day, and time zone) during which Amazon MQ performs maintenance on the broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.mqtt_endpoints: The list of MQTT protocol endpoints (host and port) for the Amazon MQ broker, computed and returned as strings for client connections.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.open_wire_endpoints: The list of OpenWire protocol endpoints (broker host and port) that clients can use to connect to the Amazon MQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.publicly_accessible: Determines whether the broker can be reached from the public internet (true) or only from within the associated VPC (false).
aws_amazon_mq_broker.security_groups: List of security group IDs to associate with the broker for controlling network traffic.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.stomp_endpoints: The list of STOMP protocol endpoints (URLs) that clients use to connect to the broker, including both plain and TLS-secured connection strings.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.storage_type: The storage type (EBS or EFS) used for the broker's message store, determining the underlying storage backend for the Amazon MQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.subnet_ids: Specifies the subnets where the broker's instances are deployed: one subnet for a single-instance broker, or two subnets in different Availability Zones for an active/standby broker; if you provide subnet IDs, you must also provide the SecurityGroups property.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.tags.value: The value part of a key-value tag assigned to the Amazon MQ broker, used to categorize, identify, and manage the broker for cost allocation and resource grouping.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.users.console_access: Whether the user is allowed to access the ActiveMQ web console for this broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.users.groups: Specifies the list of authorization groups that this user belongs to, which define the user's permissions on the Amazon MQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.users.password: The password for the Amazon MQ broker user, used to authenticate client connections to the broker's messaging endpoints.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.users.replication_user: Indicates whether this user is a replication user, which is required for ActiveMQ brokers to replicate data between active and standby brokers.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.users.username: The username for a user that can access the broker, used as part of the credentials to authenticate to the ActiveMQ broker.
aws_amazon_mq_broker.wss_endpoints: The list of WebSocket Secure (WSS) protocol endpoints for the Amazon MQ broker, automatically populated after the broker is created.

aws_amazon_mq_configuration.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon MQ configuration, used to identify and organize the resource.

aws_amazon_mq_configuration_association.configuration: Specifies the Amazon MQ configuration (ID and revision) to associate with the broker in a ConfigurationAssociation resource.

aws_amplify_app.access_token: GitHub personal access token Amplify uses to authenticate and pull the source repository linked to this app.
aws_amplify_app.app_id: The unique ID that AWS Amplify assigns to the app upon creation, used to reference the app in Amplify console and API operations.
aws_amplify_app.app_name: The read-only name assigned to the Amplify app, which identifies the application in the Amplify console and is returned by the Amplify service.
aws_amplify_app.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amplify app, uniquely identifying it within AWS.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config: Configures which Git branches are automatically created in Amplify and the build/render settings (such as build spec, environment variables, and stage) applied to those branches.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.auto_branch_: Specifies the branch name patterns that automatically trigger creation of matching branches in the Amplify app.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.basic_auth_c: Configures basic authentication credentials (username and password) that are automatically applied to branches created according to the auto branch creation patterns.
Whether to enable basic authentication for automatically created branches, requiring a username and password to access them.
The password to use for basic authentication when automatically creating branches for this Amplify app.
Specifies the username used for basic authentication on branches that are automatically created by Amplify.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.build_spec: The build specification (buildspec) content, in YAML or JSON format, that AWS Amplify uses to run the build for branches created automatically via the auto branch creation configuration.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.enable_auto_: Indicates whether Amplify automatically creates a new app branch for every branch in the connected repository that matches the configured auto branch creation patterns.
Enables automated build and deployment of branches that are automatically created for this app when they match the auto-branch-creation pattern.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.enable_perfo: Enables Amplify's performance mode for automatically created branches, which applies performance optimizations such as caching to the deployed app.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.enable_pull_: Enables pull request previews for branches that are automatically created by Amplify, allowing you to preview changes from pull requests before merging.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.environment_: Specifies the environment variables (as key-value pairs) that are applied to branches automatically created for the Amplify app.
The name of the environment variable to configure for automatically created branches in the Amplify app.
The value of the environment variable that is automatically set for branches created via auto branch creation in the Amplify app.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.framework: The framework (e.g., React, Angular, Next.js) that AWS Amplify uses to configure the build process for automatically created branches of the app.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.pull_request: Sets the name of the environment (for example, 'pr') used for pull request preview deployments in the Amplify app's automatic branch creation configuration, so that pull request branches are built and deployed to a separate preview environment.
aws_amplify_app.auto_branch_creation_config.stage: The stage (e.g., PRODUCTION, BETA, DEVELOPMENT) assigned to branches created automatically by the Amplify app's auto branch creation configuration.
aws_amplify_app.basic_auth_config: Configures basic authorization for the Amplify app, including an enable flag and the username and password used to protect access.
aws_amplify_app.basic_auth_config.enable_basic_auth: When true, this enables basic authentication for the Amplify app, requiring users to enter the configured username and password to access the app.
aws_amplify_app.basic_auth_config.password: The password used for basic authentication to the Amplify app, paired with the username in the basic_auth_config block.
aws_amplify_app.basic_auth_config.username: The username used for basic authentication to protect access to the Amplify app's branches.
aws_amplify_app.build_spec: The build specification (buildspec) content for the Amplify app, which defines the build phases and commands used to compile and deploy the application.
aws_amplify_app.cache_config: Defines the cache configuration for the Amplify app, including the cache type (`AMPLIFY_MANAGED` or `AMAZON_CLOUDFRONT`) that controls how the application's static assets are cached.
aws_amplify_app.cache_config.type: Determines whether the Amplify app uses the Amplify-managed cache (`AMPLIFY_MANAGED`) or the Amplify-managed cache without cookies (`AMPLIFY_MANAGED_NO_COOKIES`), controlling how edge cache keys are constructed for the app.
aws_amplify_app.compute_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM service role that AWS Amplify assumes to access AWS resources on behalf of the app, used for backend deployments and resource provisioning.
aws_amplify_app.custom_headers: Configures custom HTTP headers for the Amplify app, passed as a string containing header rules (e.g., YAML with pattern and header key-value pairs) that apply to specific path patterns.
aws_amplify_app.custom_rules: Specifies a list of custom rewrite and redirect rules for the Amplify app, each defining a source pattern, target URL, HTTP status code, and optional condition for matching requests.
aws_amplify_app.custom_rules.condition: The condition expression string (e.g., a country code, IP address, or header match) that controls when this custom redirect or rewrite rule is applied.
aws_amplify_app.custom_rules.source: The source pattern that matches incoming request URLs to trigger the custom rewrite or redirect rule.
aws_amplify_app.custom_rules.status: The HTTP status code (e.g., '200' for a rewrite, '301' for a permanent redirect, or '404' for a not-found response) that Amplify applies to this custom rewrite/redirect rule.
aws_amplify_app.custom_rules.target: The target field of a custom rule specifies the destination URL or path that requests matching the source pattern are redirected or rewritten to in an AWS Amplify app.
aws_amplify_app.default_domain: The default domain automatically assigned to the Amplify app (e.g., a unique subdomain under amplifyapp.com), served as the primary URL for the app.
aws_amplify_app.description: A user-defined description that provides additional information about the Amplify application.
aws_amplify_app.enable_branch_auto_deletion: If enabled, Amplify automatically deletes the corresponding branch in the Amplify app when a branch is deleted in the connected repository.
aws_amplify_app.environment_variables: A list of key-value pairs that define environment variables for the Amplify app, made available during build and runtime.
aws_amplify_app.environment_variables.name: The name (key) of an environment variable to set for the Amplify app, which is referenced during build and runtime.
aws_amplify_app.environment_variables.value: The value assigned to an environment variable for the Amplify app, which is injected into the app's build and runtime environment.
aws_amplify_app.iamservice_role: The ARN of the IAM service role that AWS Amplify assumes to access AWS resources on your behalf.
aws_amplify_app.job_config: Configures an initial Amplify job that runs when the app is created, specifying the deployment branch and job type (e.g., BUILD or RELEASE).
aws_amplify_app.job_config.build_compute_type: Specifies the compute resources (size tier) for Amplify build jobs, with valid values BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL, BUILD_GENERAL1_MEDIUM, or BUILD_GENERAL1_LARGE.
aws_amplify_app.name: The name of the Amplify application, which is a required human-readable identifier displayed in the Amplify console.
aws_amplify_app.oauth_token: The personal OAuth token from the Git provider (GitHub or Bitbucket) used to authorize AWS Amplify to access the repository associated with the app.
aws_amplify_app.platform: Sets the deployment platform for the Amplify app, with valid values including WEB, WEB_DYNAMIC, and WEB_COMPUTE, which determine how the app is built and hosted (e.g., static, dynamic, or server-side rendered).
aws_amplify_app.repository: The HTTPS URL of the Git repository that AWS Amplify connects to and deploys for the app; if omitted, Amplify creates a blank app with no repository connected.
aws_amplify_app.tags: Specifies custom tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the Amplify app, which can be used for resource-level permissions, cost allocation, and organizing the app within AWS.
aws_amplify_app.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the Amplify application.
aws_amplify_app.tags.value: The value portion of a user-defined tag assigned to the Amplify app, used for organizing and identifying AWS resources.

aws_amplify_branch.app_id: The unique ID of the Amplify app that this branch belongs to.
aws_amplify_branch.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Amplify branch, assigned by AWS upon creation.
aws_amplify_branch.backend: The backend configuration for the subdomain, represented as a nested object that contains the ARN of the AWS CloudFormation stack providing the linked backend environment for the branch.
aws_amplify_branch.backend.stack_arn: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudFormation stack that provides the backend environment for this Amplify branch, associating the branch with the corresponding backend resources.
aws_amplify_branch.basic_auth_config: Configures basic authentication settings (username and password) for the branch, allowing per-branch overrides of the app-level basic auth configuration.
aws_amplify_branch.basic_auth_config.enable_basic_auth: Enables basic authorization for the Amplify branch, requiring users to enter a username and password to access the branch's app.
aws_amplify_branch.basic_auth_config.password: The password used for basic authentication to access the branch, which must be at least 8 characters and at most 128 characters long.
aws_amplify_branch.basic_auth_config.username: The username for basic authentication that protects access to the Amplify branch's app.
aws_amplify_branch.branch_name: The name of the branch in the Amplify app, such as 'main' or 'dev', which uniquely identifies the branch within the Amplify service.
aws_amplify_branch.build_spec: Sets the branch's build specification (buildspec) as a YAML/JSON string, which overrides the app-level build settings for the Amplify branch.
aws_amplify_branch.compute_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM service role that AWS Amplify uses to deploy the branch.
aws_amplify_branch.description: An optional free-form string that describes the purpose or content of the Amplify branch.
aws_amplify_branch.enable_auto_build: Indicates whether automatic builds are enabled for the branch, causing Amplify to build the branch automatically every time a code change is pushed to the repository.
aws_amplify_branch.enable_pull_request_preview: Indicates whether Amplify automatically generates a preview of the branch for every pull request, enabling you to test changes before merging them into the main branch.
aws_amplify_branch.enable_skew_protection: When set to true, enables skew protection for the Amplify branch, which redirects users to the correct version of the app when the frontend and backend deployments are out of sync.
aws_amplify_branch.environment_variables: Defines custom environment variables (name/value pairs) available to the Amplify branch for builds and other operations.
aws_amplify_branch.environment_variables.name: The name (key) of an environment variable to set for the Amplify branch, which is used to override or provide configuration to the build process.
aws_amplify_branch.environment_variables.value: Specifies the value assigned to the environment variable key for the Amplify branch.
aws_amplify_branch.framework: Specifies the web framework used to build the application branch, such as React, Next.js, or Angular.
aws_amplify_branch.pull_request_environment_name: Specifies the name of the Amplify backend environment that is used for pull request preview deployments for this branch.
aws_amplify_branch.stage: Configures the deployment stage for the branch, which determines its environment type in AWS Amplify (e.g., PRODUCTION, BETA, DEVELOPMENT, EXPERIMENTAL).
aws_amplify_branch.tags: A list of key-value pairs that assign metadata tags to the Amplify branch, which can be used for organizing and managing branch resources.
aws_amplify_branch.tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag to attach to the Amplify branch resource for organization and cost tracking.
aws_amplify_branch.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the Amplify branch, used to label the branch with arbitrary metadata such as environment, owner, or cost center.

aws_amplify_domain.app_id: The unique ID of the Amplify app to which this domain association belongs.
aws_amplify_domain.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Amplify custom domain association in AWS.
aws_amplify_domain.auto_sub_domain_creation_patterns: Specifies the list of branch name patterns that automatically create subdomains for the Amplify app's domain, such as wildcard patterns like '*' to cover all branches.
aws_amplify_domain.auto_sub_domain_iamrole: The IAM service role that AWS Amplify assumes to automatically manage the Route 53 records for subdomains associated with this domain.
aws_amplify_domain.certificate: Contains the details of the SSL/TLS certificate associated with the Amplify domain, including the certificate Amazon Resource Name (ARN), certificate type (e.g., AMPLIFY_MANAGED or CUSTOM), and the certificate's current status (such as ISSUED or PENDING_VERIFICATION).
aws_amplify_domain.certificate.certificate_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the custom SSL/TLS certificate to use for the domain association, typically from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) or IAM.
aws_amplify_domain.certificate.certificate_type: Specifies the type of SSL/TLS certificate for the custom domain, such as AMPLIFY_MANAGED for Amplify's managed certificate or CUSTOM for a certificate you import or supply.
aws_amplify_domain.certificate.certificate_verification_dns: The DNS record value that must be added to the domain's DNS configuration to verify ownership and enable certificate issuance for the Amplify domain.
aws_amplify_domain.certificate_record: The DNS CNAME record that you must add to your domain's DNS settings to verify domain ownership and issue the SSL certificate for the Amplify domain association.
aws_amplify_domain.certificate_settings: Configures the SSL/TLS certificate for the domain association, including whether to use an Amplify-managed certificate or a custom certificate ARN.
aws_amplify_domain.certificate_settings.certificate_type: Specifies the type of certificate used for the domain's HTTPS connection, either 'amazon-issued' for an AWS-issued ACM certificate or 'custom' to use a custom certificate via a provided ARN.
aws_amplify_domain.certificate_settings.custom_certificate_: The ARN of the custom SSL/TLS certificate that Amplify uses to serve HTTPS for the domain when you choose to use your own certificate instead of the Amplify-managed one.
aws_amplify_domain.domain_name: The custom root domain name (for example, example.com) that you associate with the Amplify application, serving as the base for the subdomains configured in this domain association.
aws_amplify_domain.domain_status: The status of the domain association, which indicates the current lifecycle state of the domain in Amplify, such as CREATING, VERIFYING, AVAILABLE, UPDATING, or PENDING_DEPLOYMENT.
aws_amplify_domain.enable_auto_sub_domain: Determines whether Amplify automatically creates subdomains for all branches in the app associated with this domain.
aws_amplify_domain.status_reason: Provides the reason associated with the current status of the Amplify domain association, such as a failed domain verification or certificate issuance failure.
aws_amplify_domain.sub_domain_settings: Configures the subdomains for this domain, where each item maps a subdomain prefix (like 'www' or 'app') to a specific Amplify branch, controlling how requests to that subdomain are served.
aws_amplify_domain.sub_domain_settings.branch_name: The name of the Amplify app branch that this subdomain setting points to, serving the app content from that branch.
aws_amplify_domain.sub_domain_settings.prefix: Defines the subdomain prefix (for example, `www` or `api`) that routes traffic to a specific branch of the Amplify application, creating a subdomain like `www.example.com` when combined with the domain name.
aws_amplify_domain.update_status: The current update status of the Amplify domain association, such as 'REQUESTING_CERTIFICATE' or 'UPDATING', indicating the progress of an in-progress operation.

aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.app_id: The unique ID of the Amplify app that this UI Builder component is associated with, scoping the component to the correct application.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.binding_properties: Defines the data binding configuration for the Amplify UI Builder component, mapping component properties to data source fields or static values.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.children: Defines the list of child components nested within this Amplify UI Builder component, allowing hierarchical composition of UI elements where each child can have its own properties and bindings.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.children.children: This property contains the nested child elements for each child component in the parent children list, recursively defining the UI component hierarchy.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.children.component_type: Specifies the UI component type for each child in the children list (e.g., 'Button', 'TextField'), defining what kind of element that child renders in the Amplify UI Builder component.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.children.events: Defines the event bindings for a child component, mapping event names (such as 'onClick') to the actions that should be triggered when that event occurs.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.children.name: The unique name of a child component within the parent component's children list, used to identify and reference the child in the Amplify UI Builder component hierarchy.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.children.properties: Defines the properties of each child component in the component's children list, mapping property names to property values (such as text, colors, or data bindings) that determine how the child component renders within the Amplify UI Builder component.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.children.source_id: Identifies the unique ID of the source Amplify UI Builder component that this child component is instantiated from, used to reuse or reference a previously defined component within a parent component's hierarchy.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.collection_properties: Defines the data-binding configuration for a collection-based component, specifying properties such as the data model, query predicate, sorting, and pagination settings.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.component_type: Specifies the type of UI component (e.g., Button, Text, Image), which determines the rendering behavior and available properties for the component in AWS Amplify UI Builder.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.created_at: The timestamp of when the Amplify UI Builder component was created, returned as a read-only string value.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.environment_name: The name of the Amplify environment (e.g., 'dev' or 'prod') that the UI builder component is associated with.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.events: Configures event handlers for the component, mapping event names (such as onClick) to action definitions for user interactions.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.modified_at: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the component was last updated.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.name: The name of the Amplify UI Builder component, which serves as its unique identifier within the app and is used when the component is referenced by other Amplify UI Builder resources or in code generation.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.overrides: Overrides specifies a JSON object of custom property values that override the default configurations of the component's UI elements, allowing targeted styling and behavior changes without modifying the underlying component definition.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.properties: Specifies the map of component properties for the Amplify UI Builder component, where each key-value pair represents a configurable attribute (e.g., text, style, or event handler) available on the component.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.schema_version: The schema version of the component, indicating which version of the Amplify UI Builder component schema the component adheres to.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.tags: A map of key-value pairs used to assign metadata tags to the Amplify UI Builder component for identification and organization.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.variants: Specifies a list of variants for the component, each containing variant values and overrides that adjust the component's properties for different conditions such as breakpoints or themes.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.variants.overrides: A map of property overrides applied to the component when it is rendered in this variant.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_component.variants.variant_values: Defines the key-value pairs that specify a variant's properties, such as viewport or type, for a component variant in AWS Amplify UI Builder.

aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.app_id: The unique identifier of the Amplify application to which this UI Builder form belongs, scoping the form resource to a specific app.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta: Configures the call-to-action button settings for the Amplify UI Builder form, including the placement (e.g., top, bottom, or both) and the labels/behavior of buttons like submit and clear.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.cancel: Defines the cancel button's configuration, including its label (children) and position, within the form's call-to-action area.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.cancel.children: The text content (label) displayed on the Cancel button within the call-to-action (CTA) section of the form.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.cancel.excluded: Determines whether the cancel button is excluded from the form's call-to-action (CTA) area.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.cancel.position: Defines the offset coordinates (top, right, bottom, left) that determine where the cancel button is placed within the form's call-to-action area in the AWS Amplify UI Builder form definition.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.cancel.position.right_of: Specifies the name of the field that the cancel button should be placed to the right of within the form layout.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.clear: Configures the clear button within the form's call-to-action (CTA) area, including its visibility (excluded) and label text (children).
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.clear.children: The text label displayed on the 'Clear' call-to-action button in the form's CTA section.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.clear.excluded: When set to true, this field excludes the clear (reset) button from the form's call-to-action section, so the button is not displayed to users.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.clear.position: This field is a FieldPosition object that controls where the Clear CTA button is placed in the form layout, by setting `fixed` to `first` or `last` or by referencing another field via `rightOf`.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.clear.position.fixed: Sets the fixed positioning value for the clear button in the call-to-action (CTA) section of the Amplify UI Builder form, determining its anchored placement when using the 'fixed' position option.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.clear.position.right_of: Specifies the identifier of another form element that the clear button is positioned to the right of in the call-to-action layout.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.position: Determines where the call-to-action button is placed within the form layout (e.g., top, bottom, start, or end).
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.submit: Configures the submit button for the form's call-to-action (CTA) area, specifying its label text and visibility.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.submit.children: The text label displayed on the submit button in the form's call-to-action section.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.submit.excluded: Indicates whether the submit button is excluded from the form's call-to-action configuration.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.submit.position.fixed: Specifies the CSS position value (e.g., 'fixed' or 'sticky') for the submit button in the form's call-to-action, controlling how the button is anchored relative to the form or viewport.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.cta.submit.position.right_of: The identifier of the element (e.g., the cancel button) that the form's submit button is positioned to the right of within the CTA section.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.data_type: Specifies the data source for the form, including the data source type such as DataStore or custom, and the associated name of the underlying model or data source.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.data_type.data_source_type: Specifies whether the form's data type is backed by an Amplify DataStore model (using 'DataStore') or by a custom data source (using 'Custom').
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.data_type.data_type_name: The name of the data type (e.g., an Amplify GraphQL model or custom data source) that the form is associated with, as defined in the Amplify UI Builder form's dataType configuration.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.environment_name: The name of the Amplify environment (such as 'dev' or 'prod') in which this UI Builder form is created and managed.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.fields: Configures the fields that appear in the form, including each field's label, data type, display position, and validation rules.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.form_action_type: Specifies the operation the form performs on the data model, with valid values limited to 'create', 'update', or 'delete'.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.id: The unique identifier assigned to this Amplify UI Builder form, used to reference the form within its app and environment.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.label_decorator: Determines the visual decorator applied to field labels in the generated form, with allowed values such as 'none', 'asterisk', or 'optional' to indicate required or optional fields.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.name: The name of the Amplify UI Builder form, used to identify the form within the Amplify application.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.schema_version: The version of the form schema that defines the structure and validation rules for the form, used by Amplify UI Builder to interpret the form data correctly.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.sectional_elements: Configures the sectional (layout) elements of the form—such as headers, footers, or field groups—by providing a map of section names to their positional and styling settings.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style: Specifies the styling for the form's layout, including horizontal gap, vertical gap, and outer padding values used to space form elements and the container.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.horizontal_gap: The horizontal gap (spacing) between form fields in the style configuration of an AWS Amplify UI Builder form, typically a numeric value representing pixels.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.horizontal_gap.token_reference: Defines the horizontal spacing between form elements by referencing a design token from the associated Amplify UI Builder theme.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.horizontal_gap.value: The concrete CSS gap value (e.g., '1rem' or '12px') applied as the horizontal spacing between form elements when the gap is specified as a literal value rather than referencing a design token.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.outer_padding: Specifies the outer padding around the form, which can be configured as a fixed value or a token reference.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.outer_padding.token_reference: Specifies the design token reference that resolves the outer padding value for the form, enabling the padding to be controlled by a shared token rather than a fixed value.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.outer_padding.value: The static (non-token) value for the outer padding of the form, such as '10px', used when the outer padding is configured as a fixed value.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.vertical_gap: Configures the vertical gap between form elements by providing either a fixed spacing value or a reference to an Amplify design token, controlling the vertical layout spacing within the form's style.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.vertical_gap.token_reference: The token reference for the vertical gap style, pointing to a design token that defines the vertical spacing between form elements.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.style.vertical_gap.value: Specifies the numeric value for the vertical gap between form fields, as part of the form style's vertical gap setting (with units defined separately in style.vertical_gap.unit).
aws_amplify_uibuilder_form.tags: Specifies a map of tag key-value pairs to attach to the Amplify UI Builder form, used for resource categorization and access control.

aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.app_id: The unique ID of the Amplify application that this UI Builder theme belongs to.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.created_at: The date and time (in ISO 8601 format) when the theme was created, automatically set by AWS.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.environment_name: The name of the Amplify backend environment (e.g., dev, prod) to which this UI Builder theme belongs, scoping the theme to that environment within the Amplify app.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.id: The unique identifier for this Amplify UI Builder theme, generated by the service upon creation.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.modified_at: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the theme resource was last modified, set automatically by AWS Amplify UI Builder.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.name: The human-readable name assigned to the Amplify UI Builder theme, used to identify it in the Amplify console and through the Amplify UI Builder APIs.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.overrides: Specifies a list of theme value overrides that supersede the base theme values for the Amplify UI Builder theme.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.overrides.key: The key (unique name) of a single override in the Amplify UI Builder theme's overrides list, which selects the specific theme value to be overridden.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.overrides.value: For each entry in the `overrides` list, the `value` field holds the concrete string value (such as a color, spacing token, or other style primitive) that is applied in place of the theme's base value when rendering an Amplify UI component.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.overrides.value.value: The string value of a theme override entry, specifying the actual design-token value (such as a color, spacing, or font size) that replaces the default theme value.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.values: Defines the list of theme value objects (key-value pairs) that create design tokens for the Amplify UI Builder theme, where each object can also contain nested children for grouped tokens.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.values.key: The name of a theme variable (e.g., 'colorPrimary' or 'spacingLarge') defined in the Amplify UI Builder theme's values list, used to reference the variable in generated UI components.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.values.value: In the list of theme tokens, the `value` object holds the actual design token definition, which can be a simple string value or a nested list of child token values that together style Amplify UI components.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.values.value.children: This list defines the nested child theme values that branch off the current value, enabling themes to represent hierarchical design token trees.
aws_amplify_uibuilder_theme.values.value.value: The theme token value (e.g., a color hex code, size, or other design token string) paired with its key in an AWS Amplify UI Builder theme's values collection.

aws_api_gateway_account.cloud_watch_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon API Gateway assumes to write logs and metrics to CloudWatch.
aws_api_gateway_account.id: The id is the AWS account ID for which the API Gateway account settings are configured.

aws_api_gateway_api_key.apikey_id: The unique identifier that API Gateway assigns to the API key.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.customer_id: Specifies an optional customer identifier that can be associated with the API key for tracking or organizational purposes.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.description: Specifies a user-defined description of the API key, which can be used to provide additional context or metadata about the key.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.enabled: Indicates whether the API key is enabled for use, where setting it to false disables the key so that client requests using the key are rejected by API Gateway.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.generate_distinct_id: When set to true, it instructs AWS to generate a unique API key value automatically, so you do not need to provide a Value and the resulting key is guaranteed distinct from other API keys.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.stage_keys: A list of stage keys, each identifying an API Gateway REST API and stage, that associates the API key with those stages so it can be used to access their methods.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.stage_keys.rest_api_id: The ID of the REST API that this API key is tied to for the stage key entry, indicating which API's stage the key can access.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.stage_keys.stage_name: The name of the API Gateway stage to which this API key is associated, enabling the key to access APIs in that stage.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.tags: Specifies a list of tags, each containing a Key and Value, to attach to the API Gateway API key for cost allocation and resource management.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the API key, which can be used for metadata, cost tracking, and access control.
aws_api_gateway_api_key.value: The alphanumeric string value of the API key; if omitted, API Gateway generates a unique value.

aws_api_gateway_authorizer.auth_type: Specifies the required authentication type (such as 'oauth' or 'openid') for the custom authorizer, which is optional and only relevant when the authorizer type is 'CUSTOM'.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.authorizer_credentials: Specifies the ARN of an IAM role that Amazon API Gateway assumes when invoking the authorizer, used to grant permissions for the authorizer's backend (such as a Lambda function) to be called.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.authorizer_id: The unique identifier assigned by Amazon API Gateway to the authorizer when it is created.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.authorizer_result_ttl_in_seconds: The number of seconds that API Gateway caches the authorizer result before re-invoking the authorizer Lambda function.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.authorizer_uri: The URI of the Lambda function that serves as the custom authorizer, typically formatted as arn:aws:apigateway:{region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/{lambda-arn}/invocations.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.identity_source: Defines the request parameter (e.g., method.request.header.Authorization) from which API Gateway extracts the caller's identity token for the custom or token authorizer.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.identity_validation_expression: Specifies a regular expression that AWS API Gateway uses to validate the incoming identity (such as a bearer token) for the authorizer; if the identity does not match the expression, API Gateway rejects the request with a 401 response.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.name: The name of the custom authorizer, which must be unique within the API Gateway REST API.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.provider_arns: The list of Amazon Cognito user pool ARNs that this API Gateway authorizer uses to validate tokens for a COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer type.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.rest_api_id: The unique identifier or reference (typically the logical ID of an aws_api_gateway_rest_api resource) of the REST API in API Gateway that this custom authorizer is associated with.
aws_api_gateway_authorizer.type: Specifies the authorizer type, which determines the authorization mechanism for API Gateway requests: valid values are TOKEN, REQUEST, or COGNITO_USER_POOLS, corresponding to Lambda token authorizers, Lambda request authorizers, and Amazon Cognito user pool authorizers respectively.

aws_api_gateway_base_path_mapping.base_path: Specifies the base path of the custom domain that maps to the API, such that requests to that path are routed to the associated API and stage; if not set, the API is served at the root of the domain (path '/').
aws_api_gateway_base_path_mapping.domain_name: The custom domain name (e.g., api.example.com) registered in API Gateway to which this base path mapping is attached, matching the DomainName property of an AWS::ApiGateway::DomainName resource.
aws_api_gateway_base_path_mapping.rest_api_id: The ID of the API Gateway REST API to which the base path mapping routes traffic.
aws_api_gateway_base_path_mapping.stage: The name of the API Gateway stage that the base path mapping targets.

aws_api_gateway_client_certificate.client_certificate_id: The unique identifier assigned by Amazon API Gateway to the client certificate, used to reference this certificate in other API Gateway resources (e.g., domain names) and returned automatically upon creation.
aws_api_gateway_client_certificate.description: A user-provided description for the client certificate, used to annotate or identify it.
aws_api_gateway_client_certificate.tags: Associates a list of key-value tag pairs with the API Gateway client certificate, enabling cost allocation, access control, and resource categorization.
