aws_api_gateway_client_certificate.tags.value: The value of an individual tag assigned to the API Gateway client certificate, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_api_gateway_deployment.deployment_canary_settings.percent_traff: The percentage (0.0 to 100.0) of live traffic routed to the canary deployment, controlling gradual traffic shifting.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.deployment_canary_settings.stage_variabl: A map of stage variable names to their override values, applied to the canary stage so that the canary deployment uses different variable settings than the regular deployment.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.deployment_canary_settings.use_stage_cac: Determines whether the canary deployment uses the stage cache for caching responses when a canary release is enabled.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.deployment_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this API Gateway deployment, which is used to reference the deployment in other resources such as stages and usage plans.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.description: Specifies a description for this API Gateway deployment, which is often used to document the purpose or version of the deployed API.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.rest_api_id: The identifier of the RestApi resource that this deployment belongs to.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.access_log_setting.des: The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which API Gateway sends access logs for the stage described by this deployment.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.access_log_setting.for: Defines the format of the access log written to CloudWatch Logs, supporting context variables like $context.requestId and $context.identity.sourceIp.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.cache_cluster_enabled: Whether to enable a cache cluster for the API Gateway stage, allowing responses from integrations to be cached to improve performance and reduce backend load.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.canary_setting.percent: The percentage of traffic to route to the canary stage during a canary release deployment.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.canary_setting.stage_v: A map of stage variable names to values that overrides the canary stage's stage variables for this deployment.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.canary_setting.use_sta: Determines whether the canary deployment uses the stage cache, rather than bypassing it, for this deployment's canary settings.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.method_settings.cache_: Whether the data stored in the API Gateway method cache is encrypted.
Specifies the time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for the API Gateway cache for a given method, determining how long cached responses are stored before being invalidated.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.method_settings.cachin: Indicates whether API Gateway caches responses from the method for the associated stage.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.method_settings.data_t: Specifies whether data trace logging is enabled for this method, which affects the log entries pushed to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.method_settings.http_m: The HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) to which this method setting applies for the API Gateway stage.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.method_settings.loggin: Specifies the logging level (OFF, ERROR, or INFO) for this API Gateway method, controlling the verbosity of CloudWatch Logs entries pushed from the method execution.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.method_settings.metric: Enables or disables CloudWatch metrics for the API method, allowing monitoring of latency, error rates, and call counts in the stage.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.method_settings.resour: The API resource path (e.g., /pets) for which these method-level settings (like caching, throttling, logging) apply in the API Gateway deployment stage.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.method_settings.thrott: The maximum number of requests per second that Amazon API Gateway can service for the given method before throttling is applied (the burst limit).
The throttling rate limit (in requests per second) for the method, used by API Gateway to control the steady-state request rate for that method in the deployment's stage description method settings.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.tags.key: The key of a tag entry in the stage description's tags map, which attaches that tag to the API Gateway stage created by this deployment.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_description.tags.value: The value of a tag (key-value pair) assigned to the API Gateway stage defined in this deployment's stage description, used for metadata and resource categorization.
aws_api_gateway_deployment.stage_name: The name of the API Gateway stage (e.g., 'prod', 'dev') that this deployment is associated with, and when specified, the deployment updates or creates that stage's current deployment.

aws_api_gateway_documentation_part.documentation_part_id: This read-only attribute contains the unique ID that Amazon API Gateway assigns to the documentation part when it is created.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_part.location.method: Specifies the HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) of the API method that this documentation part applies to, used when the location type is METHOD or a method-specific entity.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_part.location.name: The name of the targeted API entity (such as an authorizer, model, path parameter, query parameter, header, or body) that this documentation part applies to, required for location types that identify a specific entity by name.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_part.location.path: The URL path of the API resource (e.g., /pets) to which this documentation part applies, used when the location type is PATH or RESOURCE.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_part.location.status_code: Specifies the HTTP status code (e.g., 200, 404) of the API response for which this documentation part applies, used when the location type is set to RESPONSE or RESPONSE_BODY.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_part.location.type: Specifies the type of API entity (such as API, METHOD, MODEL, RESOURCE, AUTHORIZER, QUERY_PARAMETER, REQUEST_BODY, or HTTP_METHOD) that the documentation part targets, determining which component of the API the documentation describes.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_part.properties: The documentation content (plain text or Markdown) that describes the targeted API entity, as defined by the Location, and is displayed by API Gateway.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_part.rest_api_id: The identifier of the API Gateway REST API to which this documentation part belongs.

aws_api_gateway_documentation_version.description: Provides a human-readable description for the documentation version snapshot, typically indicating the changes or purpose of that version.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_version.documentation_version: The version identifier of the API documentation snapshot that this documentation version represents.
aws_api_gateway_documentation_version.rest_api_id: The identifier of the REST API to which this documentation version is attached.

aws_api_gateway_domain_name.certificate_arn: The ARN of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to secure the edge-optimized domain name's TLS/SSL connections.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.distribution_domain_name: The CloudFront distribution domain name that API Gateway assigns to the custom domain name, used as the target for a Route 53 alias record or CNAME to point the custom domain to the API endpoints.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.distribution_hosted_zone_id: The Route 53 hosted zone ID of the CloudFront distribution associated with this API Gateway custom domain name (used for edge-optimized endpoints).
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.domain_name: The custom domain name (e.g., api.example.com) that API Gateway serves for this domain name resource, which must be registered and associated with an ACM certificate.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.domain_name_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the API Gateway domain name.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.endpoint_access_mode: This field sets the endpoint access mode for the API Gateway custom domain name, either PUBLIC for internet access or PRIVATE to restrict access to private VPC endpoints.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.endpoint_configuration.ip_address_type: Determines the IP address version (IPv4 or IPv6) used by the regional API Gateway custom domain name when the endpoint type is REGIONAL.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.endpoint_configuration.types: Specifies the list of endpoint types (EDGE, REGIONAL, or PRIVATE) that determine how the API Gateway domain name is exposed and routed across AWS regions and VPCs.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.mutual_tls_authentication: Configures mutual TLS (mTLS) for the API Gateway domain name by providing the truststore URI and version used to validate client certificates.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.mutual_tls_authentication.truststore_uri: The Amazon S3 URI of the truststore containing the trusted CA certificates used for mutual TLS authentication on the API Gateway domain name.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.mutual_tls_authentication.truststore_ver: The version of the S3 object that contains the truststore for mutual TLS authentication.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.regional_certificate_arn: Specifies the ARN of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to use for the domain name's regional API endpoint, which serves requests for a specific AWS region.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.regional_domain_name: The auto-generated regional domain name (e.g., d-xxxxxxxx.execute-api.region.amazonaws.com) that API Gateway assigns to this custom domain name when configured for a regional endpoint, which is used as the DNS target for routing traffic to API Gateway.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.regional_hosted_zone_id: The Route 53 hosted zone ID for the regional API Gateway endpoint, used to configure DNS alias records pointing to the regional domain name.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.security_policy: Specifies the minimum TLS version (e.g., 'TLS_1_0' or 'TLS_1_2') that API Gateway uses for the custom domain name's HTTPS connections.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name.tags: Specifies the list of key-value tags to attach to the API Gateway domain name.

aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.certificate_arn: The ARN of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to secure the custom domain name's endpoint, such as edge-optimized or regional, for API Gateway v2.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.domain_name: The custom domain name (e.g., api.example.com) that this API Gateway v2 domain name configuration represents, which must be owned by the user and is used as the public endpoint for invoking the associated APIs.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.domain_name_id: The computed unique identifier for the API Gateway v2 domain name resource, which is the domain name string itself used as the resource's primary key in the service.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.endpoint_configuration.ip_address_type: Specifies whether the API Gateway custom domain name endpoint uses IPv4 only (IPV4) or both IPv4 and IPv6 (DUALSTACK).
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.endpoint_configuration.types: Specifies the endpoint type for the domain name, where 'REGIONAL' is the only supported value in API Gateway v2 to indicate a regional endpoint.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.policy: A JSON string specifying an IAM resource policy that controls access to the API Gateway domain name's endpoints by allowing or denying invoking principals, source IPs, or VPC origins.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.security_policy: The security_policy field specifies the minimum Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol version for the API Gateway custom domain name's endpoint, with supported values of 'TLS_1_0' and 'TLS_1_2'.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.tags: Specifies the tags (list of objects with Key and Value) to associate with the API Gateway v2 domain name, enabling metadata management and cost allocation.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the API Gateway custom domain name, which you can use to categorize the resource for cost allocation and IAM-based access control.
aws_api_gateway_domain_name_v2.tags.value: The value for a tag key assigned to the API Gateway domain name v2 resource.

aws_api_gateway_gateway_response.id: The unique physical resource id of the gateway response, formed as a composite of the associated REST API ID and the response type (for example, 'restApiId/DEFAULT_4XX') separated by a slash.
aws_api_gateway_gateway_response.response_parameters: Specifies a map of response parameters (such as headers) to customize the API Gateway response, where each key is a parameter name and the value indicates whether the parameter is enabled.
aws_api_gateway_gateway_response.response_templates: Maps MIME content types to Velocity templates that generate the response body for this API Gateway gateway response.
aws_api_gateway_gateway_response.response_type: Specifies the type of API Gateway response to customize (e.g., MISSING_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, DEFAULT_4XX), which must be one of the predefined gateway response types.
aws_api_gateway_gateway_response.rest_api_id: The identifier of the REST API to which this gateway response is attached.
aws_api_gateway_gateway_response.status_code: Specifies the HTTP status code that API Gateway returns for this gateway response, allowing you to override the default status code for the corresponding error type.

aws_api_gateway_method.api_key_required: Whether this method requires clients to submit a valid API key, enforced by API Gateway.
aws_api_gateway_method.authorization_scopes: Specifies the list of OAuth scopes required for the method to be called when the authorization type is set to a Cognito User Pool or OAuth, so only clients presenting a token containing all listed scopes are allowed to invoke the method.
aws_api_gateway_method.authorizer_id: The ID of the API Gateway custom or Cognito authorizer that authorizes requests to this method.
aws_api_gateway_method.http_method: Specifies the HTTP method (such as GET, POST, PUT, or DELETE) that this API Gateway method handles for the given resource path.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.cache_key_parameters: Specifies the list of request parameters (such as query string or header parameters) that define the cache key for the API method's integration, controlling how cached responses are keyed.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.cache_namespace: The cache namespace for the integration's caching behavior, used to scope cached responses so that different integrations under the same method do not share cache entries.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.connection_id: The ID of the VPC link used by this integration when the connection type is VPC_LINK, enabling private connectivity to the integration endpoint.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.connection_type: Determines the connection type for the integration endpoint, either 'INTERNET' for a public endpoint or 'VPC_LINK' for a private connection via a VPC Link.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.content_handling: Determines how API Gateway converts the request payload between binary and text formats for the integration, with valid values CONVERT_TO_BINARY or CONVERT_TO_TEXT.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.credentials: The ARN of an IAM role that API Gateway assumes to invoke the backend integration, required for AWS service and VPC link integrations.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.integration_http_method: Specifies the HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) that API Gateway uses to invoke the backend integration, which can differ from the frontend method of the API Gateway method.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.integration_responses: Defines the integration response status codes and their associated response templates, headers, and selection patterns for the method's integration.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.integration_responses.conten: Specifies how the response payload from the backend integration is handled, such as converting to binary (CONVERT_TO_BINARY), converting to text (CONVERT_TO_TEXT), or leaving it unmodified (passthrough).
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.integration_responses.respon: Maps integration response parameters (e.g., backend headers) to method response parameters (e.g., client headers) for this integration response.
Maps media types (e.g., application/json) to Velocity templates that transform the integration response payload before it is returned to the API client.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.integration_responses.select: Specifies a regular expression that API Gateway matches against the backend integration's response body to determine which integration response mapping to use for the corresponding method response.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.integration_responses.status: The HTTP status code that API Gateway returns to the client when the integration response matches the associated selection pattern.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.integration_target: The target backend endpoint (URI or ARN) that receives requests through this API Gateway method's integration.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.passthrough_behavior: Specifies how the API Gateway integration handles the request body when the Content-Type header does not match any mapping template, with values such as WHEN_NO_MATCH, WHEN_NO_TEMPLATES, or NEVER.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.request_parameters: Specifies a map of integration request parameters, where each key is an integration request parameter name (e.g., `integration.request.path.id`) and each value is a method request expression (e.g., `method.request.path.id`), controlling how method request data is passed to the backend integration.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.request_templates: Maps MIME content types to mapping template strings that API Gateway uses to transform the client's request body before sending it to the backend integration.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.response_transfer_mode: Specifies the response transfer mode for the integration, with valid values of 'binary' (to have the response body base64-encoded for binary media types) or 'passthrough' (to pass the response body unchanged).
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.timeout_in_millis: Specifies the maximum amount of time, in milliseconds, that API Gateway waits for the integration (backend) to respond before returning an error to the client.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.type: Specifies the type of backend integration for the method, such as AWS, AWS_PROXY, HTTP, HTTP_PROXY, or MOCK, which determines how API Gateway routes requests to the backend.
aws_api_gateway_method.integration.uri: The URI of the backend endpoint that API Gateway invokes for this integration, such as an HTTP/HTTPS URL for HTTP integrations, a Lambda function ARN for AWS integrations, or an AWS service action ARN for other AWS services.
aws_api_gateway_method.method_responses: Specifies the responses that the method can return, including status codes, response parameters, and response models.
aws_api_gateway_method.method_responses.response_models: Maps response media (MIME) types to the name of the model that describes the response body for the corresponding method response, allowing API Gateway to generate or validate the payload.
aws_api_gateway_method.method_responses.response_parameters: Specifies a map of response parameter names (e.g., 'method.response.header.Content-Type') to booleans that indicate whether the response parameter is required, for a method response defined on the API Gateway method.
aws_api_gateway_method.method_responses.status_code: The HTTP status code of the method response that API Gateway returns to the client.
aws_api_gateway_method.operation_name: The operation name for the method, used to identify the operation in API Gateway's generated OpenAPI/Swagger definitions.
aws_api_gateway_method.request_models: A map of media types to model names for the request body, defining the expected schemas for incoming request payloads.
aws_api_gateway_method.request_parameters: Maps request parameter names to a boolean indicating whether each parameter is required in the method request, allowing you to enforce required query strings, headers, or path parameters.
aws_api_gateway_method.request_validator_id: Specifies the ID of the API Gateway request validator that defines the validation rules for this method's request body and parameters.
aws_api_gateway_method.resource_id: The identifier of the API Gateway resource to which this method is attached.
aws_api_gateway_method.rest_api_id: The ID of the REST API (aws_api_gateway_rest_api) that this method belongs to.

aws_api_gateway_model.content_type: The content type (e.g., application/json) for the API Gateway model, used to associate the model with a specific media type in API requests and responses.
aws_api_gateway_model.description: This field specifies a human-readable description of the API Gateway model, used to document the model's purpose and assist in management within the API definition.
aws_api_gateway_model.rest_api_id: The ID of the RestApi that this model belongs to, linking the model to its parent API Gateway REST API.
aws_api_gateway_model.schema: Defines the JSON schema (as a string) that describes the data structure for the API Gateway model, used for request/response validation.

aws_api_gateway_request_validator.name: Specifies the name of the API Gateway request validator for identification; if omitted, API Gateway generates a name.
aws_api_gateway_request_validator.request_validator_id: The unique identifier assigned by API Gateway to the request validator, returned after creation.
aws_api_gateway_request_validator.rest_api_id: The ID of the REST API to which this request validator belongs.
aws_api_gateway_request_validator.validate_request_body: Indicates whether the request validator checks the request body against the configured model schema for the API method.
aws_api_gateway_request_validator.validate_request_parameters: Indicates whether this request validator validates the query string and header parameters of incoming API requests.

aws_api_gateway_resource.parent_id: The identifier of the parent Resource in this REST API's resource hierarchy, determining the path of this resource relative to the API's root resource.
aws_api_gateway_resource.path_part: The URL path segment (e.g., 'users' or a path parameter like '{userId}') that defines this resource's location in the API's URL hierarchy, appended to the parent resource's path to form the full resource path.
aws_api_gateway_resource.resource_id: The unique identifier assigned to this API Gateway resource by the service, used to reference the resource in method and integration configurations within the same REST API.
aws_api_gateway_resource.rest_api_id: The ID of the parent RestApi in API Gateway to which this resource belongs.

aws_api_gateway_rest_api.api_key_source_type: Determines whether API keys are sourced from the request header or from an authorizer, with allowed values HEADER and AUTHORIZER.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.binary_media_types: Defines the binary media types (e.g., image/png, application/octet-stream) that the REST API treats as binary data, enabling API Gateway to handle binary payloads for those content types.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.clone_from: The ID of an existing RestApi from which to clone the configuration to create this API.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.description: Specifies a user-defined description for the REST API, which is displayed in the API Gateway console to document the API's purpose.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.disable_execute_api_endpoint: When set to true, disables the default execute-api endpoint for the REST API, so the API is accessible only through custom domain names.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.endpoint_configuration.ip_address_type: Specifies the IP address type for the API Gateway REST API endpoint, supporting values of 'ipv4' or 'ipv6' to indicate whether the endpoint uses IPv4 or IPv6 addressing.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.endpoint_configuration.types: The list of endpoint types for the REST API, specifying whether it is deployed at an edge location, in a specific region, or privately, with valid values EDGE, REGIONAL, and PRIVATE.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.endpoint_configuration.vpc_endpoint_ids: A list of VPC endpoint IDs attached to the REST API, used to create regional or private endpoints that allow access from within those VPC endpoints.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.fail_on_warnings: When creating or updating the REST API from an OpenAPI definition, setting this to true causes the operation to fail if any warnings are generated, while false (the default) allows warnings to be ignored.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.minimum_compression_size: Sets the minimum threshold in bytes that a response payload must reach before API Gateway applies compression to the response, enabling gzip compression for larger payloads.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.parameters: Map of API Gateway configuration parameters for the REST API, supporting the 'endpointConfigurationTypes' (comma-separated list of endpoint types) and 'binaryMediaTypes' (comma-separated list of binary media types) keys.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.rest_api_id: The unique identifier for the REST API, assigned by AWS API Gateway when the resource is created.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.root_resource_id: The unique identifier of the root resource (the top-level path '/') of the API Gateway REST API.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.security_policy: Specifies the minimum TLS version allowed for the REST API's endpoint, either 'TLS_1_0' or 'TLS_1_2'.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.tags: Defines a list of key-value pairs to tag the API Gateway REST API, enabling cost allocation, resource-level access control, and management of the API resource.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.tags.key: A tag key that you assign to this API Gateway REST API, used for cost allocation and organizational metadata.
aws_api_gateway_rest_api.tags.value: The value for a user-defined tag assigned to the API Gateway REST API, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_api_gateway_stage.cache_cluster_enabled: Indicates whether a cache cluster is enabled for the API Gateway stage, allowing responses to be cached for performance.
aws_api_gateway_stage.cache_cluster_size: Specifies the cache cluster size (in gigabytes) for the API Gateway stage, using string values such as '0.5' or '1.6' when caching is enabled.
aws_api_gateway_stage.canary_setting: Configures the canary deployment settings for the stage, including the percentage of traffic to route to the canary deployment, the deployment ID, and optional stage variable overrides and cache usage.
aws_api_gateway_stage.canary_setting.deployment_id: The ID of the deployment that the canary will route a percentage of traffic to, allowing you to test changes before shifting all traffic to that deployment.
aws_api_gateway_stage.canary_setting.percent_traffic: Specifies the percentage of traffic that API Gateway routes to the canary deployment.
aws_api_gateway_stage.canary_setting.stage_variable_overrides: A map of stage variable names to values that temporarily override the stage's normal variables for canary traffic in the API Gateway stage, allowing different configuration for the canary version.
aws_api_gateway_stage.canary_setting.use_stage_cache: Indicates whether the canary should use the stage cache, enabling the canary's traffic to share the cache configured for the API Gateway stage.
aws_api_gateway_stage.client_certificate_id: The ID of the client certificate that API Gateway uses to authenticate client requests to the stage.
aws_api_gateway_stage.deployment_id: The ID of the API Gateway deployment that this stage points to, determining which version of the API is exposed at this stage's endpoint.
aws_api_gateway_stage.description: A description of the API Gateway stage, providing additional context about its purpose or contents.
aws_api_gateway_stage.documentation_version: The identifier of the API documentation version to associate with this stage, controlling which published documentation snapshot is exposed for the stage.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings: Configures per-method settings for the stage, including throttling, caching, metrics, and logging, keyed by method path.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.cache_data_encrypted: Specifies whether the method-level cache in the API Gateway stage encrypts cached response data before storing it.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.cache_ttl_in_seconds: Specifies the time-to-live (TTL) duration, in seconds, for cached responses for a specific method in the API Gateway stage, controlling how long API Gateway caches a method's response before forwarding a new request to the backend.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.caching_enabled: Enables or disables API caching for this stage's method, so responses are cached and served from the cache until the cache TTL expires.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.data_trace_enabled: Enables data tracing for the method, capturing full request and response payloads in execution logs.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.http_method: The HTTP method (for example GET, POST, or *) to which these method settings apply, where * matches all methods.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.logging_level: Specifies the logging level (OFF, ERROR, or INFO) for the method's execution logs in API Gateway.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.metrics_enabled: Enables CloudWatch metrics for the API Gateway method associated with this method setting.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.resource_path: The resource path (e.g., '/pets') in the API Gateway API for which these method settings apply, used together with the HTTP method to identify a specific method on the stage.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.throttling_burst_limit: Sets the maximum number of requests per second that API Gateway can serve for the method during a burst, used to control throttling behavior.
aws_api_gateway_stage.method_settings.throttling_rate_limit: Sets the maximum steady-state request rate (requests per second) allowed for a method's throttling configuration in this API Gateway stage.
aws_api_gateway_stage.rest_api_id: The ID of the REST API that this stage is associated with.
aws_api_gateway_stage.stage_name: The name of the API Gateway stage (e.g., 'prod', 'dev'), which appears in the API's invoke URL and identifies the deployment associated with this stage.
aws_api_gateway_stage.tags: A list of key-value pairs used to associate metadata with the API Gateway stage for cost allocation and management.
aws_api_gateway_stage.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the API Gateway stage, used for organizing and identifying the stage in AWS cost allocation and resource management.
aws_api_gateway_stage.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag assigned to the API Gateway stage, which can be used for cost allocation, resource organization, and access control.
aws_api_gateway_stage.tracing_enabled: Indicates whether active tracing with AWS X-Ray is enabled for the API Gateway stage.

aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.api_stages: Associates this usage plan with specific API Gateway stages, optionally configuring per-stage throttling and quota limits for those stages.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.api_stages.api_id: The identifier of the API for which this usage plan stage association is configured, referencing the API Gateway REST API.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.api_stages.stage: In the API Gateway UsagePlan's ApiStages list, this is the name of the deployed stage (such as 'prod') that the usage plan applies to.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.api_stages.throttle: Defines method-level throttling limits for the associated API stage, mapping individual method paths (e.g., 'GET /resource') to their own burst and rate limits.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.description: An optional description that provides a friendly label or purpose for the usage plan, helping to distinguish it from other plans in the API Gateway.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS API Gateway to this usage plan, used as the resource's id.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.quota.limit: The maximum number of API requests permitted during a specified quota period (day, week, or month) for the usage plan, as configured in the quota settings.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.quota.offset: Specifies the number of requests that are deducted from the quota limit at the beginning of each period, effectively reducing the total number of requests allowed for that period.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.quota.period: The time period (DAY, WEEK, or MONTH) over which the usage plan's request quota is measured and enforced.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.tags: Specifies the key-value tags to assign to the usage plan, which AWS uses for cost allocation and resource management.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.tags.key: Defines the key of a user-defined tag attached to the API Gateway usage plan, used for metadata, cost allocation, and resource organization.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.tags.value: The tag value paired with a tag key on the API Gateway usage plan, used for cost allocation, resource organization, and IAM-based access control.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.throttle.burst_limit: The maximum API request rate limit over a time-varying window of one second, defining the burst limit for the usage plan's throttling settings.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.throttle.rate_limit: Sets the steady-state request rate limit (in requests per second) allowed for API requests covered by the usage plan's throttling configuration.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan.usage_plan_name: A friendly name for the usage plan, used to identify it in the API Gateway console and API calls.

aws_api_gateway_usage_plan_key.id: The unique resource identifier in Terraform, formed by joining the usage plan ID and the API key ID with a colon.
aws_api_gateway_usage_plan_key.key_type: Indicates the type of the API key associated with the usage plan, either 'API_KEY' for a standard API Gateway key or 'CUSTOM' for a custom imported key.

aws_api_gateway_v2_api.api_endpoint: The automatically generated endpoint URL (e.g., https://<api-id>.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws.com) that clients use to invoke the API.
aws_api_gateway_v2_api.api_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS API Gateway v2 to this API when it is created, used to reference the API in other resources.

aws_api_gateway_v2_api_gateway_managed_o.integration: The integration property is an object that overrides integration settings, such as integration type, HTTP method, payload format version, and timeout, for all integrations defined in the API's OpenAPI definition.
aws_api_gateway_v2_api_gateway_managed_o.route: Overrides the configuration of a specific Route in an API Gateway v2 (WebSocket or HTTP) API by specifying properties such as authorization settings, request models, and route response selection expression, replacing the managed defaults.
aws_api_gateway_v2_api_gateway_managed_o.stage: The stage property defines overrides for the API Gateway v2 stage, configuring settings such as access log settings, default route throttling, and stage variables that replace the managed stage defaults.
aws_api_gateway_v2_api_gateway_managed_o.stage.access_log_settings: Overrides the access log settings (destination ARN and log format) for the API Gateway v2 stage, determining how access logs are delivered and formatted.
aws_api_gateway_v2_api_gateway_managed_o.stage.default_route_settings: Overrides the default route settings for the API Gateway v2 stage, which specify throttling, logging, and other behaviors applied to all routes that do not have their own settings.

aws_api_gateway_v2_api_mapping.api_mapping_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this API mapping, used to reference the mapping in API Gateway v2 operations.

aws_api_gateway_v2_authorizer.authorizer_id: The unique AuthorizerId assigned by AWS to the API Gateway v2 authorizer, returned as a read-only attribute and used to reference the authorizer in other resources.

aws_api_gateway_v2_deployment.deployment_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this API Gateway v2 deployment.

aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.domain_name_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the API Gateway v2 domain name, used to uniquely identify this domain for IAM policies and resource references.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.domain_name_configurations.certificate_a: The ARN of an AWS Certificate Manager certificate that is used to secure the custom domain name's TLS connections.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.domain_name_configurations.certificate_n: Specifies a customer-friendly name for the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate associated with the API Gateway v2 domain name configuration, used for identification purposes alongside the certificate ARN.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.domain_name_configurations.endpoint_type: Defines the endpoint type for the API Gateway domain name, either 'REGIONAL' or 'EDGE', determining how the domain name is routed within AWS.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.domain_name_configurations.ip_address_ty: Specifies the IP address type (IPv4 or dual-stack) used by the custom domain name's endpoint, controlling whether the domain resolves to IPv4-only or both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.domain_name_configurations.ownership_ver: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to verify ownership of the custom domain name in the API Gateway v2 domain name configuration.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.domain_name_configurations.security_poli: Specifies the TLS security policy (TLS_1_0 or TLS_1_2) applied to the custom domain name's API Gateway HTTPS endpoint.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.regional_domain_name: The regional domain name automatically assigned by API Gateway v2 to this domain name, serving as the regional endpoint target for routing traffic to the API.
aws_api_gateway_v2_domain_name.regional_hosted_zone_id: The Amazon Route 53 hosted zone ID associated with the regional endpoint of this API Gateway v2 domain name.

aws_api_gateway_v2_integration.tls_config.server_name_to_verify: Defines the server name that API Gateway uses to verify the certificate presented by the target endpoint for a private integration, overriding the target hostname when necessary.

aws_api_gateway_v2_integration_response.integration_response_id: The automatically generated identifier for this integration response, assigned by AWS when the resource is created.

aws_api_gateway_v2_model.model_id: The unique identifier automatically assigned by Amazon API Gateway to this model when it is created.

aws_api_gateway_v2_route_response.response_parameters: A map of route response parameter names (e.g., header.x-custom-header) to a boolean indicating whether that parameter is required in the route response.
aws_api_gateway_v2_route_response.route_response_id: The unique identifier that AWS API Gateway assigns to the route response upon creation, returned as a read-only value for referencing the route response in subsequent API operations.

aws_api_gateway_v2_routing_rule.conditions.match_headers.any_of.header: The name of the HTTP request header that is evaluated by the 'any_of' header-matching condition to determine if the routing rule applies.
aws_api_gateway_v2_routing_rule.routing_rule_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this API Gateway v2 routing rule within the AWS account and region, used for IAM policies and resource-level references.

aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.access_log_settings: Configures access logging for the API Gateway stage, including the CloudWatch Logs destination ARN and the log format template.
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.access_log_settings.destination_arn: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which the API Gateway stage sends access logs.
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.access_log_settings.format: The format string used to customize the access log output for the API Gateway v2 stage, which can include API Gateway context variables such as $context.requestId and $context.identity.sourceIp.
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.default_route_settings: The default route settings for the stage, including throttling, logging, and data trace settings, that apply to all routes unless a specific route overrides them.
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.default_route_settings.data_trace_enable: Enables detailed tracing (full request/response data capture) for the default route of the API Gateway stage, which is used with integration logging.
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.default_route_settings.detailed_metrics_: When true, enables detailed CloudWatch metrics for the default route of the API Gateway v2 stage.
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.default_route_settings.logging_level: Sets the logging level for the default route in the API Gateway v2 stage, controlling which execution logs are emitted (values such as ERROR, WARN, INFO, or OFF).
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.default_route_settings.throttling_burst_: Sets the throttling burst limit for the default route of the API Gateway v2 stage, controlling the maximum number of requests that can be handled before throttling is applied.
aws_api_gateway_v2_stage.default_route_settings.throttling_rate_l: Sets the per-second request rate limit for the default route throttling settings of the API Gateway v2 stage, used to control the maximum number of requests per second before throttling occurs.

aws_api_gateway_v2_vpc_link.vpc_link_id: The service-generated unique identifier (VpcLinkId) assigned to the VPC link when it is created.

aws_api_gateway_vpc_link.description: A user-defined textual description of the VPC link, used to identify and manage the link in API Gateway.
aws_api_gateway_vpc_link.name: The user-friendly name of the VPC link, which identifies it within API Gateway.
aws_api_gateway_vpc_link.tags.key: Identifies the key of a user-defined tag attached to the API Gateway VPC Link, used to organize and categorize the resource via AWS tagging conventions.
aws_api_gateway_vpc_link.tags.value: Specifies the value for a tag key attached to the VPC Link, enabling metadata-based management, cost allocation, and access control for the resource.
aws_api_gateway_vpc_link.target_arns: Specifies the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the Network Load Balancers that the VPC link routes API traffic to, allowing API Gateway to access private resources in a VPC.
aws_api_gateway_vpc_link.vpc_link_id: The unique identifier (e.g., an alphanumeric string) assigned by AWS to this VPC link, used to reference the link in API Gateway configurations.

aws_app_config_application.tags.key: The tag key of a key-value pair attached to the AWS AppConfig application, used for metadata, cost tracking, and IAM-based access control.

aws_app_config_configuration_profile.tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag to attach to the AppConfig configuration profile, used for categorizing or identifying the resource.
aws_app_config_configuration_profile.tags.value: The value of a tag key-value pair applied to the AppConfig configuration profile, used for resource categorization and management.
aws_app_config_configuration_profile.validators.content: The content of the validator, which is a JSON schema when the validator type is JSON_SCHEMA or the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Lambda function when the validator type is LAMBDA.
aws_app_config_configuration_profile.validators.type: The type of the validator, which determines whether it validates the configuration using a JSON schema (JSON_SCHEMA) or a custom AWS Lambda function (LAMBDA).

aws_app_config_deployment.dynamic_extension_parameters: A list of key-value pairs that specify dynamic parameter values to be passed to the AppConfig extension hooks (e.g., Lambda functions) when the deployment is executed.
aws_app_config_deployment.dynamic_extension_parameters.extension_r: The name of the AppConfig extension that consumes this dynamic parameter during deployment.
aws_app_config_deployment.dynamic_extension_parameters.parameter_n: The name of the dynamic extension parameter being set for the AppConfig deployment, used to pass custom configuration to an extension (such as a Lambda function) during a deployment event.
aws_app_config_deployment.dynamic_extension_parameters.parameter_v: Provides the dynamic value supplied to an extension parameter at deployment time, overriding the extension's default parameter value for this deployment.

aws_app_config_deployment_strategy.tags.key: The key portion of a key-value tag applied to the AWS AppConfig deployment strategy, used to assign custom metadata for resource management and cost allocation.
aws_app_config_deployment_strategy.tags.value: The value portion of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS AppConfig deployment strategy, used to label and categorize the resource for cost tracking and operational management.

aws_app_config_environment.monitors.alarm_arn: The ARN of the Amazon CloudWatch alarm that AppConfig monitors for this environment to detect potential issues during configuration deployments.
aws_app_config_environment.monitors.alarm_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS AppConfig assumes to evaluate the CloudWatch alarm for this monitor during a deployment.
aws_app_config_environment.tags.key: The key of a tag applied to the AWS AppConfig environment, used for resource organization and cost allocation.
aws_app_config_environment.tags.value: The value of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS AppConfig environment, used for managing and identifying the resource (e.g., cost allocation or categorization).

aws_app_config_experiment_definition.treatments.description: A user-defined description of a treatment, which explains the purpose or configuration of that treatment in an AWS AppConfig experiment.

aws_app_config_extension.actions: The actions that this AppConfig extension performs when invoked, each defining an action name, target URI, and optional IAM role ARN.
aws_app_config_extension.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AppConfig extension.
aws_app_config_extension.latest_version_number: The version number of the current extension to be replaced, used as an optimistic concurrency check when updating the extension to prevent overwriting concurrent changes.
aws_app_config_extension.parameters: Defines the set of input parameters for the extension, including each parameter's name, description, whether it is required, and an optional default value, which are referenced when the extension is invoked during AppConfig configuration deployments.
aws_app_config_extension.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AWS AppConfig extension, used to organize and identify the extension resource.
aws_app_config_extension.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the AWS AppConfig extension, used to assign custom metadata for identifying, organizing, and managing the extension resource.
aws_app_config_extension.version_number: The version number assigned to the extension by AWS AppConfig, which increments each time the extension is updated.

aws_app_config_extension_association.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AppConfig extension association.
aws_app_config_extension_association.extension_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AppConfig extension that this association applies to.
aws_app_config_extension_association.extension_identifier: The name, ID, or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS AppConfig extension to associate with the target resource.
aws_app_config_extension_association.extension_version_number: The version number of the extension to associate with the resource; if not specified, the latest version of the extension is used.
aws_app_config_extension_association.id: The system-generated unique identifier for the extension association.
aws_app_config_extension_association.parameters: Specifies the key-value pairs of parameters defined by the AppConfig extension that are passed to the extension when it runs for the associated resource.
aws_app_config_extension_association.resource_arn: The ARN of the AppConfig resource (such as an application, environment, or configuration profile) with which the extension is associated.
aws_app_config_extension_association.resource_identifier: The ARN of the AppConfig application, environment, or configuration profile to which the extension is associated and will be applied.
aws_app_config_extension_association.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the AppConfig extension association, used to organize and identify the resource.
aws_app_config_extension_association.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the AppConfig extension association, where the tag key is the map key in the tags block.

aws_app_flow_connector_profile.connector_profile_config.connector_profi: The Amplitude connector-specific credentials, including the API key and secret key, used to authorize AWS AppFlow to access your Amplitude data.
The Amplitude API key used by AppFlow to authenticate the connector profile with Amplitude's analytics service.
The Amplitude API secret key used by AppFlow to authenticate with your Amplitude account when establishing the connector profile.
The credentials for a custom connector, containing properties for custom authentication, API key, or basic authentication parameters.
Contains the API key and, optionally, the secret key used for API key authentication with a custom connector in AppFlow.
This field holds the actual API key value used for authenticating with the custom connector in AWS AppFlow, which is required when API key-based credentials are configured.
This field specifies the secret key that accompanies the API key for authenticating requests to the custom connector endpoint in AWS AppFlow.
Specifies the authentication mechanism for the custom connector, which must be one of APIKEY, BASIC, CUSTOM, or OAUTH2.
Contains the username and password used for basic authentication when connecting to the custom connector endpoint.
The password to use with the username for basic authentication to the custom connector.
The username used for basic (username/password) authentication when connecting to the custom connector in AppFlow.
Specifies custom authentication credentials for the custom connector, including the custom authentication type and a map of credential key-value pairs required by the external system.

Specifies the named custom authentication type (e.g., a connector-specific scheme) that the AppFlow custom connector uses for custom authentication, and is required when configuring custom connector credentials for this profile.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 token URL and grant type used by the custom connector to obtain an access token for authorization.
The OAuth 2.0 access token that AppFlow uses to authenticate requests to the custom connector's API.
The client identifier (client ID) issued by the OAuth2 authorization server for the custom connector application.
The client secret paired with the OAuth 2.0 client ID, used by AppFlow to authenticate with the custom connector's authorization server when refreshing access tokens.
The OAuth 2.0 request details containing the authorization code and redirect URI used to obtain or refresh access tokens for the custom connector profile.
The refresh token used to obtain new access tokens when the current access token expires for the custom connector's OAuth2 authentication.
Specifies the credentials required to authenticate with Datadog, including the API key and application key, for use in an AppFlow connector profile.
The Datadog API key that authenticates the AppFlow connector profile to the Datadog API, required for establishing a connection.
The application key for the Datadog API, used with the API key to authenticate the Datadog connector profile in Amazon AppFlow.
The Dynatrace credentials object holds the API token that AppFlow uses to authenticate with a Dynatrace instance for data transfer operations.
The API token used to authenticate with Dynatrace when creating the AppFlow connector profile.
Specifies the Google Analytics-specific OAuth 2.0 credentials (access token, refresh token, and OAuth request details) used to authorize AWS AppFlow to connect to Google Analytics.
The OAuth 2.0 access token used by the AppFlow connector to authenticate with Google Analytics.
The OAuth client ID issued by Google for the Google Analytics connector, used in AppFlow to authenticate and authorize access to Google Analytics data.

aws_app_flow_connector_profile.connector_type: Specifies the service or data source type for the connector profile (e.g., Salesforce, SAPOData, Google BigQuery), which determines which connector-specific profile fields are applicable.

aws_app_flow_flow.destination_flow_config_list.api_version: Specifies the API version that the destination connector uses to interact with the target service when this flow writes data to the destination.
aws_app_flow_flow.destination_flow_config_list.connector_p: The name of the connector profile that specifies the destination connector's authentication and access settings, used by AppFlow to write data to the target system.
aws_app_flow_flow.destination_flow_config_list.connector_t: Specifies the connector type for the destination, such as Salesforce, Amazon S3, or Snowflake, which determines how AppFlow writes data to that destination.
aws_app_flow_flow.destination_flow_config_list.destination: Specifies the connector-specific properties required to configure the destination, such as the Amazon S3 bucket name, prefix, and output format when the destination is S3.
Defines the destination properties for a custom connector in AppFlow, specifying the target entity name and any custom properties required to write data to the third-party application.
A map of custom key-value properties required by the custom connector to configure the destination when writing data to the target system.
The name of the entity (such as a table or object) in the custom connector destination that the AppFlow flow writes data to.

Specifies how errors are handled when AppFlow writes data to the custom connector destination, including the S3 bucket and optional prefix for storing failed records and whether the flow fails on the first error.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket used to store error records when AppFlow fails to write data to the custom connector destination, as part of the error handling configuration.
The object key prefix to apply to error records that AppFlow writes to the configured S3 bucket when processing fails for this custom connector destination.
Specifies whether the flow stops processing at the first error, rather than continuing and writing error details to the configured error handling bucket.
Specifies the list of field names that uniquely identify records in the custom connector destination, used to determine record identity for deduplication or upsert operations.
Specifies the write operation type (INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, or DELETE) that AppFlow performs on the custom connector destination when transferring data.
Specifies the destination connector properties for Amazon EventBridge, including the name of the EventBridge event bus (the Object property) that receives the flow's data.

Configures how AppFlow handles errors when writing to the EventBridge destination, including the Amazon S3 bucket and prefix for storing error records and whether the flow fails on the first destination error.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where AppFlow stores failed records when error handling is configured for the destination EventBridge connector.
Specifies the S3 object key prefix under which error logs and failed event delivery records are stored when a flow targeting Amazon EventBridge encounters data processing errors.
Determines whether the flow immediately fails when the first destination write error occurs, instead of skipping the failed record and continuing with the remaining data.
Specifies the name of the Amazon EventBridge event bus that this AppFlow flow targets as the destination.
Defines the destination configuration for Amazon Lookout for Metrics, including the required `object` field that identifies the target dataset (measure set) in Lookout for Metrics.
The name of the Amazon Lookout for Metrics dataset (object) that receives the data from the flow.
Contains the destination-specific settings for Amazon AppFlow to write data to Marketo, including the required Marketo object name and optional error handling configuration.
Specifies how errors encountered during data transfer to Marketo are handled, including the Amazon S3 bucket and prefix for storing error logs and whether to fail on the first error.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that AppFlow uses to store error logs and failed records when handling errors for the Marketo destination connector.
The S3 prefix (folder path) within the configured Amazon S3 bucket where AppFlow writes error logs or failed records when transferring data to the Marketo destination.
Indicates whether the Amazon AppFlow flow stops and fails on the first error encountered when writing to Marketo, rather than continuing with subsequent records.
The Marketo object (such as Lead or Company) in the destination Marketo instance that the flow writes records to.

Specifies the configuration for writing data to an Amazon Redshift destination, including the S3 staging bucket (intermediateBucketName), the target Redshift table/object name, and optional error handling settings.
The object key prefix under which AppFlow writes staged data files in the intermediate S3 bucket before loading them into the Amazon Redshift destination.
Defines how errors encountered while writing data to Amazon Redshift are handled, including options to fail the flow on the first error or write error logs to a specified S3 bucket.
The S3 bucket name that AppFlow uses to store error logs or failed records when the Redshift destination connector encounters errors during a flow run.
The prefix applied to the S3 bucket path where AppFlow stores error logs or failed records when writing to Redshift, allowing you to organize error files under a common folder.

When set to true, the AppFlow flow stops immediately at the first error encountered while writing to the Redshift destination; when false, it continues processing and sends error records to the configured error-handling Amazon S3 bucket.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that AppFlow uses as a staging location to write data before copying it into Amazon Redshift.
The Amazon S3 object key in the intermediate bucket where the flow stages data before copying it into Redshift.
Configures Amazon S3 as the destination connector by specifying properties such as the target bucket name, object key prefix, and output format settings for the flow's destination.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where AppFlow writes the data for this destination flow configuration.
Specifies the object key prefix prepended to the names of files that AppFlow writes to the destination S3 bucket.
Configures the output file format and related settings, such as file type, prefix, and aggregation, for data written by the flow to the S3 destination.
Specifies the aggregation settings (e.g., None or SingleFile) that control whether AppFlow combines all flow-run data into a single S3 file or writes multiple files.
Specifies whether the flow's S3 destination output is aggregated into a single file (SingleFile) or kept as separate files (None, the default), directly controlling file grouping in the S3 bucket.
Specifies the target file size in megabytes for aggregated files written to Amazon S3 when aggregation is enabled in the flow destination configuration.
Specifies the file format (such as CSV, JSON, or Parquet) for the output files that AppFlow writes to the destination S3 bucket.
Defines the prefix type and format applied to S3 object keys (e.g., EXECUTION_ID, PATH, or a custom prefix) to organize output files in the configured S3 destination.
Specifies a list of source data fields whose values are used to construct a hierarchical path prefix in the S3 destination bucket, enabling partition-based organization of flow output files.

Sets the timestamp resolution (YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR, or MINUTE) used to generate the dynamic prefix for Amazon S3 output objects, controlling how files are grouped by time in the destination bucket.
Determines whether the prefix is applied to the individual file name (FILENAME) or to the entire object key path (PATH) for Amazon S3 destinations in AppFlow.

When enabled, this boolean preserves the original data types (such as string, integer, or boolean) of source fields when AppFlow writes to the S3 destination, instead of converting them, ensuring type fidelity during the flow.

Defines the Salesforce-specific destination properties for a flow, such as the target Salesforce object and the write operation type (e.g., INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT), used when AppFlow writes data to Salesforce.
Specifies the Salesforce Data Transfer API (e.g., REST, BULK, BULKV2) that AppFlow uses to write data to the destination Salesforce object.
Specifies error handling for the Salesforce destination, including the Amazon S3 bucket and prefix for error records and whether the flow fails on the first error.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where AppFlow stores error logs and failed record data when writes to the Salesforce destination fail.
The S3 object key prefix that is prepended to the filenames when AppFlow writes error handling files (such as failed records) to the specified error handling bucket.
When true, the AppFlow flow stops processing and fails immediately on the first record write error to Salesforce, rather than skipping the failed record and continuing with remaining records.
Specifies the list of field names in the Salesforce object that are used as external identifiers for upsert operations when writing records to the destination.
The Salesforce object name (e.g., Account, Contact) into which the flow writes the destination records.
Specifies the write operation type (INSERT, UPDATE, or UPSERT) that AppFlow performs when writing data to the Salesforce destination.
This object specifies the SAPOData destination-specific settings for the AppFlow flow, such as the target SAP object path and the configuration for error and success response handling.
Configures error handling for the SAPOData destination connector, allowing you to specify the S3 bucket where failed records are written and whether the flow stops on the first error.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where AppFlow writes error logs or failed records when a transfer to the SAPOData destination fails.
The Amazon S3 object key prefix under which error logs are stored for this SAPOData destination when flow runs encounter errors, as part of the error handling configuration.
Determines whether the flow fails on the first error encountered during data transfer to the SAPOData destination, causing the flow run to stop immediately instead of processing remaining records.
The list of field names that serve as the unique identifier (primary key) for records written to the SAPOData destination, enabling upsert and deduplication operations in the AppFlow flow.
The object path for the SAP OData entity to which data is written, such as the entity set name in the SAP OData service.
Configuration specifying the Amazon S3 bucket and optional prefix where AWS AppFlow stores the response payload for successfully processed records when using SAPOData as a destination.
The name of the S3 bucket where AppFlow stores the success response payload for SAPOData destination operations when response handling is enabled.
The S3 object key prefix under which successful response files are saved when the SAPOData destination writes response data to the configured Amazon S3 bucket.
Specifies the write operation type (such as INSERT, UPDATE, or UPSERT) that AppFlow uses when writing data to the SAP OData destination.
Configuration for Snowflake as the destination connector, including target object, intermediate bucket, and error handling settings, within an AppFlow flow's destination properties.
The object key prefix applied to files staged in the intermediate S3 bucket before Amazon AppFlow loads them into the Snowflake table.
Configuration for handling errors when writing to Snowflake, including an S3 bucket and prefix for storing failed records and an option to fail the flow on the first error.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where AWS AppFlow writes failed records when error handling is configured for the Snowflake destination connector.
The S3 object key prefix under the error-handling bucket where AppFlow writes failed records for Snowflake destination flows.

If set to true, the AppFlow flow fails immediately on the first error encountered while writing to Snowflake; if false, the flow continues and errors are handled according to the surrounding error handling configuration.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket used as an intermediate staging location for data before it is loaded into Snowflake.
The name of the target Snowflake table (object) where the flow writes the transferred data.
Configuration for the Upsolver destination connector, defining the target S3 bucket, optional prefix, and output format for data delivery via AppFlow.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket to which Upsolver writes the data flowing from AppFlow.
The Amazon S3 object key prefix under which Upsolver writes the flow's output files, used to organize and locate exported data within the destination bucket.
Specifies the S3 output format for Upsolver destination, including the file type, aggregation configuration, and S3 key prefix settings.

Determines how Upsolver aggregates the data files written to Amazon S3, allowing you to specify an aggregation type such as 'None' or 'SingleFile' to control whether records are written as individual objects or combined into a single file.
Specifies how Upsolver aggregates data in Amazon S3 output, with values such as 'None' for individual records or 'Aggregate' to combine records based on the configured aggregation threshold.
The target file size (in megabytes) that Upsolver uses to determine when to roll over aggregated records into a new output file in Amazon S3.
Specifies the format (such as JSON or CSV) of the data files that AppFlow writes to Amazon S3 when using Upsolver as the destination connector.
Defines the prefix (folder structure and naming) for S3 object keys when Upsolver writes output data to Amazon S3, including the prefix type and format used to organize files.

Specifies the list of path prefix hierarchy components (e.g., EXECUTION_ID, SCHEMA_VERSION, CONNECTOR_ENTITY) that Amazon AppFlow uses to organize output files written by the Upsolver connector to Amazon S3.

Determines the time granularity (such as YEAR, MONTH, DAY, or HOUR) that AppFlow appends to the S3 object key prefix when delivering data to Upsolver, controlling how output files are partitioned by time.
Specifies whether the prefix for S3 object keys is configured as a filename prefix or a path prefix when Upsolver writes data to Amazon S3.
Defines the Zendesk-specific destination connector settings, such as the target Zendesk object, that AppFlow uses when writing flow records to Zendesk.

Specifies the error handling configuration (such as the Amazon S3 bucket for storing error records and whether to fail on the first error) for records that fail during transfer to the Zendesk destination.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where AppFlow stores error records and logs when the Zendesk destination connector fails during a flow run.
Amazon S3 bucket prefix under which error/failed records for the Zendesk destination connector are stored when error handling is enabled.
Controls whether an Amazon AppFlow flow stops and fails on the first error encountered when writing data to Zendesk, or continues and logs errors to the configured error handling bucket.
A list of field names that serve as the unique identifier (primary key) for records written to the Zendesk destination, enabling AppFlow to upsert records correctly.
Specifies the Zendesk object (such as Ticket or User) that Amazon AppFlow writes the flow's records into as the destination.
Specifies the write operation type (INSERT, UPDATE, or UPSERT) used when writing data to the Zendesk destination in the AppFlow flow.

Defines the Datadog source configuration for the flow, where the ApiKey and ApplicationKey fields provide the credentials needed to connect to and pull data from Datadog.
Specifies the Datadog object name (such as an event, metric, or other Datadog data source) from which AppFlow reads data in the flow.

Specifies the S3 source connector settings in AppFlow, such as the bucket name, optional object prefix, and the format of the input files (e.g., CSV or JSON) to read from Amazon S3.
The name of the S3 bucket from which the AppFlow flow reads source data for ingestion.
The object key prefix used to filter S3 objects for the source connector in the AppFlow flow.
Determines the file format (for example, CSV or JSON) that the S3 source connector expects when reading source files for the AppFlow flow.
Specifies the file format of the source data in S3 (e.g., CSV, JSON, or Parquet) for the AppFlow flow's S3 source.
Defines the Salesforce-specific source configuration for the flow, including the Salesforce object to read from and optionally the fields to retrieve.
Specifies whether AppFlow uses the Salesforce REST or Bulk API to transfer data from Salesforce for this source connection.
