aws_app_stream_app_block_builder.vpc_config: Specifies the VPC configuration for the AppStream 2.0 app block builder, including the security group IDs and subnet IDs that define the network environment in which the builder runs.
aws_app_stream_app_block_builder.vpc_config.security_group_ids: Specifies the list of EC2 security group IDs to associate with the AppStream 2.0 App Block Builder's elastic network interface within the configured VPC.
aws_app_stream_app_block_builder.vpc_config.subnet_ids: Specifies the list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the AppStream 2.0 app block builder will be launched, controlling which subnets are used for its elastic network interface.

aws_app_stream_application.app_block_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the app block that the application is associated with.
aws_app_stream_application.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AppStream 2.0 application.
aws_app_stream_application.attributes_to_delete: A list of application attribute names to delete from the AppStream application when the CloudFormation stack is updated, used to remove properties that were omitted from the updated template.
aws_app_stream_application.created_time: The timestamp when the AppStream application was created.
aws_app_stream_application.description: A user-facing description of the AppStream 2.0 application that is displayed to end users when browsing available applications.
aws_app_stream_application.display_name: A user-friendly name for the application that is displayed in the AppStream 2.0 application catalog.
aws_app_stream_application.icon_s3_location: Specifies the S3 bucket and key where the application's icon image file is stored.
aws_app_stream_application.icon_s3_location.s3_bucket: The S3 bucket that holds the application icon image file for the AppStream application.
aws_app_stream_application.icon_s3_location.s3_key: The S3 object key (path) of the application icon image within the S3 bucket specified by the parent IconS3Location property.
aws_app_stream_application.instance_families: Specifies the list of AppStream 2.0 instance families (e.g., GENERAL_PURPOSE, MEMORY_OPTIMIZED) that this application supports, determining which fleet instance types can launch it.
aws_app_stream_application.launch_parameters: The command-line arguments (parameters) passed to the application when it is launched in an AppStream 2.0 streaming session.
aws_app_stream_application.launch_path: The path to the executable file of the application that AppStream 2.0 launches on the streaming instance.
aws_app_stream_application.name: The unique name of the AppStream 2.0 application, which serves as its identifier within the AWS account and region.
aws_app_stream_application.platforms: Identifies the operating system platforms on which the AppStream 2.0 application can be launched, with valid values including WINDOWS and AMAZON_LINUX.
aws_app_stream_application.tags.tag_value: The value of a tag assigned to the AppStream application, paired with the corresponding tag key in the tags list.
aws_app_stream_application.tags.value: The value for the specified tag key, which can be used to categorize and manage the AppStream application resource.
aws_app_stream_application.working_directory: Specifies the working directory that the application uses when launched on a streaming instance.

aws_app_stream_application_entitlement_a.application_identifier: The ARN of the AppStream application that is being associated with the entitlement.
aws_app_stream_application_entitlement_a.entitlement_name: The name of the AppStream 2.0 entitlement that the application is being associated with.
aws_app_stream_application_entitlement_a.stack_name: The name of the AppStream 2.0 stack to which the application and entitlement association is attached.

aws_app_stream_application_fleet_associa.application_arn: The ARN of the AppStream 2.0 application to associate with the fleet.
aws_app_stream_application_fleet_associa.fleet_name: The name of the AppStream 2.0 fleet to which the application is associated.

aws_app_stream_directory_config.certificate_based_auth_properties: Configures certificate-based authentication for the AppStream 2.0 directory configuration, specifying the status (enabled/disabled) and the ARN of the certificate authority used to issue and validate user certificates.
aws_app_stream_directory_config.certificate_based_auth_properties.certif: The ARN of the AWS Certificate Manager Private CA that AppStream 2.0 uses to issue certificates for certificate-based authentication in this directory configuration.
aws_app_stream_directory_config.certificate_based_auth_properties.status: Indicates whether certificate-based authentication is enabled or disabled for the AppStream directory configuration.
aws_app_stream_directory_config.directory_name: The fully qualified name of the Active Directory domain (for example, corp.example.com) that the AppStream 2.0 directory configuration connects to.
aws_app_stream_directory_config.organizational_unit_distinguished_names: Specifies the list of organizational unit (OU) distinguished names in the Active Directory where computer objects for streaming instances are created.
aws_app_stream_directory_config.service_account_credentials: The service account credentials (account name and password) that AppStream 2.0 uses to join streaming instances to the Active Directory domain.
aws_app_stream_directory_config.service_account_credentials.account_name: The user name of the service account that AppStream 2.0 uses to join streaming instances to the Active Directory domain.
aws_app_stream_directory_config.service_account_credentials.account_pass: The password for the service account that AppStream 2.0 uses to join streaming instances to the Active Directory domain.

aws_app_stream_entitlement.app_visibility: Specifies whether the entitlement grants access to all applications in the stack ('ALL') or only to applications explicitly associated with the entitlement ('ASSOCIATED').
aws_app_stream_entitlement.attributes: A list of key-value attribute pairs that define the entitlement's user-specific settings, such as a user group membership or rule, which AppStream matches against the user's identity to determine which applications they can access.
aws_app_stream_entitlement.attributes.name: The unique name assigned to the AppStream 2.0 entitlement, used to reference the entitlement within its stack.
aws_app_stream_entitlement.attributes.value: The 'Value' field of a single attribute in the list of attributes attached to an AWS AppStream 2.0 entitlement, providing the string value associated with the attribute's Name.
aws_app_stream_entitlement.created_time: The date and time when the AppStream 2.0 entitlement was created, returned in ISO 8601 format.
aws_app_stream_entitlement.description: A text description of the entitlement that helps administrators identify its purpose or usage within the AppStream 2.0 stack.
aws_app_stream_entitlement.last_modified_time: The date and time when the AppStream entitlement was last modified, automatically computed by AWS and returned as a string (read-only).
aws_app_stream_entitlement.name: Specifies the unique name for the AppStream 2.0 entitlement, used as the primary identifier within its parent stack.
aws_app_stream_entitlement.stack_name: The name of the AppStream stack that this entitlement is associated with, specifying which stack the entitlement grants access to.

aws_app_stream_fleet.compute_capacity: Configures the compute capacity for the fleet by specifying the desired number of streaming instances.
aws_app_stream_fleet.compute_capacity.desired_instances: The desired number of streaming instances that AppStream 2.0 maintains in the fleet.
aws_app_stream_fleet.compute_capacity.desired_sessions: Specifies the desired number of concurrent streaming sessions for an On-Demand AppStream 2.0 fleet, which AppStream uses to scale the fleet's capacity.
aws_app_stream_fleet.description: A user-provided description that clarifies the purpose or use of the AppStream 2.0 fleet.
aws_app_stream_fleet.disable_imdsv1: When true, disables the use of the EC2 Instance Metadata Service version 1 (IMDSv1) on the streaming instances of this AppStream 2.0 fleet, forcing IMDSv2 for instance metadata access.
aws_app_stream_fleet.disconnect_timeout_in_seconds: The maximum time in seconds that a streaming session remains active after a user disconnects before the session is terminated.
aws_app_stream_fleet.display_name: A user-friendly name for the fleet that is displayed in the AppStream 2.0 console and to end users.
aws_app_stream_fleet.domain_join_info: Specifies the Active Directory domain and organizational unit (OU) that the fleet's streaming instances will join, including the directory name and OU distinguished name, to enable domain authentication.
aws_app_stream_fleet.domain_join_info.directory_name: Specifies the fully qualified name of the Active Directory domain (e.g., corp.example.com) that the AppStream 2.0 streaming instances will join when the fleet is launched.
aws_app_stream_fleet.domain_join_info.organizational_unit_dis: The distinguished name of the organizational unit (OU) in Active Directory where the computer accounts for the streaming instances are created when they join the domain.
aws_app_stream_fleet.enable_default_internet_access: Indicates whether the fleet's streaming instances are given a default internet gateway, enabling users to access the internet from their streaming sessions.
aws_app_stream_fleet.fleet_type: Specifies whether the AppStream 2.0 fleet uses Always On instances that run continuously or On Demand instances that start only when a user connects, governing instance provisioning and cost.
aws_app_stream_fleet.iam_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AppStream 2.0 assumes to call AWS APIs on behalf of the fleet's streaming instances.
aws_app_stream_fleet.id: The unique identifier of the AppStream fleet, which is set to the fleet name provided during creation.
aws_app_stream_fleet.idle_disconnect_timeout_in_seconds: Specifies the number of seconds a user can remain idle in an AppStream 2.0 streaming session before being automatically disconnected, where 0 means no idle timeout is applied.
aws_app_stream_fleet.image_arn: The ARN of the AppStream 2.0 image that the fleet uses to launch streaming instances.
aws_app_stream_fleet.image_name: The name of the AppStream 2.0 image to use for the fleet's streaming instances, specified as an alternative to ImageArn.
aws_app_stream_fleet.instance_type: The Amazon EC2 instance type (e.g., stream.standard.medium) that specifies the compute and memory resources for the streaming instances in the AppStream 2.0 fleet.
aws_app_stream_fleet.max_concurrent_sessions: The maximum number of concurrent sessions that the fleet can support, limiting how many users can stream simultaneously.
aws_app_stream_fleet.max_sessions_per_instance: Specifies the maximum number of concurrent streaming sessions that a single fleet instance can host, which AppStream 2.0 uses to determine how many instances to start and stop to meet capacity.
aws_app_stream_fleet.max_user_duration_in_seconds: Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, that a streaming session can remain active before AppStream 2.0 disconnects the user.
aws_app_stream_fleet.name: The required name of the AppStream 2.0 fleet, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region.
aws_app_stream_fleet.platform: Specifies the operating system platform for the fleet's streaming instances, with valid values of WINDOWS or AMAZON_LINUX2.
aws_app_stream_fleet.root_volume_config: Configures the root volume of the AppStream 2.0 fleet's streaming instances, specifying the volume size in gigabytes and optional USB device filter strings.
aws_app_stream_fleet.root_volume_config.volume_size_in_gb: The size, in gigabytes, of the root volume (C: drive) for each streaming instance in the AppStream 2.0 fleet, which determines the storage capacity available for the operating system and installed applications.
aws_app_stream_fleet.session_script_s3_location: Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and object key that contains the session script to be run on AppStream 2.0 streaming instances for user sessions.
aws_app_stream_fleet.session_script_s3_location.s3_bucket: The name of the S3 bucket where the session script file is stored for the AppStream fleet.
aws_app_stream_fleet.session_script_s3_location.s3_key: The S3 object key (file path/name) of the session script within the S3 bucket specified in the session_script_s3_location.
aws_app_stream_fleet.stream_view: Determines whether the fleet streams applications to users (APP) or provides a full desktop view (DESKTOP).
aws_app_stream_fleet.tags: A list of key-value tags to attach to the AppStream fleet, used to categorize and manage the fleet resource.
aws_app_stream_fleet.tags.value: The value of a tag to associate with the AppStream 2.0 fleet.
aws_app_stream_fleet.usb_device_filter_strings: Specifies the USB device filter strings that control which USB devices are available to users during AppStream 2.0 streaming sessions, such as 'vendorId:productId' patterns (up to 20 strings).
aws_app_stream_fleet.vpc_config: Specifies the VPC configuration for the AppStream fleet, including the subnets and security group IDs that the fleet's streaming instances use.
aws_app_stream_fleet.vpc_config.security_group_ids: The list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the fleet instances, controlling inbound and outbound network traffic for AppStream 2.0 streaming instances.
aws_app_stream_fleet.vpc_config.subnet_ids: Identifies the subnets where the fleet's streaming instances are launched, to place them within your VPC.

aws_app_stream_image_builder.access_endpoints: Specifies the VPC endpoints (via endpoint type and VPC endpoint ID) used for the image builder's streaming sessions, controlling the network access for the image builder.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.access_endpoints.endpoint_type: Specifies whether the VPC endpoint for this access endpoint is used for AppStream 2.0 streaming or desktop sessions, with valid values such as AppStream.Streaming and AppStream.Desktop.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.access_endpoints.vpce_id: The ID of the VPC endpoint used as a private access endpoint for the image builder's streaming session.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.appstream_agent_version: Specifies the version of the AppStream 2.0 agent to install on the image builder, such as a date-based version string (e.g., '01-04-2022') or 'LATEST' to use the latest version.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.description: A user-provided description of the AppStream 2.0 image builder.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.display_name: The display name of the image builder, which is a user-friendly name shown in the AppStream 2.0 console.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.domain_join_info: Specifies the Active Directory domain and service account credentials used to join the image builder to a domain.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.domain_join_info.directory_name: The fully qualified name of the Active Directory domain (e.g., example.com) that the image builder joins via the domain join configuration.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.domain_join_info.organizational_unit_dis: The distinguished name of the organizational unit in the Active Directory domain where the image builder computer account is created.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.enable_default_internet_access: Whether the image builder has default internet access enabled, allowing it to connect to the internet without a custom VPC configuration.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.iam_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AppStream 2.0 assumes to grant the image builder permissions to access AWS services and resources on your behalf.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.image_arn: The ARN of the AppStream image to use as the base for this image builder.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.image_name: The name of the AppStream 2.0 image used as the base for the image builder.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.instance_type: The Amazon EC2 instance type (e.g., stream.standard.medium) used to launch the AppStream 2.0 image builder, determining the compute and memory resources available during image creation.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.name: The name of the AppStream 2.0 image builder, which must be unique within the AWS account and is used to identify the image builder in AppStream 2.0.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.root_volume_config: Specifies the size and encryption settings for the root volume of the AppStream 2.0 image builder, including the volume size in gigabytes and an optional AWS KMS key for encryption.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.root_volume_config.volume_size_in_gb: Specifies the size of the root volume of the image builder in gigabytes.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.softwares_to_install: A list of software applications to install on the image builder during initial setup, enabling common applications like Chrome or Firefox to be pre-installed for customized images.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.softwares_to_uninstall: Specifies a list of software to uninstall from the base image when creating the AppStream image builder, letting you remove pre-installed applications to customize the image for your needs.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.streaming_url: The URL used to connect to the image builder from a web browser for administrative tasks.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.tags: Specifies the list of key-value tags to attach to the AppStream 2.0 image builder resource.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag applied to this AppStream 2.0 image builder, allowing you to organize, track, and control access to the resource.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.tags.value: The value part of a key-value tag applied to the AppStream 2.0 Image Builder, enabling you to categorize and track the resource for cost allocation and operational management.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.vpc_config: Specifies the VPC configuration for the image builder, including the security group IDs and subnet IDs that the image builder uses for network access.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.vpc_config.security_group_ids: The list of security group IDs that are attached to the image builder's elastic network interface within the specified VPC.
aws_app_stream_image_builder.vpc_config.subnet_ids: Specifies the list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the AppStream image builder is launched.

aws_app_stream_stack.access_endpoints.endpoint_type: Determines the type of access endpoint for the AppStream stack, either APPSTREAM for the AppStream 2.0 streaming interface or INTERNET for a public internet interface.
aws_app_stream_stack.access_endpoints.vpce_id: The VPC endpoint ID that AppStream 2.0 uses for this access endpoint, enabling controlled streaming access through a private VPC endpoint.
aws_app_stream_stack.agent_access_config.settings.agent_actio: Specifies whether to allow or deny access to the AppStream 2.0 agent version indicated by the corresponding version setting, where the action can be 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
aws_app_stream_stack.agent_access_config.settings.permission: Specifies whether the AppStream 2.0 stack permits agent access during streaming sessions, with the permission value controlling the enabled/disabled state of the agent access configuration.
aws_app_stream_stack.storage_connectors.connector_type: The type of storage connector to enable for this AppStream stack, such as HOMEFOLDERS, GOOGLE_DRIVE, or ONE_DRIVE.
aws_app_stream_stack.storage_connectors.domains: Specifies the list of domains (e.g., Google Drive or OneDrive) that this storage connector is allowed to use, restricting the connector to those domains for file access and synchronization.
aws_app_stream_stack.storage_connectors.resource_identifier: The ResourceIdentifier for a storage connector specifies the backing resource: for HOME_FOLDERS it is the ARN of the Amazon S3 bucket that stores home folders, while for GOOGLE_DRIVE or ONE_DRIVE it is the domain name of the user's cloud storage account.
aws_app_stream_stack.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AWS AppStream stack, used to organize and identify the stack for cost allocation and access control.
aws_app_stream_stack.tags.value: The value of an AWS tag applied to the AppStream 2.0 stack, used for organizing and identifying the stack in cost allocation and resource management.
aws_app_stream_stack.user_settings.action: The AppStream 2.0 user action (such as CLIPBOARD_COPY_FROM_LOCAL_DEVICE or FILE_UPLOAD) to which the permission setting applies.
aws_app_stream_stack.user_settings.maximum_length: For each entry in the stack's user settings, this field defines the maximum clipboard data size (in bytes) allowed for actions that copy clipboard content to or from the local device.
aws_app_stream_stack.user_settings.permission: Specifies whether the user action (identified by the sibling 'action' field) is enabled or disabled for the AppStream 2.0 stack, with valid values being 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

aws_app_stream_stack_fleet_association.fleet_name: The name of the AppStream 2.0 fleet to associate with the stack.
aws_app_stream_stack_fleet_association.id: This computed identifier uniquely identifies the AppStream 2.0 stack-fleet association and is formed from the stack name and fleet name separated by a comma.
aws_app_stream_stack_fleet_association.stack_name: The name of the AppStream stack that the fleet will be associated with.

aws_app_sync_api.dns.http: The HTTP endpoint (URL) for the AppSync API, which is used to send GraphQL requests over unencrypted HTTP.
aws_app_sync_api.dns.realtime: The realtime DNS endpoint (fully qualified domain name) for the AppSync API, used by clients to establish WebSocket connections for real-time GraphQL subscriptions.
aws_app_sync_api.event_config.auth_providers.auth_type: Specifies the authentication type (e.g., AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS, AWS_IAM, OPENID_CONNECT) for an auth provider used in the AppSync API's event configuration for real-time WebSocket subscriptions.
aws_app_sync_api.event_config.auth_providers.cognito_conf: Configures Amazon Cognito User Pools as an authentication provider for the AppSync Events API by specifying the AWS region, user pool ID, and optional app client regex for authorization.
Defines a regular expression that the Cognito app client ID must match for the AppSync Event API's auth provider to grant access.
Specifies the AWS region where the associated Cognito User Pool is located, used to resolve the pool for event API authentication.
The ID of the Cognito user pool used as an authentication provider for the AppSync event API.
aws_app_sync_api.event_config.auth_providers.lambda_autho: Configures the Lambda authorizer settings (such as the Lambda function URI, result caching TTL, and identity validation expression) for an AWS_LAMBDA authentication provider used in the event configuration of an AWS AppSync API.
Specifies the time-to-live duration, in seconds, for caching the Lambda authorizer's result in an AWS AppSync event API.
The URI of the Lambda function that acts as the custom authorizer for this auth provider, which AppSync invokes to authorize requests to the event API.
A regular expression that the identity token must match for the Lambda authorizer to accept the request; if the token does not match, the request is denied.
aws_app_sync_api.event_config.auth_providers.open_idconne: Defines the OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication parameters—such as issuer, client ID, and token time-to-live settings—used by the event API's authentication provider to validate OIDC tokens for real-time connections.

Specifies the authorization token time-to-live (TTL) in seconds that AppSync uses to determine how long an OpenID Connect token remains valid for the event API's OpenID Connect authentication provider.
The client ID issued by your OpenID Connect provider for the AppSync API, used by AppSync to validate incoming tokens.
The number of milliseconds that a token remains valid after its issued-at (iat) time, used to validate the OIDC token in the AppSync API's event authentication provider.
The issuer URL of the OpenID Connect provider used to validate tokens for authorizing requests to the AWS AppSync event API.
aws_app_sync_api.event_config.connection_auth_modes.auth_: The authentication type (such as API_KEY, AWS_IAM, or AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS) used by AppSync to authorize client connections to the event API's real-time WebSocket endpoint.
Specifies the authentication mode type (such as API_KEY, AWS_IAM, or AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS) for one of the default authorization modes allowed when publishing to this AppSync event API's event configuration.
aws_app_sync_api.event_config.default_subscribe_auth_mode: The authentication type (e.g., API_KEY, AWS_IAM, AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS) that AppSync uses by default to authorize client subscribe operations on the Event API when no per-channel auth mode is configured.
aws_app_sync_api.event_config.log_config.cloud_watch_logs: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS AppSync assumes to write event logs to CloudWatch Logs for this API.
aws_app_sync_api.tags.key: The key of a tag to be applied to the AWS AppSync GraphQL API for resource management and cost allocation.
aws_app_sync_api.tags.value: The value of a tag key-value pair applied to the AWS AppSync API.

aws_app_sync_api_cache.api_caching_behavior: Determines the caching behavior for the AppSync API cache, either caching entire requests (FULL_REQUEST_CACHING) or only per-resolver results (PER_RESOLVER_CACHING).
aws_app_sync_api_cache.api_id: The unique ID of the AppSync API to which this cache configuration applies.
aws_app_sync_api_cache.at_rest_encryption_enabled: Indicates whether encryption at rest is enabled for the AppSync API cache, protecting cached data in the underlying ElastiCache for Redis cluster.
aws_app_sync_api_cache.health_metrics_config: Configures whether cache health metrics are enabled for the AppSync API cache, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.
aws_app_sync_api_cache.transit_encryption_enabled: Indicates whether encryption in transit is enabled for the AppSync API cache.
aws_app_sync_api_cache.ttl: Specifies the time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for cached responses, controlling how long items remain in the API cache before being purged.
aws_app_sync_api_cache.type: The cache instance type for the AppSync API cache (e.g., T2_SMALL, T2_MEDIUM, R4_LARGE), which determines the cache size and performance characteristics.

aws_app_sync_api_key.api_id: The unique identifier of the AppSync GraphQL API that this API key is associated with.
aws_app_sync_api_key.api_key: The generated API key value used for authenticating requests to the AppSync GraphQL API.
aws_app_sync_api_key.api_key_id: The unique identifier automatically assigned to the API key by AWS AppSync on creation.
aws_app_sync_api_key.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AppSync API key.
aws_app_sync_api_key.description: An optional user-provided description that helps identify the purpose or owner of the API key.
aws_app_sync_api_key.expires: The expiration time of the API key, expressed as the number of seconds since the Unix epoch.

aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.handler_configs: A map of named event handler configurations for this AppSync channel namespace, where each value defines the code executed by AppSync to process events on that handler.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.handler_configs.on_publish: Configures the runtime and entry point for the publish handler in the AppSync channel namespace, controlling how publish events are processed.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.handler_configs.on_publish.integration.l: This object configures the AWS Lambda integration for the on-publish handler, specifying the Lambda function ARN (and optional payload format) to invoke when a message is published to the channel namespace.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.handler_configs.on_subscribe: Defines the Lambda function settings (such as function ARN and invocation configuration) that AppSync invokes for the onSubscribe event in the channel namespace, enabling custom authorization and channel routing for client subscription requests.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.handler_configs.on_subscribe.integration: The Lambda configuration for the on_subscribe handler integration, specifying the ARN of the AWS Lambda function AppSync invokes to process or validate subscription requests in this channel namespace.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.publish_auth_modes: Configures the set of authorization modes (such as API key, IAM, or Cognito user pools) that are allowed for publishing messages to channels within this AWS AppSync channel namespace.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.publish_auth_modes.auth_type: Specifies the identity/authorization mode (such as API_KEY, AWS_IAM, AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS, OPENID_CONNECT, or AWS_LAMBDA) that clients must present when publishing events to the AppSync channel namespace.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.subscribe_auth_modes: Specifies the list of authorization modes permitted for clients when subscribing to events in this AppSync channel namespace.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.subscribe_auth_modes.auth_type: Specifies the authentication type (such as API_KEY, AWS_IAM, or AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS) that clients must use when subscribing to messages in this AWS AppSync channel namespace.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.tags.key: The key part of a key-value tag attached to the AWS AppSync channel namespace, providing metadata used to categorize the resource.
aws_app_sync_channel_namespace.tags.value: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the AppSync channel namespace resource.

aws_app_sync_data_source.dynamo_dbconfig: Provides the DynamoDB-specific configuration for the AppSync data source, including the target table name and AWS region (and optionally the read and write capacity settings used by the data source).
aws_app_sync_data_source.dynamo_dbconfig.delta_sync_config: Configures delta synchronization for the DynamoDB-backed AppSync data source, defining the delta sync table and TTL settings that allow the API to push incremental changes (including deletes) to connected clients.
aws_app_sync_data_source.elasticsearch_config: Specifies the endpoint and AWS region of an Amazon OpenSearch Service (formerly Elasticsearch) domain that the AppSync data source connects to when the data source type is AMAZON_ELASTICSEARCH.
aws_app_sync_data_source.event_bridge_config: Configures an Amazon EventBridge data source by specifying the event bus ARN that the AppSync data source will use to interact with EventBridge events.
aws_app_sync_data_source.http_config: Configures the HTTP endpoint and optional authorization settings for an AWS AppSync HTTP data source, including the endpoint URL and any IAM or API key authorization details.
aws_app_sync_data_source.http_config.authorization_config: Specifies the authorization type and, when using AWS_IAM, the AWS IAM signing configuration (signing region and service name) for requests to the HTTP endpoint.
aws_app_sync_data_source.http_config.authorization_config.aws_iam: Specifies the IAM signing region and service name for signing HTTP requests to the data source endpoint when the authorization type is AWS_IAM.
aws_app_sync_data_source.lambda_config: The configuration for an AWS Lambda data source, including the ARN of the Lambda function that AppSync invokes to read and write data.
aws_app_sync_data_source.metrics_config: Specifies whether CloudWatch metrics are enabled for this AppSync data source, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
aws_app_sync_data_source.open_search_service_config: Defines the connection settings (endpoint and region) for using an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain as the AppSync data source.
aws_app_sync_data_source.relational_database_config: Specifies the configuration for connecting the AppSync data source to an Amazon RDS or Aurora relational database, defining either the RDS HTTP endpoint (Data API) settings or a Lambda function that accesses the database.
aws_app_sync_data_source.relational_database_config.rds_http_endp: The HTTP endpoint configuration for the Amazon RDS relational database used by the AppSync data source, specifying the Aurora Serverless DB cluster, AWS Secrets Manager secret ARN, database name, and region to connect to.

aws_app_sync_domain_name.app_sync_domain_name: The actual AppSync domain name (e.g., `xxxxxxxxxx.appsync-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`) automatically generated by AppSync for this custom domain, read-only.
aws_app_sync_domain_name.certificate_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Certificate Manager certificate to associate with the AppSync custom domain name.
aws_app_sync_domain_name.description: An optional user-provided free-text description that identifies the purpose or context of the AppSync custom domain name in AWS management tools and APIs.
aws_app_sync_domain_name.domain_name: The fully qualified domain name (FQDN), such as api.example.com, that is associated with the AppSync API as its custom domain endpoint.
aws_app_sync_domain_name.hosted_zone_id: The Route 53 hosted zone ID associated with the AppSync domain name, used to configure DNS records that route traffic to the AppSync endpoint.
aws_app_sync_domain_name.tags.key: The key portion of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS::AppSync::DomainName resource, used to assign metadata for filtering, access control, or cost allocation to the AppSync custom domain.

aws_app_sync_domain_name_api_association.api_association_identifier: The unique identifier that AWS AppSync assigns to the domain name–API association, usable to reference the association in API calls and automation.
aws_app_sync_domain_name_api_association.api_id: The ID of the AppSync API to associate with the custom domain name.
aws_app_sync_domain_name_api_association.domain_name: The custom domain name (e.g., api.example.com) that is associated with the AWS AppSync API.

aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.additional_authentication_providers.auth: Defines the AWS AppSync authentication method (e.g., API_KEY, AWS_IAM, AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS, OPENID_CONNECT, or AWS_LAMBDA) that this additional authentication provider uses to authorize requests to the GraphQL API.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.additional_authentication_providers.lamb: Configures the Lambda authorizer settings, such as the authorizer URI and identity validation expression, for the additional authentication provider on the AppSync GraphQL API.

Specifies the time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for caching the Lambda authorizer result, after which AppSync discards the cached authorization response and invokes the Lambda authorizer again for the next request.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that serves as the custom authorizer for this additional AppSync authentication provider, invoked by AppSync to authorize requests.
Specifies a regular expression that AppSync uses to validate the identity token before invoking the Lambda authorizer function.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.additional_authentication_providers.open: Configuration for an OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication provider, including the issuer URL, client ID, and optional token TTL settings, used when adding an additional authentication provider to the GraphQL API.
The number of milliseconds that an OpenID Connect token remains valid after being issued to a user, controlling token expiration for authentication in AppSync.
The client identifier (audience) that AWS AppSync expects in the 'aud' claim of JWT tokens from the configured OpenID Connect provider, used to validate tokens presented by client applications.
The number of milliseconds that a token issued by the OpenID Connect provider remains valid after its 'issued at' (iat) time, controlling how long an issued token can be used for authentication.
The issuer URL for the OpenID Connect provider, which identifies the OIDC provider issuing the authentication tokens for this additional authentication provider.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.additional_authentication_providers.user: Configures the Amazon Cognito user pool settings for an additional authentication provider, specifying the user pool ID, AWS region, and default action for authentication.
A regular expression used to validate the app client ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool that is allowed to authenticate through this additional authentication provider.
The AWS Region in which the specified Amazon Cognito user pool for this additional authentication provider is located.
The ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool that this additional authentication provider uses to authenticate requests for the AppSync GraphQL API.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.enhanced_metrics_config: Specifies the enhanced metrics configuration for this AppSync GraphQL API, including toggles for resolver-level, data source-level, and operation-level CloudWatch metrics.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.lambda_authorizer_config: Defines the Lambda authorizer configuration for the GraphQL API, specifying the Lambda function ARN and optional settings for result caching and identity validation.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.log_config: The log_config block configures CloudWatch Logs for the AppSync GraphQL API, specifying the IAM role ARN and the field-level log level (e.g., ERROR or ALL) for the API's execution logs.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.open_idconnect_config: Configures the OpenID Connect (OIDC) settings for the GraphQL API, including the issuer, client ID, and token lifetime values for API authentication.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.tags.value: The value part of a tag (key-value pair) that is assigned to the AWS AppSync GraphQL API resource.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlapi.user_pool_config: Configures Amazon Cognito user pool authorization for the GraphQL API, including the user pool ID, AWS region, default action (ALLOW or DENY), and optional app client regex filter.

aws_app_sync_graph_qlschema.api_id: The unique identifier (API ID) of the AWS AppSync GraphQL API to which this schema definition is attached.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlschema.definition: The GraphQL schema definition text, which defines the types, queries, mutations, and subscriptions for the AppSync GraphQL API.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlschema.definition_s3_location: The S3 URI (e.g., s3://bucket/key) of the GraphQL schema definition file, used as an alternative to providing the schema inline via the `definition` argument.
aws_app_sync_graph_qlschema.id: The id is the GraphQL API ID that this schema is attached to.

aws_app_sync_resolver.resolver_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AppSync resolver, which uniquely identifies it across all AWS resources.

aws_app_sync_source_api_association.source_api_association_config: The configuration for this AppSync source API association, including the merge type (AUTO_MERGE or MANUAL_MERGE) that controls how the source API's schema is merged into the associated merged API.

aws_app_test_test_case.creation_time: The timestamp indicating when the AppTest test case was created.
aws_app_test_test_case.last_update_time: The timestamp, as a string, indicating when this test case was last updated.
aws_app_test_test_case.latest_version: A read-only object representing the most recent revision of the test case in AWS AppTest, containing its version metadata and test step definitions as managed by the service.
aws_app_test_test_case.latest_version.status: The status of the latest version of the AWS AppTest test case, indicating whether that version is in a draft state or has been activated for use.
aws_app_test_test_case.name: The human-readable name of the AWS AppTest test case, which is required when creating this resource.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps: The 'steps' property defines the ordered list of test steps that constitute the test case, where each step specifies an action (such as invoking an API or comparing outputs) to be executed during the test.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action: The action object of each step in the test case defines the specific operation to be performed during the test, such as starting a batch job on a mainframe environment, transferring files, or validating data, with its properties determined by the action type.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.compare_action.input: The input object defines the paired source and target endpoints (for databases or data sets) whose contents the compare action step checks for equality.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.compare_action.input.file: Defines the input file object for the compare action, which references the Amazon S3 path of the actual file to be validated against the expected output.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.compare_action.input.file.f: Specifies the list of mainframe data sets within the input file, defining their names and formats, which are used by the compare action to validate file content.
Specifies the coded character set identifier (CCSID) used to encode the data set, which AWS Application Testing uses to correctly interpret the file's character data during the compare action.
For each data set in the input file metadata, the `format` specifies the record format (such as fixed-block or variable-block) of the mainframe data set that the compare action uses as input.
The record length (in bytes) for each data set in the file metadata, used by the compare action to validate the data set during the test case step.
Specifies the type of the mainframe data set (such as physical sequential or partitioned) that the file metadata describes in the compare action's input.
The database_cdc object contains the change data capture (CDC) metadata for the source database file used as the input to the compare action in the AWS AppTest test case.

Specifies the change-data-capture tool used to collect the source database changes, with allowed values including 'DMS' and 'FSxForLustre', for the database CDC source metadata in the compare action's input file.
Specifies the database engine type (e.g., MySQL or Oracle) for the change-data-capture source in the compare action's file metadata.
Provides the configuration metadata for the target database in a database change-data-capture (CDC) comparison, allowing the compare action step to identify and connect to the destination database.
The name or identifier of the change-data-capture (CDC) tool used on the target database side of a database CDC compare step, such as AWS Database Migration Service or other supported tools.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.compare_action.input.file.s: The S3 URI of the source file that serves as the input for the compare action in the test case step.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.compare_action.input.file.t: Specifies the location (such as an S3 URI or file path) of the target file used as the expected result in a compare action step within an AWS AppTest test case.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.compare_action.output: The output configuration for the compare action, defining where the results of the comparison will be stored, such as in an S3 bucket.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.compare_action.output.file: Specifies the file configuration (e.g., S3 object location) that defines the expected output for the compare action in the test step.
The S3 URI or file path pointing to the output file generated by the compare action, used as the expected result for the test case step.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.mainframe_action: Defines the mainframe action to be executed in the test step, identifying the mainframe resource and whether the action is a batch or data set operation with its associated parameters.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.mainframe_action.action_typ: Defines the type of mainframe action to run in the test step, containing either batch job or data set operation details.
Specifies the configuration for a batch job action within the mainframe action type, defining the batch job details for the test step.
Specifies the name of the mainframe batch job that the test case step's mainframe action executes.
Defines a map of key-value pairs representing parameters to pass to the mainframe batch job executed in this test case step.
The list of data set names to export from the mainframe after the batch job is executed as part of this step's mainframe action.

Defines the TN3270 configuration for a mainframe action in an AWS AppTest test case step, specifying the target mainframe resource identifier and the Amazon S3 location of the script that automates the 3270 terminal session.
The list of mainframe data set names to be exported as part of the TN3270 action within this AWS Application Testing (AppTest) test case step.
This object specifies the TN3270 script, including its S3 location and script type, which defines the mainframe terminal interactions to be executed for this test step's mainframe action.
The Amazon S3 URI that specifies where the TN3270 automation script for this mainframe action step is stored.
Specifies the format of the TN3270 script used in the mainframe action, determining how AWS AppTest interprets and executes the script's commands during the test case run.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.mainframe_action.properties: Provides the mainframe action's configuration properties in an AWS AppTest test case step, including test data definitions and DMS resource settings.
The ARN of the AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) replication task that the mainframe action in this test case step uses to perform data replication or migration.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.mainframe_action.resource: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) application that the mainframe action is executed against.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.resource_action: Specifies a resource-based action, such as comparing data on an S3 object, that the test case step will perform.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.resource_action.cloud_forma: Specifies the CloudFormation stack operation (such as create, update, or delete) that this resource action step performs, along with the target stack or template resource, in the AWS AppTest test case.
The type of operation (e.g., Create or Delete) that this CloudFormation action performs on the stack during the test step.
The name of the CloudFormation stack on which the create, update, or delete action is performed during this test step.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.resource_action.m2_managed_: This structured field defines an action to be executed against an AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) managed application during an AWS AppTest test case step, specifying the target M2 application and the operation (e.g., start/stop) to perform.
This field specifies the type of action to perform on the AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) managed application, with valid values being 'Read' or 'Write'.

The properties object defines the custom input parameters (key-value pairs) for the M2 managed application action, such as the name of the database or application to use when starting or stopping the managed application.
Determines whether the AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) managed application is forcibly stopped (hard stop) during the test step instead of performing a graceful stop.
The Amazon S3 URI (or other location) of the data set to import into the AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) managed application as part of this test step action.
The resource ID of the AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) managed application that this M2 action step operates on.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.action.resource_action.m2_non_mana: Specifies the action to start or stop an AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) non-managed application as part of the test case step.
The ARN of the AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) non-managed application that this action validates or interacts with, as the target of the property or data set validation.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.description: The description of a test step within an AWS AppTest test case, providing a human-readable explanation of the step's purpose or expected behavior.
aws_app_test_test_case.steps.name: The name of a step in the AWS AppTest test case, which uniquely identifies the step within the list of steps.
aws_app_test_test_case.tags: A map of key-value pairs to assign as tags to the AWS AppTest test case, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_ta.id: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Application Auto Scaling scalable target, uniquely identifying it within AWS.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_ta.scheduled_actions.end_time: The date and time (in ISO 8601 format) at which the scheduled scaling action stops being active and no longer runs.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_ta.scheduled_actions.scalable_target_action: The scaling action to apply when the scheduled action is triggered, specifying the minimum and maximum capacities for the scalable target.
Sets the maximum capacity of the scalable target when the scheduled action runs, defining the upper bound for scaling during that time period.
The minimum capacity value that the scalable target is adjusted to when the scheduled action executes, as part of the scaling action that overrides the target's current minimum capacity.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_ta.scheduled_actions.schedule: The cron, rate, or at expression that determines when the scheduled scaling action is triggered for the scalable target.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_ta.scheduled_actions.scheduled_action_name: The name of the scheduled action, uniquely identifying it among the scheduled actions for this scalable target.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_ta.scheduled_actions.start_time: The date and time (in UTC) when the scheduled scaling action is set to start, specified in ISO 8601 format.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_ta.scheduled_actions.timezone: The time zone ID (such as 'UTC' or 'America/New_York') that the scheduled action's cron or rate expression is evaluated in.

aws_application_auto_scaling_scaling_pol.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Auto Scaling scaling policy.
Specifies a custom CloudWatch metric that represents the capacity of the scaling target (e.g., an Auto Scaling group), including the metric name, namespace, and statistic, which Application Auto Scaling uses for predictive scaling forecasting.

Specifies the metric data queries that define the customized capacity metric(s) used to calculate the target capacity for predictive scaling, where each query can reference a CloudWatch metric or be a math expression based on other queries.
The math expression used in the metric data query for the customized capacity metric specification, enabling calculated metrics such as aggregation of raw metrics for predictive scaling.
A short name that uniquely identifies this metric data query within the customized capacity metric specification, used to reference the returned data in metric expressions.
A human-readable label for the metric data query that identifies the metric or expression used in the customized capacity metric specification for predictive scaling.

Specifies the CloudWatch metric statistic to use in the metric data query, providing the metric's namespace, name, dimensions, and the statistic (e.g., Sum) that predictive scaling uses to compute capacity.
Identifies the CloudWatch metric (by its namespace, metric name, and dimensions) that this metric stat uses as the source data for the customized capacity metric specification in predictive scaling.
The list of CloudWatch metric dimensions (each a name-value pair) that uniquely identify the metric used as the customized capacity metric in the predictive scaling policy.
The name of the CloudWatch metric dimension (e.g., 'AutoScalingGroupName') used as a key to identify a specific attribute of the customized capacity metric for predictive scaling.
The value part of a name/value pair that defines a CloudWatch metric dimension for the customized capacity metric used in predictive scaling.
The name of the CloudWatch metric used as the source for the metric statistic in this metric data query within the custom capacity metric specification of the predictive scaling policy.

The namespace of the CloudWatch metric (e.g., AWS/EC2, AWS/ApplicationELB) that identifies the AWS service emitting the metric used in the customized capacity metric specification for predictive scaling.

The CloudWatch statistic (e.g., Sum, Average, Minimum, Maximum, SampleCount, or a percentile like p99) for the metric used in this customized capacity metric specification of the predictive scaling policy.
The unit of measurement for the metric statistic (e.g., 'Count', 'Percent', 'Bytes') in the customized capacity metric specification for the predictive scaling policy.

Indicates whether the result of this metric data query is returned and used as the customized capacity metric in the predictive scaling policy's metric specification, typically set to true for the query that provides the actual capacity value.
The custom load metric specification for the predictive scaling policy, defining the metric name, namespace, dimensions, and statistic used to represent the resource's load.
Specifies the metric data queries that define the customized load metric for predictive scaling, allowing you to combine multiple CloudWatch metrics and expressions to represent the target load.

In the customized load metric specification for a predictive scaling policy, this expression defines the mathematical formula (using CloudWatch metrics, math functions, and other queries) that produces the custom load metric value Application Auto Scaling uses for forecast calculations.
The unique identifier for a metric data query, used to reference this query within math expressions or to aggregate results in the customized load metric specification for predictive scaling.

The label field provides a human-readable name or description for a metric data query within a customized load metric specification used by a predictive scaling policy, helping to identify the query in alarms and dashboards.
Defines the CloudWatch metric statistics (metric, period, stat, and unit) used for this metric data query in the customized load metric specification of the predictive scaling policy.

Specifies the CloudWatch metric referenced by the metric data query in the customized load metric specification, identifying the load metric via its namespace, metric name, and dimensions for use in predictive scaling.
Dimensions specify the CloudWatch metric dimensions (name/value pairs) that identify the specific metric data to use as the customized load metric for predictive scaling.
The name of a CloudWatch metric dimension key-value pair that identifies the scope of the customized load metric used in the predictive scaling policy, such as AutoScalingGroupName.
Specifies the value for a CloudWatch metric dimension (key-value pair) that identifies the customized load metric used in the predictive scaling policy configuration.
The name of the CloudWatch metric to use in the metric statistic for the customized load metric specification of the predictive scaling policy.

Specifies the CloudWatch namespace for the metric used in the custom load metric specification, which identifies the service or application that emitted the metric (e.g., AWS/EC2 or a custom namespace).
The CloudWatch statistic (e.g., Sum, Average, SampleCount) applied to the metric in this metric data query when evaluating the customized load metric for predictive scaling.
The unit of measurement for the customized load metric statistic (e.g., 'Count', 'Percent', 'Bytes'), used by the predictive scaling policy to interpret the metric's value.
Indicates whether the metric data query results are returned and used as part of the customized load metric specification for the predictive scaling policy.
Defines the custom CloudWatch metric specification that this predictive scaling metric specification uses for forecasting, including metric name, namespace, dimensions, and statistic.

The list of metric data queries that define the customized metric specification for the predictive scaling policy, where each query specifies a metric expression or metric stat used to calculate the target metric.

The CloudWatch metrics math expression that defines the value of this metric data query, allowing multi-metric calculations via logical ids (e.g., m1, m2) for the customized scaling metric specification in a predictive scaling policy.
A unique, required identifier for this metric data query that allows other queries in the same customized scaling metric specification to reference its result via math expressions.
A human-readable label for this metric data query, used to reference its result in other queries or math expressions within the same metric specification.
Defines the CloudWatch metric statistic to use for this metric data query, specifying the metric name, namespace, dimensions, and the statistic to return for predictive scaling.

Defines the CloudWatch metric (namespace, metric name, and dimensions) used by the metric stat within this metric data query, part of the customized scaling metric specification for a predictive scaling policy.
Defines the list of CloudWatch metric dimensions (key-value pairs) used to identify the specific metric for a customized scaling metric in the predictive scaling policy's metric data query.
The name of a CloudWatch metric dimension that, together with its value, identifies the custom metric used in the predictive scaling policy's metric specification.

The value of the dimension, paired with the dimension name, that uniquely identifies a CloudWatch metric for the customized scaling metric specification in an Application Auto Scaling predictive scaling policy.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that the customized predictive scaling metric specification uses as its data source.
The CloudWatch namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2) of the metric referenced by the metric_stat in this metric data query within the customized scaling metric specification for the predictive scaling policy.
The statistic (e.g., Average, Sum, SampleCount, Maximum, Minimum) applied to the CloudWatch metric values for this metric data query, used to aggregate data for the predictive scaling policy.
The unit of measure for the CloudWatch metric (such as Count, Percent, or Bytes) used in the metric stat for the customized scaling metric specification in the predictive scaling policy.

Indicates whether to return the data from this metric data query, where true designates the metric as the resulting scaling metric and false is used for intermediate expression queries in the customized scaling metric specification.

PredefinedLoadMetricSpecification specifies a predefined metric (e.g., ALBRequestCountPerTarget) to be used as the load metric for the predictive scaling policy, optionally identifying the specific resource with a ResourceLabel.
The predefined load metric type for predictive scaling, such as ASGCPUUtilization or ALBRequestCountPerTarget, which determines the load metric used to compute the capacity forecast.

The resource label that identifies the specific AWS resource (such as an Application Load Balancer or target group) to associate with the predefined load metric for predictive scaling, required for metrics like ALBRequestCountPerTarget.
Defines a predefined metric pair to be used for predictive scaling, specifying the predefined metric type and, for metrics that require it, the resource label.
The predefined metric type that identifies the pair of Auto Scaling metrics used for predictive scaling, such as ASGCPUUtilization or ASGNetworkIn.
Identifies the target resource (such as a DynamoDB table name or Auto Scaling group name) whose CloudWatch metrics are used for the predefined metric pair in predictive scaling.

Defines the predefined CloudWatch metric (e.g., ASG CPU utilization or request count per target) that the predictive scaling policy uses as the basis for load forecasts, with an optional resource label to identify the specific resource.
Identifies the predefined scaling metric type (e.g., ASGCPUUtilization or ASGInboundBytes) that the predictive scaling policy uses to forecast capacity.

The resource label (e.g., the load balancer and target group identifiers) used to disambiguate the resource to which the predefined CloudWatch metric applies, such as for the ALBRequestCount metric in a predictive scaling policy.
The target value for the scaling metric defined in this specification, which the predictive scaling policy uses to determine the required capacity and adjust the resource's scale.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scaling_pol.step_scaling_policy_configuration.step_a: Defines the exclusive lower bound of the metric value range that triggers this step adjustment, where the range is evaluated relative to the alarm threshold and the associated scaling adjustment is applied only when the CloudWatch metric value falls within that interval.
Specifies the upper bound (exclusive) of the metric value range that triggers this step adjustment, used in step scaling policies to map metric values to scaling adjustments.
The amount, in capacity units, by which to scale (positive to add capacity, negative to remove capacity) when the corresponding step adjustment's metric breach threshold is met.
aws_application_auto_scaling_scaling_pol.target_tracking_scaling_policy_configura: The name of a metric dimension (e.g., LoadBalancerName or InstanceId) in a customized metric specification for a target tracking scaling policy, used to identify the metric's associated dimension when the metric is published with custom dimensions.
Specifies the value of the dimension for the custom metric used in the target tracking scaling policy.
Defines the mathematical expression for a metric math query in the customized metric specification, enabling calculated metrics by referencing other metrics in the same query list.
The Id is a short, unique name for this metric data query within the customized metric specification, used to reference it in the query's Expression or MetricStat.
A user-defined human-readable label for this metric data query, used to identify the query within the target tracking scaling policy.
Defines the metric and statistic (e.g., Average, Sum) for a single metric data query within the customized metric specification of a target tracking scaling policy.
Defines the CloudWatch metric referenced by the metric stat, specifying its namespace, metric name, and dimensions.

Defines the list of dimensions (name-value pairs) for the CloudWatch metric used in the customized metric specification of the target tracking scaling policy, which together with the metric name and namespace uniquely identify the metric and its scope (e.g., the resource being scaled).
The name of a CloudWatch metric dimension for the customized metric used in the target tracking scaling policy, identifying a particular characteristic such as an instance ID or queue name.

The value of a CloudWatch metric dimension in the customized metric specification of an Application Auto Scaling target tracking policy, which is a string that identifies the specific resource or aspect being measured (e.g., a queue URL, instance ID, or environment name).
The name of the CloudWatch metric used in the custom metric specification for the target tracking scaling policy, identifying the specific metric to track for scaling.

The namespace of the CloudWatch metric referenced by the metric stat in the customized metric specification for this target tracking scaling policy, identifying the service or custom application that publishes the metric.
The statistic to apply to the CloudWatch metric in the metric math expression (e.g., 'Sum', 'Average', 'Minimum', 'Maximum', 'SampleCount').

The unit of measure (such as Count, Bytes, Percent, or Seconds) for the CloudWatch metric used in the metric stat of a target tracking scaling policy's customized metric specification, which Application Auto Scaling validates against the metric stream and uses to interpret the target value.

Indicates whether the metric data from this query is returned as the utilization metric for the target tracking policy; set to `true` for the primary metric the policy scales on and `false` for any helper metrics used only in metric math expressions.

aws_application_insights_application.component_monitoring_settings.component_: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the component to which these monitoring settings apply, used as an alternative to component name to identify a specific component.
Specifies whether the component uses default monitoring settings, default settings with overwrites, or fully custom configuration, with allowed values DEFAULT, DEFAULT_WITH_OVERWRITE, or CUSTOM.
Specifies the name of the application component to which these monitoring settings apply.
aws_application_insights_application.component_monitoring_settings.custom_com: In an Application Insights application's component monitoring settings, the custom_component_configuration field defines the exact monitoring configuration (including sub-component type configurations and monitored metrics/logs) for a component when the component configuration mode is set to CUSTOM.
Specifies the detailed monitoring configuration for a custom component, including the metrics, logs, and Windows events that AWS Application Insights will collect and analyze for that component.
Defines the list of CloudWatch alarm metrics to monitor for the custom component, where each object specifies a CloudWatch alarm by name (AlarmMetricName) to include in the component's configuration.
Specifies the name of the Amazon CloudWatch metric to be monitored for generating alarms in the custom component configuration of Application Insights.
A list of CloudWatch alarms to be monitored for the custom component, where each alarm specifies an alarm name and an optional severity level.
The name of the CloudWatch alarm that Application Insights monitors for the custom component's configuration details.

Specifies the severity level (e.g., HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW) assigned to a CloudWatch alarm in the custom component configuration, which determines the alarm's criticality in Application Insights monitoring.
Configuration for the HA cluster Prometheus exporter, specifying exporter-specific settings such as the Prometheus port to enable collection of HA cluster metrics for the custom component.
Specifies the port number that the HA Cluster Prometheus Exporter listens on to expose Prometheus metrics for the custom component's monitoring configuration.
Contains the settings for the SAP HANA Prometheus exporter, such as the exporter type and the port on which Prometheus metrics are exposed for Application Insights monitoring.
Whether to agree to install the SAP HANA database client on the monitored server for the HANA Prometheus exporter configuration.
The port number (specified as a string) that the SAP HANA Prometheus exporter listens on, used by Application Insights to collect HANA performance metrics from that endpoint.
The name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the HANA database credentials used by the HANA Prometheus exporter for authentication.
The SAP HANA system ID (SID) of the HANA database that the HANA Prometheus exporter monitors, used to identify the HANA instance when collecting metrics for the custom component.
Specifies the network port on which the HANA Prometheus exporter exposes metrics for collection by Application Insights.
Defines the JMX Prometheus exporter endpoint (hostname and port) that CloudWatch Application Insights uses to scrape Java application metrics for the custom component.
Specifies the host and port of the JMX endpoint that the Prometheus exporter scrapes to collect metrics.
For a custom component using JMXPrometheusExporter, this URL defines the JMX endpoint the exporter connects to in order to scrape Java application metrics.
The port on which the JMX Prometheus exporter exposes metrics for the custom component.
Specifies the log files to monitor for the custom component, including the log type, file path, and optional log encoding settings.
Specifies the character encoding (e.g., UTF-8) that Application Insights uses when reading the log file for the custom component.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group that Application Insights monitors for the custom component's logs.

Specifies the list of CloudWatch metric-based alarms that overwrite the default component configuration, determining which metrics trigger alerts for the monitored application.

Specifies the list of log sources (e.g., log groups or file paths) that Application Insights monitors for the component, including per-log settings such as log type and encoding.

The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group that Application Insights monitors for the component.
The file system path to the log file or directory that Application Insights monitors for the component.

This object configures the SAP NetWeaver Prometheus exporter for Application Insights, specifying the port and protocol used to scrape metrics from the SAP NetWeaver system.

Specifies the list of processes to monitor in the component, where each process object defines the process name and the alarm metrics used to monitor that process.

Specifies the list of CloudWatch alarm metrics to monitor for the process, enabling custom alarm-based health monitoring for each process in the Application Insights application's component configuration.
The name of the metric (e.g., CPU Utilization, Memory) to monitor for the process's alarm, used to define alarm metrics in the default component configuration.

This object configures the SQL Server Prometheus exporter, specifying settings such as the exporter's listening port and Prometheus endpoint path used by Application Insights to collect SQL Server metrics.

The name of the Windows Event Log (e.g., Application, System, or Security) to monitor for the component's configuration details.

For a given log in a sub-component's configuration, pattern_set specifies custom log patterns (typically one per line) that Application Insights uses to match and highlight specific events in that log, overriding the default pattern set.

Specifies the CloudWatch metrics to monitor for the processes defined in the sub-component type configuration, where each object in the list identifies a metric name to be used for creating alarms.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that the alarm monitors for the process (for example, CPU or memory usage).

Specifies the Windows event logs to monitor for the sub-component, where each entry defines an event name (e.g., Application, System) and optionally its log group, event levels, and pattern set to determine which events are collected.
The list of Windows Event Log levels (e.g., ERROR, WARNING, INFO) to monitor for the specified Windows Event in the sub-component configuration.
The name of the Windows Event Log to monitor, such as Application, System, or a custom log name, when overriding configuration for a sub-component type.

The comma-separated list of Windows Event Log patterns (e.g., 'Application', 'System') used to filter which Windows events are monitored for this sub-component.

Identifies the AWS resource type of the sub-component (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance or AWS::DynamoDB::Table) so that the accompanying sub-component configuration details can be applied to that specific resource type when overwriting default monitoring settings.
aws_application_insights_application.component_monitoring_settings.tier: The tier property specifies the application tier (e.g., DOT_NET_CORE, JAVA_JMX, MYSQL) that defines which monitoring settings apply to the component.
aws_application_insights_application.custom_components.component_name: The user-defined name for the custom component that groups related resources for monitoring in the Application Insights application.
aws_application_insights_application.custom_components.resource_list: Defines the list of AWS resources, specified by ARN or resource identifier, that are grouped together into this custom component for monitoring by Application Insights.
aws_application_insights_application.log_pattern_sets.log_patterns: Defines the list of log patterns within a log pattern set, where each pattern specifies a regular expression (Pattern), a name (PatternName), and a rank for evaluation order.
aws_application_insights_application.log_pattern_sets.log_patterns.pattern: The regular expression pattern used to match log lines for this custom log pattern in Application Insights.
aws_application_insights_application.log_pattern_sets.log_patterns.pattern_na: The name to assign to this log pattern within a log pattern set, used to identify the pattern in the configuration.
aws_application_insights_application.log_pattern_sets.log_patterns.rank: A numeric value that sets the priority order of this log pattern within its log pattern set, where lower ranks are evaluated first.
aws_application_insights_application.log_pattern_sets.pattern_set_name: The name of a log pattern set in AWS Application Insights, which groups a collection of log patterns to detect specific issues in application logs.
aws_application_insights_application.tags.value: The value of a tag associated with the Application Insights application, used to categorize and manage the resource within AWS.

aws_application_signals_grouping_configu.grouping_attribute_definitions.default_g: Specifies the fallback value used to group telemetry under a particular application or service when the source attribute defined by this grouping attribute definition is missing from the telemetry data.
aws_application_signals_grouping_configu.grouping_attribute_definitions.grouping_: The name of the grouping attribute (used as the key in a grouping attribute definition) that identifies how telemetry is grouped in Application Signals, such as an environment or service name.

Specifies the list of source telemetry attribute keys (e.g., service.name, environment) that are combined to derive the value of the corresponding grouping attribute in this grouping attribute definition, determining how Application Signals groups telemetry into applications or services.
aws_application_signals_grouping_configu.updated_at: The timestamp of when the grouping configuration was last updated, as set by the AWS service.

aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.burn_rate_configurations.look_back_windo: The length of the look-back window, in minutes, over which the burn rate is evaluated for this burn rate configuration.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.exclusion_windows.reason: The reason or annotation for excluding this time window from the SLO's evaluation, commonly used to document planned maintenance or expected anomalies.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.exclusion_windows.recurrence_rule: Defines the recurrence schedule (cron or rate expression) for a time window during which the service level objective's evaluation is excluded.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.exclusion_windows.recurrence_rule.expres: The cron expression that defines the recurring schedule for this exclusion window, during which the SLO is not evaluated.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.exclusion_windows.start_time: Defines the start of an exclusion window, a time period during which the SLO's evaluation is paused so that planned maintenance or other excluded events do not affect the objective's availability calculation.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.exclusion_windows.window: This object specifies the start and end times of the exclusion window, during which the SLO's attainment metric is not evaluated.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.exclusion_windows.window.duration: The duration in minutes of the exclusion window, during which the SLO's metric data is excluded from evaluation.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.exclusion_windows.window.duration_unit: The unit of time (such as Days or Hours) for the numeric duration of the exclusion window, determining how long the service level objective evaluation is paused.
aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.request_based_sli.request_based_sli_metr: Configures the request-based SLI as a composite SLI, which aggregates multiple underlying service level indicators into a single SLI metric for the SLO.
Defines the list of individual SLI components (each with its own SLI metric configuration and weight) that are combined to calculate the composite SLI metric for this service level objective.
The name of the specific operation (e.g., an HTTP endpoint or API call) that this composite SLI component uses to evaluate performance against the SLO.
Defines which underlying service level indicators (SLIs) are selected and combined to calculate the composite SLI for the SLO.
A string specifying the boolean formula (e.g., `${sl1} AND ${sl2}`) that determines how the referenced individual SLIs are combined to form the composite service level objective.
Determines the selection mode for a composite SLI, using 'ANY' to require that at least one of the selected operations meets the SLO, or 'ALL' to require that every selected operation meets the SLO.
The AWS account ID that owns the CloudWatch metric used as the bad count metric for the monitored request count in the SLO, typically needed when the metric is in a different account.
The CloudWatch metrics expression that defines the bad count metric used to calculate the service level objective.
The unique identifier assigned to this bad-count metric definition within the request-based SLI, used to reference the metric in the SLO's monitored request count configuration.

This object defines the CloudWatch metric statistic (including namespace, metric name, dimensions, period, and statistic) that is used to count the number of bad requests for the request-based SLI's monitored request count metric in the SLO.
The CloudWatch metric that defines the bad count metric, including its namespace, metric name, and dimensions, used to calculate the number of bad requests for the request-based SLI.

Defines the CloudWatch metric dimensions (name-value pairs) that identify the bad count metric used in the request-based SLI's monitored request count metric, enabling the SLI to track unsuccessful requests.

Specifies the name of a CloudWatch metric dimension (for example, 'ServiceName' or 'Operation') that, together with the dimension value, identifies the bad count metric used in the request-based SLO's monitored request count metric.
The value of a dimension that identifies the CloudWatch metric used to count bad requests for the request-based SLO.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that represents the count of bad or failing requests used to calculate the service level objective's request-based SLI.

Specifies the CloudWatch namespace of the metric used as the bad request count for the monitored request count metric in the request-based SLI, identifying the service or application that emits the metric.

The period, in seconds, for the CloudWatch metric statistic that collects the bad count metric, which is used as part of the monitored request count metric in the request-based SLI for this Service Level Objective.

The statistic (e.g., Sum, Average) to apply to the metric data for the bad request count metric in the request-based SLI's monitored request count metric, used to evaluate requests that do not meet the SLI objective.
