aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.loop.defi: The inline definition of the sub-flow that the loop node iterates over, specifying the nodes and connections that constitute the repeated workflow body.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.loop_cont: Defines the loop control parameters for a Bedrock Flow loop node, including the array of items to iterate over and optional maximum iteration count.
Specifies the condition that determines whether the loop continues to the next iteration, evaluated after each pass through the loop node's body.
The expression, written in Amazon Bedrock Flow expression syntax, that is evaluated to a boolean to determine whether the loop controller should repeat the iteration.
The name of the condition that determines whether the loop controller node in the flow continues to the next iteration.
Specifies the maximum number of iterations the loop node can execute before the flow terminates the loop, preventing infinite loops.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.loop_inpu: Defines the input for a loop node in the flow, specifying the flow variable or expression that the loop iterates over.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.output: Defines the output configuration for an Output node in a Bedrock flow, specifying the data type and optional name of the flow's output.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.prompt: Defines the prompt settings for a prompt node, including the prompt template, model selection, and inference configuration.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.prompt.gu: Defines the Amazon Bedrock guardrail applied to the prompt node, specifying the guardrail's unique identifier and version to filter or moderate content.
The Amazon Bedrock guardrail ARN that this prompt node uses to apply content filters and safeguards to the prompt and the model's response.
The version of the guardrail to apply to the prompt node, such as a specific numeric version or 'DRAFT' for the unpublished version.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.prompt.so: Specifies the source of the prompt for the prompt node in the Bedrock flow, which can be either inline text configured directly or a reference to an existing prompt resource.

Specifies the inline definition of the prompt, including the model ID, template type (e.g., TEXT), template configuration, and optional inference settings, used directly within the flow node rather than referencing an external prompt resource.
Configures the model inference parameters for the inline prompt source, such as temperature, maximum tokens, and stop sequences, used when the prompt node invokes a model in the Bedrock flow.
Specifies the text inference configuration (e.g., temperature, topP, maxTokens, and stopSequences) for the inline prompt's model invocation.
Specifies the maximum number of tokens that the model is allowed to generate in the response for the inline prompt's text inference configuration, capping the length of the generated output.
Specifies a list of string sequences that, when generated by the model, cause it to stop generating further output tokens.

Controls the randomness of the model's text output in this prompt's inference configuration, where higher values produce more varied and creative responses and lower values produce more focused and deterministic responses.
The top_p value for nucleus sampling, controlling the cumulative probability mass of tokens considered for generation in the text inference configuration of the prompt node.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock foundation model ID used by the inline prompt configuration for this prompt node in the flow.
Specifies the template type (TEXT or CHAT) and the actual prompt template content for an inline prompt source in a Bedrock flow node.
Defines the textual prompt template used for the prompt node when the source is configured inline, supporting variable placeholders for dynamic inputs.
Defines the list of input variables for the inline text prompt template, where each variable's name is declared so it can be referenced as a placeholder in the template text.
The name of the input variable that is referenced within the prompt template text and substituted with a runtime value when the flow node executes.
Specifies the actual prompt text used in the inline prompt template, which can include Bedrock prompt variables such as {{variableName}} for dynamic content.
This field specifies the prompt template format (such as TEXT or CHAT) for an inline prompt source in a Bedrock Flow prompt node, determining how the prompt content is structured and parsed.
For a prompt node within a Bedrock flow, this object specifies the source configuration to reference an existing Amazon Bedrock prompt resource by its ARN rather than defining the prompt inline.
The Amazon Bedrock prompt ARN that supplies the prompt text or prompt template for this node's prompt source configuration.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.retrieval: Configures a retrieval node in an Amazon Bedrock flow by specifying the knowledge base to query and the retrieval settings used to fetch relevant information for downstream processing.
Configuration for the retrieval service used by the retrieval node, specifying the knowledge base (and optionally model settings) that the node queries to fetch relevant information.
Specifies the Amazon S3 data source for the retrieval node's service configuration, with properties such as the S3 bucket name and an optional object key prefix.
Specifies the name of the S3 bucket from which the retrieval node in this Bedrock flow retrieves data.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.storage: Specifies the configuration for a storage node in the Bedrock flow, including the S3 location where the flow's input data should be saved.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.configuration.storage.s: Defines the S3-specific settings for the storage node's service configuration, including the bucket name and optional object key prefix where the flow output will be written.
The name of the S3 bucket used by the flow node's S3 storage service configuration, defining the bucket from which the node reads or to which it writes data.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.inputs: Specifies the input parameters that a node in an Amazon Bedrock Flow consumes from the flow's initial inputs or from outputs of preceding nodes, enabling data to be passed into the node's processing logic such as a prompt or condition.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.inputs.category: Specifies the source category of a node input in a Bedrock flow definition, such as `FLOW` for a flow-level parameter or `NODE` for a reference to another node's output, which determines how the flow engine resolves the input's `value` field.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.inputs.expression: Specifies the expression that resolves the value for this input, commonly referencing outputs of other nodes using ${...} syntax in Amazon Bedrock flows.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.inputs.name: The name of the input, which uniquely identifies it within the node and is used as the reference key for accessing the input's value in expressions and for wiring connections between nodes.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.inputs.type: Specifies the data type of the node input, such as String, Number, Boolean, Object, Array, or Reference.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.name: A unique name for the node within the flow, used to identify the node when defining connections to and from other nodes in the flow definition.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.outputs: Specifies the list of outputs for a node, where each output includes a name, data type, and an expression that determines the value exposed to downstream nodes in the flow.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.outputs.name: The name of this node output, which uniquely identifies it within the node and is used to reference it in downstream node expressions.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.outputs.type: Specifies the data type of the node output (e.g., String, Number, Boolean) so downstream nodes can interpret the value correctly.
aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.type: Specifies the type of the node (for example, Input, Output, Prompt, or Condition) in the Amazon Bedrock flow, which determines the node's behavior and required properties.
aws_bedrock_flow.validations.message: The message field of a validation object provides a human-readable description of a validation issue found in the flow's definition.

aws_bedrock_flow_alias.concurrency_configuration.type: The concurrency configuration type for a Bedrock flow alias, which can be set to SINGLE to restrict the alias to one active flow invocation at a time or PARALLEL to allow multiple concurrent invocations, controlling how the alias handles runtime requests.
aws_bedrock_flow_alias.routing_configuration.flow_version: The version of the Amazon Bedrock flow (such as a numeric version or 'DRAFT') that this alias routes traffic to.

aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.connections.configuration: Defines the type-specific settings for a connection between two flow nodes, such as mapping the source node's output fields to the target node's input fields for data connections, or the condition expression that triggers the connection for conditional connections.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.connections.configuration.con: Defines the conditional configuration for a flow connection, specifying the condition expression that must evaluate to true for the flow to follow this connection from the source node to the target node.
Defines the expression evaluated at a conditional node that, when true, causes the flow to traverse this connection, using Amazon Bedrock's expression syntax.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.connections.configuration.dat: Specifies the data flow configuration for a connection, defining which output of the source node connects to which input of the target node.
The name of the output from the source node that this connection uses to pass data to the target node.
The target input field name in the destination node that receives data from the source output when this data connection is used in the flow definition.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.connections.name: The name that uniquely identifies a connection between a source node and a target node in a Bedrock flow definition.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.connections.source: The name of the source node from which this connection originates in the flow definition.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.connections.target: The name of the target node in the Bedrock flow to which this connection routes data from the source node.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.connections.type: Specifies the connection type as either 'Data' for regular node-to-node data flow or 'Conditional' for a condition-based edge in the flow graph.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration: For each node in a Bedrock flow's definition, this object holds the node-type-specific configuration (e.g., prompt, knowledge base, Lambda, or condition settings) that defines the node's behavior.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.agent: Defines the configuration for invoking an Amazon Bedrock agent at this flow node, including the agent ID, alias, and the mapping of inputs and outputs between the flow and the agent.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.agent.age: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Bedrock agent alias that this agent node uses to invoke the agent within the flow.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.collector: This field specifies the configuration for a collector node in a Bedrock flow, which aggregates multiple upstream outputs into a single list for downstream processing.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.condition: Defines the branch condition for a condition node in the flow, including the boolean expression and the list of conditions that determine which downstream node to invoke.
The list of condition rules that a Condition node in the flow evaluates against the flow's data to decide which outgoing branch to follow.

In an Amazon Bedrock flow's condition node, this expression is a Boolean-valued string that evaluates flow variables (e.g., using comparison or logical operators) to determine whether the corresponding condition is met and the flow should follow that branch.

Specifies the name of an individual condition within a condition node in a Bedrock flow, used to identify and route execution to the corresponding branch when that condition's expression is evaluated.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.inline_co: The inline code configuration for a node of type 'inline_code' in the flow definition, specifying the source code that the node executes.
The source code to be executed by the inline code node within the Bedrock flow, typically written in JavaScript or Python.
Specifies the programming language of the inline code (e.g., Python, JavaScript) executed by the code node in the Bedrock flow.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.input: This field specifies the configuration for an Input-type node in a Bedrock flow version, marking it as the flow's entry point and defining the flow's input variable or schema.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.iterator: The `iterator` configuration block for an Iterator node in an Amazon Bedrock flow specifies the collection expression to iterate over (typically referencing an upstream node's array output) so the flow can loop through items.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.knowledge: Specifies the knowledge base configuration for a node in an Amazon Bedrock flow, including the knowledge base ID and retrieval settings used to query information during flow execution.
Configures the guardrail used by the knowledge base node in the flow, specifying the guardrail identifier and version to apply.
The unique identifier or ARN of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail applied to this knowledge base node, used to filter or moderate content during flow processing.
The version of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail (e.g., 'DRAFT' or a numeric version like '1') to apply to the knowledge base node within the flow version.
Specifies the model inference parameters (such as temperature, topP, maximum tokens, and stop sequences) for the knowledge base node's response generation in the flow.
Specifies the text inference configuration for the knowledge base node, including parameters like temperature, maximum tokens, and stop sequences.
The maximum number of tokens the model can generate in text inference for a knowledge base node in an Amazon Bedrock flow.
Specifies the list of character sequences that, when produced by the model, cause text generation to stop early within the knowledge base node's inference configuration.
Temperature controls the randomness of text generation in the knowledge base node's inference configuration, where lower values produce more deterministic and higher values more creative output.

Sets the nucleus sampling top-p probability threshold for the text generation model in the knowledge base node, controlling the cumulative probability mass of token candidates considered during sampling.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base that this flow node is configured to query for information.
The identifier of the foundation model used by the knowledge base node in this flow version to synthesize answers from the retrieved knowledge base context.
Specifies the maximum number of results (chunks) to retrieve from the knowledge base when this flow node executes a query.

Specifies additional model invocation parameters (as a dynamic map of key-value pairs) to pass to the underlying model when the knowledge-base orchestration step runs, allowing fine-grained control beyond the standard configured fields.

Specifies the inference configuration for the knowledge base node's orchestration, such as temperature, top-p, and max output tokens, that control how the underlying foundation model generates responses from retrieved context.
Sets the text generation inference settings (e.g., temperature, topP, maxTokens) for the knowledge base node's orchestration step in the flow version.
The maximum number of tokens to generate in a text response when the knowledge base node's orchestration invokes the foundation model for text inference.
A list of strings that define the stop sequences for text generation in the knowledge base orchestration configuration, causing the model to halt generation when it encounters any of these sequences.
The temperature parameter for the text inference configuration of the knowledge base orchestration node, which controls the randomness or creativity of the model's generated responses.

Sets the top-p nucleus sampling probability for text generation in the knowledge base orchestration step of a Bedrock flow, restricting the model to tokens whose cumulative probability mass reaches this threshold.
The latency mode (e.g., 'STANDARD' or 'OPTIMIZED') that controls the response-time vs. accuracy trade-off for the knowledge base orchestration.

Provides the prompt template (as an object) that the knowledge base node's orchestration configuration uses to construct the model prompt, formatting how the retrieved context and the user's query are combined, typically via placeholders like {{context}} and {{query}}.
The text of the prompt template used by the knowledge base node to formulate queries or generate responses, supporting placeholders like {{query}}.

Specifies the prompt template for the knowledge base node, which can be provided as inline text or as a reference to a stored prompt, and is used to instruct the model on how to incorporate retrieved knowledge base context into its response.
Defines the text of the prompt template that the knowledge base node in a Bedrock flow uses to generate the search query for retrieval.
Configures how retrieved knowledge base results are reranked for this flow node, including the reranker model to use for reordering query results.

Specifies the Bedrock reranker model configuration for knowledge base retrieval reranking, including the model ARN and optionally the number of results to return, used when the reranking configuration type is BEDROCK.
Specifies the metadata selection configuration for the Bedrock reranker, defining whether all or specific metadata fields from the retrieved documents are passed to the reranking model.
Determines whether all metadata fields are included in the reranking request or only a specified subset, using values ALL or SELECTIVE.
Configures selective-mode metadata selection for the Bedrock reranking model, including the list of metadata fields to exclude during reranking.

Specifies the list of metadata fields to exclude from consideration when the reranker scores retrieved knowledge base chunks, so those fields are ignored in the reranking process under selective mode.
Defines the name of a metadata field to exclude from the reranking process when selective mode is configured for the knowledge base's reranking step.
Specifies the list of metadata fields to include when the reranking metadata configuration is in selective mode, ensuring that only these fields are used for reranking.
The name of a metadata field to include in the selective metadata configuration used for reranking a knowledge base node's responses in the Flow Version.
Specifies the configuration for the reranking model used by the knowledge base node, including the model ARN and optional additional model request fields passed to the reranking model.

A map of additional model request fields to include in the inference request sent to the Bedrock reranking model specified in the model configuration, allowing customization beyond the default parameters.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Bedrock reranking model used to reorder knowledge base retrieval results.
Specifies the number of top retrieval results to be returned after reranking by the Bedrock reranking model in the knowledge base node's reranking configuration.
Specifies whether reranking is disabled or performed using a Bedrock reranking model for knowledge base retrieval in this flow node.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.lambda_fu: Specifies the AWS Lambda function to invoke for a Lambda node in the Amazon Bedrock flow, including its ARN and related invocation settings.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Lambda function that this Lambda function node in the Bedrock flow invokes.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.lex: Configuration for a flow node that invokes an Amazon Lex bot, specifying the bot alias ARN and locale ID.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.lex.bot_a: The ARN of the Amazon Lex bot alias that this Lex node in the Bedrock flow definition uses to interact with the specified Lex bot.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.lex.local: The locale ID (e.g., en_US) of the Amazon Lex bot that this flow node interacts with, used to select the appropriate language/locale for the Lex conversation.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.loop: Configuration for a loop node in an Amazon Bedrock flow version, specifying the child nodes to execute repeatedly and the condition that controls when the loop ends.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.loop.defi: Specifies the loop body definition for a loop node, including the sequence of nodes to execute on each iteration and the condition that terminates the loop.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.loop_cont: Configures the loop controller for a Loop-type node in the Bedrock flow, specifying the maximum number of iterations the loop can execute.
Defines the condition that is evaluated after each iteration of a Bedrock Flow loop node to determine whether the loop should continue to the next iteration or terminate.
The expression string that defines the condition evaluated after each loop iteration to determine whether the loop should continue iterating in the flow version.
The logical name of the continue condition used by the loop controller to determine whether to proceed with another loop iteration.
Specifies the maximum number of iterations that the loop node's controller can run in the Amazon Bedrock flow version definition before the loop terminates.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.loop_inpu: In the configuration for a Loop node within a Bedrock flow definition, this field specifies the variable or expression that supplies the list of items the loop will iterate over.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.prompt: The prompt object within a node's configuration defines the prompt settings for a prompt-type node in the Bedrock flow, including the prompt template and the model configuration for generating responses.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.prompt.gu: Configures the Amazon Bedrock guardrail (by identifier and version) to be applied to the prompt in this node, providing content filtering and privacy controls during flow execution.
Specifies the ARN or identifier of the Bedrock guardrail applied to this prompt node to enforce content moderation and safety policies.
Specifies the version of the guardrail attached to this prompt node, used to select which guardrail policy set is enforced during prompt processing in the flow.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.prompt.so: Specifies the source of the prompt for a prompt flow node, either referencing an existing Bedrock prompt resource by ARN or defining the prompt inline with text or chat configuration.
Contains the inline prompt definition used by a prompt node in the Bedrock flow, specifying the actual prompt text and related model inference settings.
Specifies the inference parameters (such as temperature, top P, and maximum tokens) applied when the inline prompt in this prompt node is invoked.
Specifies the text model inference parameters (such as temperature, max tokens, top P, and stop sequences) applied when the prompt node generates text output.
Sets the maximum number of tokens the model can generate in the response for this prompt configuration.
Specifies the custom text sequences that cause the model to stop generating further output when encountered during inference for the prompt.
The temperature setting for text generation in the inline prompt's inference configuration, controlling the randomness and creativity of the model's output.

Specifies the top_p (nucleus sampling) value, a number between 0 and 1, that controls the cumulative probability threshold for token selection in the text inference configuration of the prompt node's inline source.
The unique identifier (model ID or ARN) of the Amazon Bedrock foundation or custom model used to run the inline prompt in a prompt node.

Specifies the prompt template configuration for the inline source of a prompt node, holding the template text (including placeholders for prompt variables) that Amazon Bedrock uses to generate the prompt when the flow version executes.
Specifies the prompt template text used by an inline prompt node's source configuration in the Bedrock flow version definition.
Defines the list of input variables for the inline text prompt template, where each variable supplies a name and value substituted into the template at flow runtime.
The name of an input variable defined for an inline text prompt template in a prompt node within a flow version, which the prompt template references to substitute the variable's value at runtime.
Defines the prompt text template used by the inline prompt configuration in the Bedrock flow node.

Determines the format of the inline prompt template for a prompt node in the flow, where TEXT specifies a single plain-text prompt and CHAT specifies a chat-style prompt with conversation turns and role-based messages.
Defines the Amazon S3 resource that supplies the prompt text for the prompt node, containing the S3 URI of the prompt file.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Bedrock prompt that serves as the source for this prompt node's configuration in the flow version definition.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.retrieval: Configuration for a 'retrieval' node in a Bedrock flow, specifying the knowledge base to query when the node executes.
This object specifies the retrieval service (either Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base or Amazon S3) and its configuration for the retrieval node in the Bedrock flow definition.
This object specifies the S3 bucket and object prefix configuration used by the retrieval node in the Bedrock flow definition to fetch data from Amazon S3.
The name of the S3 bucket from which the Bedrock flow's retrieval node retrieves data when its service configuration is set to S3.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.configuration.storage.s: Specifies the service configuration for a storage node in the Bedrock flow version, such as the Amazon S3 bucket and prefix used for reading or writing data.
Specifies the S3 bucket and optional key prefix used as the storage destination for a Storage node in the Bedrock flow version's definition.
The name of the S3 bucket used for the storage configuration of this node in the Amazon Bedrock flow version.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.inputs: Defines the list of input bindings for each node in the flow, where each input maps an expression (like a literal or a reference to another node's output) to a named input expected by the node's configuration.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.inputs.expression: A string expression that resolves to the value of this node input at runtime, typically referencing other nodes' outputs using the Bedrock flow expression syntax.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.inputs.name: The name of this input to the flow node, which identifies the input variable that the node consumes and references in its configuration.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.name: Specifies the name of a node in the flow definition, which must be unique within the flow and is used as the identifier for the node in connections and other flow elements.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.outputs: Defines the list of output definitions (name and data type) for a node in the Bedrock flow version, enabling downstream nodes to reference these outputs by name.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.outputs.name: The name of a node's output in the Bedrock flow definition, which downstream nodes use to reference the output data in expressions.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.outputs.type: Specifies the data type of the output produced by a node in the Amazon Bedrock flow, such as String, Number, or Boolean, affecting how downstream nodes process the value.
aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.nodes.type: Specifies the type of node within the flow definition, determining what operation the node performs (for example, Input, Output, KnowledgeBase, or Prompt).

aws_bedrock_guardrail.content_policy_config.filters_config.inp: Specifies whether the guardrail's content filter blocks or allows the matched content type in user input prompts, accepting values like 'BLOCK' or 'NONE'.
Specifies whether this content filter is enabled for user inputs (prompts) processed by the guardrail.
Specifies the input modalities (e.g., TEXT or IMAGE) that the content filter applies to, allowing the filter to target specific types of content entering the guardrail.
Specifies the strength of the content filter applied to user input prompts, controlling how aggressively the guardrail filters content for the input direction (e.g., NONE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH).
aws_bedrock_guardrail.content_policy_config.filters_config.out: Determines whether content matching the filter category is blocked (BLOCK) or allowed (NONE) when it appears in model-generated output.
Determines whether the content policy filter applies to generated model outputs, enabling or disabling the evaluation and filtering of the guardrail's responses for the specified filter category.
Specifies the output modalities (such as TEXT or IMAGE) to which this content filter applies for generated responses.

The strength (e.g., NONE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) applied when filtering the model's generated (output) content for the specified content policy filter type, determining how aggressively the guardrail blocks or moderates that content.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.content_policy_config.filters_config.typ: The category of harmful content that this guardrail filter targets, such as SEXUAL, VIOLENCE, HATE, INSULTS, MISCONDUCT, or PROMPT_ATTACK.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.contextual_grounding_policy_config.filte: Specifies whether the contextual grounding filter blocks the request (BLOCK) or allows it (NONE) when the filter's check fails.
Boolean that enables or disables this specific contextual grounding filter (e.g., grounding or relevance) within the guardrail's contextual grounding policy.

The confidence threshold (between 0 and 1) for a contextual grounding filter (of type GROUNDING or RELEVANCE), which sets the minimum score the model's response must meet to be considered grounded or relevant, and responses scoring below this threshold are blocked.
The type of the contextual grounding filter, which must be either GROUNDING or RELEVANCE, controlling whether the filter checks factual grounding or query relevance.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.sensitive_information_policy_config.pii_: In an AWS Bedrock Guardrail's sensitive information policy, the `action` property for each PII entity config determines the enforcement response when that type of personally identifiable information is detected, with valid values such as `BLOCK` to deny the input or output, or `ANONYMIZE` to replace it with a placeholder.

Defines how the guardrail responds to detected personally identifiable information (PII) in an end-user prompt, allowing values like 'BLOCK' to deny the request or 'ANONYMIZE' to replace the PII with a placeholder before processing.
Indicates whether the PII filter for this entity type is enabled on input (prompt) text in the guardrail's sensitive information policy.
Specifies the action (e.g., BLOCK or ANONYMIZE) the guardrail applies when the configured PII entity type is detected in the model's output.
Specifies the type of PII entity (e.g., EMAIL, PHONE, SSN) to be filtered by the guardrail's sensitive information policy.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.sensitive_information_policy_config.rege: Determines whether a regex-pattern match triggers blocking (BLOCK) or anonymization/masking (ANONYMIZE) of the detected sensitive information in guarded content.
A user-defined textual description that explains the purpose or context of this custom regex pattern in the guardrail's sensitive information policy.
Defines the action (BLOCK or ANONYMIZE) the guardrail takes when a regex pattern in this configuration matches sensitive information in the prompt (input).
Indicates whether this regex pattern in the guardrail's sensitive information policy is applied to model inputs (prompts) as opposed to only model outputs (responses).
The name of the custom regex pattern defined in the guardrail's sensitive information policy, used to identify and reference the regex-based filter.
Specifies whether a matched regex pattern in the model's output is blocked or anonymized when detected by the Bedrock guardrail.
Indicates whether the regex pattern for this sensitive information filter is enabled on model output; when false, the pattern is only applied to input.
The regular expression pattern used to detect sensitive information in the guardrail's sensitive information policy.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.tags.key: The key of a tag to apply to the Bedrock guardrail, used for organizing and identifying the resource.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.topic_policy_config.topics_config.defini: In the topic policy of an Amazon Bedrock guardrail, each topic's definition provides a natural-language description of the specific subject matter that the guardrail should identify and block or deny in model responses.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.topic_policy_config.topics_config.exampl: Specifies a list of sample phrases that illustrate the topic, used to improve the accuracy of the guardrail's detection of the topic.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.topic_policy_config.topics_config.input_: Specifies the action the guardrail takes when user input matches this topic, such as BLOCK or ALLOW.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.topic_policy_config.topics_config.name: The user-defined name of a topic configured in the guardrail's topic policy, used to identify a specific subject (e.g., 'investment advice') that the model is instructed to avoid discussing.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.topic_policy_config.topics_config.output: Specifies the action taken on the output when a user query or model response matches the topic, with allowed values 'BLOCK' to deny the content and 'NONE' to allow it.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.topic_policy_config.topics_config.type: Specifies whether the topic is defined as a denied (DENY) or allowed (ALLOW) topic in the guardrail's topic policy.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.word_policy_config.managed_word_lists_co: Determines the action applied to the input when a word from the managed word list is detected, with values such as BLOCK to block the input or NONE to allow it.
Enables or disables the managed word list (e.g., profanity) filter for user input prompts in the guardrail.

For each managed word list configured in the guardrail's word policy, this field determines the action taken when a word from that list is detected, with allowed values of 'BLOCK' (block the content) or 'NONE' (allow the content).
Indicates whether the managed word list (e.g., profanity) is applied to filter the model's output text.
Specifies the managed word list category to apply to the guardrail, with the supported value PROFANITY for filtering profane language.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.word_policy_config.words_config.input_ac: Determines whether a word in this list is blocked when it appears in the user prompt (input) text, with `BLOCK` filtering it out and `NONE` permitting it.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.word_policy_config.words_config.input_en: Indicates whether this custom word in the word policy is filtered from the input (user prompt) traffic, as opposed to output (model response) traffic.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.word_policy_config.words_config.output_a: Specifies the action the guardrail takes when a model output contains the configured word, with BLOCKED causing the word to be blocked and NONE allowing it to pass through.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.word_policy_config.words_config.output_e: Indicates whether the word is enabled for output filtering, meaning that when true, the guardrail prevents the word from appearing in model-generated responses.
aws_bedrock_guardrail.word_policy_config.words_config.text: The word or phrase that the guardrail's word policy will filter or block in model responses.

aws_bedrock_intelligent_prompt_router.models.model_arn: The ARN of a Bedrock foundation model that the intelligent prompt router can select among, defining a candidate model in the router's `models` list for routing prompts.
aws_bedrock_intelligent_prompt_router.routing_criteria.response_quality_differ: The minimum difference in predicted response quality between the larger and smaller models that the intelligent prompt router uses as a threshold to decide whether to route the prompt to the larger model.

aws_bedrock_knowledge_base.knowledge_base_configuration.managed_kno: Configures how audio content is split into segments for embedding generation, including segmentation strategy and segment duration, when creating a knowledge base in Amazon Bedrock.
Specifies the fixed duration in seconds for splitting audio into segments for embedding in the Bedrock knowledge base.
Defines how uploaded videos are divided into discrete segments (e.g., segment length and overlap) so the embedding model processes each segment separately for the knowledge base.
The duration in seconds of each fixed-length segment into which the video is divided before being embedded, used when the video segmentation configuration specifies a fixed-length segmentation mode.
aws_bedrock_knowledge_base.knowledge_base_configuration.sql_knowled: The natural language phrasing of a curated example query, representing the user's question or intent that the corresponding SQL statement is meant to answer.
The SQL query string of a curated query that serves as an example to guide the model's SQL generation for the Redshift-based knowledge base.
Specifies the list of columns for each table in the query generation context, where each column object defines the column name and data type used by the model to generate SQL queries.
Provides a natural-language description of a column in the table context, used by Bedrock to generate accurate SQL queries against the Redshift database.
Specifies whether the column is included in the generation context for query generation in the Redshift configuration of the SQL knowledge base.
Specifies the name of a column in a Redshift table that the knowledge base uses as context for generating SQL queries.
Provides a human-readable description of the table to help the query generation model understand its purpose and contents for generating SQL queries.
Specifies whether the listed Redshift table is included in or excluded from the query generation context, using an enum value such as 'INCLUDE' or 'EXCLUDE'.
The name of the Redshift table that is included in the query generation context, allowing the knowledge base to reference this table when generating SQL queries.
Defines the AWS Glue Data Catalog settings (catalog ID, database name, and table name) that identify the Redshift data source to use for the knowledge base's SQL configuration.
The list of table names in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that the Redshift SQL knowledge base will use for querying and retrieving data.
Defines the Amazon Redshift connection details for one storage configuration in an Amazon Bedrock SQL knowledge base, including the Redshift server and authentication parameters.
Specifies the name of the Redshift database that the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base uses to store and query data within the configured Redshift cluster.
Specifies the storage format for the Redshift table in the knowledge base's SQL configuration, with allowed values 'ROW' or 'COLUMNAR'.
aws_bedrock_knowledge_base.knowledge_base_configuration.vector_know: Configures how audio files are split into segments for embedding generation, such as the duration of each audio segment, when using a Bedrock embedding model with audio support.
When the audio segmentation strategy is set to FIXED_LENGTH, this property defines the duration (in seconds) of each audio segment before embedding.
This object specifies how input videos are segmented into smaller pieces before the embedding model processes them, controlling the granularity of video embeddings in the knowledge base.
Specifies the fixed segment duration (in seconds) used to split a video into chunks before generating embeddings for a Bedrock knowledge base.
The S3 location (bucket and key prefix) that specifies where supplemental data files for the knowledge base are stored, used alongside the vector index for retrieval.
The S3 URI (e.g., s3://bucket-name/object-key) of a supplemental data storage location where additional data for the Bedrock vector knowledge base is stored.
Specifies whether the supplemental data storage location is an Amazon S3 bucket (S3) or in-memory storage (IN_MEMORY) for the Bedrock knowledge base.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.additional_model_request_fields: Defines additional model request fields as key-value pairs that are passed through to the underlying foundation model for this prompt variant, augmenting or overriding standard inference parameters.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.gen_ai_resource.agent: Specifies the Amazon Bedrock agent to associate with the prompt variant, identified by the agent's ARN.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.gen_ai_resource.agent.agent_ide: The identifier of the Amazon Bedrock agent that serves as the generative AI resource for this prompt variant.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.inference_configuration: Configures the inference settings for the prompt variant, controlling response generation parameters such as temperature, topP, and maximum token count.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.inference_configuration.text: Represents the text inference configuration for the prompt variant, specifying generation parameters such as temperature, topP, maximum tokens, and stop sequences that guide the model's text output.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.inference_configuration.text.ma: Sets the maximum number of tokens the model can generate for text responses in this prompt variant's inference configuration, capping the output length.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.inference_configuration.text.st: Specifies a list of character sequences that will cause the model to stop generating further text when any of them is encountered in the output.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.inference_configuration.text.te: In the Bedrock prompt variant's text inference configuration, temperature controls the randomness of generated text, with lower values yielding more deterministic outputs and higher values increasing creative diversity.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.inference_configuration.text.to: Controls nucleus sampling by setting the cumulative probability threshold for token selection in the text generation inference configuration of the prompt variant.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.metadata.key: In the metadata map of a Bedrock prompt variant, this key defines the name of a user-specified attribute whose value is a string, enabling you to attach custom labels or annotations to the variant.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.model_id: The Amazon Bedrock foundation model ID (e.g., anthropic.claude-v2) that this prompt variant uses for generating responses.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.name: The name of the prompt variant, used to uniquely identify and reference this specific variant within the AWS Bedrock prompt.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration: Specifies the prompt template configuration for this variant, defining the text or chat template structure and how input variables are substituted in the prompt.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.chat: The chat object defines the prompt template configuration for chat-based interactions, including the required list of messages (each with a role and content) and an optional set of system prompts used by the Bedrock prompt variant.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.chat.inp: Defines the list of named variables used in the chat prompt template configuration, each containing a name that corresponds to placeholders substituted with runtime values when invoking the model.
The name of an input variable that serves as a placeholder within the chat prompt variant's template, replaced by a concrete value when the prompt is invoked.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.chat.mes: Specifies the chat messages (each with a role like user or assistant and content) that define the chat prompt template for this variant.
The list of content blocks (such as text or image) that make up the body of a message in a chat prompt template for the prompt variant.

Defines a cache point within a chat message content block, used to enable prompt caching in Amazon Bedrock by marking a position in the conversation where the prompt can be cached for subsequent requests.
Specifies the type of the cache point marker within a message's content, which must be set to 'default' to indicate that the preceding content should be cached for subsequent prompt invocations.
Specifies the literal text of a message content block within a chat prompt template for a Bedrock prompt variant, defining the actual wording of a user or assistant message.
Specifies the conversational role of the message in the chat prompt template, such as 'user' or 'assistant', which determines how the message is positioned in the prompt for the model.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.chat.sys: Defines the system content blocks for the chat prompt template, containing the high-level instructions and context provided to the model before the conversation messages.

Defines a cache point block (with type and optional label) in the system prompt of a chat template, specifying where prompt caching begins so that repeated system-prompt prefixes are cached across API requests to reduce cost and latency.
Defines the cache point type for a prompt-caching break in a chat system prompt, with the only supported value being 'default'.
The text of the system prompt included in the chat template for this prompt variant.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.chat.too: Specifies the list of tools (functions) the model may call in a chat prompt variant, along with optional tool choice settings.
Determines how the model selects which tool to invoke when multiple tools are available, supporting automatic, any-of, or a forced specific tool choice.
When specified under tool_choice, this property instructs the model to select and invoke at least one available tool in the current turn, rather than allowing an automatic or no-tool choice.
When enabled (e.g., set to true or an empty object), this property sets the tool choice to auto, allowing the model to autonomously decide whether to call a tool and, if so, which one.
Specifies the particular tool the model must use, defined by the tool's name within the configured tool list, when the tool choice strategy is set to a specific tool.
The name of the tool to select when the prompt's tool configuration specifies a specific tool choice rather than auto or any.
Specifies the list of tools available to the model in the chat tool configuration of the prompt, where each tool object defines its name, description, and input schema for invocation.

The cachePoint property defines a cache point in the tool configuration, enabling the prompt up to this point to be cached, and its 'type' field (e.g., 'default') specifies the kind of cache point to use.
Specifies the cache point type for a tool in a Bedrock prompt's chat tool configuration, where the value 'default' enables prompt caching for that tool's definition.
Defines the tool's specification, including its name, description, and a JSON schema that describes the expected input parameters for the model to invoke it.
Provides a description of the tool that the model uses to understand its purpose and decide when to invoke it.
The JSON schema that defines the expected input parameters for the tool, used by the model to construct valid function calls.
Defines the JSON schema that specifies the input parameters expected by the tool, used by the model to understand how to call the tool.
The name of the tool (function) that the model can invoke, as defined in the tool specification for the chat configuration of this prompt variant.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.text: This block configures the text prompt template for the variant, containing the prompt text and optional input variables that are substituted into the template.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.text.cac: Defines a cache point in the text prompt, with a type that chooses between caching the entire prompt ('default') or only the final portion ('final') to optimize prompt caching during inference.
Specifies the cache point type in the prompt template, which must be `default` to enable caching of the preceding prompt content for reuse across invocations.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.text.inp: Defines the list of placeholder variables (e.g., `{{name}}`, `{{age}}`) used in the text prompt template of this variant, each specifying a name and data type that get substituted at invocation time.
The name of the input variable that is used as a placeholder within the prompt template text, which will be replaced with actual values at runtime.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_configuration.text.tex: The string content of the text prompt template configured for this Bedrock prompt variant.
Specifies the Amazon S3 object location (bucket, key, and optionally version) from which this text prompt variant's template text is loaded, instead of being supplied inline in the text field.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that contains the prompt template text file for this variant's text configuration.
The S3 object key of the text prompt template stored in Amazon S3, used as an alternative to inline text for the prompt variant's text template configuration.
The version field specifies the version ID of the S3 object containing the prompt template text, enabling retrieval of a specific version of the object from Amazon S3.
aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_type: Specifies the format of the prompt template for this variant, where 'TEXT' indicates a plain-text prompt and 'CHAT' indicates a chat-message-style prompt.

aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.additional_model_request_fields: For each prompt variant in the Bedrock prompt version, additional_model_request_fields is a JSON object containing extra inference parameters (such as top_k or stopSequences) that are passed through to the model's API request.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.gen_ai_resource: Defines the Amazon Bedrock GenAI resource attached to the prompt variant, encapsulating the resource type and its ARN so the prompt version can target that specific agent or model resource.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.gen_ai_resource.agent: Configures the Amazon Bedrock agent that this prompt variant is linked to, holding the agent's unique identifier (such as its ARN) in the AgentIdentifier property.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.gen_ai_resource.agent.agent_ide: Identifies the Amazon Bedrock agent to which this prompt version's variant is attached, so the prompt is used with that agent.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.inference_configuration: Configures the inference parameters (such as temperature, top-p, and max tokens) applied when the model runs the prompt for this variant.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.inference_configuration.text: Specifies the text-specific inference parameters (temperature, topP, maxTokens, and stop sequences) for a prompt variant in the AWS Bedrock prompt version.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.inference_configuration.text.ma: Sets the maximum number of tokens the model is allowed to generate in the response for this variant's text inference configuration, effectively capping the output length.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.inference_configuration.text.st: List of character sequences that stop the model from generating further output when encountered in the generated text.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.inference_configuration.text.te: Controls the randomness of the model's text generation, where lower values produce more deterministic and focused outputs and higher values produce more creative or varied outputs.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.inference_configuration.text.to: Specifies the top_p (nucleus sampling) probability threshold for the text inference configuration, determining the cumulative probability mass from which tokens are sampled.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.metadata: The `variants.metadata` field lists the metadata entries (as key-value pairs) attached to each prompt variant in the prompt version, allowing you to store arbitrary additional information (such as author or notes) for a specific variant.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.metadata.key: The key of a metadata entry for a prompt variant, representing a user-defined string key in the variant's metadata map.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.model_id: The unique identifier of the foundation model used by this variant of the prompt version.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.name: The name that uniquely identifies this variant within the prompt version's set of variants.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration: Defines the prompt template configuration for a variant, specifying whether it uses a text or chat template along with its content and input variables.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.chat: The chat template configuration for a prompt variant, defining the structured conversation messages (with user/assistant roles) and optional system prompts that shape the model's responses.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.chat.inp: Defines the list of input variables for the chat template configuration, allowing a prompt variant to reference variable names that are substituted with values at runtime.
The placeholder name for an input variable in the chat prompt template, which is substituted with a value when the prompt is invoked.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.chat.mes: Defines the ordered list of chat messages (each with a role and content) that form the conversation template for a variant in this prompt version, providing the model input for chat-style prompts.
Defines the individual content blocks (such as text) that make up a chat message's content within the Bedrock prompt version's chat template configuration.
Configures a cache point in the message content, marking a location in the conversation where Bedrock can cache and reuse the preceding context to reduce inference cost and latency.
Specifies the cache point type as 'default', which instructs Bedrock to cache the preceding message content in the prompt for reuse across subsequent model invocations.
The text of the chat message content block within the prompt template's chat configuration, used as the message body when the prompt is invoked.
The role of the chat message in the prompt template, such as 'user' or 'assistant'.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.chat.sys: Specifies the list of system content blocks (each containing text) that define the system prompt for the chat template configuration of a prompt variant, providing high-level instructions to the model.
Specifies a cache point within a system prompt for a chat prompt template, allowing prompt caching to be applied from that point onward in the conversation.
Specifies the type of cache point marker within the system block of the chat template configuration, where the only supported value is 'default' to mark where prompt caching begins.
Specifies the text of a system prompt in the chat template configuration for a prompt variant, which defines the model's behavior and context before user messages are processed.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.chat.too: Specifies the tool configuration for the chat template, defining the tools (e.g., function schemas) available for the model to call during prompt execution.
Specifies how the model should select which tool to use during chat prompt processing, with options for automatic selection, requiring a tool, or forcing a specific named tool.
When present in tool_choice, this empty object instructs the model to invoke any one of the available tools from the chat tool configuration.
Specifies the tool selection as automatic (Auto), letting the model choose the most appropriate tool from the configured tool list rather than forcing a specific tool or allowing any tool.
This object specifies the exact tool the model is required to use, identified by the tool's name within the prompt's tool configuration when the tool choice is set to a specific tool.
The name of the specific tool that the model is directed to use when the tool_choice type is set to 'tool'.
A list of tool definitions that the chat model can invoke, where each tool includes its name, description, and input schema.
Defines a cache point on a tool within the Bedrock prompt version's chat tool configuration, allowing the tool's definition to be cached for prompt-caching efficiency.
In an AWS Bedrock prompt version's tool configuration, this string specifies the cache point type; the only supported value is 'default'.
Defines the tool specification for a tool available to the model, containing its name, description, and the JSON schema for its input parameters.
The description of the tool, which is passed to the model to help it understand the tool's purpose and decide when to invoke it.
The JSON Schema object that defines the input parameters expected by the tool, including their types, constraints, and required fields, which the model uses to format tool invocation arguments.
The JSON schema that defines the input parameters for the tool, specifying the structure and validation constraints for the tool's invocation.
The name of the tool, which is the unique identifier the model uses to invoke the tool during inference.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.text: In each variant of the Bedrock prompt version, this object specifies the text prompt template configuration, defining the prompt text and its input variables for use during model invocation.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.text.cac: Specifies a cache point within the text prompt template configuration, marking a location in the prompt where Bedrock will cache the preceding content to reuse across requests with the same prefix, reducing latency and cost.
Specifies the type of cache point, which enables caching of intermediate results in the prompt; the only supported value is 'default'.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.text.inp: A list of input variables for the text prompt template, each specifying a variable name that can be used as a placeholder within the template text.
Specifies the name of the input variable that is referenced as a placeholder within the prompt template text, which will be substituted with an actual value when the prompt is invoked.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_configuration.text.tex: The prompt text content for the text template configuration of this variant in a Bedrock prompt version.
aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.template_type: Indicates the type of prompt template used by this variant, either TEXT, CHAT, or IMAGE, which determines how the variant's prompt is structured and processed.

aws_bedrock_session.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Bedrock session, used to assign metadata for organizing, filtering, and managing the session.

aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.account_grouping: Specifies the linked accounts (by their account IDs) that are grouped together in this AWS Billing Conductor billing group for consolidated billing and custom pricing.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.account_grouping.auto_associate: When enabled, accounts in the organization that are not already associated with another billing group are automatically added to this billing group.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.account_grouping.linked_account_ids: Identifies the AWS accounts that are members of this billing group by their linked account IDs, determining which accounts are billed together under the group's pricing rules.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.computation_preference: Specifies the cost computation preference for the billing group, referencing the pricing rule ARN that determines how the group's billed amounts are calculated.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.description: An optional string that supplies a human-readable explanation of the billing group's purpose or contents, limited to 1024 characters.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.name: The user-defined name of the billing group, which must be unique within the AWS account and is used to identify the billing group in the Billing Conductor console and APIs.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.status: This read-only field indicates the current lifecycle status of the billing group, such as ACTIVE, in the AWS Billing Conductor service.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.status_reason: The reason for the current status of the billing group, providing contextual details when the group is not fully active (e.g., why it failed or is in a transient state).
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.tags: A list of tag objects that define key-value pairs to attach to the billing group, enabling you to categorize and manage billing groups within AWS Billing Conductor.
aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag assigned to an AWS Billing Conductor billing group, used to organize and identify the group for cost tracking and management.

aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.billing_period_range: The range of billing periods during which the custom line item is active, defined by an inclusive start and exclusive end billing period.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.billing_period_range.exclusive_end_billi: The exclusive_end_billing_period sets the cutoff billing period, in YYYY-MM-DD format, after which the custom line item is no longer applied, with the range being exclusive so the item remains active through the end of the previous billing period.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.billing_period_range.inclusive_start_bil: The inclusive start billing period that defines the first billing period in the range for which the custom line item is applied.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.currency_code: The ISO currency code (e.g., 'USD') that denominates the custom line item's charges, automatically set to the currency of the associated billing group.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.custom_line_item_charge_details: Defines the billing charge type (fee or credit) and the associated flat or percentage amount details for the custom line item.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.custom_line_item_charge_details.flat: Specifies the flat-rate charge details for the custom line item, defining a fixed monetary amount (charge_value) that is applied to the associated billing group's usage.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.custom_line_item_charge_details.flat.cha: The required fixed amount (in USD) that AWS Billing Conductor charges for the custom line item when its charge type is set to FLAT.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.custom_line_item_charge_details.line_ite: A list of filters that specify which underlying billing line items the custom line item charge applies to, based on matching attributes such as the AWS service, usage type, or operation.
Specifies the billing line item attribute (e.g., LINE_ITEM_TYPE, OPERATION, or USAGE_TYPE) that the filter's value is matched against to determine whether the custom line item is applied.
The list of attribute values that the line item filter matches against, determining which billing line items are selected for the custom line item's charge calculations.
Determines whether the line item filter should match all, any, or none of the specified filter values, with valid values including MATCH_ALL, MATCH_ANY, NOT_MATCH_ALL, and NOT_MATCH_ANY.
Defines the list of matching values (e.g., specific line item types or product names) for the line item filter key, determining which billing line items the custom charge is applied to.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.custom_line_item_charge_details.percenta: The percentage-based charge configuration for the custom line item, which defines the percentage of the associated billing group's usage that is charged and optionally includes child resources.

Specifies a list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the associated resources that the percentage-based custom line item charge applies to; if omitted, the percentage applies to all resources in the billing group.
The percentage of the custom line item charge, expressed as a numeric percentage (e.g., 10 for 10%).
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.custom_line_item_charge_details.type: The type of custom line item charge, which determines whether the line item is a fee (FEE) or a credit (CREDIT) applied to the customer's bill.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.description: An optional, user-defined text description that provides additional context about the custom line item, aiding identification in billing reports.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.name: The descriptive name assigned to the custom line item, which appears in billing reports to identify the charge.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.presentation_details: Specifies the customer-facing presentation of the custom line item, including its display name and whether it is visible or hidden on the customer's invoice.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.presentation_details.service: Specifies the AWS service (e.g., AmazonS3, AmazonEC2) that the custom line item's charge applies to, as displayed in the customer's billing presentation.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.product_code: The unique AWS-generated product code that identifies the custom line item in billing reports and invoices.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.tags: Assigns a set of AWS resource tags (key-value pairs) to the custom line item for cost allocation, billing group identification, and resource management.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the custom line item, used for organizing, categorizing, and filtering billing resources in AWS Billing Conductor.
aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.tags.value: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the custom line item, enabling you to categorize and track this item in AWS Billing Conductor for cost allocation and management.

aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan.name: The user-defined name for the pricing plan, required when creating the plan in AWS Billing Conductor and used for identification and display.
aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan.pricing_rule_arns: The ARNs of the pricing rules to associate with this pricing plan.
aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan.tags.key: The key portion of a user-defined tag assigned to the AWS Billing Conductor pricing plan, used to identify and categorize the plan within the resource's tag set.
aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag key-value pair attached to the AWS Billing Conductor pricing plan, used to organize, track, or control access to the plan.

aws_billing_conductor_pricing_rule.tags: Specifies a list of tags, each with a Key and Value, to associate with the pricing rule for labeling and cost management.
aws_billing_conductor_pricing_rule.tiering.free_tier.activated: Whether the free tier is activated for this pricing rule, enabling the first set of units to be billed at zero when set to true and disabling the free tier allowance when false.

aws_billing_view.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Billing billing view.
aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression: DataFilterExpression selects which cost and usage records are included in the billing view by specifying dimension filters such as service, region, record type, or linked account.
aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression.dimensions: The dimensions property of the data filter expression specifies dimension filters (such as service or region) that restrict the billing view to only include matching billing data.
aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression.dimensions.key: The name of the billing dimension to filter on (for example, 'SERVICE' or 'REGION'), which along with the dimension values determines which data is included in the billing view.
aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression.dimensions.values: Specifies a list of dimension values (such as AWS service names or linked account IDs) that the billing view's data filter expression will match against when selecting which cost and usage data to include in the view.
aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression.tags: Specifies tag key-value pairs used by the data filter expression to include only resources that have those tags in the billing view.
aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression.tags.key: The tag key used by the billing view's data filter expression to match cost items associated with resources that have a tag with this key.
aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression.tags.values: Defines the list of tag values that the billing view's data filter expression uses to match resources with a specific tag key, thereby including only matching cost and usage data in the view.
aws_billing_view.description: An optional user-provided text that gives a human-readable explanation or context for the billing view, helping to distinguish it from other views.
aws_billing_view.name: The name of the AWS Billing view, which is required to uniquely identify the view within your account.
aws_billing_view.owner_account_id: The AWS account ID of the account that owns the billing view, which is set automatically at creation and cannot be modified.
aws_billing_view.tags.key: The key (name) of a tag attached to this billing view, used for cost allocation and management in AWS Billing.

aws_braket_spending_limit.tags.value: The value part of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS::Braket::SpendingLimit resource, used to categorize and manage the spending limit with arbitrary metadata.

aws_budgets_budget.budget: The budget object defines the essential budget configuration, including the budget name, type (COST or USAGE), amount limit, time unit, and optional cost filters and cost types.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.auto_adjust_data: Configuration for automatic budget limit adjustment, where AWS adjusts the budget's limit based on historical usage or a forecast, including the autoAdjustType (HISTORICAL or FORECAST) and the corresponding adjustment period options.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.auto_adjust_data.auto_adjust_type: Indicates whether the budget's automatic adjustment is based on a forecast of future spend (FORECAST) or on historical spending patterns (HISTORICAL).
aws_budgets_budget.budget.auto_adjust_data.historical_optio: Specifies the number of historical budget periods (months) of past spending that AWS Budgets uses to calculate the automatically adjusted budget amount.
Specifies the number of months of historical spending data that AWS Budgets uses to automatically calculate the adjusted budget amount.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.billing_view_arn: Specifies the ARN of an AWS Billing view that the budget is scoped to, allowing the budget to track costs only for the accounts and usage associated with that billing view.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_limit: Specifies the cost or usage threshold for the budget, defined by an amount and unit (for example, '100.0' and 'USD').
aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_limit.amount: The numerical amount of the budget limit, representing the maximum cost or usage allowed by the budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_limit.unit: The three-letter currency code (e.g., USD) that defines the monetary unit for the budget limit amount and must match the currency of the AWS account.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_name: The name of the budget, which acts as a unique identifier within the AWS account for the specified budget type; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name (e.g., the logical ID).
aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_type: Specifies the type of budget, such as COST, USAGE, RI_UTILIZATION, RI_COVERAGE, SAVINGS_PLANS_UTILIZATION, or SAVINGS_PLANS_COVERAGE, which determines the metric and dimensions used to track your AWS spend or usage.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_filters: A map of cost filter dimension names (such as Service, LinkedAccount, Region, or TagKeyValue) to lists of values that restricts the budget to matching AWS costs, analogous to the CostFilters property in the AWS Budgets API.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types: Specifies the CostTypes object that controls which AWS cost types (such as taxes, subscriptions, recurring charges, support, discounts, credits, and upfront fees) are included or excluded when calculating the budget's actual and forecasted costs.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_credit: Specifies whether credits (such as promotional AWS credits) are included when calculating the costs covered by this budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_discount: Determines whether discounts are included in the cost amounts tracked by this budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_other_subscrip: Controls whether the budget includes other non-recurring subscription costs, such as one-time fees for services like Amazon QuickSight.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_recurring: Whether the budget includes recurring costs (such as monthly subscription or recurring service fees) when calculating actual spend against the budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_refund: Indicates whether the budget includes refunds when calculating costs.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_subscription: Specifies whether the budget includes subscription costs (such as AWS Support) when determining actual and forecasted spend.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_support: Determines whether AWS Support charges (such as subscription fees for AWS Support plans) are included when calculating the costs tracked by this budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_tax: Specifies whether the budget includes taxes associated with your usage.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.include_upfront: Specifies whether to include upfront fees, such as the one-time payment for Reserved Instances, in the budget's cost calculations.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.use_amortized: In AWS Budgets, this boolean flag in the budget's cost types controls whether the budget includes amortized costs, which spread upfront reservation or savings plan charges over the term of the commitment.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.use_blended: A boolean flag that indicates whether the budget includes blended costs, which are calculated by mixing the effective rates of on-demand and reserved-instance usage.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression: Specifies a logical expression of key-value filters (such as service, tag, or account) and an operator (AND or OR) that determines which cost and usage data is included in the budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.and: Specifies a list of filter expressions that must all be satisfied (logical AND) for a cost or usage item to be counted in the budget, enabling combined dimension-based filtering (e.g., service and region together).
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.cost_categories: Maps cost category names to lists of values within the budget's filter expression; only actual costs that match at least one of the listed values for each configured cost category are counted toward the budget.
The name of the AWS Cost Category to use as a filter key for this budget.
Specifies the matching options (such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH) that apply to the cost category values in the budget's filter expression.
Defines the specific values of the chosen cost category that the budget filter matches, restricting the budget to only include costs associated with those cost category values.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.dimensions: Defines the AWS cost dimensions (like SERVICE or REGION) and their allowed values that this budget's filter expression uses to match and track specific cost and usage.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.dimensions.key: Specifies the dimension name (e.g., SERVICE, REGION, or AZ) that the budget's filter expression uses to filter cost or usage data.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.dimensions.matc: Specifies a list of match options (such as EQUALS or STARTS_WITH) that determine how the dimension values in the filter are matched against actual budget costs.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.dimensions.valu: The list of specific values for the dimension in the budget's filter expression, such as service names (e.g., AmazonS3) when the dimension is SERVICE.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.not: The `not` field holds a nested filter expression that is logically negated, so the budget applies only to costs that do not match the nested criteria.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.or: A list of filter sub-expressions that are combined using OR logic, so that a cost is included in the budget if it matches any of the listed sub-expressions.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.tags: Defines the tag-based filters (tag key and list of values) that restrict the budget's cost scope to matching tagged resources in the budget filter expression.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.tags.key: The tag key used in the budget's filter expression to scope the budget to costs associated with that tag.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.tags.match_opti: Defines how the cost allocation tag key-value pairs in the budget filter expression are matched (e.g., using EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, or CONTAINS) against the tags applied to your resources, controlling which resource usage is included in the budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_expression.tags.values: Specifies the list of tag values to match when the budget's filter expression filters by a tag key, limiting the budget's coverage to costs from resources tagged with any of these values.
