aws_budgets_budget.budget.planned_budget_limits: Specifies budget limits for future cost budget periods, mapping each period's start date (YYYY-MM-DD) to a budget limit amount and unit for that period.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.time_period: Specifies the start and end dates that determine the period covered by the budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.time_period.end: The end date of the budget time period, indicating the last day the budget is active; if omitted, the budget period is open-ended.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.time_period.start: The start date and time of the budget's coverage period, expressed in UTC (usually ISO 8601 format), which determines the beginning of the time window over which costs are evaluated against the budget.
aws_budgets_budget.budget.time_unit: The time unit (DAILY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, or ANNUALLY) that defines the period over which the budget tracks costs or usage and resets.
aws_budgets_budget.id: The budget name, which uniquely identifies the budget within the AWS account and is used as the resource's primary identifier.
aws_budgets_budget.notifications_with_subscribers: Specifies the budget notifications and the email or SNS subscribers to receive alerts when the budget threshold is exceeded.
aws_budgets_budget.notifications_with_subscribers.notificat: Defines the notification configuration for a budget, including threshold value, comparison operator (e.g., GREATER_THAN), threshold type (PERCENTAGE or ABSOLUTE_VALUE), and notification type (e.g., ACTUAL or FORECASTED), which triggers an alert to the subscribed SNS topics or email addresses.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN, EQUAL_TO) used to evaluate the budget's actual or forecasted value against the notification threshold.
Specifies whether the budget notification is triggered by actual spending or a forecasted spend amount.
The numeric threshold value that, when compared against the actual or forecasted budget cost or usage using the notification's comparison operator, triggers the budget notification.

Specifies whether the budget notification threshold is expressed as a percentage of the budget limit or as an absolute value (e.g., a dollar amount or usage quantity), corresponding to the PERCENTAGE or ABSOLUTE_VALUE enum values for the budget alarm.
aws_budgets_budget.notifications_with_subscribers.subscribe: Specifies the list of subscribers (email addresses or SNS topic ARNs) that receive the budget notification.
The email address or SNS topic ARN that receives the budget notification for the associated subscriber type.
The subscription channel type used by the subscriber to receive budget notifications, such as SNS or EMAIL.
aws_budgets_budget.resource_tags: Specifies a list of resource tag key-value pairs (with Key and Value properties) that are attached to this AWS Budgets budget to help categorize and manage it for cost allocation and filtering.
aws_budgets_budget.resource_tags.key: The key of a resource tag (a key-value pair) applied to the budget, used to categorize or identify the budget for cost allocation and management.
aws_budgets_budget.resource_tags.value: The value of a tag entry in the resource_tags map, used to attach metadata to the budget resource for identification and organization.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.action_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this budget action, returned as a read-only attribute after creation.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.action_threshold: Defines the threshold (a numeric value and type, either absolute dollar amount or percentage) that triggers the budget action when the actual or forecasted budget usage exceeds it.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.action_threshold.type: Determines whether the threshold value is interpreted as an absolute dollar amount or as a percentage of the budget.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.action_threshold.value: The numeric threshold value that triggers the budget action, interpreted according to the sibling threshold type (e.g., as a percentage of the budget limit or as an absolute monetary amount).
aws_budgets_budgets_action.action_type: Specifies the type of budget action to execute when a budget threshold is exceeded, such as APPLY_IAM_POLICY, APPLY_SCP_POLICY, or RUN_SSM_DOCUMENT, which determines whether the action applies an IAM policy, a service control policy, or runs an SSM document.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.approval_model: Defines whether the budget action executes automatically or requires manual approval after it is triggered (valid values: AUTOMATIC or MANUAL).
aws_budgets_budgets_action.budget_name: The name of the AWS Budgets budget that this action is associated with.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition: The definition object specifies the budget action's type and its configuration, including the action type (such as APPLY_IAM_POLICY or RESET_IAM_POLICY) and the corresponding details like the IAM policy ARN or target account for the action.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.iam_action_definition: This object specifies the IAM action definition for a budget action, including the IAM policy ARN and the IAM roles, groups, or users to which the policy is applied.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.iam_action_definition.groups: Specifies a list of IAM group names to which the budget action's IAM policy will be applied, allowing the action to modify permissions for those groups.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.iam_action_definition.policy_: The ARN of the IAM policy that the budget action attaches to or detaches from the specified IAM role, user, or group when the action is triggered.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.iam_action_definition.roles: The list of IAM roles to which the budget action applies the IAM policy defined in the IamActionDefinition.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.iam_action_definition.users: The list of IAM user ARNs to which the budget action's IAM policy will be applied.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.scp_action_definition: Configuration for a budget action that applies a service control policy (SCP), specifying the SCP policy ID and target account IDs.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.scp_action_definition.policy_: The unique ID of the service control policy (SCP) that this budget action applies to when the budget threshold is exceeded.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.scp_action_definition.target_: The list of AWS account or organizational unit IDs to which the service control policy is applied by this budget action.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.ssm_action_definition: The SSM action definition under 'definition' that specifies the target instance IDs, AWS Region, and subtype (such as STOP_EC2_INSTANCES or STOP_RDS_INSTANCES) used to execute the associated Systems Manager automation document as a budget action.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.ssm_action_definition.instanc: Specifies the list of EC2 instance IDs on which the SSM action (such as stopping or terminating instances) is executed when the budget action is triggered.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.ssm_action_definition.region: The AWS Region where the target EC2 instances for the Systems Manager (SSM) budget action are located.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.ssm_action_definition.subtype: The subtype of the Systems Manager action, specifying whether to stop Amazon EC2 instances or Amazon RDS instances.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.execution_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Budgets assumes to execute the budget action, such as applying a policy or sending a notification.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.notification_type: The type of budget notification that triggers the action, either ACTUAL (fired when actual spending exceeds the threshold) or FORECASTED (fired when spending is projected to exceed the threshold).
aws_budgets_budgets_action.resource_tags: Specifies the list of resource tags to apply to the budget action, enabling you to add metadata for identification, cost allocation, and management of the action resource.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.resource_tags.key: The key of a resource tag attached to this AWS budget action, used to label and organize the action with custom metadata.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.resource_tags.value: The value of a resource tag key-value pair assigned to the AWS Budgets action.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.subscribers: The list of subscribers to notify when the budget action is triggered, where each subscriber defines the notification method (email address or SNS topic) and the corresponding address.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.subscribers.address: The email address or SNS topic ARN that serves as the destination for the budget action notification sent to this subscriber.
aws_budgets_budgets_action.subscribers.type: Specifies the notification channel for a budget action subscriber, either SNS or EMAIL, which determines how the subscriber receives the alert or action notification.

aws_cases_case.tags.value: The value component of a tag attached to the AWS Cases case, used to store user-defined metadata for organizing, searching, or managing the case.

aws_cases_case_rule.rule.hidden.conditions: Within an Amazon Connect Cases case rule, this list contains the conditions under which the rule will hide the designated case fields from the case view.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.hidden.conditions.equal_to: Defines an equality condition for a hidden case rule, matching when the value of the referenced case field exactly equals the configured value.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.hidden.conditions.equal_to.operand_: This object is the first operand of an equality condition within the hidden conditions of an Amazon Connect Cases rule, specifying the source value (such as a case field reference or literal) to be compared against the second operand.
Specifies the unique identifier of the case field that acts as the first operand in an equal-to condition used to determine whether the hidden rule action applies.

Defines the second operand (typically a literal value or field reference) in an equality condition of an AWS Cases case rule, specifying what the first operand must match for the condition to be true.
The Boolean value to which the case field is compared in the equal_to condition, determining when the hidden rule action applies.
The double_value specifies the numeric floating-point value that operand_two must hold on a case for the equal_to condition to match during evaluation of the rule's hidden conditions.
When set, this field indicates that the second operand of the 'equals' condition is an empty value, causing the rule to trigger when the specified case field is empty.

For an `equal_to` condition in an AWS Cases case rule's hidden condition set, this field holds the second operand's string literal, which is compared against the first operand (typically a case field) to determine when the rule's action is triggered.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.hidden.conditions.not_equal_to: This object specifies a 'not equal to' comparison condition that, when true, contributes to hiding the associated field in an AWS Cases case layout.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.hidden.conditions.not_equal_to.oper: Specifies the first operand to be compared in a 'not equal to' condition within the hidden conditions of the AWS Cases rule, which can reference a case field by ID or a literal value.
The unique identifier of the case field used as the left operand in a 'NotEqualTo' condition, evaluated within the rule's hidden conditions to determine if the rule is hidden.
Defines the second operand (either a case field reference or a fixed value) that the first operand is compared against in a 'not_equal_to' condition within a hidden rule of an AWS Cases case rule.
Specifies the Boolean value to compare a Boolean field against in a 'not equal to' rule condition, triggering the rule when the field's value does not equal this boolean.
In AWS Cases case rules, this number is the double-precision value used as the second operand in a 'not equal to' condition, serving as the literal that the evaluated case field is compared against.
When present in operand_two of a 'not_equal_to' condition in an AWS Cases case rule, this empty_value object indicates that the rule evaluates whether the specified field's value is not empty.
The string value of the right-hand side operand in a 'not equal to' comparison within a condition of a hidden rule for an AWS Cases case rule.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.hidden.default_value: Determines whether the field is hidden by default when the hidden rule's condition does not evaluate to true (or when no condition is specified).
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.required: Defines the required-field criteria for the rule, specifying which case fields must be present or carry a particular value for a case to comply with the rule.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.required.conditions.equal_to: Specifies an equality comparison condition that must be met for the AWS Cases rule to trigger, evaluating whether a case field equals a defined value.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.required.conditions.equal_to.operan: Defines the first operand of an equality condition in a case rule, which is compared against the second operand to determine whether the condition matches and triggers the rule's action.
The identifier of a case field whose value is compared to the second operand in an equal-to condition within an AWS Cases case rule.
The second operand of this 'equal to' condition, which can be a reference to a case field or a static value, used alongside the first operand to evaluate whether the rule's condition is satisfied.
In the 'equal_to' condition of a case rule, this boolean value specifies the second operand's literal value, matching when the evaluated field equals that boolean (true or false).
Specifies the double-precision floating-point value to which a case field is compared in an 'equal_to' condition within a rule's required condition set.
When set to an empty object, this indicates that the second operand of the 'equal to' rule condition is the empty value, so the condition matches when the case field is empty.
Specifies the literal string value of the second operand in an equal-to condition, used to compare against the first operand (a case field's value) to determine whether the rule's condition is met.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.required.conditions.equal_to.result: Specifies the boolean value to set on the target field when the equal-to condition in this AWS Cases case rule is satisfied.
aws_cases_case_rule.rule.required.conditions.not_equal_to.op: Specifies the left operand for a 'not equal to' comparison in an Amazon Connect Cases rule condition, containing either a case field reference or a literal value that is compared against the second operand to trigger the rule action.
The field_id of operand_one is the unique identifier of a case field whose value is used as the left operand in the not_equal_to condition.
The second operand in a 'not equal to' condition of an Amazon Connect Cases rule, which holds the value (or field reference) that the first operand must not equal for the condition to match.
The boolean value that serves as the second operand for the 'not_equal_to' comparison in a case rule condition.
The double-precision numeric literal for the second operand of the 'not equal to' condition, representing the value the rule expects the field (first operand) to not match.
Indicates that the second operand of the `not_equal_to` condition is treated as an empty value, causing the rule to match when the source field is not empty.

Defines the string literal for the second operand (the comparison value) in a NotEqualTo condition, so that the rule condition is satisfied only when the selected case field's value does not equal this string.
aws_cases_case_rule.tags.value: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Cases case rule, used for organizing, filtering, and managing the rule resource.

aws_cases_domain.tags.key: The tag key for a tag attached to the AWS Cases domain.
aws_cases_domain.tags.value: The value string of a key-value tag applied to the Amazon Connect Cases domain, used to store metadata such as environment or cost center for the resource.

aws_cases_field.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Cases field, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_cases_layout.content.basic: The basic layout configuration for the case layout, defining how case panel and additional information sections are arranged on the page.
aws_cases_layout.content.basic.more_info: The 'more_info' object configures the 'More Info' section of a basic layout, defining which case fields are displayed in that additional, separate area of the AWS Cases layout.
aws_cases_layout.content.basic.more_info.sections: Specifies the list of sections that make up the 'More Info' area of a basic layout in an AWS Cases layout, where each section can contain text or a reference to a case field.
aws_cases_layout.content.basic.more_info.sections.field_g: Defines a field group within a section of the 'More Info' area of the basic case layout, containing the ordered list of field items to be displayed together.
Specifies the list of case fields to display in this field group within the 'More info' section of the basic layout.
The id of a field within a field group in the 'more info' section of a layout's basic content, referencing the unique identifier of the Amazon Connect Cases case field to display at that position.
The display name of the field group, shown as a heading in the case layout section to visually group related case fields.
aws_cases_layout.content.basic.top_panel: Specifies the top panel of the basic layout, defining the sections and field items displayed at the top of the case view.
aws_cases_layout.content.basic.top_panel.sections: Specifies the ordered list of sections in the top panel of the basic layout, where each section groups a set of case fields with an optional title for display in the case details view.
aws_cases_layout.content.basic.top_panel.sections.field_g: Defines the field group for a section in the top panel of the basic layout, including the group name and the list of case fields to display in that section.
Defines the list of fields included in this field group for the layout, each referencing a field from the case template by its identifier.
The unique identifier of the case field to display, referencing an existing field in the case domain.
The name of the field group, which serves as the display label for the set of fields grouped within the top panel section of the case layout.
aws_cases_layout.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Cases layout, used to store arbitrary metadata for the layout.

aws_cases_template.required_fields.field_id: The identifier of the case field that must be included when creating a case using this template.
aws_cases_template.rules.case_rule_id: Specifies the unique identifier for a rule within the AWS Cases template, used to reference the rule when defining conditional field requirements.
aws_cases_template.rules.field_id: The unique identifier of the case field in Amazon Cases that this rule applies to, matching a field defined in the associated domain.

aws_cassandra_keyspace.replication_specification: Specifies the replication strategy (single or multi-Region) and the list of Regions for a multi-Region Amazon Keyspaces keyspace.
aws_cassandra_keyspace.replication_specification.region_list: A list of AWS regions where the keyspace is replicated for Multi-Region Replication, enabling data availability across those regions.
aws_cassandra_keyspace.replication_specification.replication_st: Specifies the replication strategy for the keyspace, either SINGLE_REGION for single-region replication or MULTI_REGION for replicating data across multiple AWS regions.
aws_cassandra_keyspace.tags: Assigns a list of key-value metadata tags to the Cassandra keyspace, which can be used for categorization and cost tracking.

aws_cassandra_table.auto_scaling_specifications.read_capacit: When true, disables auto scaling for the table's read capacity, reverting to the fixed read capacity units configured on the table.
The maximum number of read capacity units (RCUs) that the table's read capacity can scale up to when auto scaling is enabled.
Sets the minimum number of read capacity units for the table's read capacity auto scaling policy in Amazon Keyspaces.
When true, prevents the target tracking scaling policy from reducing (scaling in) the table's read capacity.
The amount of time in seconds after a scale-in activity completes before another scale-in can begin for the read capacity of the Cassandra table's auto scaling target tracking policy.

The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-out (increase) activity completes before another scale-out activity can start, used in the target tracking scaling policy for read capacity auto scaling of an Amazon Keyspaces (Cassandra) table.
The target value, expressed as a percentage, for read capacity utilization that the auto scaling policy maintains.
aws_cassandra_table.auto_scaling_specifications.write_capaci: Disables automatic scaling of write capacity for the Amazon Keyspaces table, preventing CloudFormation from adjusting provisioned write capacity based on traffic.
The maximum number of write capacity units that the AWS Keyspaces table can scale up to when auto scaling is enabled for write capacity.
Specifies the minimum number of write capacity units that the table can scale down to when write capacity auto scaling is enabled.
Specifies whether scale-in (reducing write capacity) is disabled for this target tracking scaling policy, so the policy can scale out but not automatically scale in.
The cooldown period in seconds after a scale-in activity completes before the write capacity auto scaling policy can trigger another scale-in operation for the Cassandra table.
The number of seconds to wait after a scale-out activity completes before another scale-out activity can start for write capacity auto scaling on the Cassandra table.
The target utilization percentage (e.g., 50 for 50%) that the Amazon Keyspaces write capacity target tracking scaling policy aims to maintain for auto scaling.
aws_cassandra_table.billing_mode: Specifies the billing mode for the Cassandra table, choosing between on-demand and provisioned capacity, and when provisioned, includes the read/write capacity settings.
aws_cassandra_table.billing_mode.provisioned_throughput.read: The number of read capacity units to provision for the Cassandra table when billing mode is set to provisioned.
aws_cassandra_table.billing_mode.provisioned_throughput.writ: Specifies the number of write capacity units (writes per second) that this Cassandra table can sustain when using provisioned billing mode.
aws_cassandra_table.clustering_key_columns.column: Specifies the name and type of a single column that is used as the clustering key, determining the sort order of rows within a partition in the Cassandra table.
aws_cassandra_table.clustering_key_columns.column.column_nam: The name of the clustering key column that defines the sort order of rows within each partition of the Cassandra table.
aws_cassandra_table.clustering_key_columns.column.column_typ: The Cassandra data type of the clustering key column (e.g., 'text', 'int', 'uuid').
aws_cassandra_table.clustering_key_columns.order_by: Specifies the sort order (ASC or DESC) for this clustering key column, determining how rows are stored and queried in the Cassandra table.
aws_cassandra_table.partition_key_columns.column_name: The name of a column that is part of the table's partition key, determining how rows are distributed across partitions in the Cassandra table.
aws_cassandra_table.partition_key_columns.column_type: The Cassandra data type (e.g., TEXT, INT, UUID, TIMESTAMP) assigned to this partition key column in the AWS::Cassandra::Table resource, matching the supported column types for Cassandra tables.
aws_cassandra_table.regular_columns.column_name: The name of a regular (non-partition-key and non-clustering) column in the Cassandra table, defining the column's identifier in the table schema.
aws_cassandra_table.regular_columns.column_type: The Cassandra data type for the regular column, such as text, int, or timestamp, as defined in the regular_columns list of the table.
aws_cassandra_table.replica_specifications: Defines the AWS Regions and optional provisioned read/write capacity settings for each replica in a multi-Region Amazon Keyspaces table.
aws_cassandra_table.replica_specifications.read_capacity_aut: Configures the auto scaling settings for read capacity of an Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) table replica, including enablement, minimum and maximum capacity units, and target utilization.
When true, disables automatic scaling of read capacity for the replica, requiring you to specify fixed read capacity instead.
The maximum number of read capacity units that the table can scale up to under automatic scaling.
Specifies the minimum read capacity (in read request units per second) that Amazon Keyspaces can scale down to for the corresponding replica in this table.
Defines the target tracking scaling policy configuration (e.g., target utilization and scale-in/out behavior) for the read capacity auto scaling of the Cassandra table replica.
Specifies the target tracking scaling policy configuration, including the target value and scale-in behavior, used for read capacity auto scaling on this replica.
When true, this target tracking scaling policy will not scale in (reduce provisioned read capacity) in response to low utilization, allowing only scale-out actions.

The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-in activity completes before the read capacity target tracking policy can initiate another scale-in, used to prevent rapid repeated scaling down for a Cassandra table replica.
The cooldown period (in seconds) that elapses before a scale-out activity can start, preventing rapid increases in read capacity for the replica.
The target utilization percentage for read capacity that the auto scaling policy aims to maintain, triggering scaling adjustments to keep provisioned read capacity in line with the workload.
aws_cassandra_table.replica_specifications.read_capacity_uni: The number of read capacity units provisioned for this specific replica of the Cassandra table in its designated AWS region.
aws_cassandra_table.replica_specifications.region: Specifies the AWS Region where the Cassandra table replica is created, enabling multi-Region replication.
aws_cassandra_table.tags.key: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the Cassandra table.
aws_cassandra_table.tags.value: The value component of a tag assigned to the Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) table, used for cost allocation and resource management.
aws_cassandra_table.warm_throughput.read_units_per_second: Number of warm read capacity units per second for the table's warm throughput configuration.
aws_cassandra_table.warm_throughput.write_units_per_second: The number of write capacity units per second allocated for throughput on warm data stored in the Amazon Keyspaces table.

aws_cassandra_type.fields.field_name: The name of a field within a user-defined Cassandra type in Amazon Keyspaces, defining the structure of the type.
aws_cassandra_type.fields.field_type: The Cassandra data type assigned to this field within the custom type definition, specified as a string such as 'int' or 'text'.

aws_ce_anomaly_monitor.monitor_specification: A JSON-formatted string that defines the custom monitoring criteria for the cost anomaly monitor, such as filtering by services, linked accounts, or cost categories, used when the monitor type is CUSTOM.
aws_ce_anomaly_monitor.monitor_type: Specifies whether the anomaly monitor is a DIMENSIONAL monitor (which watches a specific dimension like service or linked account) or a CUSTOM monitor (which uses a custom threshold on the anomaly score).
aws_ce_anomaly_monitor.resource_tags.key: The tag key for a resource tag applied to the Cost Explorer anomaly monitor, used for identifying and organizing the monitor among AWS resources.
aws_ce_anomaly_monitor.resource_tags.value: The value of a resource tag attached to the AWS Cost Explorer anomaly monitor, used for tagging and cost allocation.

aws_ce_anomaly_subscription.resource_tags.key: The key of a resource tag attached to the AWS Cost Explorer anomaly subscription, used to identify or categorize the subscription within a key-value pair.
aws_ce_anomaly_subscription.resource_tags.value: Specifies the value of a key-value tag applied to the AWS Cost Explorer anomaly subscription, used for organizing, filtering, and controlling access to the subscription resource.
aws_ce_anomaly_subscription.subscribers.address: The email address or Amazon SNS topic ARN that receives notifications for this anomaly subscription.
aws_ce_anomaly_subscription.subscribers.status: The subscription status of the subscriber, indicating whether the subscriber has confirmed or declined the anomaly alert subscription.
aws_ce_anomaly_subscription.subscribers.type: Specifies the type of AWS Cost Explorer anomaly subscription subscriber, either EMAIL or SNS_TOPIC.

aws_ce_cost_category.name: The name of the cost category, which must be unique within your AWS account and is used to identify the cost category in the AWS Cost Management console and APIs.
aws_ce_cost_category.rule_version: Specifies the version of the cost category rule syntax, which must be set to 'CostCategoryExpression.v1' for the rule expressions.
aws_ce_cost_category.tags.key: The key portion of a tag applied to the AWS Cost Category.
aws_ce_cost_category.tags.value: Specifies the value portion of a user-defined tag (key-value pair) applied to the AWS Cost Category, used to categorize and track cost allocation.

aws_certificate_manager_account.account_id: The AWS account ID that owns this ACM account-level configuration, automatically derived from the account in which the resource is deployed.
aws_certificate_manager_account.expiry_events_configuration: Configures the day-based threshold (DaysBeforeExpiry) at which AWS Certificate Manager emits certificate expiration events, enabling EventBridge notifications for upcoming renewals.
aws_certificate_manager_account.expiry_events_configuration.days_before_: Specifies the number of days before certificate expiration when ACM begins emitting expiry-related events, allowing you to adjust the notification lead time.

aws_certificate_manager_certificate.domain_validation_options.domain_name: The domain name for which certificate validation options are specified, corresponding to one of the domains in the certificate's Subject Alternative Names.
aws_certificate_manager_certificate.domain_validation_options.hosted_zone_id: The ID of the hosted zone in Route 53 where the DNS validation record for this domain will be created.
aws_certificate_manager_certificate.domain_validation_options.validation_dom: The domain that AWS Certificate Manager will use for validation (e.g., email or DNS checks), which can be a different domain than the one being certified.
aws_certificate_manager_certificate.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Certificate Manager certificate, used for metadata, cost allocation, and resource organization.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.action_name: A unique, human-readable name for the custom action, used to identify and invoke it within AWS Chatbot (e.g., in Slack or Teams slash commands).
aws_chatbot_custom_action.alias_name: Specifies the alias for the custom action, allowing users to invoke the action with a shorter or alternate name in chat.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.button_text: The text displayed on the button within the message attachment for the AWS Chatbot custom action.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.criteria: The `criteria` list holds filter conditions that determine whether a given notification or command invocation should use this attachment, restricting the custom action to matching events.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.criteria.operator: The operator in an attachment criteria condition for an AWS Chatbot custom action, specifying the comparison method (e.g., 'CONTAINS' or 'EQUALS') used to match message attachment key/value pairs when determining whether the action can be invoked.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.criteria.value: The value that AWS Chatbot compares against the event attribute specified by the sibling 'key' field using the sibling 'operator' logic, to decide whether the attachment should be included for a custom action invocation.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.criteria.variable_name: Specifies the name of a notification message variable that this attachment criterion evaluates (together with an operator and value) to decide whether the corresponding custom action is presented for that notification.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.notification_type: Specifies the type of AWS notification (such as a CloudWatch alarm state change) that this attachment associates with the chatbot custom action.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.variables: Defines the map of variable names to values that are substituted into the custom action's command when this attachment is used.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.custom_action_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the custom action in AWS Chatbot, assigned by AWS when the resource is created.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.definition: Defines the custom action by providing the command text (CommandText) that the AWS Chatbot runs when the action is invoked.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.definition.command_text: The command text that defines the custom action's behavior, such as a shell command or script, which is executed when the action is triggered.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.tags: A list of key-value pairs that can be attached to the AWS Chatbot custom action to help identify, organize, and manage the resource, with each object containing a Key and Value property.
aws_chatbot_custom_action.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Chatbot custom action, used to identify and categorize the resource for management and cost tracking.

aws_chatbot_microsoft_teams_channel_conf.tags.key: The user-defined key for a tag attached to an AWS Chatbot Microsoft Teams channel configuration, used for organizing, filtering, and cost-tracking the resource.
aws_chatbot_microsoft_teams_channel_conf.tags.value: The tag value for a key-value pair applied to the AWS Chatbot Microsoft Teams channel configuration resource.

aws_chatbot_slack_channel_configuration.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to an AWS Chatbot Slack channel configuration, enabling cost allocation tracking and resource categorization within AWS.
aws_chatbot_slack_channel_configuration.tags.value: The value component of a key-value tag that can be attached to the AWS Chatbot Slack channel configuration for resource organization and cost allocation.

aws_chime_app_instance.tags.key: The key of a tag that is attached to the Amazon Chime AppInstance resource for identification and organization.
aws_chime_app_instance.tags.value: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the Chime AppInstance, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_chime_app_instance_bot.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AppInstanceBot, used to categorize and manage the resource (e.g., environment, project) in AWS Chime.
aws_chime_app_instance_bot.tags.value: The value of a user-defined metadata tag attached to the Amazon Chime App Instance Bot.

aws_chime_app_instance_user.app_instance_arn: The ARN of the Amazon Chime AppInstance in which this user is created, uniquely identifying the parent app instance for the user.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.app_instance_user_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AppInstanceUser, assigned by AWS when the user is created.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.app_instance_user_id: The client-supplied unique identifier for the user within the specified Amazon Chime AppInstance, which is required at creation and is used to form the user's ARN.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.expiration_settings: Configures automatic deletion of the AppInstanceUser after a specified number of days from its creation timestamp, using an expiration criterion and day count.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.expiration_settings.expiration_criterion: Specifies whether the expiration date for the AppInstanceUser is calculated from the user's creation timestamp (CREATED_TIMESTAMP) or their last activity timestamp (LAST_ACTIVE_TIMESTAMP).
aws_chime_app_instance_user.expiration_settings.expiration_days: The number of days after which the Amazon Chime AppInstanceUser account automatically expires and is deleted.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.metadata: An optional user-defined metadata string (up to 1000 characters) attached to the AppInstanceUser for app-specific information.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.name: Sets the display name for the AppInstanceUser, which is used to identify the user within the Amazon Chime app instance.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.tags: Specifies a list of tags to associate with the App Instance User, used for organizing and managing the user in AWS Chime.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.tags.key: The key of a key-value tag attached to the Amazon Chime AppInstanceUser, used to label and categorize the resource.
aws_chime_app_instance_user.tags.value: The value portion of a tag attached to an Amazon Chime AppInstanceUser, used to add user-defined metadata to the identity for management and tracking.

aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.configuration: Defines the configuration for a processor in the channel flow, specifying the Lambda function ARN and the invocation role ARN used when the processor type is Lambda.
aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.configuration.lambda: The configuration block for a Lambda processor in a Chime channel flow, specifying the Lambda function ARN and the IAM role ARN used to invoke it.
aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.configuration.lambda.invocati: Specifies whether the Lambda function is invoked asynchronously (ASYNC) or synchronously (SYNC) for this processor in the channel flow.
aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.configuration.lambda.resource: The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that the Amazon Chime channel flow invokes to process messages for this processor.
aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.execution_order: The integer execution order of this processor within the channel flow, which determines the sequence in which processors are invoked during message processing.
aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.fallback_action: The action to execute if the processor's primary action fails, such as 'SEND' or 'DELETE'.
aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.name: The user-defined name that identifies this processor within the channel flow's processor list, used for configuration and runtime reference.
aws_chime_channel_flow.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Chime ChannelFlow resource.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.analysis_parameters.default_value: The default value to use for the analysis parameter when a value is not provided at runtime.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.analysis_parameters.name: Specifies the name of an analysis parameter in the analysis template, which is used as a placeholder in the template's SQL query.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.analysis_parameters.type: Defines the SQL data type of the parameter (e.g., INT, STRING, BOOLEAN) used to enforce type-checking when the analysis template is run in a Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.analysis_template_identifier: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this analysis template, returned after creation.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the analysis template in AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.collaboration_arn: The ARN of the collaboration that this analysis template belongs to.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.collaboration_identifier: The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this analysis template belongs to, which is assigned by AWS and cannot be changed.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.description: Specifies a user-provided description for the analysis template to help identify its purpose.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.error_message_configuration: Specifies the custom error message (including subject and body) that AWS Clean Rooms returns to users when a query based on this analysis template is denied or fails.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.error_message_configuration.type: Indicates the type of error message delivery mechanism; when set to 'S3', error messages from the analysis template are written to an Amazon S3 bucket configured in the accompanying S3 property.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.format: Specifies the query language of the analysis template, with valid values being 'SQL' or 'PYTHON'.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.membership_arn: The ARN of the AWS Clean Rooms membership associated with this analysis template, automatically assigned by AWS.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.membership_identifier: The unique identifier of the membership that owns this analysis template.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.name: The name of the analysis template, used to identify and reference the template within the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.schema: Specifies the referenced tables (via an AnalysisSchema object) that the analysis template's SQL query is allowed to access.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.schema.referenced_tables: The list of table names in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that the analysis template's SQL query is permitted to reference, restricting the query's data access.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source: The source object defines the SQL query content for the analysis template, containing the query text that will be executed against the collaboration data.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.artifacts: The S3 URIs of the analysis artifacts (such as SQL query files) that make up the source of the Clean Rooms analysis template.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.artifacts.additional_artifacts: Specifies additional artifacts (as objects containing artifact URIs) to be included with the analysis template's source, enabling the analysis to use supporting files beyond the primary SQL query.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.artifacts.additional_artifacts.lo: Specifies the S3 location (bucket and key) of an additional artifact, such as a supporting file or script, that is part of the analysis template's source artifacts.

The S3 bucket name that stores an additional artifact (such as a custom analysis script or supporting file) for the AWS Clean Rooms analysis template's source, as specified in the source's artifacts list.
The Amazon S3 object key (file name) of an additional artifact that is part of the analysis template's source artifacts.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.artifacts.entry_point: The entry_point object specifies the S3 location of the main Python script that serves as the starting point for the analysis in an AWS Clean Rooms analysis template.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.artifacts.entry_point.location: The S3 location of the entry point query file, specified as an object with a bucket and key that identify the SQL script in Amazon S3.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.artifacts.entry_point.location.bu: The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that stores the entry-point artifact (the primary analysis file) for the analysis template's source artifacts.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.artifacts.entry_point.location.ke: The S3 object key within the specified S3 bucket that identifies the entry point file (e.g., a SQL script) for the analysis template's source artifacts.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.artifacts.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS Clean Rooms read access to the S3 objects in the source artifacts location.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.text: The SQL query text that defines the analysis template's source, used as the basis for the analysis.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source_metadata.artifacts: Maps artifact names to their S3 URI locations, defining the source code artifacts for the analysis template within the source_metadata block.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source_metadata.artifacts.additional_art: Specifies the SHA-256 hash of an additional artifact file that is part of the source metadata for the analysis template.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source_metadata.artifacts.entry_point_ha: The SHA256 hash of the entry point artifact (SQL script) in the analysis template's source metadata, used to verify the integrity of the source code.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.synthetic_data_parameters: Configures the generation of synthetic data based on the analysis template's schema, including the desired row count, for testing analysis queries without using real data.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.synthetic_data_parameters.ml_synthetic_d: Configures the machine learning model parameters for generating a differentially private synthetic dataset from the analysis template's query results.

Specifies the per-column classification (such as categorical or numeric) applied when generating ML synthetic data from the analysis template's underlying dataset, controlling how each column is modeled by the synthetic data generator.
The name of the source column that is assigned a classification in the column mapping for generating ML synthetic data in the analysis template.

The semantic type assigned to the mapped column (for example, categorical, numeric, datetime, or free_text) that AWS Clean Rooms uses to guide the ML synthetic data generation process for the analysis template.

Indicates whether this column is classified as a predictive feature (input variable) for the machine learning model when generating synthetic data in AWS Clean Rooms, so the service preserves its relationship to the training label.
Specifies the privacy loss budget (epsilon) for the differentially private synthetic data generation, where lower values produce more private but less accurate data.

The maximum acceptable membership inference attack score for synthetic data generated for machine learning, providing a privacy threshold to limit the risk of inferring original data membership from the synthetic dataset.
aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.tags.key: The user-defined key of a tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms analysis template, used to categorize, organize, and identify the resource.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.allowed_result_regions: Limits the AWS Regions where members of the collaboration can write query results, restricting result outputs to the specified regions.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.analytics_engine: Specifies the analytics engine for the collaboration, which must be either `CLEAN_ROOMS_SQL` (the default) or `SPARK`, and controls the query engine used by members of the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.collaboration_identifier: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_display_name: Specifies the display name of the member who creates the collaboration, which is visible to other members in the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_member_abilities: Defines the set of abilities (e.g., CAN_QUERY, CAN_RECEIVE_RESULTS) that are granted to the creator of the collaboration, determining what actions the creator can perform within the Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_mlmember_abilities: This object specifies the machine learning abilities granted to the creator member of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, determining which custom and standard ML member operations (such as receiving model output or trained models) the creator is permitted to perform.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_mlmember_abilities.custom_mlmemb: Specifies a list of custom machine learning member ability names to be granted to the creator member of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, defining customized ML permissions beyond the default standard abilities.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_payment_configuration: Determines how the collaboration creator is compensated for query compute costs, including whether the creator accepts responsibility for those costs and the number of query credits provided to collaborating members.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_payment_configuration.job_comput: Specifies how the collaboration creator pays for compute resources used by members when running jobs (as opposed to interactive queries) within the clean rooms collaboration.
Specifies whether the collaboration creator is responsible for paying for job compute costs in the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_payment_configuration.machine_le: Specifies the configuration for whether the collaboration creator is responsible for costs incurred by machine learning queries, typically by setting a status like ENABLED or DISABLED.
Configures the payment responsibility for machine learning model inference in the collaboration, indicating whether the collaboration creator is responsible for the resulting charges.
Indicates whether the collaboration creator is responsible for the costs incurred by machine learning model inference.
Configuration specifying whether the collaboration creator is responsible for the costs of training machine learning models.
Indicates whether the creator of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration is responsible for the cost of training machine learning models under the creator payment configuration.

Defines the payment configuration for the synthetic data generation capability under machine learning settings, specifying how the collaboration creator is billed for using this feature in an AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
Indicates whether the collaboration creator is responsible for the costs associated with synthetic data generation.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_payment_configuration.query_comp: Specifies the payment configuration for query compute in the collaboration, determining whether the collaboration creator pays for query compute usage.
Indicates whether the creator of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration is responsible for the query compute costs.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.data_encryption_metadata: Specifies the data encryption metadata for the collaboration, controlling whether clear text is allowed, duplicate rows are permitted, joins on columns with different names are allowed, and how null values are preserved.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.data_encryption_metadata.allow_cleartext: Indicates whether encrypted tables in the collaboration are allowed to contain cleartext (unencrypted) data.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.data_encryption_metadata.allow_duplicate: Specifies whether this collaboration permits query results to contain duplicate rows under the configured encryption metadata.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.data_encryption_metadata.allow_joins_on_: Controls whether a query in the collaboration can join tables on columns that have different names across different members' datasets.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.data_encryption_metadata.preserve_nulls: This required Boolean value determines whether nulls in the underlying data remain as nulls when encrypted in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, rather than being encrypted into a non-null value.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.description: The user-provided description of the collaboration, which helps identify its purpose and can be updated after creation.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.is_metrics_enabled: Whether the collaboration collects metrics about query activity (such as query counts and latency), enabling you to monitor and analyze usage patterns.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members: Defines the AWS accounts that participate in the collaboration, each with an account ID, display name, and the abilities (such as CAN_QUERY or CAN_RECEIVE_RESULTS) granted to that member.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.account_id: The AWS account ID of the member being added to the Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.display_name: The friendly, human-readable name assigned to a member's AWS account, used to identify that member within the Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.member_abilities: Specifies the list of allowable operations (e.g., CAN_QUERY, CAN_RECEIVE_RESULTS) that this collaboration member is permitted to perform.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.mlmember_abilities: Specifies the ML-specific abilities for the member, such as whether they can query ML-protected data and receive results from ML queries.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.mlmember_abilities.custom_mlmemb: Specifies the list of custom machine learning (ML) member abilities granted to this member in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, allowing them to perform additional ML operations beyond the predefined ML member abilities.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.payment_configuration: Configures how the member pays for query compute in the collaboration, specifically indicating whether the member is responsible for query compute costs via the query_compute.is_responsible property.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.payment_configuration.job_comput: The `job_compute` object within a member's `payment_configuration` specifies which party pays for the compute used when this member runs analysis jobs, with its `type` field indicating either `MEMBER` (the member pays) or `COLLABORATOR` (the collaboration creator pays).
Indicates whether this member is responsible for paying the compute costs for job compute queries in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.payment_configuration.machine_le: Determines how this member pays for machine learning tasks (model training and inference) within the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.

Specifies the payment configuration for machine learning model inference activity, typically including the payment amount (in USD) that a collaboration member pays for each model inference operation run in the collaboration.
Indicates whether this member is the payer (responsible party) for costs incurred from machine learning model inference queries in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
Payment configuration for machine learning model training, indicating whether the member is responsible for the costs of model training in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
Indicates whether this member is responsible for paying for the costs associated with training the machine learning model in the collaboration.
An object that specifies whether this collaboration member enables synthetic data generation jobs and which party (the collaboration creator or the member) is responsible for paying for those jobs.
Indicates whether this collaboration member is responsible for payment for synthetic data generation under the machine learning payment configuration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.payment_configuration.query_comp: Specifies whether this collaboration member is responsible for paying the compute costs for queries run in the collaboration.
Indicates whether this member is responsible for paying the query compute costs incurred by the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.name: The name of the collaboration, a user-defined friendly identifier that must be unique within the AWS account and can be up to 128 characters.
aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.query_log_status: Determines whether query logs are enabled for the collaboration, accepting the enum values ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.allowed_columns: Specifies the list of column names from the underlying AWS Glue table that are allowed to be used in analyses using this configured table, restricting which columns are accessible to collaborators.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_method: Specifies the analysis method for the configured table, which determines how queries can be executed against the data (supported value: DIRECT_QUERY).
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules: Defines the analysis rules for the configured table, specifying the allowed analysis types (such as aggregation or list) and the associated policy constraints that govern how the data can be queried.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy: Configures the analysis rule policy, which defines the rule type (aggregation, list, or custom) and its specific settings such as aggregate columns, join columns, and allowed operations.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1: The analysis rule policy version 1 object, which contains the aggregation or list rule settings (such as join columns and aggregate columns) that govern how members can query the configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.aggregation: Specifies the aggregation analysis rule policy, controlling how aggregate queries can be run on the configured table within AWS Clean Rooms, including allowed aggregation functions, join requirements, and output constraints.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.aggregation.add: Controls whether the output of queries run under this aggregation analysis rule can be used as input to additional analyses, accepting values of 'ALLOWED' or 'REQUIRED'.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.aggregation.agg: Defines the columns that queries are allowed to aggregate under this aggregation analysis rule, along with the permitted aggregation functions (e.g., SUM, AVG, COUNT) for each column.
The list of column names that are allowed to be used as aggregate columns in the aggregation analysis rule of this AWS Clean Rooms configured table.
Specifies the aggregation function (e.g., SUM, AVG, COUNT) applied to the column names in this aggregate column definition of the aggregation analysis rule.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.aggregation.all: Specifies which join operators (such as AND, OR, or NOT) are permitted in queries against the configured table when using this aggregation analysis rule.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.aggregation.dim: Specifies the columns of the configured table that can be used as grouping dimensions in aggregate queries under this analysis rule.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.aggregation.joi: Lists the column names that can be used as join keys in aggregation queries when this analysis rule's policy is applied to the configured table.
Specifies whether queries using this aggregation rule must include a join condition on the configured table's join columns.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.aggregation.out: A list of output constraints, each specifying a column name and the minimum number of distinct values that must appear in that column for an aggregation query to produce output, preventing re-identification.

Specifies the name of a column that must appear in the aggregated query output, where each distinct value in that column must occur at least the specified minimum number of rows to satisfy the analysis rule's privacy constraint.
Specifies the minimum allowable value for the aggregated output column, enforcing a privacy floor (e.g., to prevent revealing small counts) in the aggregation query results.
Defines the allowed aggregate function (such as COUNT, SUM, or AVG) for the associated output column in the aggregation analysis rule, restricting how that column can be aggregated in queries.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.aggregation.sca: The list of scalar SQL functions (e.g., UPPER, ROUND) that are permitted to be used in aggregation queries under this analysis rule's aggregation policy.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom: Defines the custom analysis rule policy, which lists the SQL queries (allowed analyses) and related settings that collaboration members can use when querying the configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom.addition: Specifies whether the results of a query executed on this configured table can be used in subsequent additional analyses, with allowed values ALLOWED, REQUIRED, or NOT_ALLOWED.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom.allowed_: A list of allowed analysis template identifiers (such as ARNs) that are permitted to run against the configured table under this custom analysis rule.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the analysis providers that are permitted to run analyses on the configured table under this custom analysis rule.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom.differen: Specifies the differential privacy configuration for the custom analysis rule, including the list of protected columns and the epsilon value that controls the privacy-accuracy trade-off for query results.

Specifies the list of columns in the configured table to which differential privacy protection is applied, causing query outputs over these columns to be perturbed and tracked against a privacy budget for Clean Rooms analyses.
The name of a column that is included in the differential privacy policy of the custom analysis rule, specifying which configured table column is protected by the differential privacy aggregation.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom.disallow: Specifies the list of column names that must be excluded from the output of queries run under this custom analysis rule policy, preventing collaborators from viewing those columns.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.list: Defines the list-based analysis rule policy for the configured table, specifying the columns that can be used in list queries and any associated constraints or parameters.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.list.additional: Specifies whether additional analyses may be run on the output of list queries governed by this list analysis rule, typically with enum values like ALLOWED or NOT_ALLOWED.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.list.allowed_jo: Specifies the allowed join operators (e.g., EQ, NEQ, LT, LE, GT, GE) that can be used when this configured table is joined with other tables in list-type analyses under the policy analysis rule.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.list.join_colum: The join_columns attribute specifies the list of column names in the configured table that can be used in JOIN operations when running queries under the 'list' analysis rule policy.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.list.list_colum: Specifies the list of columns in the configured table that are allowed to appear in the results of a list query under this analysis rule.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysis_rules.type: Specifies the type of analysis rule (e.g., AGGREGATION, LIST) that governs how query results are computed and displayed for the configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.configured_table_identifier: The unique identifier (such as an ARN) that AWS assigns to the configured table upon creation.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.description: A free-form text description of the configured table that helps identify its purpose or contents.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.name: The name of the configured table, which is a required, user-defined identifier for the table within AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.selected_analysis_methods: Specifies the list of allowed analysis methods (such as DIRECT_QUERY or ADDITIONAL_ANALYSES) that can be used against the configured table, defining the permitted query types in its analysis rule policy.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference: Defines the source AWS Glue table (via its database name and table name) that this configured table references.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.athena: Defines the Amazon Athena table that the configured table references, specifying the database name, table name, and optionally the workgroup where the table resides.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.athena.catalog_name: The name of the Athena data catalog that contains the table referenced by this configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.athena.database_name: The name of the Athena database that contains the table referenced by this configured table for querying in AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.athena.table_name: The name of the Athena table that this configured table references for analysis in AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.athena.work_group: The name of the Athena workgroup in which the referenced table resides for this AWS Clean Rooms configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.glue: The 'glue' object in 'table_reference' specifies the AWS Glue table that the configured table references, including the database name and table name.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.glue.database_name: The name of the AWS Glue database in the Data Catalog that contains the table referenced by this configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.glue.region: The AWS Region where the referenced AWS Glue table is located.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.glue.table_name: The name of the AWS Glue table used as the data source for this configured table in AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.snowflake: Specifies the Snowflake table reference properties, including the account identifier, database name, schema name, and table name, to identify the source table for the configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.snowflake.account_identi: The Snowflake account identifier that uniquely identifies the Snowflake account hosting the source table referenced by this configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.snowflake.database_name: The name of the Snowflake database that contains the table referenced by this configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.snowflake.schema_name: The name of the Snowflake schema that contains the table referenced by this configured table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.snowflake.secret_arn: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Snowflake credentials used to connect to the Snowflake data source for this configured table reference.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.snowflake.table_name: The name of the Snowflake table that this configured table references.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_reference.snowflake.table_schema.v: Specifies version 1 of the column schema for the referenced Snowflake table, where each object in the list defines a column's name, data type, and nullability.
The name of a column within the Snowflake table schema that AWS Clean Rooms uses to define the configured table's column list.
Specifies the data type of a column in the Snowflake table schema that defines the table reference for the AWS Clean Rooms configured table.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the configured table association, assigned by AWS when the association is created.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.configured_table_association_analysis_ru: Configures the analysis rules for the configured table association, specifying the permitted analysis types (e.g., list, aggregate, custom) and their policy constraints for querying the associated configured table within a collaboration.

This object specifies the policy for an analysis rule attached to a configured table association, defining the type of analysis (e.g., aggregation, list, or custom) along with the detailed constraints and parameters (such as aggregation columns, join conditions, and output limits) that govern queries run by collaboration members on the associated table.

Specifies the versioned analysis rule policy for a configured table association, containing the v1 policy that defines allowed aggregation columns, join columns, or custom SQL templates used to constrain queries in the collaboration.

Specifies the aggregation analysis rule policy parameters for the configured table association, including the allowed aggregate columns, dimension columns, join requirements, and permitted aggregation operators.
Specifies which additional analyses (such as CORRELATION or REGRESSION) are permitted on the output of aggregation queries governed by this configured table association's aggregation analysis rule.
The list of collaboration member account IDs (or member ARNs) allowed to receive query results from aggregation queries run against this configured table association.

The custom analysis rule policy (version v1) for this AWS Clean Rooms configured table association, defining the allowed SQL operations such as joins, aggregations, and output columns that members can use when querying the associated table.

This field specifies the additional types of analyses (e.g., SQL, Python) that are permitted to be run on the configured table when using a custom analysis rule policy, extending the set defined in `allowedAnalyses`.
Specifies the list of member account IDs that are allowed to receive query results when this custom analysis rule is used.
Configures the list analysis rule for the configured table association, defining the allowed columns that members can select in list queries.
Specifies the list of additional analysis types (such as AGGREGATE or CUSTOM) that are permitted for queries on the configured table association when the base analysis rule is of type LIST.
Specifies the list of allowed result receivers (e.g., AWS account IDs or IAM roles) that may receive query results when a LIST analysis rule is applied to the associated configured table.
Specifies the type of analysis rule for the configured table association (e.g., AGGREGATION or LIST), which defines the privacy-enforcing query operations allowed on the associated table.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.configured_table_association_identifier: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the configured table association within the membership.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.configured_table_identifier: The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms configured table that this association links to a membership for collaborative analysis.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.description: An optional free-form description of the configured table association, used to provide additional context or identity for the association within the AWS Clean Rooms membership.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.membership_identifier: The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms membership for which this configured table association is created, linking the configured table to that membership.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.name: A unique, user-provided name for the configured table association, used to identify and manage the association within the AWS Clean Rooms membership.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Clean Rooms assumes to access the underlying data referenced by the configured table when the associated table is used in analyses.
aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.tags.value: Specifies the value of a tag key attached to the AWS Clean Rooms configured table association, used to classify and manage the resource.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Clean Rooms ID mapping table in AWS.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.collaboration_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that contains this ID mapping table, automatically assigned by AWS.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.collaboration_identifier: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the collaboration that contains this ID mapping table.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.description: An optional user-defined description that provides context or identification for the ID mapping table in AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.id_mapping_table_identifier: The system-generated unique identifier (such as the Amazon Resource Name) of the AWS Clean Rooms ID mapping table, used to reference the table within the service.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.input_reference_config: Configures the input reference for the ID mapping table, specifying the ARN of the source data or entity resolution resource and whether AWS Clean Rooms manages the resource policies.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.input_reference_config.input_reference_a: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the input reference data source (such as an Amazon S3 bucket) that contains the records used to create the ID mapping table in AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.input_reference_config.manage_resource_p: A Boolean flag that indicates whether AWS Clean Rooms automatically manages the resource policies for the input reference (the underlying AWS resource) so that the ID mapping table can access it; if set to true, Clean Rooms handles required policy changes, and if false, you are responsible for managing them.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.input_reference_properties: The computed inputReferenceProperties object contains the resolved list of input reference column/table pairs that define how the ID mapping table maps identifiers across its referenced tables.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.input_reference_properties.id_mapping_ta: Specifies the S3 data source(s) that AWS Clean Rooms reads to build the ID mapping table, with each item providing an input source ARN.
The unique identifier of the ID namespace association that serves as the input source for this ID mapping table, linking the ID namespace to the collaboration.
Specifies whether the associated input source ARN represents the source or target for the ID mapping table, with allowed values SOURCE or TARGET.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.kms_key_arn: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the ID mapping table data.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.membership_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that owns this ID mapping table.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.membership_identifier: The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that owns this ID mapping table.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.name: The user-defined name of the ID mapping table, used to identify and reference it within the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.tags: The list of tags to apply to the ID mapping table, where each tag consists of a required key and an optional value.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.tags.key: The key (name) of a user-defined tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS Clean Rooms ID mapping table, used for metadata organization and resource identification.
aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag associated with the AWS Clean Rooms ID Mapping Table, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this ID namespace association within AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.collaboration_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the collaboration that this ID namespace association belongs to.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.collaboration_identifier: The unique identifier of the collaboration to which this ID namespace association belongs.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.description: An optional free-text field for storing a human-readable note about the AWS Clean Rooms ID namespace association, helping to indicate its business purpose or configuration context.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.id_mapping_config: Configures the ID mapping behavior for this ID namespace association, specifying whether the namespace acts as a source or target in AWS Clean Rooms ID mapping.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.id_mapping_config.allow_use_as_dimension: When set to true, allows the ID namespace to be used as a dimension column in AWS Clean Rooms queries and analyses.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.id_namespace_association_identifier: The unique system-generated identifier for this Clean Rooms ID namespace association.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.input_reference_config: Defines the input reference for the ID namespace association, specifying the ARN of the underlying data source (such as an AWS Glue table) and whether AWS Clean Rooms manages resource policies on that source.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.input_reference_config.input_reference_a: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the entity reference data that the ID namespace association uses to resolve identities, as specified in the input reference configuration.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.input_reference_config.manage_resource_p: A Boolean flag that, when true, indicates AWS Clean Rooms automatically manages the resource policies for the referenced input resource (such as an S3 bucket) to allow access for the ID namespace association, and when false, requires the user to manage those policies manually.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.input_reference_properties: The read-only InputReferenceProperties object that AWS returns for a Clean Rooms ID namespace association, specifying the ID namespace type (e.g., SOURCE or TARGET) and the member columns used as the input reference for ID matching.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.input_reference_properties.id_mapping_wo: A list of ID mapping workflow types (e.g., UseProvidedSource or UseProvidedTarget) that this Clean Rooms ID namespace association supports, determining which matching workflows can be run with the associated namespace.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.input_reference_properties.id_namespace_: Specifies whether the associated ID namespace functions as a SOURCE or TARGET in the Clean Rooms collaboration's matching workflow.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.membership_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the membership that contains this ID namespace association.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.membership_identifier: The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that this ID namespace association belongs to.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.name: A required, user-specified name for the ID namespace association, used to identify and manage the association within an AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.tags: Specifies the list of tag key-value pairs to assign to the ID namespace association, enabling cost allocation and resource metadata organization.
aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms ID namespace association, used to organize, filter, and manage this resource.
