aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms ID namespace association, used to store arbitrary metadata for resource categorization and management.

aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.analysis_rules: Defines the analysis constraints that govern how members can query the intermediate table, including the allowed analysis methods and their configurations.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom: Defines the custom analysis rule variant within the V1 analysis rule policy, specifying which SQL analyses (e.g., SELECT) are allowed and any restrictions on analysis providers or output columns for the table.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom.addition: This field specifies the ARNs of additional analyses that are allowed to be run on the intermediate table under the custom analysis rule policy.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom.allowed_: Specifies the list of allowed analysis template names (strings) that collaborators may run on the configured table under this custom analysis rule, restricting which analyses are permitted.

This list of strings defines the AWS account IDs that are authorized to act as analysis providers for the custom analysis rule, restricting which accounts can run SQL queries against the intermediate table.
Specifies the list of member account identifiers that are allowed to receive the results of queries run under this custom analysis rule policy.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom.differen: Defines the differential privacy settings for the custom analysis rule, specifying the privacy budget and noise injection mechanism applied to prevent re-identification of individual records.
Specifies the columns in the AWS Clean Rooms intermediate table that are protected by the differential privacy policy within this custom analysis rule.
The name of the column in the configured table to which the differential privacy policy is applied.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.analysis_rules.policy.v1.custom.disallow: Specifies the list of column names from the intermediate table that are prohibited from being included in the output of any query executed under this custom analysis rule, preventing sensitive data from being exposed.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.collaboration_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration in which the intermediate table is defined.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.collaboration_identifier: The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this intermediate table belongs to.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.intermediate_table_identifier: The system-generated unique identifier assigned by AWS Clean Rooms to this intermediate table, used to reference and manage the table resource.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.kms_key_arn: Specifies the AWS KMS key ARN used to encrypt the intermediate table, enabling customer-managed server-side encryption for the table's data.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.membership_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that owns or contains the intermediate table, provided as a read-only identifier.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.membership_identifier: The unique identifier of the membership within the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this intermediate table belongs to.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.population_analysis_configuration.sql_pa: The sql_parameters object provides named values for the placeholders defined in the SQL query of the population analysis configuration, enabling the analysis to be customized with different parameter values at execution time.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the analysis template that the SQL parameters in this block are associated with, used to identify which template's parameters are being configured for the population analysis.
The SQL query text that defines the population analysis logic for generating the intermediate table in AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms intermediate table, serving as the identifier for the tag's metadata label.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Clean Rooms membership.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.collaboration_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this membership is associated with.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.collaboration_creator_account_id: The `collaboration_creator_account_id` attribute returns the AWS account ID of the account that created the collaboration to which this Clean Rooms membership belongs.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.collaboration_identifier: The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this membership is associated with.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.default_job_result_configuration: Specifies the default configuration for storing query results, including the S3 output location and the IAM role used to write results for jobs run by this membership.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.default_job_result_configuration.output_: Specifies the S3 bucket (and optional key prefix) that serves as the default destination for query results when running jobs in this membership.
The S3 output configuration for the default job result configuration, specifying the Amazon S3 bucket (and optional key prefix) where analysis job results are delivered.
The name of the S3 bucket where the default job results are delivered, as part of the membership's default job result output configuration.
The S3 key prefix under which the default analysis job result objects are stored in the specified output S3 bucket.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.default_job_result_configuration.role_ar: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Clean Rooms assumes to write query results to the S3 location configured in the default job result configuration.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.default_result_configuration: Specifies the default output configuration (such as the S3 bucket and IAM role) used to write query results for the membership.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.default_result_configuration.output_conf: Specifies the Amazon S3 destination (bucket and optional key prefix) used to store the default query results for this Clean Rooms membership.
Specifies the S3 bucket and optional key prefix where query results for this Clean Rooms membership are stored.
The name of the S3 bucket to which the default result configuration delivers query results for this AWS Clean Rooms membership.
The S3 object key prefix that is applied to the output files when the Clean Rooms membership's default result configuration writes query results to the specified S3 bucket.
Specifies the file format (CSV or PARQUET) for query results written to the S3 bucket and key prefix in the membership's default result configuration.
Determines whether the default result configuration writes query output to a single S3 file (true) or multiple files (false).
aws_clean_rooms_membership.default_result_configuration.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Clean Rooms assumes to write query results to the default output location configured for the membership.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.is_metrics_enabled: Whether query metrics are enabled for the Clean Rooms membership, which if true enables Amazon CloudWatch metrics for queries run within the membership.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.membership_identifier: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for this AWS Clean Rooms membership.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_configuration: Configures the payment details for the membership, including the mode that determines which member is billed for query compute in the clean room.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_configuration.job_compute: Specifies the payment configuration for job compute in the membership, indicating which party (the 'MemberWhoPays' value) is responsible for paying for compute jobs run under the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_configuration.job_compute.is_res: Indicates whether this Clean Rooms membership is responsible for paying the compute costs for analysis jobs run in the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_configuration.machine_learning: Configures which party (the member or the collaborator) is responsible for paying for machine learning operations within the AWS Clean Rooms membership, as part of the overarching payment configuration.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_configuration.machine_learning.m: Specifies the payment configuration for machine learning model inference jobs in the Clean Rooms membership, including which member is responsible for associated costs.
Indicates whether the member associated with this Clean Rooms membership is responsible for the costs of machine learning model inference under this payment configuration.
Defines the payment responsibility for machine learning model training in the membership's payment configuration, indicating whether the membership is responsible for the associated costs.
Indicates whether the membership owner is responsible for covering the costs incurred by machine learning model training in the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_configuration.machine_learning.s: Configures synthetic data generation for Clean Rooms ML by providing an IsEnabled flag that determines whether the feature is active and thus billing for it is incurred.
Indicates whether the membership is responsible for the costs of synthetic data generation queries in the machine learning payment configuration.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_configuration.query_compute: This configuration block indicates whether this Clean Rooms membership is responsible for the compute costs associated with running queries in the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_configuration.query_compute.is_r: Indicates whether this membership is responsible for paying the query compute costs incurred by queries in the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.query_log_status: Specifies whether query logging is enabled for the Clean Rooms membership, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED to control retention of query activity records.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.tags.key: The key portion of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms membership, used to categorize and identify the resource.
aws_clean_rooms_membership.tags.value: A user-defined tag value attached to the AWS Clean Rooms membership, providing metadata that can be used for categorization, cost allocation, or access control.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.configured_model_algorithm_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the configured model algorithm.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.description: An optional, human-readable description that identifies the configured model algorithm and explains its purpose within the AWS Clean Rooms ML resource.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.inference_container_config: Specifies the container configuration, including the Amazon ECR image URI and optional environment variables, for running inference with this configured model algorithm.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.inference_container_config.image_uri: The URI of the container image (stored in Amazon ECR) that hosts the model inference code for this configured model algorithm.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.kms_key_arn: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the configured model algorithm data.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.name: The required name for the configured model algorithm, which uniquely identifies it within an AWS account and Region and is used as the resource identifier when referencing it in Clean Rooms ML operations.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that grants the configured model algorithm the necessary permissions to access customer data and other AWS resources during analysis within an AWS Clean Rooms ML collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to this AWS Clean Rooms ML configured model algorithm, used to organize, identify, and manage the resource through metadata.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.training_container_config: Configures the Docker container (e.g., image URI and runtime parameters) that runs the training algorithm for this configured model algorithm in AWS Clean Rooms ML.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.training_container_config.arguments: The `arguments` field of the training container configuration for an AWS Clean Rooms ML configured model algorithm is a list of strings that specify command-line arguments to be passed to the training container when it runs.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.training_container_config.entrypoint: Specifies the entrypoint command (as a list of strings) that the training container executes when started, overriding any image default entrypoint.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.training_container_config.image_uri: Specifies the Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) image URI of the container that runs the model training job for this configured model algorithm.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.training_container_config.metric_definit: Defines the metrics (e.g., loss, accuracy) to capture from the training container's logs by specifying a name and a regular expression pattern to extract each metric value.
Specifies the name of a metric to extract from the training container's output logs, enabling CloudWatch monitoring of that metric during model training.
The regular expression pattern used to extract the metric value from the training container logs for this metric definition.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.collaboration_identifier: The identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that contains this configured model algorithm association, used to scope the association to a specific collaboration environment.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.configured_model_algorithm_arn: The ARN of the configured model algorithm that this association links to the configured model.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.configured_model_algorithm_association_a: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the configured model algorithm association.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.description: The description field is an optional, user-defined text string that describes the configured model algorithm association, allowing you to identify its purpose or context within AWS Clean Rooms ML.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.membership_identifier: The unique identifier (UUID) of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that this configured model algorithm association is created within and scoped to.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.name: The name of the configured model algorithm association, which provides a required identifier for the association within AWS Clean Rooms ML.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.privacy_configuration: Defines the privacy policies for the configured model algorithm association, including the direct analysis privacy budget template and output configuration constraints that govern how query results are protected in the collaboration.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.privacy_configuration.policies.trained_m: Defines the policy for exporting trained models from the configured model algorithm association, specifying the allowed S3 destinations and any restrictions on where model artifacts may be written.
The list of file names that are allowed to be exported from the trained model when this trained model exports policy is applied in the privacy configuration.
Limits the maximum size of a trained model export allowed by the privacy policy, preventing the export of models larger than the specified threshold.
The maximum size, in bytes, allowed for a trained model export as part of the privacy configuration's trained model exports policy.
Specifies the privacy policy for trained model inference jobs on this configured model algorithm association, governing how inference job outputs are handled and where they may be sent.
Lists the AWS account IDs permitted to access the container logs produced during trained model inference jobs, as configured in the association's privacy policy.

The filter pattern defines a pattern (e.g., a CloudWatch Logs-style filter) used to select which container log lines are captured or recorded for trained model inference jobs under this privacy policy.

Defines the redaction settings applied to container logs from trained model inference jobs, ensuring sensitive data is removed before logs are stored or processed, as part of the privacy configuration for the configured model algorithm association.
Configures custom entities for log redaction in trained model inference jobs, defining the names and regular expression patterns used to redact sensitive data from container logs.

Specifies the list of custom data identifier patterns (regular expressions) used by the log redaction configuration to detect and redact sensitive custom entities in container logs from trained model inference jobs for this configured model algorithm association.
Specifies the list of sensitive data entity types that should be redacted from the container logs of trained model inference jobs in this configured model algorithm association.
Defines the maximum output size cap for trained model inference jobs, enforcing privacy constraints by limiting the volume of data that can be returned.
The unit of measurement for the maximum output size of a trained model inference job, with the only valid value being GB (gigabytes).
The numeric value of the maximum output size allowed for a trained model inference job, enforced by the privacy configuration's policy for the Clean Rooms ML configured model algorithm association.

Defines the trained models policy within the privacy configuration, specifying how trained models generated from the associated configured model algorithm can be accessed and used by collaboration members.

Defines the list of container log configurations (each specifying a CloudWatch Logs log group ARN and a log type) that are permitted for the trained model container as part of this algorithm association's privacy policy.
Defines the list of AWS account IDs permitted to access container logs for trained models, as part of the privacy configuration's trained models policy.

Specifies a pattern (likely a CloudWatch Logs filter pattern) applied to container logs of trained models to exclude sensitive information as part of the privacy configuration in the AWS Clean Rooms ML algorithm association.
Configures how sensitive data in the container logs of trained models is redacted, including the patterns to match and the redaction method to apply.
Specifies the list of custom data identifiers used by the custom entity configuration to redact matching sensitive data from the trained model's container logs.

Specifies the list of sensitive data entity types (e.g., personal identifiers) that are redacted from the container logs of the trained model, under the log redaction configuration of the privacy policy.

The noise level (HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW) that sets the amount of differential privacy noise added to container metrics for trained models, balancing privacy protection against metric utility in the Clean Rooms ML association.
Sets the maximum size limit for trained model artifacts in the privacy configuration, expressed as an object with a numeric size and a unit, to prevent overly large models from being exported.
The unit of measurement for the maximum size of a trained model artifact, such as MB or GB.
Specifies the numeric component of the maximum trained model artifact size, which the privacy configuration uses to limit the size of model outputs that can be shared.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.description: A user-provided free-form description of the training dataset in AWS Clean Rooms ML, used to annotate and identify the dataset's purpose or contents.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.name: The name of the training dataset, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Clean Rooms ML assumes to read your training data from the configured data source, granting the necessary permissions for dataset access.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.status: The current status of the training dataset (e.g., ACTIVE or INACTIVE), indicating whether it is available for use.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.tags.value: The value of a tag key attached to the AWS Clean Rooms ML Training Dataset, used to organize, identify, and manage the dataset through metadata labels.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.training_data: The list of training data configurations, each specifying a data source (such as a Glue table) and its column schema, that the Clean Rooms ML training dataset uses to define the input for model training.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.training_data.input_config: Specifies the input configuration for the training dataset, including the S3 data source location and the list of column names that make up the schema.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.training_data.input_config.data_source: Specifies the S3 location (URI) and type of the data source that provides the training input data for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.training_data.input_config.data_source.g: This object defines the AWS Glue table that supplies the training data for this Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
The AWS account ID of the Glue Data Catalog that contains the table used as the training data source for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
The name of the AWS Glue Data Catalog database containing the source table for the training dataset input.
The name of the AWS Glue table that contains the training data for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.training_data.input_config.schema: Defines the schema of the training data input by listing column objects, each specifying a column name and its data type for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.training_data.input_config.schema.column: Specifies the name of a column in the training data schema, which maps to a column in the configured data source for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
Specifies the data type (e.g., INTEGER, STRING) for each column in the training dataset schema, used by AWS Clean Rooms ML to interpret the input data.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.training_data.type: Defines whether the training data for this Clean Rooms ML training dataset is sourced from an Amazon S3 bucket or an AWS Glue table.
aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.training_dataset_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Clean Rooms ML training dataset.

aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the privacy budget template.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.auto_refresh: Indicates whether the privacy budget template automatically refreshes at the end of each allocation period, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.collaboration_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the collaboration that this privacy budget template is associated with, assigned by AWS when the template is created.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.collaboration_identifier: collaboration_identifier is the unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration to which this privacy budget template belongs, automatically assigned by AWS and used as a read-only part of the resource's identity.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.membership_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the membership that this privacy budget template belongs to, which is automatically assigned by AWS Clean Rooms.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.membership_identifier: The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that this privacy budget template is associated with.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.parameters: Defines the differential privacy parameters for the privacy budget template, specifically the epsilon value and the maximum number of aggregation queries allowed.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.parameters.budget_parameters.auto_refres: Indicates whether the privacy budget template automatically refreshes the privacy budget on a recurring schedule (e.g., daily or monthly) to renew the querying allowance without manual intervention.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.parameters.budget_parameters.budget: The maximum number of privacy budget units allocated to a parameter, determining how much aggregate data can be exposed while preserving differential privacy.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.parameters.budget_parameters.type: Defines the kind of privacy budget parameter (currently supported value: DIFFERENTIAL_PRIVACY) that determines how the analysis rule enforces differential privacy limits in the template.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.parameters.epsilon: Specifies the epsilon value for the differential privacy budget, which limits the amount of privacy loss allowed for queries using this template.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.parameters.users_noise_per_query: The number of users' worth of noise added to each query in the privacy budget template, controlling the level of differential privacy applied to query results.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.privacy_budget_template_identifier: The AWS-assigned unique identifier for this privacy budget template, used to reference the template in Clean Rooms operations.
aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template.privacy_budget_type: The privacy budget type, either 'DIRECT' or 'DIFFERENTIAL_PRIVACY', determines whether the template enforces a direct query budget or a differential-privacy-based budget with noise for members' queries in the collaboration.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Cloud9 EC2 development environment.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.automatic_stop_time_minutes: The number of minutes of inactivity after which AWS Cloud9 automatically stops the environment's EC2 instance, shutting down the environment when this time is reached.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.connection_type: Specifies whether AWS Cloud9 connects to the environment's Amazon EC2 instance via SSH (CONNECT_SSH, the default) or AWS Systems Manager (CONNECT_SSM).
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.description: An optional description that provides additional non-identifying context about the Cloud9 environment.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Cloud9 to the environment, such as 'env-1234567890abcdef0'.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.image_id: The image_id specifies the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID used to launch the Amazon EC2 instance that hosts the Cloud9 environment.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.instance_type: Specifies the EC2 instance type (e.g., t2.micro, m5.large) that the AWS Cloud9 environment runs on, determining the compute and memory resources available.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.name: Specifies the name of the Cloud9 development environment.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.owner_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the environment owner; if not specified, the environment is owned by the user who created it.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.repositories: A list of repositories to clone into the environment, each containing the repository URL and the path component where it should be cloned.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.repositories.path_component: The relative path component within the AWS Cloud9 environment where the source repository will be cloned, serving as the directory name for the repository.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.repositories.repository_url: The URL of the source code repository to clone into the Cloud9 environment when the environment is created.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.subnet_id: The ID of the subnet in which the Cloud9 environment's EC2 instance is launched, allowing the environment to reside in a specific VPC and network configuration.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.tags: Specifies a list of tag key-value pairs to associate with the Cloud9 EC2 environment.
aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.tags.value: Specifies the value for a tag key on the AWS Cloud9 EC2 environment, allowing you to add arbitrary metadata for identifying or organizing the environment.

aws_cloud_formation_custom_resource.service_timeout: The maximum amount of time (in seconds) that AWS CloudFormation waits for the custom resource provider to respond before considering the resource operation failed.
aws_cloud_formation_custom_resource.service_token: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Lambda function or Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) topic that implements the custom resource's provisioning logic.

aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.options: Specifies the Guard hook options, including the RuleStack property that gives the Amazon S3 location of the Guard rules file CloudFormation uses to apply policy validation.
aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.target_filters.actions: Specifies the list of stack operations (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE) for which the Guard hook is invoked on the targeted resources.
aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.target_filters.invocation_points: The invocation points of the target filter, which are the stack lifecycle events (such as BEFORE_CREATION or BEFORE_UPDATE) at which the Guard hook runs for the matched resources.
aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.target_filters.target_names: Specifies the list of AWS resource type names (for example, 'AWS::S3::Bucket') that this Guard hook evaluates for violations during CloudFormation operations.
aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.target_filters.targets: Defines the resource targets that the Guard hook applies to, using include and exclude patterns based on resource type and resource identifiers.
aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.target_filters.targets.action: Specifies whether the Guard hook should be invoked (INVOKE) or skipped (SKIP) for resources matching the target in this target filter.
aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.target_filters.targets.invocation_point: The invocation point for a target in the Guard hook's target filter, indicating which CloudFormation resource lifecycle event (CREATE, UPDATE, or DELETE) triggers the hook for that target.
aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.target_filters.targets.target_name: The name of a target resource type (for example, AWS::S3::Bucket) that this Guard hook filter matches so the hook is invoked only for resources of that type.

aws_cloud_formation_hook_version.logging_config: Configures the logging destination for the hook version, specifying the CloudWatch Logs log group and IAM role where the hook's execution logs are sent.

aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook.target_filters.actions: Specifies the list of CloudFormation change actions (e.g., Create, Update, Delete) that trigger the Lambda hook invocation.
aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook.target_filters.invocation_points: Specifies the list of CloudFormation hook invocation points (such as BEFORE_CREATE, BEFORE_UPDATE, BEFORE_DELETE) at which the Lambda hook is triggered for the matching target resources.
aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook.target_filters.target_names: Specifies the list of AWS resource type names (e.g., AWS::S3::Bucket) that this Lambda hook targets, controlling which resource types trigger the hook.
aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook.target_filters.targets: The list of target objects that define which CloudFormation resources this Lambda hook is triggered for, where each target specifies a resource type (e.g., AWS::S3::Bucket) and optionally a specific resource name to narrow the hook's scope.
aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook.target_filters.targets.action: Specifies the CloudFormation action (e.g., CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE) that triggers the Lambda hook for the targeted resource types.
aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook.target_filters.targets.invocation_point: Specifies the invocation timing relative to the targeted CloudFormation operation (e.g., `BEFORE` or `AFTER`), determining whether the Lambda hook runs before or after the action on the matched resources.
aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook.target_filters.targets.target_name: The name of the resource type (e.g., AWS::S3::Bucket) or logical resource ID that the CloudFormation Lambda hook's target filter matches, depending on whether the target type is RESOURCE_TYPE or RESOURCE_NAME.

aws_cloud_formation_macro.description: The description field provides a human-readable summary of the macro's purpose or transformation logic, aiding users in understanding what the macro does.
aws_cloud_formation_macro.function_name: Specifies the name of the AWS Lambda function that AWS CloudFormation invokes to process template snippets when the macro is executed.
aws_cloud_formation_macro.id: The macro's name, which serves as its unique identifier within CloudFormation.
aws_cloud_formation_macro.log_group_name: The Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group where the macro function's execution logs are delivered.
aws_cloud_formation_macro.log_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that CloudFormation assumes to send logs about the macro execution to the CloudWatch log group.
aws_cloud_formation_macro.name: Defines the name of the macro, used to reference it in CloudFormation templates and required to be unique within the account and region.

aws_cloud_formation_resource_version.logging_config: Specifies the logging configuration for the resource type, including the CloudWatch Logs log group name and the IAM role ARN used to deliver logs from the resource provider.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.capabilities: A list of capability values (e.g., CAPABILITY_IAM, CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM, CAPABILITY_AUTO_EXPAND) that the stack operation requires to acknowledge creation or modification of IAM resources or to expand macros.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.change_set_id: The unique ID of the change set that was last executed to create or update the stack, useful for tracking which changes were applied.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.creation_time: The timestamp indicating when the CloudFormation stack was created, typically in ISO 8601 format.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.description: Provides a freely formed text description for the AWS CloudFormation stack, which is passed to the AWS CloudFormation service and helps identify the stack's purpose.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.disable_rollback: Disables rollback of the stack if stack creation fails, allowing the stack to remain in a failed state for troubleshooting.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.enable_termination_protection: When set to true, enables termination protection on the CloudFormation stack, preventing the stack from being deleted until this setting is disabled.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.last_update_time: The timestamp of when the CloudFormation stack was last updated, provided as a string.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.notification_arns: The Amazon SNS topic ARNs to which CloudFormation sends stack event notifications, such as resource creation or deletion events.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs: A list of the CloudFormation stack's output entries, each containing a key and value from the Outputs section of the stack template, as returned by AWS.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs.description: The description of a CloudFormation stack output, as defined in the stack template, providing human-readable context for the output value.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs.export_name: The export name for a stack output, which makes the output value available to other CloudFormation stacks via Fn::ImportValue.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs.output_key: Specifies the name of an output exported by the AWS CloudFormation stack, used to identify the corresponding output value within the stack's list of outputs.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs.output_value: The actual value of a CloudFormation stack output, returned after the stack has been created or updated.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.parameters: A map of input parameters to pass to the CloudFormation stack, matching the Parameters declared in the stack's template.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.parent_id: The unique identifier of the parent CloudFormation stack that this stack is nested within, or an empty string if this is a root-level stack.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.role_arn: ARN of the IAM role that AWS CloudFormation assumes to create, update, or delete the stack's resources.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.root_id: The root stack ID of a CloudFormation stack, which is the unique identifier of the top-level stack that this stack belongs to (equal to the stack's own ID for a top-level stack).
aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_id: The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the CloudFormation stack by AWS when it is created.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_name: The name of the CloudFormation stack, which must be unique within an AWS region and is used to identify the stack in operations.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_policy_body: Specifies the JSON body of a stack policy, which defines permissions that protect stack resources from accidental updates or deletions during stack operations.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_policy_url: The URL to the stack policy file, which restricts updates to specific resources within the CloudFormation stack during a stack update.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_status: The current status of the CloudFormation stack as reported by AWS, such as CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_COMPLETE, or DELETE_COMPLETE, and is read-only since it is determined by the service.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_status_reason: The reason provided by AWS CloudFormation for the stack's current status, such as why a create, update, or delete operation failed.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.tags: Specifies the list of key-value tags to associate with the CloudFormation stack, which are used to identify, organize, and manage the stack, and which are propagated to tag-supporting resources created by the stack.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.tags.key: The tag key to associate with the CloudFormation stack, used to organize and identify the stack for cost allocation and management.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the CloudFormation stack, used for cost allocation, access control, and organizing stack resources.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.template_body: The CloudFormation template body, in JSON or YAML format, that defines the stack's resources and properties; you can use this instead of providing a template URL.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.template_url: The URL of a file (typically in Amazon S3) that contains the CloudFormation template body, used instead of inline template_body.
aws_cloud_formation_stack.timeout_in_minutes: The maximum number of minutes that CloudFormation allows for the stack creation to complete before the stack creation fails.

aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.auto_deployment: Enables automatic deployment of stack instances to accounts added to the target organizational units or accounts, and optionally retains the stacks when an account is removed from the target scope.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.operation_preferences.failure_tolerance_: Specifies the maximum number of accounts per Region in which stack instance creation, update, or deletion can fail before CloudFormation stops the stack set operation in that Region.
The percentage of total stack instances in the stack set that can fail during an operation before CloudFormation stops the operation and considers it failed.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.operation_preferences.max_concurrent_cou: Specifies the maximum number of stack instances that can be operated on concurrently during a stack set operation, as an absolute count rather than a percentage.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.operation_preferences.max_concurrent_per: Specifies the maximum percentage of accounts in the stack set that can be brought online or updated concurrently during stack operations, helping to limit the number of simultaneous deployments.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.operation_preferences.region_order: Specifies the custom order in which AWS Regions are traversed during stack set operations (create, update, or delete), controlling the sequence of stack instance deployments across those regions.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.parameters.parameter_key: The key of a parameter passed to the CloudFormation StackSet, which must match a parameter name declared in the stack template used by the StackSet.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.parameters.parameter_value: The value to assign to a specific parameter key when provisioning stacks within the CloudFormation StackSet.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.stack_instances_group.deployment_targets: DeploymentTargets specifies the target AWS accounts or Organizational Units (OUs) in AWS Organizations for stack instance deployment, including optional account list URL and account filter type.

Specifies how AWS CloudFormation filters accounts within an organization for stack set deployments: 'ALL' targets every account in the organization, while 'INTERSECTION' deploys only to accounts that appear in both the specified target accounts/OrganizationalUnitIds and the organization.
Specifies the list of AWS account IDs to which stack instances are deployed for this stack instances group in the StackSet.
The `accounts_url` field specifies a pre-signed Amazon S3 URL to a file containing a list of AWS account IDs that are the deployment targets for stack instances in the stack set group.
The list of organizational unit (OU) IDs in AWS Organizations to which the stack set deploys stack instances when using service-managed permissions.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.stack_instances_group.parameter_override: Provides the parameter values that override the stack set's default parameters for the stack instances in this group, enabling different configurations per account/region group.
The key of a parameter override applied to the stack instances in this group, replacing the default parameter value from the stack set's template.
The value to assign to a stack template parameter for the stack instances in this group, overriding the default parameter value defined in the StackSet template.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.stack_instances_group.regions: The list of AWS Regions in which to create stack instances for this stack set instance group.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the CloudFormation stack set, used to organize, identify, and manage the stack set via cost allocation tags and IAM policies.
aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.tags.value: The value of the tag to assign to the StackSet, used for cost allocation, access control, and identifying the StackSet in the AWS Management Console.

aws_cloud_formation_type_activation.logging_config: Specifies the Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group name and IAM role ARN used to deliver logs for the registered resource type.

aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition.count: The number of success signals that must be received by the CloudFormation wait condition before it is considered complete, matching the Count property of the associated CloudFormation WaitCondition.
aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition.data: The map of data returned by the signaled resource or application once the wait condition is fulfilled, providing the payload sent via the signal URL.
aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition.handle: The handle property is the pre-signed URL (from the associated WaitConditionHandle) that a signal is sent to, marking the wait as complete and allowing CloudFormation to finish creating this WaitCondition resource.
aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition.timeout: The number of seconds to wait for the required number of signals to arrive before the wait condition times out.

aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition_handl.id: The unique identifier for the wait condition handle, which is a pre-signed URL used by external signals to notify CloudFormation of completion.

aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_config_results: This field is the read-only list of IPAM CIDR configuration results for the CloudFront anycast IP list, reporting the allocated CIDR block and its allocation status for each specified IPAM configuration.
The anycast IP address allocated from the IPAM CIDR configuration for this CloudFront anycast IP list.
The CIDR block (e.g., '10.0.0.0/24') allocated from the IPAM pool for the anycast IP list, as reported in each IPAM CIDR configuration result.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IPAM pool associated with a CIDR configuration result for the CloudFront anycast IP list.
The lifecycle status of an individual IPAM CIDR allocation in the CloudFront anycast IP list, such as whether the CIDR is active and ready for use or still pending provisioning.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.etag: The entity tag (ETag) of the Anycast IP list, which is updated every time the list is modified and is used for conditional updates (e.g., If-Match requests).
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ip_address_type: Specifies whether the anycast IP list contains IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, determining which type of IPs can be included in the IpList property.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_config_results: This computed attribute returns a list of objects, each representing the IPAM CIDR configuration result for a CIDR block associated with this anycast IP list, including details such as the CIDR and its allocation status.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_config_results.anycast_ip: The anycast IP address allocated from the IPAM pool, returned as part of the per-CIDR configuration result for this CloudFront anycast IP list.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_config_results.cidr: The CIDR address range (e.g., 203.0.113.0/24) from an IPAM CIDR configuration result that is included in the CloudFront Anycast IP list's IP address inventory.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_config_results.ipam_pool_arn: The ARN of the IPAM pool from which the CIDR block for this anycast IP list configuration result is allocated.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_config_results.status: The provisioning status of each CIDR block returned in the IPAM configuration results for a CloudFront Anycast IP list, such as available, pending, or failed.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_configs: Specifies the IPAM pool CIDR allocations (each including an IPAM pool ID and netmask length) that define the IP address ranges CloudFront will advertise as anycast for this IP list.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_configs.cidr: The CIDR block, specified within an IPAM CIDR configuration, that determines the IP address range used for the CloudFront anycast IP list.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cidr_configs.ipam_pool_arn: The ARN of the IPAM pool that supplies the CIDR block for this anycast IP list configuration in CloudFront.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.tags.items.key: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the CloudFront Anycast IP list, providing a user-defined label for the tag's value.
aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.tags.items.value: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the CloudFront anycast IP list, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.

aws_cloud_front_cache_policy.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS CloudFront to this cache policy, used to reference it in distributions and other resources.
aws_cloud_front_cache_policy.last_modified_time: The timestamp (ISO 8601) of when the cache policy was last modified.

aws_cloud_front_cloud_front_origin_acces.id: The unique identifier assigned to the CloudFront origin access identity, which is used as the principal in S3 bucket policies and referenced in CloudFront distribution origin settings.
aws_cloud_front_cloud_front_origin_acces.s3_canonical_user_id: The canonical user ID associated with the CloudFront origin access identity, which you can use to grant the OAI permissions to access S3 objects via a bucket policy.

aws_cloud_front_connection_function.connection_function_config.key_value_sto: The ARN of the CloudFront key value store to associate with the function, granting the function read access to that store's data during invocation at the edge.
aws_cloud_front_connection_function.created_time: The date and time when the CloudFront function was created, as reported by AWS.
aws_cloud_front_connection_function.etag: Represents the current ETag version identifier of the CloudFront connection function, used for optimistic concurrency control during update/delete operations.
aws_cloud_front_connection_function.last_modified_time: The date and time when the CloudFront function was last modified, returned by the API and updated automatically whenever the function's code or configuration changes.

aws_cloud_front_continuous_deployment_po.continuous_deployment_policy_config.sing: The HTTP header name that CloudFront inspects to route requests to the staging distribution in this continuous deployment policy.
The header value that CloudFront uses to route requests to the staging distribution in the continuous deployment policy.
Specifies the percentage of traffic to route to the staging distribution, with a value between 0 and 100, where 100 sends all traffic to the staging distribution.
aws_cloud_front_continuous_deployment_po.id: The unique identifier that CloudFront assigns to the continuous deployment policy when it is created.
aws_cloud_front_continuous_deployment_po.last_modified_time: The date and time when the continuous deployment policy was last modified, returned as a string in ISO 8601 format.

aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.allo: The HTTP methods (e.g., GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE) that CloudFront processes and forwards to the origin for this cache behavior.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.cach: The ID of the cache policy attached to this CloudFront cache behavior, which determines the time-to-live (TTL) settings and which HTTP headers, cookies, or query strings are included in the cache key.
Specifies which HTTP methods (such as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE) CloudFront caches responses for in this cache behavior.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.comp: Indicates whether CloudFront automatically compresses files (such as HTML, CSS, or JavaScript) for this cache behavior when serving them to viewers.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.defa: Specifies the default time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for objects in the CloudFront cache for this cache behavior, controlling how long CloudFront retains an object before checking the origin for an updated version.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.fiel: The ID of the field-level encryption configuration to apply to responses that match this cache behavior, enabling protection of sensitive data fields.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.forw: Specifies which query strings, cookies, and headers are forwarded to the origin and included in the cache key for requests that match this cache behavior.
Specifies how CloudFront forwards cookies from viewer requests to the origin for this cache behavior, controlling whether all, none, or a specific whitelist of cookies are forwarded.
Specifies which cookies to forward to the origin for this cache behavior: 'all', 'none', or 'whitelist' (the latter requires listing cookie names in 'whitelistedNames').
A list of specific cookie names that CloudFront includes in the origin request when forwarding cookies for this cache behavior, used when the cookie forwarding policy is 'whitelist'.
Specifies the list of HTTP header names that CloudFront includes in viewer requests forwarded to the origin for this cache behavior, alongside the default headers.
Specifies whether CloudFront forwards query string parameters to the origin; set to true to forward them (and optionally cache based on them) or false to not forward them.

The list of query string parameter names (keys) to include in the cache key for this cache behavior, controlling which query strings are used to determine cache hits when QueryString forwarding is enabled.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.func: Associates CloudFront Functions with this cache behavior, specifying the function ARN and the event type (viewer-request or viewer-response) at which the function is invoked.
Specifies the CloudFront event type (such as viewer-request or viewer-response) that triggers the associated CloudFront Function for this cache behavior.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudFront function that is associated with the cache behavior to perform request and response manipulation.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.grpc: Specifies whether gRPC is enabled for this cache behavior.
Whether gRPC is enabled for this CloudFront cache behavior.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.lamb: Specifies the Lambda@Edge functions to invoke for a cache behavior, along with the CloudFront event type (such as viewer-request or origin-response) that triggers each function.
Specifies the CloudFront event that triggers the Lambda function, such as viewer-request, viewer-response, origin-request, or origin-response.
When true, includes the request body in the event passed to the associated Lambda function, allowing the function to inspect or modify the body for viewer-request or origin-request triggers.
The ARN of the Lambda function (Lambda@Edge) to associate with this cache behavior, which is invoked to process viewer or origin requests/responses for the specified path pattern.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.max_: The maximum time (in seconds) that objects are cached in CloudFront edge locations for this cache behavior, after which CloudFront will query the origin again regardless of the origin's Cache-Control headers.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.min_: Defines the minimum time in seconds that CloudFront retains objects in its cache for this cache behavior, ensuring that even if the origin provides a shorter Cache-Control max-age or Expires header, CloudFront still caches the object for at least this duration.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.orig: The unique identifier of the origin request policy attached to this cache behavior, which determines which headers, cookies, and query string parameters are forwarded from viewers to the origin.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.path: Specifies the URL path pattern (e.g., /images/*) that determines which requests this cache behavior applies to, routing matching requests to the behavior's origin and caching settings.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.real: Specifies the ARN of the real-time log configuration that determines which requests are logged in real time for this cache behavior.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.resp: Specifies the ID of the response headers policy that CloudFront attaches to HTTP responses for requests that match this cache behavior.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.smoo: Indicates whether to enable Smooth Streaming support for this cache behavior, allowing CloudFront to properly serve Microsoft Smooth Streaming media content such as manifests and fragments.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.targ: The ID of the origin (from the distribution's origins) to which requests matching this cache behavior are forwarded.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.trus: Specifies the list of key group IDs whose public keys can be used to verify signed URLs or signed cookies for this cache behavior.
Specifies the AWS account IDs (or 'self') of trusted signers that are allowed to create signed URLs or signed cookies for this cache behavior, enabling access to private content.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.cache_behaviors.view: Determines the protocol policy for viewer requests matched by this cache behavior, choosing between allowing HTTP and HTTPS ('allow-all'), enforcing HTTPS only ('https-only'), or redirecting HTTP to HTTPS ('redirect-to-https').
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.custom_error_respons: The minimum time (in seconds) that CloudFront caches the custom error response for a given error code before requesting the origin again, configured as part of each custom error response entry.
The HTTP status code (e.g., 400, 403, 404, 500) for which CloudFront should return the custom error response defined in this custom_error_responses block.
Sets the HTTP status code that CloudFront returns to the viewer for this custom error response, overriding the origin's status code.
The path to the custom error page that CloudFront returns for the corresponding error code in a custom error response.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.default_cache_behavi: Specifies the CloudFront event that triggers the associated function, such as `viewer-request` or `viewer-response`, for the default cache behavior.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudFront function to associate with the default cache behavior, executed on viewer request or viewer response events.
Specifies the CloudFront event that triggers the associated Lambda function, such as viewer-request, viewer-response, origin-request, or origin-response.
Indicates whether CloudFront includes the body of the request in the event payload sent to the Lambda function when the associated CloudFront event triggers.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function to associate with this cache behavior for Lambda@Edge processing.
Specifies the HTTP status codes that, when returned by the primary origin, trigger CloudFront to fail over to the secondary origin for the origin group.

Specifies the HTTP status codes (as an object containing a list of integer codes in `items` and a `quantity` count) that, when returned by the primary origin, trigger failover to the secondary origin for a CloudFront origin group.
The list of HTTP status codes from the primary origin that trigger CloudFront to fail over to the secondary origin in the origin group.
The number of HTTP status codes in the items list that trigger failover for the origin group when a response matches one of these codes.
A unique identifier for the origin group, used to reference the origin group when associating it with cache behaviors or in the origin groups' failover configuration.
Specifies the set of origins in this origin group, including the number of origins (Quantity) and the list of origin identifiers (Items) that CloudFront can fail over between.
Specifies the list of origin IDs that belong to this origin group, allowing CloudFront to perform failover between them based on the group's failover criteria.
The unique identifier of an origin that is a member of this origin group, referencing an origin in the distribution's Origin list to enable failover between origins.
The number of origins in the origin group; in CloudFront an origin group always consists of exactly two members (primary and secondary), so this quantity must be 2.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.connection_a: Specifies the number of times that CloudFront attempts to connect to the origin before giving up, accepting values from 1 to 3.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.connection_t: For a custom origin, this sets the connection timeout in seconds (1–10, default 3) that CloudFront allows for establishing a TCP connection to the origin server.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.custom_origi: Configuration for a custom origin (non-S3) that defines the ports, protocol policy, and SSL settings used when CloudFront communicates with the origin.
Specifies the HTTP port that CloudFront uses to connect to the origin server.
The HTTPS port that CloudFront uses to connect to the custom origin, defaulting to 443 if not specified.
Specifies the IP address type (IPv4, IPv6, or IPv4 and IPv6) that CloudFront uses when connecting to the custom origin.
Specifies the duration in seconds that CloudFront should keep an idle connection to the custom origin open, with a default of 5 seconds and a valid range of 1–60 seconds.
Configures mutual TLS (mTLS) for the custom origin by specifying the S3 bucket container and the ARN of the client certificate that CloudFront presents to the origin.
The ARN of the client certificate, stored in AWS Certificate Manager, that CloudFront presents to this custom origin when using mutual TLS (mTLS).

Specifies the protocol policy that CloudFront uses to fetch files from the custom origin, allowing either HTTP only, HTTPS only, or matching the viewer's protocol (values: http-only, https-only, match-viewer).

Specifies the read timeout in seconds that CloudFront waits for a reply from a custom origin server before timing out, applicable only to custom (non-S3) origins and typically ranging from 1 to 60 seconds.
Specifies the SSL/TLS protocols that CloudFront may use to establish a secure connection with the custom origin.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.domain_name: Specifies the DNS domain name of the origin server (e.g., an S3 bucket website endpoint or custom HTTP server) from which CloudFront fetches content for this origin in the distribution.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.id: The unique identifier for this origin within the distribution, used to reference it in cache behaviors and origin groups.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.origin_acces: The ID of the origin access control (OAC) that is associated with this origin, which CloudFront uses to securely access the origin (e.g., an S3 bucket).
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.origin_custo: Specifies custom headers that CloudFront includes in requests it sends to the origin for this origin configuration.
The name of a custom header that CloudFront adds to requests sent to the origin.
The value of the custom header that CloudFront adds to requests it sends to the origin.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.origin_path: Specifies the directory path that CloudFront automatically appends to the origin's domain name for all requests forwarded to that origin, allowing content to be served from a subdirectory on the origin server.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.origin_shiel: Specifies the Origin Shield settings for this origin, including whether it is enabled and the AWS Region for the Origin Shield, to help reduce the load on your origin by caching and consolidating requests.
Specifies whether Origin Shield is enabled for this origin, adding an additional caching layer that can reduce load on the origin and improve availability.
Specifies the AWS Region where the CloudFront Origin Shield is located, providing an additional caching layer that reduces the load on the origin by aggregating requests from edge locations.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.response_com: Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, that CloudFront waits for the origin to respond to a request before timing out (also known as the origin read timeout or response completion timeout).
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.s3_origin_co: Configures the S3 bucket origin settings for this origin, including the CloudFront origin access identity that CloudFront uses to access the bucket.

Specifies the CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) that CloudFront uses to access the S3 bucket, allowing you to restrict direct access to the bucket and only allow access through the distribution.
The number of seconds CloudFront waits for a response from the S3 origin, including the time to read the response headers, before timing out (allowed range 1-60, default 30).
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.origins.vpc_origin_c: Configures this origin to use a VPC origin (e.g., an Application Load Balancer or App Runner service) by specifying the VPC origin's ID and optionally the read and keepalive timeout durations.
The amount of time, in seconds, that CloudFront keeps an idle connection to the VPC origin alive before closing it, controlling connection reuse for the VPC origin configuration.
The amount of time (in seconds) that CloudFront waits for the VPC origin to respond to a request after it has been forwarded, before considering the request failed.
The AWS account ID that owns the VPC endpoint serving as the origin, required when the endpoint is in a different account than the distribution.
The identifier of the CloudFront VPC origin that this origin references, which points to a supported resource (such as an Application Load Balancer) inside a VPC.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.distribution_config.viewer_mtls_config.m: Specifies whether viewer mutual TLS (mTLS) is enabled or disabled, where 'enabled' requires viewer requests to present a valid client certificate from the associated trust store and 'disabled' turns off mTLS enforcement.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.domain_name: The CloudFront distribution's automatically assigned domain name (e.g., d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net) that clients use to access content served by the distribution.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS CloudFront to the distribution, used to reference the distribution in other resources and APIs.
aws_cloud_front_distribution.tags.key: The key of a key-value tag applied to the CloudFront distribution, used for organizing and identifying the AWS resource.

aws_cloud_front_distribution_tenant.created_time: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the CloudFront distribution was created.

aws_cloud_front_function.function_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudFront function, assigned by AWS upon creation.
aws_cloud_front_function.function_config.key_value_store_associat: The ARN of the CloudFront KeyValueStore to associate with this function, enabling the function to read data from the key value store at runtime.
aws_cloud_front_function.stage: The CloudFront function's stage, which is read-only and indicates whether the function is in the 'DEVELOPMENT' or 'LIVE' lifecycle stage as managed by AWS.
aws_cloud_front_function.tags.key: The tag key (e.g., 'environment') assigned to the CloudFront function for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_cloud_front_key_group.id: The unique identifier assigned to the key group by CloudFront.
aws_cloud_front_key_group.last_modified_time: The timestamp of the most recent change to this CloudFront key group's configuration, automatically set by AWS when the key group is created or updated.

aws_cloud_front_key_value_store.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudFront key value store.
aws_cloud_front_key_value_store.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this CloudFront KeyValueStore, used to reference the store in other resources such as CloudFront functions.
aws_cloud_front_key_value_store.status: The current status of the CloudFront KeyValueStore, such as CREATING or READY, indicating whether the store is ready for use.
aws_cloud_front_key_value_store.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the CloudFront key value store, used to identify the tag within the tag set.

aws_cloud_front_origin_access_control.id: The id is the unique CloudFront-assigned identifier for the origin access control, which is used when associating the OAC with a distribution's cache behavior.

aws_cloud_front_origin_request_policy.id: The unique identifier assigned by CloudFront to the origin request policy.
aws_cloud_front_origin_request_policy.last_modified_time: The date and time when the origin request policy was last modified.

aws_cloud_front_public_key.created_time: The date and time when the CloudFront public key was created.

aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudFront real-time log configuration.
aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config.end_points.kinesis_stream_config: This object specifies the configuration for the Amazon Kinesis Data Streams destination of a real-time log endpoint, including the stream's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and the IAM role ARN that CloudFront assumes to publish log records to the stream.
aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config.end_points.kinesis_stream_config.role_ar: The ARN of an IAM role that CloudFront assumes to send real-time log data to the associated Kinesis data stream.
aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config.end_points.kinesis_stream_config.stream_: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis data stream to which CloudFront delivers real-time log data.
aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config.end_points.stream_type: Specifies the streaming service type for a real-time log configuration endpoint, and the only supported value is 'Kinesis'.

aws_cloud_front_response_headers_policy.id: The unique identifier assigned by CloudFront to this response headers policy, used to reference the policy in distributions.
aws_cloud_front_response_headers_policy.last_modified_time: The date and time when the response headers policy was last modified, returned as an ISO 8601 string.
aws_cloud_front_response_headers_policy.response_headers_policy_config.custom_he: The name of the HTTP response header that CloudFront adds to responses when using this policy.

Controls whether CloudFront overrides the value of the matching response header returned by the origin with the value specified in this custom header item; when false, CloudFront adds the custom header only if the origin does not already return a header with that name.
The value to be sent in the custom HTTP response header that CloudFront adds to responses for this policy.
aws_cloud_front_response_headers_policy.response_headers_policy_config.remove_he: The name of an HTTP response header that CloudFront removes from the response when the response headers policy is applied to a distribution.

aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.domain_name: The domain name (such as d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net) that CloudFront assigns to the streaming distribution and that clients use to request content.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.id: The unique identifier assigned to the CloudFront streaming distribution by AWS, used as the distribution ID.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config: The required configuration object for the CloudFront streaming distribution, specifying the S3 origin, enabled flag, optional aliases, comment, logging settings, and trusted signers for RTMP streaming.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.aliases: List of alternate domain names (CNAMEs) that can be used to access the streaming distribution in addition to the default cloudfront.net domain name.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.comment: The required string comment that describes the CloudFront streaming distribution, which must be provided in the streaming distribution configuration.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.enabled: Determines whether the CloudFront streaming distribution is enabled to accept and serve viewer requests.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.logging: Configures access logging for the streaming distribution, specifying whether logging is enabled, the S3 bucket where logs are stored, and the log file prefix.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.logging.bu: The Amazon S3 bucket to which CloudFront delivers access logs for the streaming distribution.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.logging.en: Specifies whether CloudFront writes access logs for the streaming distribution to the S3 bucket named in the logging bucket property.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.logging.pr: This string specifies the prefix that CloudFront adds to the beginning of the access log file names for this streaming distribution when it writes logs to the configured Amazon S3 bucket.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.price_clas: Specifies the price class for the CloudFront streaming distribution, which determines the geographic set of edge locations used and the associated pricing tier (e.g., PriceClass_100, PriceClass_200, or PriceClass_All).
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.s3_origin: Specifies the S3 bucket (domain_name) and CloudFront origin access identity used to authorize access for the streaming distribution's origin.
The domain name of the S3 bucket that acts as the origin for the CloudFront streaming distribution, typically formatted as `<bucket-name>.s3.amazonaws.com`.
The CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) to associate with the S3 origin for the streaming distribution, which permits CloudFront to access private S3 content.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.streaming_distribution_config.trusted_si: Specifies the AWS account IDs (or 'self' for the owner account) that are permitted to create signed URLs for private content served by this CloudFront streaming distribution, including an Enabled flag indicating whether the trusted signer list is active.
Specifies the AWS account numbers of trusted signers (accounts with CloudFront key pairs) allowed to create signed URLs or signed cookies for this streaming distribution.

Indicates whether trusted signers are enabled for the streaming distribution, so that when true, the accounts in the AwsAccountNumbers list can create signed URLs, and when false, only the creating AWS account can create signed URLs.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.tags: Configures the list of tag objects (each with a Key and Value) that are attached to the CloudFront streaming distribution for organization, cost tracking, and access management.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.tags.key: A tag key used to assign a custom metadata label to the CloudFront streaming distribution for organization, cost allocation, or access control purposes.
aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.tags.value: The value portion of a tag applied to the CloudFront streaming distribution, allowing you to associate arbitrary metadata such as environment or cost center with the resource for tracking and management.

aws_cloud_front_trust_store.etag: The entity tag (ETag) that represents the current version of the CloudFront trust store, used for optimistic concurrency control so that you can detect and avoid conflicting updates.
aws_cloud_front_trust_store.id: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the CloudFront trust store, used to reference the trust store when attaching it to a CloudFront distribution.
aws_cloud_front_trust_store.last_modified_time: A read-only timestamp indicating the date and time when the AWS CloudFront trust store was last modified.
aws_cloud_front_trust_store.number_of_ca_certificates: The number of CA certificates currently contained in the CloudFront trust store.
aws_cloud_front_trust_store.tags.key: The key (name) of a user-defined tag applied to the CloudFront trust store, used to identify and categorize the resource for cost allocation and management.
aws_cloud_front_trust_store.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the CloudFront trust store, used for resource organization and metadata management.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.account_id: The account ID of the AWS account that owns the CloudFront VPC origin, automatically populated by CloudFront and read-only.
aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this CloudFront VPC origin, automatically generated by AWS upon creation and used to reference the origin in other AWS services and IAM policies.
aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.created_time: The date and time when the CloudFront VPC origin was created, returned as a read-only string.
aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the VPC origin, used to reference this origin when configuring CloudFront distributions.
aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.last_modified_time: The date and time when the CloudFront VPC origin was last modified.
aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.status: The current deployment status of the CloudFront VPC origin, such as 'InProgress' or 'Deployed', indicating whether the origin is fully provisioned and ready for use.
aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.tags.value: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the CloudFront VPC origin, used for metadata and resource organization.
aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.vpc_origin_endpoint_config.ip_address_ty: Specifies whether the CloudFront VPC origin endpoint uses IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, with allowed values 'IPv4' or 'IPv6'.

aws_cloud_trail_channel.destinations.location: The ARN of the destination resource (e.g., an event data store ARN) where the CloudTrail channel delivers events.
aws_cloud_trail_channel.destinations.type: Specifies the type of destination for the CloudTrail channel, which can be either `EVENT_DATA_STORE` (for a CloudTrail Lake event data store) or `AWS_SERVICE` (for an AWS service such as Amazon S3, CloudWatch Logs, or EventBridge).
aws_cloud_trail_channel.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the CloudTrail channel for identification and management.
aws_cloud_trail_channel.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the CloudTrail channel, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the channel resource.

aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.created_timestamp: The timestamp, in ISO 8601 format, indicating when the CloudTrail dashboard was created, as returned by the CloudTrail DescribeDashboard API.
aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.refresh_schedule.frequency: Defines the automatic refresh frequency for the CloudTrail dashboard, expressed as a unit-value pair (e.g., HOURS with a value of 6 for a six-hour refresh interval).
aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.tags: A list of tag objects (each containing a key and value) to attach to the CloudTrail dashboard, enabling resource identification, cost allocation, and AWS resource management.
aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the CloudTrail dashboard, used to assign custom metadata for identifying, organizing, and controlling access to the dashboard (e.g., via IAM conditions and cost allocation tags).
aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.updated_timestamp: The timestamp indicating when the CloudTrail dashboard was last updated.
aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.widgets.query_parameters: For each widget in an AWS CloudTrail dashboard, this list of strings supplies the query parameter values that are substituted into the widget's query to filter or scope the displayed data.
aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.widgets.query_statement: The SQL query statement that a widget in an AWS CloudTrail dashboard uses to fetch and display data from the CloudTrail event data store.
