aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.advanced_event_selectors.field_selectors: Defines the list of field selectors within an advanced event selector that specify conditions on event fields, such as eventCategory or eventName, to determine which events are delivered to the event data store.
Matches events where the selected field's value ends with any of the specified string suffixes, defining a condition in the CloudTrail event data store's advanced event selector.

For each field selector in a CloudTrail event data store's advanced event selector, `equals` specifies the list of exact values that the named event field must match for an event to be delivered to the data store.
The name of the event attribute (e.g., eventCategory, readOnly, resources.type) that the field selector evaluates to filter which events are ingested into the event data store.
For each advanced event selector field, this list of suffixes defines a `not endsWith` condition: an event matches only if the field's value does not end with any of the specified suffix strings.
Defines a list of values that, if any matches the event field specified by the adjacent field selector, will cause the event to be excluded from the CloudTrail event data store.

For an advanced event selector on an event data store, this list contains string prefixes; events whose corresponding field value begins with any listed prefix are excluded from matching the selector.
Specifies a list of string prefixes that the value of the selected event field must start with for an event to match this advanced event selector and be included in the event data store.
aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.advanced_event_selectors.name: Provides a friendly name for the advanced event selector, used to identify it when managing multiple selectors in the CloudTrail event data store.
aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.created_timestamp: The creation time of the CloudTrail event data store, reported by CloudFormation as a read-only timestamp string.
aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.tags: Specifies the list of tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the CloudTrail event data store, enabling cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.
aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag to assign to the CloudTrail event data store, which is a custom label used for identifying and organizing the resource.
aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the CloudTrail event data store, used to organize and identify the resource for governance and cost allocation purposes.
aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.updated_timestamp: The timestamp of the last update to the event data store, indicating when its configuration was most recently modified.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.advanced_event_selectors.field_selectors: In an advanced event selector, this list defines which fields (e.g., eventCategory, resources.type, readOnly) and their matching values (equality or prefix matching) determine the data events that CloudTrail logs.
Restricts the advanced event selector to match events where the value of the specified field ends with any of the provided suffix strings.
Specifies the exact values that the field must match for a CloudTrail event to be logged, so only events whose field value equals one of the strings in this list are processed by the trail.
Specifies the event field name to filter on within a CloudTrail advanced event selector field selector, such as 'eventCategory', 'eventName', or 'readOnly'.
Matches data events where the value of the specified field does not end with any of the strings in this list, used to filter which events are delivered to the trail.

For CloudTrail advanced event selectors, this list of strings specifies field values that the event attribute must NOT equal for the selector to match (e.g., if Field is 'eventName', events with any event name not in this list are matched).
Specifies a list of strings that the value of the selected event field must not start with, so that events are included when the field value does not begin with any of these strings.
In an AWS CloudTrail advanced event selector's field selector, this list of string values defines prefixes that the event field's value must start with for the selector to match the event.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.advanced_event_selectors.name: Defines a user-friendly name for an advanced event selector, such as 'Log all events', which helps identify the selector when managing trail event filtering settings.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.aggregation_configurations.event_categor: Specifies the event category (e.g., Management, Data, Insight, or NetworkActivity) that this aggregation configuration applies to for a CloudTrail trail delivering events to a CloudTrail Lake event data store.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudTrail trail, automatically assigned by AWS when the trail is created.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.data_resources: Specifies the S3 buckets or Lambda functions for which to record data events, where each data resource includes a resource type (e.g., AWS::S3::Object or AWS::Lambda::Function) and a list of ARNs or prefixes.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.data_resources.type: Specifies the AWS resource type (e.g., AWS::S3::Object or AWS::Lambda::Function) for which to log data events within the event selector.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.data_resources.values: Contains the list of ARNs (for example, S3 object or prefix ARNs in the form arn:aws:s3:::bucket/prefix, or Lambda function ARNs) that identify the specific data resources selected for the event selector.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.exclude_management_event: For the trail's event selectors, this list specifies the event sources (such as kms.amazonaws.com) whose management events are excluded from being recorded.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.include_management_event: Indicates whether the trail includes AWS management events (such as CreateTrail or DeleteTrail) for the account; when false, only data events are logged for the selector.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.read_write_type: Specifies whether the trail records read-only, write-only, or all events (Allowed values: All, ReadOnly, WriteOnly) for the resources matched by this event selector.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.insight_selectors.event_categories: Sets the list of event categories (either 'api' or 'insight') that control which CloudTrail Insights event types are captured for the trail, allowing you to log API activity insights and/or operational insights.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.insight_selectors.insight_type: The type of CloudTrail Insights event to log, either ApiCallRateInsight for unusual API call rate or ApiErrorRateInsight for unusual API error rate.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.sns_topic_arn: The read-only Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SNS topic that CloudTrail uses to deliver notifications about log file delivery, populated automatically when the trail is configured with an SNS topic.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to this CloudTrail trail, used to categorize and identify the trail among resource groups and for cost allocation.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.tags.value: The value of an individual tag assigned to the CloudTrail trail, used for metadata, classification, or access control.
aws_cloud_trail_trail.trail_name: Specifies the name of the CloudTrail trail; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name, and trail names must start with a letter and may contain only lowercase letters, numbers, periods, underscores, and dashes.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudWatch alarm.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.dimensions.name: The name (key) of a CloudWatch metric dimension that, along with its value, is used to identify a particular metric or metric context for the alarm.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.dimensions.value: The value for a CloudWatch alarm metric dimension, which combines with the dimension name to uniquely identify a specific metric for the alarm to monitor.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.evaluation_window.wall_clock_window: The wall_clock_window within the evaluation_window configures a calendar-based evaluation window for CloudWatch anomaly detection, specifying the timezone and start/end times for when the band is computed.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.account_id: The AWS account ID associated with a metric data query, used to retrieve metrics from another account in a cross-account CloudWatch alarm.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.expression: A math expression string (e.g., 'm1 + m2') that defines a computed metric used in the alarm, referencing other metric queries in the same metrics list.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.id: A unique identifier for the metric within the alarm's metric configuration, used to reference it in metric math expressions.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.label: The label is a human-friendly name assigned to a metric or expression in a CloudWatch alarm's metric data query, which is displayed in the CloudWatch console and can be used to identify the metric in alarm graphs.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat: Defines the specific CloudWatch metric and statistic to evaluate in this metric data query, including the metric's namespace, name, dimensions, period, and statistical aggregation (e.g., Average).
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.metric: The metric that this statistic is based on, identified by its namespace, metric name, and optional dimensions.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.metric.dimensions: Specifies the dimensions for the metric, each containing a name and value pair that uniquely identifies the metric within CloudWatch.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.metric.dimensions.na: The name of the dimension, which is the key that, together with the dimension value, identifies a specific metric dimension within the metric's dimensions.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.metric.dimensions.va: The value of the CloudWatch metric dimension, which combined with the dimension key uniquely identifies the metric's associated resource or scope.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.metric.metric_name: The name of the CloudWatch metric to monitor, such as CPUUtilization or StatusCheckFailed, which must match a published metric in the specified namespace.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.metric.namespace: The namespace of the CloudWatch metric, such as AWS/EC2, that identifies the service or application emitting the metric in the metric stat of a composite alarm.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.period: The length of time in seconds to aggregate the metric data for this alarm's metric statistic, defining the granularity of data points evaluated for the alarm.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.stat: The statistic to apply to the metric (for example, SampleCount, Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, or a percentile such as p99).
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_stat.unit: Specifies the unit of measure for the metric statistic (e.g., Count, Percent, Seconds, Bytes) that the alarm evaluates.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.period: The length of time, in seconds, used each time the specified metric is evaluated for the alarm (e.g., 60 for one-minute evaluation periods).
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.return_data: Determines whether the time series data for this metric data query is returned in the CloudWatch alarm's metric math expression, and when the alarm uses multiple metric queries, exactly one query must have return_data set to true (typically the metric that drives the alarm).
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag applied to the CloudWatch alarm, used to categorize and manage the alarm resource.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the CloudWatch alarm, used to categorize or identify the alarm for management and billing purposes.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm_mute_rule.tags.key: The key portion of a tag attached to the CloudWatch alarm mute rule, enabling you to categorize and filter the rule among your AWS resources.
aws_cloud_watch_alarm_mute_rule.tags.value: Specifies the value for a tag key on the CloudWatch alarm mute rule, allowing you to categorize or filter the rule in CloudWatch and AWS billing reports.

aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.configuration: The configuration settings for the anomaly detector, specifying metric characteristics such as the period and evaluation periods (and optionally periodic spacing) that control how the detection model analyzes the metric.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.configuration.excluded_time_ranges: Specifies the time ranges, defined by start and end times, during which CloudWatch Anomaly Detector will not perform anomaly detection on the associated metric(s).
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.configuration.excluded_time_ranges.end_t: Specifies the end time of the excluded time range, in ISO 8601 format, during which the anomaly detector ignores data.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.configuration.excluded_time_ranges.start: The start time (in ISO 8601 format) of a time range to exclude from anomaly detection model training, marking the beginning of a period when the detector will not use data for learning the normal pattern.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.configuration.metric_time_zone: Sets the IANA time zone (e.g., 'America/New_York') used by the anomaly detector to evaluate and display metric anomalies, overriding the default UTC.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.dimensions: A list of dimension key-value pairs that scope the anomaly detector to a specific metric, such as an instance ID or environment, and when omitted the detector applies to the metric without any dimensions.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.dimensions.name: The name of a dimension that, along with its value and other dimensions, uniquely identifies the CloudWatch metric for which this anomaly detector is configured.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.dimensions.value: The value of the dimension that, combined with the dimension name and metric name, identifies the specific metric for which the CloudWatch anomaly detector is configured.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.metric_characteristics: The metric_characteristics object specifies the period (in seconds) and timezone (e.g., 'UTC') used by the CloudWatch anomaly detector for evaluating the metric data.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.metric_characteristics.periodic_spikes: When true, indicates that the metric is expected to have periodic spikes, causing the anomaly detector to adjust its band to be more tolerant of those recurring spikes rather than treating them as anomalies.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.metric_math_anomaly_detector: Defines the metric math expression anomaly detector configuration, including the metric data queries and the period (in seconds) that CloudWatch Anomaly Detector uses to establish a baseline for detecting anomalous behavior.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.metric_math_anomaly_detector.metric_data: Specifies the list of metric data queries that define the metric math expression evaluated by this anomaly detector.
Specifies the AWS account ID containing the metric data for this query, enabling cross-account metric math within the anomaly detector's metric math expression.
The math expression (e.g., SUM(SEARCH('Namespace=...', 'Sum', 300))) that defines the metric data query used to calculate the anomaly detection band for the metric math anomaly detector.
A short name that uniquely identifies this metric data query within the anomaly detector's metric math expression, used to reference the query in the expression (e.g., 'm1' or 'e1').
A human-readable label for the metric or expression in the metric data query, which CloudWatch displays instead of the auto-generated label if provided.

Specifies the underlying metric and its statistic (e.g., Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, or percentile), along with the period and unit, for a metric data query used in the metric math expression of the anomaly detector.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric (including namespace, metric name, and dimensions) that the metric_stat for this metric data query uses to evaluate the anomaly detector.
Defines the dimensions (name-value pairs) for the target metric in the metric stat, which identify the metric in CloudWatch and scope the anomaly detection calculations.
The name of a CloudWatch metric dimension, which is the key in a key-value pair that identifies a specific attribute of the metric (e.g., 'InstanceId', 'LoadBalancerName').
Specifies the value of a CloudWatch metric dimension, which together with the dimension key and namespace uniquely identifies a metric used in the metric math anomaly detector's metric data query.
The name of the CloudWatch metric used in the metric stat for the metric math anomaly detector, identifying the specific metric to query.
Specifies the AWS namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2) of the metric referenced by the metric stat within the metric data query for this metric math anomaly detector.
The period specifies the length of time (in seconds) over which the metric data is aggregated for the metric stat used in the anomaly detector's metric math expression.
The statistic to apply to the metric (e.g., Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, SampleCount) within the metric data query used by the anomaly detector's metric math expression.
Specifies the unit of measure (e.g., Count, Percent, Seconds) for the metric statistic that contributes to the metric math expression used by this anomaly detector.
The time interval, in seconds, used to aggregate the metric data for the metric math expression that defines this anomaly detector.

Indicates whether the time series data for this metric data query should be returned in the anomaly detector's metric math evaluation, typically set to false for intermediate helper queries and true only for the final expression whose result is used for anomaly detection.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.metric_name: The name of the CloudWatch metric that the anomaly detector monitors, required when defining a single-metric anomaly detector.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.namespace: The CloudWatch namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2 or a custom namespace) that the anomaly detector applies to, identifying the metric's source.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.single_metric_anomaly_detector: Specifies the CloudWatch metric (namespace, metric name, dimensions, and stat) used to create an anomaly detection band for a single metric, as opposed to a metric math expression.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.single_metric_anomaly_detector.account_i: The 12-digit AWS account ID that owns the metric used by the anomaly detector, enabling cross-account anomaly detection.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.single_metric_anomaly_detector.dimension: Specifies the dimensions (name-value pairs) that define the metric for which this anomaly detector is created, used to identify the metric uniquely within the single metric anomaly detector.
The name (key) of a CloudWatch metric dimension that identifies the metric in the single-metric anomaly detector.
The value of a CloudWatch metric dimension, which together with its dimension name identifies a specific dimension for the metric used by the anomaly detector.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.single_metric_anomaly_detector.metric_na: The name of the CloudWatch metric to be monitored by this single metric anomaly detector.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.single_metric_anomaly_detector.namespace: The CloudWatch namespace of the metric to monitor with the anomaly detector, such as AWS/EC2 or a custom namespace.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.single_metric_anomaly_detector.stat: Specifies the CloudWatch statistic (such as Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, or SampleCount) applied to the metric in the single-metric anomaly detector configuration.
aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.stat: The statistic (e.g., Average, Sum, Maximum) of the CloudWatch metric that this anomaly detector applies to, specifying which metric statistic the anomaly detection model analyzes.

aws_cloud_watch_composite_alarm.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the CloudWatch composite alarm, used to identify, categorize, and manage the alarm in AWS.
aws_cloud_watch_composite_alarm.tags.value: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the CloudWatch Composite Alarm, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the alarm resource.

aws_cloud_watch_dashboard.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the CloudWatch dashboard, used to identify and categorize the dashboard for resource management and cost allocation.
aws_cloud_watch_dashboard.tags.value: Specifies the value for a tag key applied to the CloudWatch dashboard for resource organization and identification.

aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.apply_on_transformed_logs: When set to true, this boolean indicates that the Contributor Insights rule evaluates logs after they have been processed by a CloudWatch Logs transformation, rather than the original raw logs.
aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudWatch contributor insights rule.
aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.rule_body: The JSON rule definition for the Contributor Insights rule, specifying the log filter, aggregation, and metric settings.
aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.rule_name: The name of the Contributor Insights rule, which must be unique within your AWS account and is used to identify and reference the rule in CloudWatch.
aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.rule_state: Specifies whether the Contributor Insights rule is enabled or disabled, with valid values ENABLED and DISABLED, controlling whether the rule continuously collects and aggregates log data for the specified metrics.
aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.tags: A list of key-value tags to attach to the CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule, enabling you to categorize and manage the rule across your AWS environment.
aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule, used for resource categorization, cost allocation, and access management.

aws_cloud_watch_log_alarm.tags.value: The value associated with a tag key applied to the CloudWatch alarm, which aids in identifying, organizing, and managing AWS resources and costs.

aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.exclude_filters.metric_names: The list of metric names within the specified namespace to exclude from the metric stream.
aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.exclude_filters.namespace: Defines the CloudWatch namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2) whose metrics are excluded from the metric stream when matched by this exclusion filter.
aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.include_filters.metric_names: The names of the metrics in the specified namespace to include in the metric stream; if omitted, all metrics in the namespace are included.
aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.include_filters.namespace: The namespace of the AWS service whose metrics must match this filter for them to be included in the metric stream (e.g., AWS/EC2).
aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.statistics_configurations.additional_sta: Specifies additional statistics (such as percentiles like p99) to include in the metric stream for metrics that match the namespace and metric name of this statistics configuration.
aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.statistics_configurations.include_metric: Specifies the list of metrics (namespace and metric name) to which the corresponding statistics configuration's allowed statistics apply, controlling which metric streams include the configured statistics.
The name of the CloudWatch metric for which the specified additional statistics are included in the metric stream.

The name of the AWS service or custom application namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2, AWS/Lambda) whose metrics are included in this statistics configuration, filtering which metric namespaces are sent to the stream.
aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the CloudWatch metric stream, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_code_artifact_domain.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to an AWS CodeArtifact domain, enabling custom metadata for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.
aws_code_artifact_domain.tags.value: The free-form value of a user-defined tag attached to an AWS CodeArtifact domain, used to add custom metadata for organizing and managing the domain.

aws_code_artifact_package_group.origin_configuration: Configures the origin restrictions for the package group, controlling whether package versions can be published directly or pulled from upstream repositories.
aws_code_artifact_package_group.origin_configuration.restrictions: Specifies the publishing and access restrictions for external and upstream origins to control how package versions are added or read within this package group.
aws_code_artifact_package_group.origin_configuration.restrictions.extern: Specifies the restriction mode (ALLOW or BLOCK) for whether package versions in this package group can be obtained from external upstream repositories, governing the origin of packages pulled into the repository.
Specifies the list of external upstream repository names to which the restriction mode (e.g., ALLOW or BLOCK) for 'external_upstream' applies in the package group's origin configuration.

This required string specifies the restriction mode for external upstream repositories (e.g., public registries) in the package group's origin configuration, with allowed values such as ALLOW, BLOCK, or ALLOW_SPECIFIC_REPOSITORIES.
aws_code_artifact_package_group.origin_configuration.restrictions.intern: Specifies the origin restriction settings for internal upstream repositories, controlling whether package versions can be pulled from other CodeArtifact repositories in the same domain via the `pull` mode (with allowed values `ALLOW`, `BLOCK`, or `ALLOW_OR_BLOCK`).

Specifies a list of CodeArtifact repository names that are allowed as internal upstream sources for this package group when the internal upstream restriction mode is set to ALLOW_SPECIFIC_REPOSITORIES.

Determines whether packages in this package group can be sourced from internal upstream repositories (upstream repositories within the same AWS CodeArtifact domain), with allowed values ALLOW, BLOCK, or ALLOW_SPECIFIC_REPOSITORIES to permit only specific repositories.
aws_code_artifact_package_group.origin_configuration.restrictions.publis: Configures the restriction mode for publishing package versions to this package group, controlling whether new package versions can be published directly to the repository associated with this group.
A list of repository ARNs that are allowed to publish packages to this package group when the publish restriction is set to ALLOW_SPECIFIC_REPOSITORIES in the origin configuration.
Controls the publish restriction mode for the package group, where ALLOW permits publishing, BLOCK denies all publishing, and READ_ONLY permits reading package metadata but blocks publishing.

aws_code_artifact_repository.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AWS CodeArtifact repository, used to organize and identify the resource.
aws_code_artifact_repository.tags.value: The value of a tag (key-value pair) applied to an AWS CodeArtifact repository, used to add metadata for organization and cost allocation.

aws_code_build_fleet.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CodeBuild fleet.
aws_code_build_fleet.base_capacity: The initial number of compute instances allocated to the CodeBuild fleet, serving as the baseline from which the fleet scales toward its maximum capacity.
aws_code_build_fleet.compute_configuration: Specifies the compute configuration for the CodeBuild fleet, including the disk size and machine type (e.g., General or ARM) used for build environments.
aws_code_build_fleet.compute_configuration.disk: Specifies the amount of disk space (in GB) allocated to each compute instance in the code build fleet.
aws_code_build_fleet.compute_configuration.instance_type: Specifies the EC2 instance type used by the compute fleet's compute configuration, such as m5.large or c5.xlarge, determining the underlying hardware for the build fleet.
aws_code_build_fleet.compute_configuration.machine_type: The machine type of the CodeBuild fleet's compute configuration, which determines the processor architecture or GPU availability (e.g., GENERAL, ARM, GPU).
aws_code_build_fleet.compute_configuration.memory: Defines the amount of memory allocated to each compute instance in an AWS CodeBuild fleet's compute configuration.
aws_code_build_fleet.compute_configuration.v_cpu: The number of virtual CPUs (vCPUs) to allocate to each compute instance in the CodeBuild fleet.
aws_code_build_fleet.compute_type: The compute type for the fleet's build instances, such as BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL or BUILD_GENERAL1_LARGE, which determines the CPU and memory allocated to each build.
aws_code_build_fleet.environment_type: The type of compute environment (e.g., LINUX_CONTAINER, WINDOWS_CONTAINER, ARM_CONTAINER) that the CodeBuild fleet uses for its build instances.
aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_proxy_configuration: Specifies the proxy configuration for a CodeBuild fleet, including the default proxy address and HTTP/HTTPS proxy ports used to route outbound traffic from the fleet's compute instances.
aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_proxy_configuration.default_behavi: Determines the default action (ALLOW_ALL or DENY_ALL) the proxy takes for traffic that does not match any ordered proxy rules.
aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_proxy_configuration.ordered_proxy_: Defines the ordered list of proxy rules (each specifying an app, domain, or IP type and a value) that control network access for the CodeBuild fleet's build environments, evaluated in the order listed.
The effect of the proxy rule, either ALLOW or DENY, determines whether traffic matching the specified entities and type is allowed or blocked.
The list of domain names or IP addresses that this ordered proxy rule matches for the CodeBuild fleet's proxy configuration.
Indicates whether the entities in this proxy rule are interpreted as URL patterns (e.g., 'URL') or as hostnames (e.g., 'HOST'), which controls how outbound traffic filtering is applied.
aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_service_role: The ARN of the IAM service role that the AWS CodeBuild fleet assumes to access necessary AWS resources such as source code repositories and build artifact storage.
aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_vpc_config: Specifies the VPC, subnets, and security group IDs that the CodeBuild fleet's compute instances use for network access.
aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_vpc_config.security_group_ids: The security group IDs that AWS CodeBuild uses to control traffic to and from the network interfaces (ENIs) that the fleet launches in the specified VPC.
aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_vpc_config.subnets: Specifies the subnet IDs in the VPC where the CodeBuild fleet's compute instances run.
aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_vpc_config.vpc_id: The ID of the VPC in which the CodeBuild fleet's compute resources are deployed.
aws_code_build_fleet.image_id: Specifies the container image (e.g., a managed CodeBuild image or a custom Docker image from Amazon ECR) that the fleet uses for its build environments.
aws_code_build_fleet.name: The name of the CodeBuild fleet, which serves as its identifier and is optional; if not provided, CloudFormation generates a unique name.
aws_code_build_fleet.overflow_behavior: Determines how builds are handled when the fleet's capacity is exhausted, either queuing them (QUEUE) or routing them to on-demand capacity (ON_DEMAND).
aws_code_build_fleet.scaling_configuration: Configures auto-scaling for the compute fleet by specifying minimum and maximum capacity and an optional target-tracking scaling policy that adjusts fleet size based on demand.
aws_code_build_fleet.scaling_configuration.max_capacity: The maximum number of compute instances that the CodeBuild fleet can scale out to.
aws_code_build_fleet.scaling_configuration.scaling_type: Determines the scaling strategy for the CodeBuild compute fleet, either TARGET_TRACKING_SCALING for dynamic auto-scaling or PAY_PER_REQUEST for on-demand capacity provisioning.
aws_code_build_fleet.scaling_configuration.target_tracking_sc: Specifies a list of target tracking scaling policies that automatically adjust the CodeBuild fleet's compute capacity to maintain a target value for a metric such as CPU or memory utilization.
Specifies the fleet utilization metric type (e.g., FLEET_UTILIZATION_RATE) that the target tracking scaling policy uses to determine when to adjust fleet capacity.
This field defines the target value for the target tracking scaling policy, which is the metric threshold (e.g., a percentage for CPU utilization) that triggers scaling of the CodeBuild fleet.
aws_code_build_fleet.tags: Assigns metadata as key-value pairs (tag key and tag value) to the CodeBuild fleet, enabling cost tracking, access control, and resource categorization.
aws_code_build_fleet.tags.key: The key portion of a tag attached to the CodeBuild fleet, used to categorize and filter the resource for management and cost tracking.
aws_code_build_fleet.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS CodeBuild fleet, used to categorize and manage the fleet resource.

aws_code_build_project.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts: Defines where CodeBuild stores the build output, including artifact type (e.g., S3), location, path, packaging, and optional encryption settings.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.artifact_identifier: Specifies an identifier for this output artifact so it can be matched against the artifact outputs declared in the project's buildspec when a build produces multiple artifact sets.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.encryption_disabled: Indicates whether encryption for the build output artifacts is disabled, allowing artifacts to be stored in S3 without server-side encryption.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.location: Specifies the name of the S3 bucket where CodeBuild stores build output artifacts when the artifact type is set to S3.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.name: The name of the build output artifact, which for S3 artifact type is the file name that CodeBuild writes to the output bucket.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.namespace_type: Determines whether the build output artifacts are stored in a path that includes the build ID (as a subdirectory) or without it, affecting the S3 key structure for the artifact location.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.override_artifact_name: When true, the name of the build output artifact is overridden by the artifact name specified in the buildspec (e.g., via the `name` property of the buildspec's `artifacts` section); otherwise, CodeBuild uses the project name and build ID as the artifact name.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.packaging: Determines whether the build output artifacts are packaged into a ZIP archive (ZIP) or left as raw files (NONE) when uploaded to the artifact repository, such as an S3 bucket.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.path: The path within the S3 bucket where the build output artifact is stored, relative to the bucket root; if omitted, the artifact is placed at the bucket root.
aws_code_build_project.artifacts.type: Specifies the type of build output artifact, which can be set to CODEPIPELINE to have CodePipeline manage the artifact, S3 to store the output in an S3 bucket, or NO_ARTIFACTS to not generate an artifact.
aws_code_build_project.auto_retry_limit: Sets the maximum number of times CodeBuild automatically retries a failed build as part of the project's batch build configuration.
aws_code_build_project.badge_enabled: Indicates whether the CodeBuild project has a build badge enabled, which provides an embeddable URL for showing the build's status in an external repository.
aws_code_build_project.build_batch_config: Configures the batch build settings for the AWS CodeBuild project, including the service role, timeout, maximum number of builds, and restrictions for running builds in a batch.
aws_code_build_project.build_batch_config.batch_report_mode: Specifies how AWS CodeBuild generates test reports for batch builds, either as a single aggregated report for the entire batch or as separate reports for each individual build.
aws_code_build_project.build_batch_config.combine_artifacts: Whether to combine all build artifacts from the batch into a single artifact location.
aws_code_build_project.build_batch_config.restrictions: Specifies the restrictions for a batch build, including the maximum number of builds that can run concurrently and the compute types allowed for the batch build.
aws_code_build_project.build_batch_config.restrictions.compute_: Restricts the batch build to only use the compute types (e.g., BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL, BUILD_GENERAL1_MEDIUM) listed here for its individual builds; if the list is empty, all compute types are allowed.
aws_code_build_project.build_batch_config.restrictions.maximum_: Specifies the maximum number of builds that can be executed concurrently in a batch build for this CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.build_batch_config.service_role: Specifies the ARN of the IAM service role that AWS CodeBuild assumes to run batch builds for this project.
aws_code_build_project.build_batch_config.timeout_in_mins: The number of minutes after which a batch build is considered expired and is cancelled.
aws_code_build_project.cache: Configures the build cache for the CodeBuild project, allowing specification of either an S3 bucket for caching or a local cache with cache modes such as LOCAL_SOURCE_CACHE, LOCAL_CUSTOM_CACHE, and LOCAL_DOCKER_LAYER_CACHE.
aws_code_build_project.cache.cache_namespace: The cache namespace groups build output cache entries so that multiple build projects sharing the same namespace can reuse the same cache.
aws_code_build_project.cache.location: The S3 bucket path (e.g., 'bucket-name/path') where CodeBuild stores the cache when the cache type is S3.
aws_code_build_project.cache.modes: Specifies the local cache modes (e.g., LOCAL_SOURCE_CACHE, LOCAL_DOCKER_LAYER_CACHE, LOCAL_CUSTOM_CACHE) to enable for the build project when using a local cache type.
aws_code_build_project.cache.type: The type of cache to use for the build project, such as NO_CACHE, S3, or LOCAL, which determines how build outputs and dependencies are cached.
aws_code_build_project.concurrent_build_limit: Maximum number of concurrent builds that can run for this CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.description: A short, optional description of the CodeBuild build project.
aws_code_build_project.encryption_key: The ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) that CodeBuild uses to encrypt the build output artifacts; if not specified, the default AWS-managed key for Amazon S3 is used.
aws_code_build_project.environment: Specifies the build environment, including the compute type, container image, environment variables, and whether to use privileged mode for the CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.environment.certificate: The ARN of an AWS Certificate Manager certificate that AWS CodeBuild associates with the project's build environment to support cryptographic operations such as signing build artifacts.
aws_code_build_project.environment.compute_type: Specifies the compute resources for the build environment (for example, BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL or BUILD_GENERAL1_LARGE), determining the CPU and memory allocated to the build job.
aws_code_build_project.environment.docker_server.security_group: The list of security group IDs to associate with the Docker server used by the CodeBuild build environment, controlling network access to the Docker server.
aws_code_build_project.environment.environment_variables: Defines custom environment variables passed to the build container, each specifying a name, value, and optional type such as PLAINTEXT, PARAMETER_STORE, or SECRETS_MANAGER.
aws_code_build_project.environment.environment_variables.name: The name of the environment variable to be set in the CodeBuild environment, used as the key to reference the variable in build commands.
aws_code_build_project.environment.environment_variables.type: The type of the environment variable, which can be PLAINTEXT, PARAMETER_STORE, or SECRETS_MANAGER, determining how the variable's value is interpreted and retrieved.
aws_code_build_project.environment.environment_variables.value: Specifies the value of the environment variable that is injected into the CodeBuild container at build time, which can be a plain string or, when the variable's type is PARAMETER_STORE, the name of a Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter whose value is resolved at runtime.
aws_code_build_project.environment.fleet: Specifies the compute fleet (via its ARN) that provides the compute resources for this CodeBuild project environment.
aws_code_build_project.environment.fleet.fleet_arn: The ARN of the compute fleet to use for the build environment, enabling the build project to run on a specific managed or reserved capacity fleet.
aws_code_build_project.environment.image: The Docker image identifier (such as aws/codebuild/standard:5.0) that specifies the build environment for the CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.environment.image_pull_credentials_type: Controls whether CodeBuild uses the build project's Docker credentials (CODEBUILD) or the service role (SERVICE_ROLE) to authenticate when pulling a private container image.
aws_code_build_project.environment.privileged_mode: Enables running the build in privileged mode, which is required when building Docker images or using Docker-in-Docker inside the CodeBuild environment.
aws_code_build_project.environment.registry_credential: Specifies the credentials, typically from AWS Secrets Manager, used to access a private Docker registry for the CodeBuild build environment.
aws_code_build_project.environment.registry_credential.credenti: The ARN or name of the credentials (such as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager) used to authenticate to a private Docker registry or other container image registry.
Specifies the service responsible for creating the registry credential, which must be set to SECRETS_MANAGER for AWS CodeBuild to retrieve the login credentials.
aws_code_build_project.environment.type: Specifies the type of build environment for the CodeBuild project, such as LINUX_CONTAINER, WINDOWS_CONTAINER, or ARM_CONTAINER.
aws_code_build_project.file_system_locations: Specifies the file system locations (such as Amazon EFS mount points) to mount to the build container during a build.
aws_code_build_project.file_system_locations.identifier: In an AWS CodeBuild project's file system location configuration, the identifier is a user-defined logical name that uniquely identifies the file system mount, used to reference and distinguish it among multiple file system locations.
aws_code_build_project.file_system_locations.location: The DNS name or path that identifies the file system to be mounted into the CodeBuild build environment, such as an Amazon EFS file system's DNS name (e.g., fs-12345678.efs.us-west-2.amazonaws.com).
aws_code_build_project.file_system_locations.mount_options: Defines the mount options (for example, NFS options such as nfsvers, rsize, wsize, hard, timeo, and retrans) that are used when mounting the file system in the CodeBuild environment.
aws_code_build_project.file_system_locations.mount_point: Mount point is the directory inside the CodeBuild container where the specified file system (e.g., Amazon EFS) is mounted, such as `/efs`.
aws_code_build_project.file_system_locations.type: Indicates the type of file system mounted in the CodeBuild project, which must be 'EFS' for an Amazon Elastic File System mount.
aws_code_build_project.id: The unique identifier for the AWS CodeBuild project, which is the project name as assigned when the project is created.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config: Configures log output for the build project, specifying CloudWatch Logs and/or S3 log settings such as status, group/stream names, path, and encryption key.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config.cloud_watch_logs: Defines the CloudWatch Logs settings for the build project's logs, including the status (enabled/disabled), the log group name, the stream name, and whether encryption using the default AWS-managed CMK is disabled.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config.cloud_watch_logs.group_name: The name of the CloudWatch Logs group to which CodeBuild publishes build logs.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config.cloud_watch_logs.status: Indicates whether CloudWatch Logs are enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for storing the build project's logs.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config.cloud_watch_logs.stream_name: Specifies the name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream where the CodeBuild project's build logs are delivered, overriding the default build-ID-based stream name.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config.s3_logs: Defines how build logs are delivered to an S3 bucket, including the S3 bucket location and path, whether S3 logging is enabled, and whether encryption is disabled.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config.s3_logs.encryption_disabled: Indicates whether S3 build logs are encrypted; when set to true, the logs are stored unencrypted, whereas the default (false or omitted) enables encryption.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config.s3_logs.location: The ARN of the S3 bucket (and optional path prefix) where CodeBuild stores build logs when S3 logging is enabled.
aws_code_build_project.logs_config.s3_logs.status: Indicates whether S3 logging is enabled for the build project, with valid values being ENABLED or DISABLED.
aws_code_build_project.name: Specifies a unique, user-defined name for the CodeBuild build project, which cannot be changed after creation; if omitted, CloudFormation automatically generates a unique name.
aws_code_build_project.queued_timeout_in_minutes: Specifies the number of minutes a build can remain in the QUEUED state before CodeBuild times it out, after which the build is marked as failed.
aws_code_build_project.resource_access_role: The ARN of an IAM role that AWS CodeBuild assumes to access and manage resources in the VPC configured for the project, such as creating network interfaces.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts: Specifies a list of additional build output artifacts (in addition to the primary artifact) that CodeBuild can produce, each configured with settings like type, location, path, namespace, packaging, and encryption.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.artifact_identifier: A string that uniquely identifies this secondary artifact within the build project, used to reference it in build commands and to distinguish it from other secondary artifacts.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.encryption_disabled: If set to true, the secondary build output artifact is stored unencrypted in S3, otherwise it is encrypted, typically using an AWS-managed or customer-managed KMS key.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.location: Specifies the S3 bucket name (or the image/container path for other artifact types) where the secondary build artifacts are output.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.name: The unique name for this secondary artifact, which must be distinct from other secondary artifact names in the project and is used to identify the artifact in build output.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.namespace_type: Controls the directory structure of the secondary artifact in the output location, where the namespaceType value (NONE, BUILD_ID, or TIMESTAMP) determines whether the build ID or timestamp is included in the artifact path.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.override_artifact_na: For secondary artifacts in an AWS CodeBuild project, setting this boolean to true overrides the default output artifact name with the value specified in the artifact's Name property, while false (or unset) lets the build spec determine the name.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.packaging: Whether the build output artifact is packaged as a single ZIP file (ZIP) or left as-is without compression (NONE).
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.path: Specifies the directory path within the output S3 bucket where the build output for this secondary artifact is stored, with the final object key also influenced by the artifact's namespace type and name.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifacts.type: Specifies the type of the secondary artifact, such as S3 to store output in an S3 bucket or CODEPIPELINE to deliver it to AWS CodePipeline.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_source_versions: Specifies the source version (e.g., branch, tag, or commit ID) for each secondary source associated with the project, enabling the build to pull a specific revision of each additional repository.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_source_versions.source_identif: Specifies the identifier of the secondary source (as defined in the project's secondary sources) that this particular source version applies to.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_source_versions.source_version: Specifies the version (such as a Git commit ID, branch name, or tag) of the secondary source that CodeBuild uses for the build, identified by the associated source identifier in the project's secondary source versions list.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources: Specifies a list of additional source repositories (such as GitHub, Bitbucket, S3, or CodeCommit) that CodeBuild uses for the build project, in addition to the primary source.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.auth: Specifies the authentication method for a Git-based secondary source (GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, or Bitbucket), including the authorization type (e.g., OAUTH or PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN) and the optional ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the credentials.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.auth.resource: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the OAuth token or personal access token used to authenticate to the secondary source repository.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.auth.type: Specifies the authentication type (e.g., OAUTH) used by CodeBuild to access the secondary source repository, as defined in the source's auth settings.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.build_spec: Specifies the buildspec file path or inline buildspec YAML/JSON content for this secondary source, allowing it to override the project-level buildspec for that source.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.build_status_config: Specifies the context and target URL used for reporting the build status of this secondary source to the source repository provider.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.build_status_config.co: The context string that identifies the build status entry for this secondary source in the repository's commit status (for example, a custom label displayed in GitHub or Bitbucket).
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.build_status_config.ta: Specifies the URL of the repository that contains the source code, which is used as the target link for the build status report for this secondary source.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.git_clone_depth: The number of commits to include in the Git clone for the secondary source, where a lower value speeds up the clone by fetching only the most recent commits.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.git_submodules_config: Specifies whether git submodules are fetched for the secondary source repository in an AWS CodeBuild project.
Determines whether Git submodules are fetched for the associated secondary source repository in the AWS CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.insecure_ssl: Indicates whether the connection to the source repository is allowed to use insecure SSL (e.g., ignoring self-signed certificate errors).
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.location: Specifies the repository URL or source location (such as an S3 bucket path, GitHub repository, or Bitbucket) for the secondary source of the CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.report_build_status: For each secondary source, report_build_status controls whether CodeBuild reports build status information back to the source provider, which is only meaningful when that secondary source's type is GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, or Bitbucket.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.source_identifier: The identifier that uniquely identifies this secondary source among all sources in the CodeBuild project, and is used to construct the environment variable names (e.g., `CODEBUILD_SOURCE_DIR_<identifier>`) that buildspec commands can use to reference the source's directory and version.
aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.type: Defines the source provider type for this secondary source, such as CODECOMMIT, S3, BITBUCKET, GITHUB, or GITHUB_ENTERPRISE.
aws_code_build_project.service_role: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS CodeBuild assumes to perform the build, granting permissions for actions like fetching source code, publishing artifacts, and writing logs.
aws_code_build_project.source: Defines the source code repository for the build, including the repository type (e.g., S3, CodeCommit, GitHub, Bitbucket) and its location, along with optional settings like buildspec file path and git clone depth.
aws_code_build_project.source.auth: Specifies the authorization configuration for the source code repository, including the authentication type (such as OAuth) and optional resource ARN, enabling AWS CodeBuild to access the source.
aws_code_build_project.source.auth.resource: The resource field specifies the endpoint URL of the source provider (such as a GitHub Enterprise Server) when the auth type is PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, and is not used for OAuth-based authorization.
aws_code_build_project.source.auth.type: Specifies the authentication method to use when accessing the source repository, such as OAUTH, BASIC_AUTH, PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, or CODECONNECTIONS.
aws_code_build_project.source.build_spec: The build specification for the build project, either the name of a buildspec file or an inline YAML/JSON string that defines the build commands.
aws_code_build_project.source.build_status_config: Determines how CodeBuild reports the build status back to the source provider (e.g., GitHub, Bitbucket, or CodeCommit) by setting the status context and a custom target URL for the status update.
aws_code_build_project.source.build_status_config.context: The identifier string for the build status update, used to distinguish this build status from others in the source provider (such as a GitHub commit status context label).
aws_code_build_project.source.build_status_config.target_url: Specifies the URL that AWS CodeBuild sends as the target link when reporting build status to the source control system (e.g., GitHub or Bitbucket), providing users with a direct link to the build details.
aws_code_build_project.source.git_clone_depth: Sets the depth of the git clone, limiting the number of commits fetched from the repository (default is 1) to create a shallow clone.
aws_code_build_project.source.git_submodules_config: Configures Git submodules for the build source, with a 'FetchSubmodules' flag that determines whether submodules are fetched before the build runs.
aws_code_build_project.source.git_submodules_config.fetch_submo: Specifies whether to fetch git submodules for the build project's source repository.
aws_code_build_project.source.insecure_ssl: Set to true to ignore SSL certificate warnings when connecting to the source repository, such as when it uses a self-signed certificate.
aws_code_build_project.source.location: The URL or location of the source repository (for example, an S3 bucket name, GitHub or Bitbucket repository URL, or CodeCommit ARN) that CodeBuild uses as the build input.
aws_code_build_project.source.report_build_status: Indicates whether to report the build's start and finish status back to the source provider (e.g., GitHub, Bitbucket) for commits and pull requests, valid only for certain source types.
aws_code_build_project.source.source_identifier: Assigns a logical identifier to the primary source that can be referenced in buildspec commands, enabling the build to distinguish this source when the project uses multiple sources.
aws_code_build_project.source.type: The type of source repository for the CodeBuild project, which determines how the build fetches source code (e.g., S3, CODECOMMIT, GITHUB, BITBUCKET, or NO_SOURCE).
aws_code_build_project.source_version: Specifies the version of the source code to build, such as a commit ID, branch, or tag for Git-based repositories (CodeCommit, GitHub, Bitbucket) or an object key/version ID for Amazon S3; if omitted, the default branch or latest source version is used.
aws_code_build_project.tags: Assigns a list of tag objects (key-value pairs) to the AWS CodeBuild project, used for cost allocation, access control, and identifying project resources.
aws_code_build_project.tags.key: The key of a tag to associate with the AWS CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.tags.value: The value component of a tag attached to the CodeBuild project, providing arbitrary metadata for cost allocation or organization.
aws_code_build_project.timeout_in_minutes: The number of minutes after which a build in this project is automatically stopped and marked as failed if it has not completed.
aws_code_build_project.triggers: Defines the webhook trigger configuration, including the build type and filter groups that control which repository events (e.g., branch pushes or pull requests) automatically initiate a build.
aws_code_build_project.triggers.build_type: Specifies whether the project's webhook triggers should initiate a build, with a value of `BUILD` enabling builds and `NO_BUILD` disabling them for incoming source events.
aws_code_build_project.triggers.filter_groups: Specifies a list of filter groups that determine which webhook events trigger a build, where each filter group is a list of webhook filters (e.g., event type, branch, file path) that must all match for the build to start.
aws_code_build_project.triggers.pull_request_build_policy: Determines which pull requests trigger a build for the CodeBuild project's webhook: ALL builds every pull request, BRANCH builds only those targeting branches that match the filter pattern, and NON_BRANCH builds only those targeting branches that do not match the pattern.
aws_code_build_project.triggers.pull_request_build_policy.appro: A list of IAM role ARNs that can approve pull requests to trigger a build, defined within the project's pull request build policy for webhook-triggered builds.
aws_code_build_project.triggers.pull_request_build_policy.requi: Indicates whether an approval comment on a pull request is required to trigger the webhook build, so that builds only run when an authorized user comments with an approval phrase.
aws_code_build_project.triggers.scope_configuration.domain: The domain of the Git repository hosting service (for example, 'github.com' or a GitHub Enterprise server hostname) that scopes the webhook trigger configuration for this CodeBuild project.
aws_code_build_project.triggers.scope_configuration.name: The name of the repository or organization (as determined by the associated scope) that this webhook filter applies to, restricting which source code events trigger the build.
aws_code_build_project.triggers.scope_configuration.scope: Specifies whether the webhook trigger is scoped to an entire Bitbucket workspace ('WORKSPACE') or to a specific repository ('REPOSITORY').
aws_code_build_project.triggers.webhook: Determines whether the CodeBuild project's webhook is enabled, allowing builds to be automatically triggered by code changes pushed to the linked source repository (such as GitHub or Bitbucket).
aws_code_build_project.visibility: Specifies the visibility of the build project, with valid values PRIVATE, PUBLIC_READ, or PUBLIC, controlling whether unauthenticated users can view or trigger builds.
aws_code_build_project.vpc_config: Configures the build project to run in a customer-managed Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), specifying the VPC ID, subnet IDs, and security group IDs for the build environment.
aws_code_build_project.vpc_config.security_group_ids: This field specifies the security group IDs for the VPC configuration of the CodeBuild project, defining which security groups apply to the build's network interfaces.
aws_code_build_project.vpc_config.subnets: The list of subnet IDs within the VPC that AWS CodeBuild uses to run the build project's containers.
aws_code_build_project.vpc_config.vpc_id: The ID of the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) in which the CodeBuild project's builds run.

aws_code_build_report_group.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CodeBuild report group, which uniquely identifies it within AWS.
aws_code_build_report_group.delete_reports: Indicates whether all reports associated with the report group are deleted when the CloudFormation stack deletes the report group.
aws_code_build_report_group.export_config: Configures how test reports are exported from the report group, specifying either an S3 bucket destination or no export, including the S3 bucket, prefix, and encryption settings.
aws_code_build_report_group.export_config.export_config_type: Specifies the type of export destination for the report group's raw test results, which is either S3 or NO_EXPORT.
aws_code_build_report_group.export_config.s3_destination: Defines the S3 bucket and object path where CodeBuild exports the test reports generated by this report group.
aws_code_build_report_group.export_config.s3_destination.bucket: The name of the S3 bucket where CodeBuild exports the report group's test results.
aws_code_build_report_group.export_config.s3_destination.bucket_owne: The AWS account ID of the S3 bucket owner, used to verify the bucket is owned by the specified account before writing report export artifacts.
aws_code_build_report_group.export_config.s3_destination.encryption_: When true, disables encryption for the S3 bucket where CodeBuild exports the report group's artifacts.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the exported test report's S3 objects; if omitted, CodeBuild uses the default AWS managed key for Amazon S3.
aws_code_build_report_group.export_config.s3_destination.packaging: Specifies whether the report is packaged as a ZIP file or not when exported to the S3 destination, with valid values ZIP or NONE.
aws_code_build_report_group.export_config.s3_destination.path: Specifies the path (prefix) within the S3 bucket where the raw data of the report is exported.
aws_code_build_report_group.id: This field is the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CodeBuild report group, which serves as the unique identifier and is generated by AWS when the report group is created.
aws_code_build_report_group.name: The name of the report group; if not provided, CloudFormation generates a unique name.
aws_code_build_report_group.tags: A list of key-value pairs to associate with the report group for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource, such as for cost allocation and access control.
aws_code_build_report_group.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the AWS CodeBuild report group, which can be used to organize, categorize, or track costs and access for the resource.
aws_code_build_report_group.type: The type of report group, which can be either TEST or CODE_COVERAGE, determining the kind of reports this group contains.

aws_code_commit_repository.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this CodeCommit repository within AWS.
aws_code_commit_repository.clone_url_http: The HTTP(S) clone URL for the AWS CodeCommit repository, which is used to clone the repository over HTTPS.
aws_code_commit_repository.clone_url_ssh: The SSH URL used to clone the CodeCommit repository over SSH.
aws_code_commit_repository.code: Defines the initial code to be committed to the repository, specifying the S3 source (bucket, key, and optional object version), target branch, and commit message.
aws_code_commit_repository.code.branch_name: The name of the branch in the repository to which the initial code (specified in the Code property) is committed when the repository is created.
aws_code_commit_repository.code.s3: The S3 location (bucket, key, and optional object version) from which AWS CodeCommit imports the code for the repository's initial commit.
aws_code_commit_repository.code.s3.bucket: The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that contains the source code to be committed to the CodeCommit repository when the repository is created.
aws_code_commit_repository.code.s3.key: The S3 object key (file path within the bucket) of a ZIP archive containing the initial code that the CodeCommit repository is populated with when the repository is created, as part of the 'code' configuration's 's3' block.
aws_code_commit_repository.code.s3.object_version: Specifies the version ID of the S3 object that contains the initial code for the repository, enabling you to use a specific version when the object has multiple versions.
aws_code_commit_repository.id: The id is the repository name, which uniquely identifies the CodeCommit repository within AWS and is automatically populated from the repository name argument when the resource is created.
aws_code_commit_repository.kms_key_id: The ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the repository contents; if omitted, an AWS-managed key is used.
aws_code_commit_repository.name: The name attribute holds the repository name, which matches the RepositoryName property set at creation and is immutable afterwards.
aws_code_commit_repository.repository_description: Specifies the description of the CodeCommit repository, which is displayed in the AWS Management Console and can be up to 1,000 characters long.
aws_code_commit_repository.repository_name: Specifies the name of the AWS CodeCommit repository, which must be unique within the AWS account and region, and is used as the repository's identifier for clone URLs and API operations.
aws_code_commit_repository.tags: Defines a list of key-value tag objects to associate with the AWS CodeCommit repository, enabling you to categorize and filter the repository for cost tracking, access management, and resource organization.
aws_code_commit_repository.tags.key: The key of a tag to associate with the AWS CodeCommit repository, used for identifying and organizing the repository.
aws_code_commit_repository.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS CodeCommit repository, used to store metadata associated with the corresponding tag key.
aws_code_commit_repository.triggers: Defines the list of SNS notification triggers for the repository, where each trigger specifies the SNS topic ARN, the repository events (such as 'all', 'update', 'create', or 'delete') that will fire the trigger, and optionally the branch names that restrict which events are published.
aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.branches: Specifies the list of branches in the repository for which the trigger's events (such as create, update, or delete) should trigger the associated action (e.g., an SNS notification); if the list is empty, the trigger applies to all branches.
aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.custom_data: The custom_data field of a trigger is an optional string that AWS CodeCommit includes in the SNS notification payload delivered to the trigger's destination ARN, allowing you to pass arbitrary metadata to downstream consumers.
aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.destination_arn: The ARN of the SNS topic that receives push notifications from this CodeCommit repository when the trigger condition is met.
aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.events: Lists the CodeCommit repository events (for example, push, createBranch, deleteBranch, createTag, deleteTag, or updateReference) that activate the trigger.
aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.name: The name of an AWS CodeCommit repository trigger, which must be unique within the repository and is used to identify the trigger when configuring and managing repository events.

aws_code_connections_connection.tags.value: The value portion of a user-defined tag assigned to an AWS CodeConnections Connection, used to store arbitrary metadata for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_code_deploy_application.tags.value: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the CodeDeploy application.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.minimum_healthy_hosts: Defines the minimum number or percentage of healthy hosts that must remain available during a deployment, where the object specifies a type (HOST_COUNT or FLEET_PERCENT) and a numerical value.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.minimum_healthy_hosts.type: Specifies whether the minimum healthy hosts value is an absolute number of instances (HOST_COUNT) or a percentage of the fleet (FLEET_PERCENT) that must remain healthy during a deployment.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.minimum_healthy_hosts.value: The numeric value that defines the minimum number of healthy hosts (when type is HOST_COUNT) or the minimum percentage of the deployment fleet that must be healthy (when type is FLEET_PERCENT) during a CodeDeploy deployment.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.traffic_routing_config: Configures how traffic is shifted from the original fleet to the replacement fleet during a deployment, such as a linear or canary strategy with a step percentage and interval.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.traffic_routing_config.time_based_canary: The time_based_canary object inside traffic_routing_config for an AWS CodeDeploy deployment config specifies a canary-style traffic shift, moving a defined percentage of traffic to the new revision first and then the remaining traffic after a fixed time interval.
In a time-based canary deployment, this is the number of minutes to wait after shifting the canary percentage of traffic before shifting the remaining traffic.

The percentage of traffic to shift to the updated deployment group in the first (canary) increment of a time-based canary deployment, with the remaining traffic shifted in the second increment after the configured interval.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.traffic_routing_config.time_based_linear: Specifies a time-based linear traffic routing configuration for a CodeDeploy deployment, which shifts a set percentage of traffic to the updated environment at regular time intervals until deployment completes.
The number of minutes to wait between each incremental shift of traffic during a time-based linear deployment, used with linear_percentage to control the pace of the rollout.
The percentage of traffic to shift to newly added instances at each interval in a time-based linear deployment configuration.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.traffic_routing_config.type: Specifies the traffic-routing strategy for the deployment — allowed values are AllAtOnce (all traffic shifted immediately), TimeBasedLinear (shift traffic incrementally at regular intervals), and TimeBasedCanary (shift a canary portion of traffic, then the remainder).
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.zonal_config: Configures zonal deployment behavior for the deployment config, including settings such as the first-zone monitoring duration, overall monitor duration, and the minimum number of healthy hosts required per zone.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.zonal_config.first_zone_monitor_duration: The number of seconds AWS CodeDeploy waits to monitor the health of the first Availability Zone in a zonal ECS deployment before proceeding to the next zone.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.zonal_config.minimum_healthy_hosts_per_z: Specifies the minimum number or percentage of healthy hosts that must be available in each Availability Zone during a CodeDeploy zonal deployment, configured via a type (HOST_COUNT or FLEET_PERCENT) and a value.
Specifies whether the minimum healthy hosts per Availability Zone is expressed as an absolute host count (HOST_COUNT) or as a percentage of the total fleet (FLEET_PERCENT).

Specifies the numeric threshold (as a host count or zone fleet percentage, determined by the associated 'type' property) for the minimum number of healthy instances that must remain available in each Availability Zone during a zonal deployment in AWS CodeDeploy.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.zonal_config.monitor_duration_in_seconds: The number of seconds that AWS CodeDeploy monitors the health of the first region after its deployment succeeds, before starting deployment to the next region in a zonal deployment.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.alarm_configuration.alarms.name: The name of a CloudWatch alarm that this CodeDeploy deployment group monitors to automatically stop a deployment if the alarm enters an alarming state.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.ec2_tag_filters.key: The EC2 tag key (e.g., 'Environment') used to match instances for the deployment group's tag filter.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.ec2_tag_filters.type: Specifies the tag filter type (KEY_ONLY, VALUE_ONLY, or KEY_AND_VALUE) used to match EC2 instances for the deployment group.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.ec2_tag_filters.value: The tag value that the deployment group's EC2 tag filter matches against to select instances for deployment.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.ec2_tag_set.ec2_tag_set_list.ec2_tag_gro: A list of EC2 tag filters (each with Key, Value, and Type) that collectively define a tag group; an instance must match all tags in this group to be included in the deployment group via this EC2 tag set list entry.
The tag key (name) of an EC2 tag filter used to match instances for inclusion in the CodeDeploy deployment group, where the filter belongs to a logical group within an EC2 tag set.
Specifies the tag filter type used to match EC2 instances in this tag group, with allowed values such as KEY_ONLY, VALUE_ONLY, and KEY_AND_VALUE.
The tag value to match for the EC2 instance tag group, used as a filter to select instances for the CodeDeploy deployment group.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.ecsservices.cluster_name: The name of the ECS cluster where the ECS service targeted by the CodeDeploy deployment group is running.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.ecsservices.service_name: The name of the ECS service that the deployment group targets, as specified in the ECSServices configuration.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.load_balancer_info.elb_info_list.name: The name of the Classic Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) that CodeDeploy deregisters instances from and registers instances to during a deployment.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.load_balancer_info.target_group_info_lis: The name of an Elastic Load Balancing target group to associate with the CodeDeploy deployment group.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.load_balancer_info.target_group_pair_inf: In an AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment using paired target groups, prod_traffic_route specifies the listener ARN (or ARNs) on the load balancer that currently routes production traffic to the original (blue) target group, which CodeDeploy automatically updates to shift traffic to the replacement (green) target group during the deployment.

The ARNs of the Elastic Load Balancing listeners that route traffic to the production target group in a blue/green deployment, enabling CodeDeploy to shift production traffic to the replacement target group after deployment.

Specifies the list of target groups that make up a blue/green target group pair for an Application Load Balancer or Network Load Balancer, each containing the name or ARN of a target group used for the blue/green deployment traffic routing.
The name of the target group that is part of a target group pair used for load balancer traffic routing in a CodeDeploy blue/green deployment.

This traffic route object lists the target group ARNs that CodeDeploy sends test traffic to during a blue/green deployment, letting you validate the replacement environment before production traffic is shifted.
A list of Application Load Balancer listener ARNs that define the test traffic route used to shift traffic to the replacement environment during an AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.on_premises_instance_tag_filters.key: The tag key used to match on-premises instances for the deployment group's on-premises instance tag filter.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.on_premises_instance_tag_filters.type: The type of tag filter used to select on-premises instances for the deployment group, such as KEY_ONLY, VALUE_ONLY, or KEY_AND_VALUE, controlling whether matching is based on the tag key, the tag value, or both.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.on_premises_instance_tag_filters.value: The tag value that an on-premises instance must match for the instance to be included in the deployment group when using tag-based instance selection.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.on_premises_tag_set.on_premises_tag_set_: Defines a list of on-premises instance tag filters (key, value, and match type) that constitute a single tag group within an on-premises tag set, used to select on-premises instances for the CodeDeploy deployment group.
The tag key used in an on-premises instance tag group to match and select on-premises instances for the deployment group.

The `type` field of an on-premises tag group in an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group specifies the tag filter matching mode, with valid values `KEY_ONLY`, `VALUE_ONLY`, or `KEY_AND_VALUE`, determining whether the filter matches on the tag key, value, or both when selecting on-premises instances.
The value of an on-premises instance tag (e.g., 'prod') that must match for an on-premises instance to be included in the deployment group when this tag group is used as a filter.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.tags.value: The user-defined value for a tag key attached to an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group, enabling resource categorization and metadata management.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.trigger_configurations.trigger_events: The list of CodeDeploy deployment or instance events (e.g., DeploymentSuccess, DeploymentFailure) that will trigger the SNS notification for this trigger configuration.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.trigger_configurations.trigger_name: The name of a trigger configuration for the deployment group, used to identify this trigger among the configured CloudWatch Events or SNS triggers.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.trigger_configurations.trigger_target_ar: The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that AWS CodeDeploy uses to send notifications when the deployment lifecycle events specified in the trigger configuration occur.

aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group.anomaly_detection_notification_configura: The unique identifier assigned by CodeGuru Profiler to an Amazon SNS notification channel used for anomaly detection, which references the channel within the profiling group's configuration.
The ARN of the SNS topic to which anomaly detection notifications are published for this profiling group.
aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the profiling group.
aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group.tags.key: A key in the tags map of an AWS CodeGuru Profiler profiling group, used to attach custom metadata (such as environment or application name) to the profiling group for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.
