Determines whether the billing_address.state profile attribute dimension includes or excludes profiles whose state matches, with allowed values INCLUSIVE and EXCLUSIVE.
The list of state values that a profile's billing address state must match for the profile to be included in the segment when this dimension is applied.
Defines the dimension configuration for the customer profile's birth date attribute, enabling segment definitions to filter profiles based on their date of birth.
Specifies the comparison operator used to evaluate a profile's birth date against the configured values, such as BETWEEN for a date range.
Specifies the list of birth date values to match in the segment definition, controlling which customers are included based on their BirthDate profile attribute.
Configures the customer profile's business email address as a profile attribute dimension used for segment filtering, allowing segment definitions to target profiles based on this email field.

For the business email address profile attribute in a Customer Profiles segment definition, this field sets the dimension type (such as EMAIL or STRING) that determines how the attribute's value is interpreted when segment filters are applied.
Defines the list of business email address values to match when filtering customer profiles on the business_email_address profile attribute.
Defines the matching criteria for the 'Business Name' profile attribute within a dimension of a segment definition, used to filter customer profiles by their business name.
For the business_name profile attribute, this value determines whether the attribute is evaluated as a PROFILE or ACCOUNT dimension in the segment definition.
Specifies the list of business name values used to match profiles when the business_name profile attribute serves as a segment dimension, determining which profiles are included in the segment.
Specifies how profiles are matched on their business phone number for this segment, using include/exclude criteria and an inclusive/exclusive dimension type.
Defines the dimension type for the business phone number profile attribute, which should be set to PHONE to treat it as a phone number dimension within the segment group.
Specifies the list of business phone number values used as filter criteria in this dimension to include or exclude customer profiles whose business phone number matches any of the given values.
Specifies the segmentation dimension for the profile's email address attribute, defining the criteria (such as matching values or ranges) used to determine which profiles belong to the segment.
Determines the comparison or matching operation applied to the email address attribute in the segment dimension, such as EXISTS, CONTAINS, or BETWEEN, to filter profiles for segmentation.
Defines the list of email address values used as an inclusion condition for this profile attribute dimension, so profiles whose email address matches any of these values are included in the segment.

Represents the configuration for using the 'FirstName' profile attribute as a dimension in a segment group, defining the condition (e.g., equal, contains, range) that determines which profiles match the segment.
Defines the matching operator for the first_name profile attribute in the segment dimension, such as INCLUSIVE or EXCLUSIVE, to include or exclude profiles based on their first name.
Specifies the list of first-name values that the segment dimension condition matches against a customer's profile to determine segment membership.
Specifies the string dimension for the customer's Gender profile attribute (e.g., matching 'Male' or 'Female' values) within a segment group's dimension criteria.

Defines whether the gender string attribute acts as an inclusive dimension (matching profiles are included in the segment) or an exclusive dimension (matching profiles are excluded) within the segment group's dimensions.
Specifies the list of gender string values (such as 'Male' or 'Female') to match when determining which profiles are included in this segment definition's dimension.

In an AWS Customer Profiles segment definition, this object defines the home phone number dimension, letting you filter which profiles are included in the segment based on matching phone number values (e.g., as an inclusive or exclusive condition).

The values field defines the list of home phone number strings used to match customer profiles in the segment, operating with the associated dimension type (INCLUSIVE or EXCLUSIVE) to include or exclude matching profiles.
Defines the dimension configuration for the customer's last name profile attribute, used to segment profiles based on the LastName field.
Determines the operator or condition type (e.g., 'EXISTS', 'STARTS_WITH', 'BETWEEN') used to evaluate the last_name profile attribute within this segment dimension.
The list of last-name values that a profile's `last_name` attribute must match (exact match against any value in the list) for the profile to be included in the segment dimension.
Defines the mailing-address components (such as city, state, or postal code) used as a dimension for segmenting customer profiles within a segment definition.
Specifies the city portion of the customer's mailing address to be used as a profile attribute dimension in the segment definition.
Determines whether the mailing address city attribute is treated as an ORDINAL (ordered) or DISCRETE (categorical) dimension within the profile attribute dimension for this segment group's criteria.
This field specifies the list of city names used as matching criteria when evaluating a profile's mailing address city in the segment definition's dimension.
Defines the matching condition (such as a set of acceptable countries and the operator to apply) for the country attribute of the mailing address when building a Customer Profiles segment.
Specifies whether the mailing address country attribute is treated as a standard profile attribute or a calculated attribute when used as a segment dimension.

In an AWS Customer Profiles segment definition, this list specifies the allowed country values for the mailing address profile attribute, and a profile is included in the segment only if its mailing address country matches one of these values.
Defines a segment dimension for the county of the profile's mailing address, allowing include/exclude criteria based on county values.

Specifies the data type (such as TEXT) for the county field of the mailing address profile attribute, which controls how the county value is interpreted when used to group customers in a segment definition.
List of county names used to match a profile's mailing address county attribute when evaluating this segment group dimension.

This object defines the segment dimension criteria for the profile's mailing address postal code, specifying whether to include or exclude certain postal code values using the DimensionType and Values attributes.
Specifies the data type (e.g., STRING) of the postal code attribute used for filtering profiles in the segment definition.
The list of postal code values that a profile's mailing address postal code must match for the profile to be included in the segment definition.
Specifies the province/state of the customer's mailing address to be used as a dimensional attribute in the segment definition, enabling segmentation based on this geographic filter.

Specifies the match operator for the mailing address province within a segment dimension, controlling whether profiles whose province matches the given value are included in or excluded from the segment.
Specifies the list of province (state) values that a profile's mailing address province must match for the profile to be included in the segment.
The state or province of the customer's mailing address, used as a dimension within a segment group to filter customer profiles by geographic location.

Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., 'IN', 'EXISTS', 'NOT_IN') used to evaluate the customer's mailing address state against configured values, controlling whether the state matches for segment membership.
Specifies the list of state values (e.g., 'CA', 'NY') used to match profiles against the mailing address state attribute in the segment definition's group dimension rule.

Defines the matching criteria for the profile's middle name attribute within a segment group's dimension, including the dimension type (e.g., STRING), allowed values, and operation used to evaluate profiles.
Specifies whether the middle name attribute dimension is inclusive or exclusive for segment membership, controlling which profiles are included or excluded when the segment is evaluated.

Specifies the list of middle-name values to match against the middle_name profile attribute when evaluating this segment group's dimension, filtering customers based on the configured include/exclude type.
Specifies how to filter profiles by mobile phone number in a segment dimension, using a dimension type (e.g., INCLUSIVE, EXCLUSIVE, CONTAINS, BEGINS_WITH) and a list of values to match.
Defines the dimension type for the mobile phone number profile attribute, using PHONE_NUMBER to indicate the value is treated as a phone number in the segment definition's filtering criteria.
The list of mobile phone numbers to match against a profile's mobile_phone_number attribute for inclusion in the segment.

This object holds the dimension criteria (inclusive/exclusive match on a set of string values) applied to the `party_type_string` profile attribute when evaluating customer profiles for segment membership.
Determines whether the provided party type string values are used to either include or exclude matching profiles from the segment, with accepted values 'INCLUSIVE' or 'EXCLUSIVE'.

Provides a list of string values that the 'party_type_string' profile attribute must match for a profile to be included in the segment, enabling segmentation by party type (e.g., 'Business' or 'Individual').
Defines the segmentation criteria (such as dimension type and matching conditions) applied to the profile's personal email address within the profile attributes of a segment group's dimensions.

Determines how the personal email address profile attribute is interpreted as a dimension in a segment group, specifying its data type so that the correct comparisons and filters are applied when building the segment.
Specifies a list of personal email addresses used as filter values for the personal_email_address profile attribute in the segment dimension.
Specifies the dimension condition for the profile phone number attribute, with fields for the comparison operation and value used to include profiles in the segment.
Specifies the phone number type (e.g., HOME, MOBILE, WORK, DIRECT, FAX) used as the dimension attribute for filtering customers in this segment definition.
Specifies the list of phone numbers to match for the phone_number profile attribute when defining this dimension's segment criteria.
Determines whether the profile attribute dimension includes or excludes profiles whose attribute value matches the listed values, accepting INCLUSIVE or EXCLUSIVE.
List of profile type values (e.g., 'Customer' or 'Business') that the profile_type attribute must match for a profile to be included in this segment group dimension.
Specifies the shipping address profile attribute as a dimension for segment filtering, enabling customer profiles to be grouped or targeted based on their shipping address.
Defines the dimension condition (e.g., IN, BETWEEN) applied to the city of the customer's shipping address, which determines the criteria for including profiles in the segment definition.

The dimension type applied to the city field under the shipping address profile attribute, indicating whether the city is treated as a customer profile attribute (PROFILE_ATTRIBUTE) or an object type attribute (OBJECT_TYPE) for the purpose of segment definition.
Defines the list of city values that the shipping address city attribute must match to include a profile in the segment.
Configures the country attribute of the shipping address as a profile attribute dimension, used to define segment membership based on a customer's shipping country.
Specifies the list of country values used to match profiles based on the shipping address country attribute in this segment dimension.

This object defines the dimension criteria used to segment profiles based on the county value of the shipping address, allowing you to include or exclude profiles whose shipping address county matches a specified condition.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as IN, NOT_IN, or EXISTS) for the shipping address county profile attribute when used as a segment dimension.
Defines the list of county names (e.g., 'Cook', 'King') used as matching criteria for the shipping address county attribute in the segment definition's group dimensions.

This object configures how the shipping address's postal code attribute is used as a profile dimension in the segment, including the dimension type (like RANGE or TOP_BOX) and any associated parameters such as range bounds or threshold values.
Specifies whether the shipping address postal code is treated as a TEXT or NUMERIC dimension in the segment definition, which determines the allowed comparison operations for the attribute.
Defines the list of postal code values used to match a profile's shipping address postal code against this dimension for segment membership evaluation.

Defines the dimension configuration for the province (state/region) component of a customer's shipping address, specifying how profile membership is evaluated based on a dimension type and matching province values.
For the shipping address province attribute within a segment definition, this dimension type value specifies whether the segment includes or excludes profiles based on the specified province values.
A list of province or state values (such as CA or NY) used to match the shipping address province of profiles in the segment definition's dimension condition.
The state or province portion of the customer's shipping address, used as a profile attribute dimension to define segment membership in a Customer Profiles segment definition.
Specifies the dimension type (PROFILE or INTERACTION) for the shipping address state attribute, determining whether the segment evaluates this field against profile data or interaction data.
Specifies the list of state values (e.g., 'CA', 'NY') used to match against the shipping address state of profiles when evaluating segment membership for this group.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.segment_groups.groups.source_segments: Specifies the list of existing segment definitions used as source inputs within this group of the segment group, enabling the new segment to be built from previously defined segments that are combined according to the group's logic.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.segment_groups.groups.source_segments.se: The name of the source segment definition to reference as a source segment within this group, used to build a segment by combining other segment definitions.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.segment_groups.groups.source_type: Determines whether a customer must match all conditions (ALL) or any one condition (ANY) in the group's source list to be included in the segment group.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.segment_groups.groups.type: Specifies whether a profile must match all conditions (ALL) or any condition (ANY) defined within this segment group of the Customer Profiles segment definition.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.segment_sort.attributes.name: The name of the Customer Profiles profile attribute that defines the sort key for the segment results in the segment sort configuration.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.segment_sort.attributes.order: Defines the sort order (ascending or descending) applied to the corresponding attribute in a segment definition's sort criteria.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.segment_sort.attributes.type: In the segment sort definition, the 'type' field specifies whether the attribute being sorted is a system-defined profile attribute (SYSTEM) or a custom attribute (CUSTOM) so Customer Profiles can correctly resolve the field to sort by.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to this Customer Profiles segment definition, used to label and categorize the resource for management, filtering, and cost allocation.
aws_customer_profiles_segment_definition.tags.value: The value for a tag assigned to the Customer Profiles segment definition, used to store arbitrary metadata such as environment, owner, or cost center for resource management and identification.

aws_data_brew_dataset.format_options.csv.delimiter: The single character used to separate columns in the CSV file when reading data into the AWS DataBrew dataset.
aws_data_brew_dataset.format_options.csv.header_row: Indicates whether the first row of the CSV file is treated as a header row containing column names.
aws_data_brew_dataset.format_options.excel: Defines format-specific settings for Excel inputs, including the sheets to read and whether the first row is treated as a header.
aws_data_brew_dataset.format_options.excel.header_row: Indicates whether the first row of the Excel file is treated as column headers.
aws_data_brew_dataset.format_options.excel.sheet_indexes: Specifies the 0-based indices of the Excel sheets to include from the workbook, letting you select specific sheets when the file contains multiple sheets.
aws_data_brew_dataset.format_options.excel.sheet_names: Specifies the names of the worksheets within an Excel workbook that DataBrew will read when creating the dataset, allowing you to limit the data to only those sheets.
aws_data_brew_dataset.format_options.json.multi_line: Specifies whether JSON objects in the dataset can span multiple lines (true) or must each be contained on a single line (false).
aws_data_brew_dataset.input.data_catalog_input_definition: Defines the AWS Glue Data Catalog database and table that AWS DataBrew uses as the source for this dataset.
aws_data_brew_dataset.input.data_catalog_input_definition.temp: The S3 bucket where DataBrew stores temporary files created while processing the dataset's Data Catalog input definition.
The S3 object key prefix within the temporary directory bucket where AWS Glue DataBrew writes intermediate query results when accessing the referenced Data Catalog table.
aws_data_brew_dataset.input.database_input_definition: Specifies the database connection and query details used to pull data into the dataset, including the connection name, database name, and query string.
aws_data_brew_dataset.input.database_input_definition.temp_dir: The name of the S3 bucket where AWS DataBrew writes temporary files while processing the database input.
Specifies the S3 object key (or key prefix) under the temporary directory bucket where DataBrew stores intermediate files when running a query against the database input.
aws_data_brew_dataset.input.metadata: Specifies metadata about the dataset's input source, including the SourceArn of the source dataset for lineage and versioning.
aws_data_brew_dataset.input.s3_input_definition.bucket: The name of the S3 bucket that contains the source data for the DataBrew dataset, specified within the S3 input definition.
aws_data_brew_dataset.input.s3_input_definition.key: Specifies the S3 object key or prefix within the S3 bucket that points to the data files used by the dataset, enabling DataBrew to discover and read the source data.
aws_data_brew_dataset.path_options.files_limit: Configures a limit on the number of files that DataBrew uses from the dataset's S3 path, optionally specifying the ordering for file selection.
aws_data_brew_dataset.path_options.last_modified_date_conditio: Defines a filter expression and value map that restricts the S3 files ingested into the dataset based on their last modified date.

Defines the key-value pairs (e.g., startDate and endDate) that substitute into the last-modified-date condition expression, filtering which S3 files are included in the DataBrew dataset based on their last modified timestamp.

For an AWS DataBrew dataset's S3 path options, this value holds the string value associated with a key in the last-modified-date condition's values map, such as the start or end date used to filter files by their last modified date.

Provides a reference to a value that DataBrew substitutes for a placeholder in the last modified date conditioning expression, allowing the dataset's path file filter to use dynamically referenced values instead of literals.
aws_data_brew_dataset.path_options.parameters: Defines the list of parameters that DataBrew uses to resolve placeholders in the S3 path expression for this dataset, with each parameter specifying its name, type (e.g., STRING or DATETIME), and optional datetime formatting or filter criteria.
aws_data_brew_dataset.path_options.parameters.dataset_paramete: Defines the data type (e.g., String, Integer, Datetime) and associated parsing options, such as datetime formatting, column creation, and filter criteria, for a single parameterized variable in the dataset's S3 path.
Determines whether AWS DataBrew adds a column to the dataset that contains the actual value of this path parameter, enabling you to use the parameter value as data.
Defines the datetime parsing options (format, locale, and timezone offset) for a path parameter of type DATETIME in an AWS DataBrew dataset.
Specifies the custom date/time format (for example, 'yyyy-MM-dd') that defines how the value of a datetime dataset parameter is parsed and interpreted.
The locale code (e.g., 'en-US') that specifies the language and region used to interpret the datetime format in the dataset path parameter.
Specifies the timezone offset (e.g., '+05:30' or '-08:00') used to interpret datetime values captured by this dataset parameter.
Specifies a regular expression that DataBrew uses to match the value of the path parameter, so that only matching files are included in the dataset.
Defines the regular expression pattern that matches file names or path segments for the dataset parameter, enabling DataBrew to include only files that conform to this expression in the dataset.
Specifies the key-value pairs of actual values referenced by the filter expression that determines which dataset paths are included for this parameter.
The actual value to substitute for a variable in the filter expression that controls which S3 object paths are eligible for the dataset.

A placeholder string used in the dataset parameter filter expression that is mapped to a list of concrete values in the corresponding values_map entry, allowing the expression to be evaluated dynamically against the actual data.
The name of the dataset parameter that is used as a placeholder in the path expression, which is substituted with the parameter's value when resolving the data source.
Specifies the data type of the dataset parameter, which can be String, Number, or Datetime, and determines how the parameter value is interpreted when resolving file paths or dataset filters.
aws_data_brew_dataset.path_options.parameters.path_parameter_n: The name of the parameter placeholder in the S3 path of the dataset, used to map to a corresponding dataset parameter definition for dynamic path resolution.
aws_data_brew_dataset.tags: Specifies the tags, each containing a key and value, that are attached to the DataBrew dataset to help identify, organize, and manage the resource.
aws_data_brew_dataset.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the DataBrew dataset, used to identify the tag in AWS resource tagging.
aws_data_brew_dataset.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to this AWS DataBrew dataset, used to categorize or manage the resource.

aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs: Specifies a list of destinations where the job writes its output to AWS Glue Data Catalog tables, each defined by a database name, table name, and optional S3 storage options.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.catalog_id: The AWS account ID (also known as the catalog ID) of the AWS Glue Data Catalog that receives the job's output table when writing to a data catalog destination.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.database_name: The name of the AWS Glue Data Catalog database where the job's data catalog output will be stored or referenced.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.database_options: Specifies database-specific options for a DataBrew job's Data Catalog output, including the target table name and an optional temporary directory for staging output data.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.database_options.ta: Specifies the name of the table in the target database that the AWS Glue DataBrew job writes to when the data catalog output is configured with database options.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.database_options.te: The Amazon S3 location (bucket and key) where AWS DataBrew stores temporary files while writing the job output to a database in a data catalog.
The S3 bucket name for the temporary directory that DataBrew uses to stage data before writing to the database output.
The AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket used as the temporary directory for this database output.
The S3 object key (prefix) of the temporary directory that AWS DataBrew uses when writing output to a database catalog as part of the DatabaseOptions for a data catalog output.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.overwrite: Whether the DataBrew job overwrites existing data in the target Glue Data Catalog table when writing output.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.s3_options: Specifies the S3 bucket and object key (prefix) where the Data Catalog output's table data is stored for this DataBrew job.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.s3_options.location: The S3 location (bucket and prefix, e.g., s3://bucket/prefix) where the job writes the data catalog output table's data.
The S3 bucket name that DataBrew uses as the destination when writing the job's data catalog output to an S3 location.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the S3 bucket owner, used to verify that the output bucket is owned by the expected account before DataBrew writes data.
The S3 object key (file name) for the location where DataBrew writes the data catalog output.
aws_data_brew_job.data_catalog_outputs.table_name: The name of the table in the AWS Glue Data Catalog where the DataBrew job writes its output.
aws_data_brew_job.database_outputs: Specifies database destinations for the output of the DataBrew job, including the connection name and target table to write results to.
aws_data_brew_job.database_outputs.database_options: The database_options object for each database output specifies the target AWS Glue Data Catalog database and table name to which the DataBrew job writes its output data.
aws_data_brew_job.database_outputs.database_options.table_: The name of the table in the target database where DataBrew writes the output of the job.
aws_data_brew_job.database_outputs.database_options.temp_d: The S3 location where AWS DataBrew stores temporary staging files while processing the job's output to the target database.
Specifies the S3 bucket name for the temporary directory used to stage data before writing job results to the target database.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket used as a temporary directory for the database output, enabling cross-account access.
The S3 object key of the temporary directory that DataBrew uses for staging data before writing to the database output.
aws_data_brew_job.database_outputs.database_output_mode: Determines how DataBrew writes job results to the target database, either creating a new table or overwriting existing data.
aws_data_brew_job.database_outputs.glue_connection_name: The name of the AWS Glue connection that defines the database connection used when writing the job's output to a database.
aws_data_brew_job.output_location.bucket: The S3 bucket name where the DataBrew job writes its output files.
aws_data_brew_job.output_location.bucket_owner: The AWS account ID of the account that owns the Amazon S3 bucket where the DataBrew job output is written.
aws_data_brew_job.output_location.key: The S3 object key or prefix within the output bucket where AWS DataBrew writes the job's output files.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs: Defines the list of output destinations for the DataBrew job, each specifying an S3 location, file format, and optional format or partition settings.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.compression_format: Specifies the compression format applied to the job's output data, such as GZIP, LZ4, SNAPPY, BZIP2, DEFLATE, LZO, BROTLI, ZSTD, or NONE, determining how the written result files are compressed.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.format: Specifies the file format for output files generated by the DataBrew job, such as CSV, JSON, PARQUET, or XML.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.format_options: Specifies format-specific output options for the job, such as the delimiter and header row for CSV files or the sheet name for Excel files.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.format_options.csv: Configures the CSV-specific output formatting for the DataBrew job, including options like delimiter and whether a header row is included.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.format_options.csv.delimiter: Specifies the character used to separate columns in the resulting comma-separated value (CSV) output file of the DataBrew job, for example a comma (`,`), tab (`\t`), or pipe (`|`).
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.location: Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and key (or prefix) that defines where the DataBrew job output is stored.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.location.bucket: The name of the S3 bucket where the DataBrew job writes its output files, specified as part of the output location.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.location.bucket_owner: The AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket where the job output is written, used to validate bucket ownership.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.location.key: The S3 object key where AWS DataBrew writes the job's output dataset as part of the configured output location.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.max_output_files: For each output location configured on an AWS DataBrew job, the MaxOutputFiles value sets the upper limit on the number of files DataBrew can write to that destination; a value of 0 indicates DataBrew should automatically determine the file count.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.overwrite: Specifies whether the DataBrew job output overwrites existing data at the destination location, or writes alongside it.
aws_data_brew_job.outputs.partition_columns: Specifies the list of column names used to partition the data in the job output stored in Amazon S3.
aws_data_brew_job.profile_configuration: Specifies the configuration for a profile job in AWS Glue DataBrew, including settings such as which columns to profile, column statistics to generate, and dataset statistics to include in the job's output.
aws_data_brew_job.profile_configuration.column_statistics_: Configures which column statistics are computed during a DataBrew profile job by specifying per-column (or column-group) selectors and the specific statistics to include.
Specifies the column selectors (such as column names or regular expression patterns) that determine which columns the data profile job's column statistics configuration applies to.
The name of a specific column to include in the column statistics configuration for this DataBrew profile job's selector.
A regular expression pattern that selects which column names to include in the column statistics configuration.
Specifies which statistics to compute for the selected columns in an AWS Glue DataBrew profile job, including the list of included statistics and any per-statistic overrides.
Specifies the list of statistic names (e.g., 'mean', 'median', 'standard deviation') to be computed and included in the profile job output for the selected columns.
Provides a list of statistic overrides, each mapping a statistic name to custom parameters that control how that statistic is computed during the DataBrew profile job.
Specifies the custom parameter values (as key-value pairs) used by an overridden statistic in a column statistics configuration of an AWS DataBrew profile job.
The name of the built-in statistic (e.g., 'Average', 'StandardDeviation') that the override applies to, used to customize its parameters in the DataBrew profile job's column statistics configuration.
aws_data_brew_job.profile_configuration.dataset_statistics: Specifies the statistics configuration for the entire dataset in a profile job, defining which dataset-level statistics (e.g., row count) are computed and any custom overrides.
Specifies the list of statistics (e.g., MEAN, MEDIAN, STDEV) to compute and include in the profile job's dataset statistics output, overriding the default of all statistics.
Specifies a list of statistic overrides for the dataset-level statistics in a DataBrew profile job, where each override identifies a statistic and provides parameters to customize its calculation.

A key-value map of parameters that configure a specific statistic override in the dataset statistics configuration of an AWS DataBrew profile job, controlling how that overridden statistic is computed.

The name of the statistic (for example, 'mean', 'median', 'stdDev', or 'count') that this override entry in the profile job's dataset statistics configuration applies to, selecting which computed statistic's parameters are being overridden.
aws_data_brew_job.profile_configuration.entity_detector_co: Specifies the entity types (such as email addresses or phone numbers) AWS Glue DataBrew should detect in the data during a profile job, and any allowed statistics that can be computed for those detected entities.

Defines the statistics configuration (including included statistics and overrides) that restricts which statistical measures are computed for the entities detected in the dataset during the profile job.

Specifies the set of statistical metrics (e.g., count, mean, median) that are permitted to be calculated for the detected entity types in the profile job, filtering which statistics appear in the output.

This required list specifies the entity types (such as email addresses, phone numbers, or credit card numbers) that DataBrew's entity detector scans for in the input dataset when generating the data profile.
aws_data_brew_job.profile_configuration.profile_columns: Defines a list of column selectors (each identifying a column by name or regular expression pattern) that specify which columns in the dataset are included in the profile job analysis.
aws_data_brew_job.profile_configuration.profile_columns.na: The name of a column that is selected for profiling in the DataBrew job's profile configuration.
aws_data_brew_job.profile_configuration.profile_columns.re: A regular expression pattern that selects columns for profiling by matching their names.
aws_data_brew_job.recipe: The recipe property specifies the name and version of the DataBrew recipe to be run by this job.
aws_data_brew_job.tags: Specifies the key-value tags to associate with the DataBrew job for managing and identifying resources.
aws_data_brew_job.tags.key: The key of an AWS tag that can be attached to this DataBrew job to help identify, organize, and control access to the job.
aws_data_brew_job.tags.value: The value part of a tag attached to the DataBrew job, used alongside a tag key to categorize, identify, and manage the job resource.
aws_data_brew_job.validation_configurations.ruleset_arn: The ARN of the AWS Glue DataBrew ruleset used to validate the output of the job.
aws_data_brew_job.validation_configurations.validation_mod: Determines how the DataBrew job applies the linked validation ruleset, either checking all records (CHECK_ALL) or suppressing failures so the job continues (SUPPRESS_FAILURES).

aws_data_brew_project.sample: Defines the sample configuration for the project's dataset, specifying the sample size and sampling type.
aws_data_brew_project.tags: Assigns metadata key-value pairs to the DataBrew project for cost allocation, access control, and organization.
aws_data_brew_project.tags.key: The key of an individual tag attached to an AWS Glue DataBrew project, used to organize, identify, and manage the project resource.
aws_data_brew_project.tags.value: The value portion of a tag attached to the DataBrew project, used to add metadata for cost allocation, access control, and resource categorization in AWS.

aws_data_brew_recipe.steps: The ordered list of transformation steps, each specifying a DataBrew action and optional condition expressions, that define the recipe's data processing logic.
aws_data_brew_recipe.steps.action: Defines the transformation to apply in this recipe step, specifying the operation type and its parameters.
aws_data_brew_recipe.steps.action.operation: Specifies the data transformation action to apply in this recipe step, such as PROJECT or FILTER, matching one of DataBrew's supported operations.
aws_data_brew_recipe.steps.action.parameters: A map of key-value pairs that provides operation-specific configuration for the transformation action, where the required and optional parameters depend on the selected operation (e.g., column names, ranges, or thresholds).
aws_data_brew_recipe.steps.condition_expressions: Defines the list of condition expressions for a recipe step, where each expression specifies a condition, target column, and optional value to evaluate whether the step should be applied.
aws_data_brew_recipe.steps.condition_expressions.condition: The condition operator (such as `isEquals`, `isNull`, or `contains`) that determines whether the recipe step is applied to the target column, compared against the configured value.
aws_data_brew_recipe.steps.condition_expressions.target_colum: Specifies the column in the dataset whose values are evaluated by the condition expression in a DataBrew recipe step.
aws_data_brew_recipe.steps.condition_expressions.value: The value to compare against the target column's content when evaluating the condition expression for a recipe step.
aws_data_brew_recipe.tags: Defines one or more custom tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the recipe for metadata and cost allocation.
aws_data_brew_recipe.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the DataBrew recipe, used to categorize and identify the resource.
aws_data_brew_recipe.tags.value: Defines the value of a tag applied to the AWS DataBrew recipe, allowing you to add arbitrary metadata for cost allocation, resource grouping, and access control.

aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.check_expression: Defines the data quality check expression, a condition that DataBrew evaluates per row to flag records that violate the rule.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.column_selectors: Specifies the column selectors for a rule, defining which columns (by exact name or regex pattern) the rule evaluates in an AWS Glue DataBrew ruleset.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.column_selectors.name: The name of the specific column that this column selector targets for the DataBrew rule.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.column_selectors.regex: A regular expression pattern used to match column names for the selector, so the rule applies to all columns whose names match this pattern.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.disabled: A boolean flag that indicates whether this rule is disabled and thus not evaluated when the DataBrew ruleset is applied.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.name: The name of an individual rule within the DataBrew ruleset, used to uniquely identify and reference that rule in the ruleset definition.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.substitution_map: Maps placeholder variable names to column references or dataset parameters that are substituted into the rule's check expression when the ruleset is evaluated.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.substitution_map.value: The value to substitute for the associated variable key when evaluating the rule's check expression, replacing references to that variable with this string.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.substitution_map.value_reference: In an AWS DataBrew Ruleset, this is the substitution variable reference (e.g., `${column_name}`) that appears in a rule's check expression and is replaced with the actual value from the `Value` property of this substitution map entry.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.threshold: Defines the threshold condition for the rule's check result, specifying a comparison type (such as GREATER_THAN or LESS_THAN) and a numeric value that determines whether the rule passes.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.threshold.type: The comparison operator (e.g., GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN, EQUAL) used to evaluate the threshold value against the metric calculated for a rule in an AWS Glue DataBrew ruleset.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.threshold.unit: Defines the unit of measurement (COUNT or PERCENTAGE) for the threshold value used in evaluating a rule's condition within the DataBrew ruleset.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.rules.threshold.value: The numeric value used as the threshold to compare against the rule's check expression result.
aws_data_brew_ruleset.tags.value: The value for a tag key on the AWS Glue DataBrew ruleset, used to assign metadata such as environment or cost center to the resource for management and cost tracking.

aws_data_brew_schedule.job_names: The list of DataBrew job names that this schedule will start when it fires.
aws_data_brew_schedule.tags: The tags to assign to the DataBrew schedule, where each tag consists of a key and an optional value used to categorize and manage the schedule.
aws_data_brew_schedule.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the DataBrew schedule, used to categorize and identify the schedule for cost allocation and access control.
aws_data_brew_schedule.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to an AWS DataBrew schedule, used to organize, categorize, and manage the schedule within AWS.

aws_data_exchange_data_set.tags.key: The key (name) of a tag attached to the AWS Data Exchange data set, used to organize, identify, and manage the resource.

aws_data_exchange_event_action.tags.key: Key of a tag attached to an AWS Data Exchange event action, used to categorize, organize, and manage event actions within your AWS account.

aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.parameter_objects.attributes: Defines the list of key-value attribute pairs (ParameterAttribute) that specify the configuration of a parameter object, such as its default value and description, in the AWS Data Pipeline pipeline definition.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.parameter_objects.attributes.key: The name of the attribute within a parameter object in an AWS Data Pipeline pipeline definition, used to specify parameter metadata such as 'description' or 'type'.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.parameter_objects.attributes.string_valu: The string value of an attribute within a parameter object, used to define a parameter's value in the pipeline definition.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.parameter_objects.id: The unique identifier for this parameter object within the pipeline's parameter definitions, used to reference it from pipeline expressions and resources.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.parameter_values.id: The identifier of a parameter defined in the pipeline's ParameterObjects list, used to map this value to that parameter.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.parameter_values.string_value: The string value assigned to a keyed parameter in the pipeline's parameter values, providing a runtime value to substitute into the pipeline definition at creation or update.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the pipeline.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_objects.fields: Defines the properties of each pipeline object via a list of key-value pairs (Field objects), which specify attributes such as name, type, schedule, and dependencies, either as literal values or references to other pipeline objects.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_objects.fields.key: The key is the name of the field in a Data Pipeline object definition, such as 'name', 'type', or 'schedule'.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_objects.fields.ref_value: The reference to another pipeline object's ID, used to link objects within the pipeline definition.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_objects.fields.string_value: Sets the literal string value for a field in a Data Pipeline object definition, used when the field holds a direct string rather than a reference to another pipeline object.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_objects.id: The unique identifier for this pipeline object within the pipeline definition, used to reference it from other objects.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_objects.name: The user-defined name of a pipeline object within the AWS Data Pipeline definition.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_tags.key: The key of a tag applied to the Data Pipeline, used to categorize and manage the pipeline within AWS.
aws_data_pipeline_pipeline.pipeline_tags.value: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the Data Pipeline, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_data_sync_location_azure_blob.tags.value: The value part of a key-value tag assigned to this AWS DataSync location for Azure Blob storage, used to identify and organize the resource.

aws_data_sync_location_efs.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to this AWS DataSync EFS location, used to identify and manage the resource.
aws_data_sync_location_efs.tags.value: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to this AWS DataSync location for EFS, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_data_sync_location_fsx_lustre.tags.key: The key of a tag to apply to the DataSync location for an FSx for Lustre file system, used for identifying and organizing the location.

aws_data_sync_location_fsx_ontap.tags.key: The key of a key-value tag applied to the FSx for ONTAP DataSync location, used to organize and identify the location for management and cost allocation.

aws_data_sync_location_fsx_open_zfs.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag (key-value pair) applied to the FSx for OpenZFS DataSync location, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_data_sync_location_fsx_windows.tags.key: The key of a tag that you can assign to the DataSync location for FSx for Windows File Server, used to identify and manage the resource.
aws_data_sync_location_fsx_windows.tags.value: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag applied to the FSx for Windows File Server DataSync location, used for cost allocation and resource management.

aws_data_sync_location_hdfs.name_nodes.hostname: The hostname or IP address of the HDFS NameNode to which AWS DataSync connects, part of the name_nodes list for the HDFS location.
aws_data_sync_location_hdfs.name_nodes.port: The port number on which the HDFS NameNode service is listening for connections.
aws_data_sync_location_hdfs.tags.value: The value portion of a key-value tag that you assign to this AWS DataSync HDFS location, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_data_sync_location_nfs.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag attached to this AWS DataSync location for NFS, used for metadata, identification, and cost allocation.

aws_data_sync_location_object_storage.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the DataSync object storage location, used to organize and identify the location for cost tracking and management.
aws_data_sync_location_object_storage.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag attached to this AWS DataSync location for object storage, used for identifying, categorizing, or managing the resource.

aws_data_sync_location_s3.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS DataSync S3 location, used to organize and identify the resource.
aws_data_sync_location_s3.tags.value: The value portion of a tag attached to this DataSync S3 location, used to identify or categorize the resource.

aws_data_sync_location_smb.tags.key: The key of a tag to assign to the DataSync SMB location, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_data_sync_task.excludes: Specifies the filter rules that define which files or directories to exclude from the data transfer, using pattern-based matching to skip matching paths during the sync task.
aws_data_sync_task.excludes.filter_type: Specifies the type of filter rule used to exclude files from the DataSync task, where the only supported value is 'SIMPLE_PATTERN' for simple pattern matching.
aws_data_sync_task.excludes.value: Specifies a pattern value for an entry in the task's Excludes filter list, which tells DataSync which files or objects to skip during a transfer using the simple pattern matching syntax.
aws_data_sync_task.includes: Specifies a list of filter rules that determine which files or S3 objects to include in the DataSync task, with each rule defining an Attribute (e.g., file path) and a Value pattern to match.
aws_data_sync_task.includes.filter_type: Specifies the filter type for the DataSync task's includes list, which determines how the filter pattern is applied (e.g., SIMPLE_PATTERN) to include files or objects in the transfer.
aws_data_sync_task.includes.value: The value pattern for an include filter rule, such as a file path or wildcard expression, that specifies which files or objects DataSync includes in the transfer.
aws_data_sync_task.tags.key: The key of a tag to associate with the AWS DataSync task, enabling you to categorize and manage tasks by metadata.
aws_data_sync_task.tags.value: The value of the tag assigned to the DataSync task, used for organizing and managing the task in AWS.

aws_data_zone_connection.aws_location.access_role: The ARN of the IAM role that DataZone assumes to access the AWS location (e.g., an S3 bucket) for this data connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.aws_location.aws_account_id: The AWS account ID of the AWS location (account and region) where the DataZone connection is hosted.
aws_data_zone_connection.aws_location.aws_region: The AWS region where the underlying data source resource (for example, a Redshift cluster or AWS Glue database) is located, used by Amazon DataZone to configure the connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.aws_location.iam_connection_id: The `iam_connection_id` field in `aws_location` specifies the identifier of the IAM role or connection used by the AWS DataZone connection to access resources in the specified AWS account and region.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.amazon_qproperties: Configuration for connecting DataZone to Amazon Q Business, including the IAM role and Amazon Q Business application used by the connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.amazon_qproperties.auth_mode: Specifies the authentication mode used to connect to Amazon Q from AWS DataZone, controlling how the connection credentials are handled and accepted.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.amazon_qproperties.is_enabled: Indicates whether the Amazon Q integration is enabled for this DataZone connection, controlling whether the connection can be used with Amazon Q features.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.amazon_qproperties.profile_arn: The ARN of the Amazon Q profile associated with the Data Zone connection, enabling Amazon Q integration for this connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.athena_properties: Provides the Athena-specific properties for the connection, such as the Athena workgroup that defines the SQL query execution context.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.athena_properties.workgroup_name: The name of the Athena workgroup that this DataZone connection uses for querying data.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.glue_properties: The glue_properties object holds the configuration for an AWS Glue connection, specifically the name of the Glue connection that this DataZone connection will use.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.glue_properties.glue_connection_in: The AWS Glue connection input that defines the parameters (such as connection type, properties, and authentication details) for the Glue connection used by the DataZone connection.

Specifies the authentication type and secret ARN (e.g., USERNAME_PASSWORD or IAM) used by the underlying AWS Glue connection, allowing the DataZone connection to securely authenticate to the target data source.
Specifies the authentication method (e.g., BASIC, OAUTH2) used for the AWS Glue connection, determining how credentials are supplied for the connection.
Specifies the username and password credentials used for basic authentication when the underlying AWS Glue connection accesses the external data source.
The password to authenticate with when using basic authentication for the Glue connection defined in this Data Zone connection's Glue properties.
The username used for basic authentication within the AWS Glue connection's authentication configuration, serving as the principal credential for connecting to the data source.
Provides the custom authentication credentials (as a JSON map of key-value pairs) for the Glue connection's authentication configuration, used when the authentication type is set to custom.
The ARN of an AWS KMS key used to encrypt the connection details (such as credentials) in this Glue connection's authentication configuration.
Defines the OAuth2 authentication parameters (such as grant type, client application, and token URL) for the underlying AWS Glue connection when the authentication type is set to OAuth2.

This object specifies the authorization code flow parameters for OAuth2 authentication (such as authorization code, token URL, and refresh URL) used within the Glue connection's authentication configuration for the DataZone connection.
The OAuth2 authorization code used to exchange for access and refresh tokens when authenticating the AWS Glue connection in Amazon Data Zone.
Specifies the redirect URI that the OAuth2 authorization code flow uses to redirect the user after authorization for this Glue connection.
Specifies the OAuth2 client application used for authentication within this connection's OAuth2 properties, which may be either an AWS-managed or a user-managed client application with credentials.
Identifier of the AWS-managed OAuth2 client application used for authentication in the AWS Glue connection of this DataZone connection.
The client ID of the user-managed OAuth2 client application used for authentication in the Glue connection.
Provides the OAuth2 credentials (including authorization code, JWT token, refresh token, or client secret) used to authenticate the Glue connection referenced by this AWS DataZone connection.
The OAuth2 access token used to authenticate to the target system for the AWS Glue connection.
The JWT (JSON Web Token) used for OAuth2 authentication in the Glue connection's authentication configuration, enabling secure access to the data source.
The OAuth2 refresh token used to obtain a new access token when the current access token expires, for authenticating the AWS Glue connection.
The client secret for a user-managed OAuth2 client application, used to authenticate the Glue connection within the DataZone connection's authentication configuration.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 grant type (e.g., AUTHORIZATION_CODE, CLIENT_CREDENTIALS) used by the AWS Glue OAuth2 authentication configuration for the connection.
The URL of the OAuth2 token endpoint used by the AWS Glue connection for authentication.
A map of key-value pairs that are appended as query parameters to the OAuth2 token request URL for the Glue connection.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials used to authenticate the Glue connection within this DataZone connection.
Specifies the key-value connection properties for the AWS Glue connection, such as the JDBC URL, username, and password, whose expected keys vary by the Glue connection type.
Specifies the type of the underlying AWS Glue connection (e.g., JDBC, SFTP, MONGODB, KAFKA) that this DataZone connection uses.
The user-provided description of the AWS Glue connection, offering additional context about the connection within the data zone connection setup.
A list of UTF-8 strings that define the criteria AWS Glue uses to match this connection to data catalog resources, mirroring the MatchCriteria field of the AWS Glue ConnectionInput API.
Specifies the name of the AWS Glue connection that this DataZone connection references or creates.
Specifies the physical connectivity requirements for the underlying AWS Glue connection, including the subnet ID, security group IDs, and availability zone where the connection's resources reside.

Specifies the Availability Zone (e.g., us-east-1a) of the subnet in the physical connection requirements for the AWS Glue connection, which determines the zone where the connection's network resources are provisioned.
Specifies the list of VPC security group IDs that define the network security rules for the AWS Glue connection used by the DataZone connection.
The subnet ID within the VPC where AWS Glue places elastic network interfaces for the physical connection, enabling network access between the connection and the target data store.
Specifies the list of subnet IDs in the virtual private cloud (VPC) that the underlying AWS Glue connection uses for its physical network connectivity.

A dynamic map of Apache Spark configuration properties (key-value pairs) for the AWS Glue connection input, used by AWS DataZone to customize Spark behavior when interacting with the connected data source.
When enabled, AWS DataZone validates the AWS Glue connection's credentials during connection creation or update, ensuring the credentials are functional before the connection is provisioned.
Specifies the compute environments (such as SPARK or ATHENA) for which the connection is validated.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.hyper_pod_properties.cluster_name: The name of the SageMaker HyperPod cluster that this DataZone connection targets, used to associate the connection with a specific compute cluster for data access operations.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.iam_properties: This object specifies the IAM role that AWS DataZone assumes when connecting to the external data source, enabling secure access for the connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.iam_properties.glue_lineage_sync_e: Specifies whether AWS Glue lineage sync is enabled for this Data Zone connection, allowing lineage metadata to be captured from Glue catalogs.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.lakehouse_properties.glue_lineage_: Indicates whether lineage metadata for the lakehouse connection is automatically synchronized with AWS Glue.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.mlflow_properties: Specifies the MLflow-specific configuration for an AWS Data Zone connection, including the MLflow tracking server endpoint and any associated authentication settings.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.mlflow_properties.tracking_server_: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the MLflow tracking server that this DataZone connection uses for accessing experiment tracking and model registry data.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties: Specifies the Amazon Redshift connection settings for the Data Zone connection, including the cluster endpoint and database details needed to connect to the Redshift data source.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.credentials: The `credentials` object within `redshift_properties` specifies the authentication details (such as a reference to an AWS Secrets Manager secret) used by AWS DataZone to securely connect to the Amazon Redshift cluster.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.credentials.se: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Amazon Redshift database credentials used by this DataZone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.credentials.us: Specifies the username and password pair used to authenticate against the Amazon Redshift data source when establishing this DataZone connection.
The password portion of the username and password credentials used to authenticate to the Amazon Redshift cluster when connecting via DataZone.
The username part of the username/password credentials used to authenticate to the connected Amazon Redshift cluster.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.database_name: The name of the Redshift database that this DataZone connection uses to connect to the Redshift cluster.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.host: The hostname of the Amazon Redshift cluster endpoint that the connection targets.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.lineage_sync: This object defines how data lineage metadata is automatically synced from the connected Redshift source, including whether it is enabled and the schedule for the sync operation.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.lineage_sync.e: A boolean that turns on or off the automatic synchronization of data lineage for the Redshift connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.lineage_sync.s: Specifies the cron-based schedule that determines when AWS DataZone runs the Redshift lineage sync for this connection.
Specifies the cron expression that defines how often AWS Data Zone syncs lineage metadata from the Redshift connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.port: The network port on which the Amazon Redshift cluster accepts connections, used as part of the redshift properties for this DataZone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.storage: The storage object in the DataZone connection's Redshift properties specifies whether the connection targets a provisioned Redshift cluster or a serverless workgroup and includes the relevant cluster or workgroup identifiers and IAM role for access.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.storage.cluste: The name of the Amazon Redshift cluster hosting the storage that this DataZone connection is configured to use.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.redshift_properties.storage.workgr: This field specifies the name of the Amazon Redshift Serverless workgroup that the DataZone connection's storage configuration uses for data access.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.s3_properties: Defines the Amazon S3-specific connection settings, such as the target bucket and object path, for a DataZone connection to an S3 data source.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.s3_properties.register_s3_access_g: Determines whether the S3 location is registered as an access grant location in Amazon Data Zone, enabling access grants to be created for that location.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.s3_properties.s3_access_grant_loca: The identifier of the S3 Access Grant location that this DataZone connection uses to grant access to data in S3.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.s3_properties.s3_uri: The Amazon S3 URI (e.g., s3://bucket-name/prefix) that specifies the location used by the connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_emr_properties: The set of configuration properties AWS DataZone uses to connect to a Spark application on an Amazon EMR cluster.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_emr_properties.compute_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon EMR cluster or compute environment that AWS DataZone uses to run Apache Spark jobs for this connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_emr_properties.instance_prof: The ARN of the IAM instance profile that the Amazon EMR cluster assumes to access AWS resources when running Spark workloads through this DataZone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_emr_properties.log_uri: The S3 URI (e.g., s3://bucket/logs/) used as the log destination for Amazon EMR Spark jobs configured in the DataZone connection's Spark EMR properties.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_emr_properties.managed_endpo: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the managed endpoint on the Amazon EMR cluster that AWS DataZone connects to for Spark workloads.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_emr_properties.python_virtua: The S3 URI of a zipped Python virtual environment used to run PySpark jobs on the Amazon EMR cluster associated with this Data Zone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_emr_properties.runtime_role: The ARN of the IAM role that the Spark EMR runtime assumes when running data processing tasks for this AWS Data Zone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_emr_properties.trusted_certi: The S3 URI of a location containing trusted certificates used to validate the connection to an Amazon EMR cluster for the DataZone Spark EMR connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_glue_properties: Specifies the configuration for connecting Amazon Data Zone to AWS Glue for Spark workloads, including the execution role and Glue connection details that enable data access and processing.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_glue_properties.additional_a: Defines key-value arguments that are passed to the AWS Glue or Apache Spark environment for this DataZone connection, enabling customization of the runtime configuration.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_glue_properties.glue_connect: The name of the AWS Glue connection to be used by Spark jobs in this DataZone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_glue_properties.glue_version: Specifies the version of AWS Glue to use for the Spark Glue connection in the DataZone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_glue_properties.number_of_wo: Specifies the number of worker nodes to allocate for the AWS Glue Spark job associated with this Data Zone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_glue_properties.python_virtu: Specifies the Amazon S3 URI of the Python virtual environment used by the AWS Glue Spark job for this DataZone connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.spark_glue_properties.worker_type: Specifies the AWS Glue worker type (e.g., Standard, G.1X, G.2X) used for the Spark job associated with the DataZone connection's Spark Glue properties.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.workflows_mwaa_properties: Specifies the Amazon MWAA environment ARN and IAM execution role ARN that AWS DataZone uses to orchestrate workflows for this connection.
aws_data_zone_connection.props.workflows_mwaa_properties.mwaa_env: The name of the Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) environment associated with the DataZone connection's workflow configuration.

aws_data_zone_data_source.asset_forms_input.content: The JSON-encoded content of the asset form input, which provides the metadata values to be associated with the asset when the data source is run.
aws_data_zone_data_source.asset_forms_input.form_name: The name of the metadata form to associate with each asset ingested through this data source, determining which form schema is applied to the asset metadata.
aws_data_zone_data_source.asset_forms_input.type_identifier: The identifier of the metadata form type that defines the structure and fields for this asset form input, used when creating or updating assets in Amazon DataZone.
aws_data_zone_data_source.asset_forms_input.type_revision: The revision identifier of the asset form type to apply, indicating which version of the form schema the data source should use when creating an asset's metadata.
aws_data_zone_data_source.configuration.glue_run_configuration: Specifies the AWS Glue database and optional filter expression used to discover and ingest data from Glue tables into the DataZone data source.
aws_data_zone_data_source.configuration.glue_run_configuration.aut: When set to true, this boolean enables automatic import of AWS Glue Data Quality results into Amazon DataZone for the data source.
aws_data_zone_data_source.configuration.glue_run_configuration.cat: The name of the AWS Glue catalog that contains the database and table from which this data source will import metadata.
aws_data_zone_data_source.configuration.glue_run_configuration.dat: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DataZone assumes to access the AWS Glue data catalog and resources for this data source.
aws_data_zone_data_source.configuration.glue_run_configuration.rel: Specifies a list of relational filter configurations, each defining a database name, optional schema name, and optional filter expression to select which tables from the AWS Glue Data Catalog are ingested by the DataZone data source.
The name of the AWS Glue database in the Data Catalog that the DataZone data source reads from when using this Glue run configuration.

List of filter expressions, each containing an expression string and a type (e.g., INCLUDE or EXCLUDE), that determine which database objects (tables or views) in the corresponding relational data source are included in or excluded from metadata ingestion in AWS DataZone.
The SQL-like filter expression string used to include or exclude specific rows from the source table when the DataZone data source runs against the Glue relational configuration.
The type of the filter expression, which indicates whether the expression is an inclusion (INCLUDE) or exclusion (EXCLUDE) rule for the relational data source tables.

For an AWS DataZone data source with a Glue run configuration, this schema name specifies the database schema within the relational database whose tables are considered for ingestion, as refined by the associated filter expressions.
aws_data_zone_data_source.configuration.redshift_run_configuration: Specifies the Redshift-specific settings (such as the IAM role, credential and storage configuration, and relational filter configurations) used when AWS DataZone runs this data source against an Amazon Redshift cluster.
The IAM role (ARN) that AWS Data Zone assumes to access the Amazon Redshift instance or database during data source runs.
Configures the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials used to connect to and query the Amazon Redshift cluster during a data source run.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Redshift credentials used to connect to the Redshift data source.

Specifies the Amazon Redshift storage source for the DataZone data source, selecting either a Redshift cluster or a Redshift Serverless workgroup via its nested RedshiftClusterSource or RedshiftServerlessSource property.
Specifies the Amazon Redshift cluster that acts as the storage source for the data source, containing the cluster name for the Redshift run configuration.
The name of the Amazon Redshift cluster that AWS Data Zone uses as the source for ingesting data into the data source.
Specifies the Amazon Redshift Serverless workgroup that provides the storage for the Redshift data source, identifying the serverless workgroup by its name.
The name of the Redshift Serverless workgroup that serves as the data source for this Amazon Data Zone data source.
Defines the list of Redshift relational filter configurations, each specifying a database, schema, table, and filter expression to control which rows are ingested during a data source run.
The name of the Redshift database to which this relational filter configuration applies.
The list of filter expressions that define which rows of the Redshift relational table are included or excluded when the DataZone data source ingests or accesses the data.
The SQL filter expression text used to select a subset of rows from the Redshift table during data ingestion.
The type of the filter expression, indicating whether the expression includes or excludes matching data assets (e.g., INCLUDE or EXCLUDE).
The name of the database schema to include when filtering relational tables for the Redshift data source run.
aws_data_zone_data_source.configuration.sage_maker_run_configurati: Specifies the SageMaker tracking assets (ARNs) that this Amazon DataZone data source will run against to discover and import metadata from SageMaker Studio.
Specifies the list of SageMaker asset types (e.g., SageMakerModelQualityJobDefinition) whose metadata this DataZone data source will track and ingest from SageMaker runs.
aws_data_zone_data_source.schedule.timezone: The IANA timezone name (e.g., 'America/New_York') used to interpret the cron expression for the data source's scheduled refresh.

aws_data_zone_domain.tags.key: The key (e.g., 'Environment') of a tag to attach to the Amazon DataZone domain, used to organize and manage the domain resource in AWS.
aws_data_zone_domain.tags.value: The value component of a tag applied to the DataZone domain, which can be used for resource identification, categorization, and cost tracking.

aws_data_zone_environment.user_parameters.name: Specifies the name of a user parameter for the environment, which must match a parameter defined by the environment blueprint to configure the deployed environment.
aws_data_zone_environment.user_parameters.value: The value for a user-defined parameter (keyed by the sibling 'name') used to configure the AWS DataZone environment.

aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.created_at: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the environment blueprint configuration was created.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.domain_id: The unique identifier of the Amazon Data Zone domain to which this environment blueprint configuration belongs.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.domain_identifier: The unique identifier of the Amazon Data Zone domain for which this environment blueprint configuration is defined.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.enabled_regions: The list of AWS Regions in which this environment blueprint configuration is enabled and can be used to provision Data Zone environments.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.environment_blueprint_id: The unique identifier of the environment blueprint that this configuration is associated with, identifying which blueprint's provisioning settings are defined.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.environment_blueprint_identifier: The unique identifier (name or ID) of the Amazon DataZone environment blueprint that this configuration applies to within the domain.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.environment_role_permission_boundary: The ARN of an IAM policy used as the permission boundary for the environment's service role, limiting the maximum permissions that can be granted to the role.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.manage_access_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that permits Amazon DataZone to manage access to resources created for the environment blueprint.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.provisioning_configurations: Specifies the list of AWS regions where environments can be provisioned from this blueprint, along with the IAM environment role ARN to use for each region.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.provisioning_configurations.lake_formati: Defines the AWS Lake Formation configuration for the environment blueprint, specifying how Data Zone provisions and manages Lake Formation data lake resources, including trusted service principals and location registration settings, when creating environments from the blueprint.
Defines a list of S3 paths to exclude from Lake Formation location registration when provisioning the environment, preventing those locations from being registered as data lake locations.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DataZone uses to register data lake locations with Lake Formation for this environment blueprint configuration.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.provisioning_role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DataZone assumes to provision and manage resources for environments created from this blueprint configuration.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.regional_parameters: Specifies a list of region-specific parameter settings, where each item contains an AWS Region and a set of key-value configuration parameters applied to the environment blueprint in that region.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.regional_parameters.parameters: The parameters map within each regional parameter set provides the blueprint configuration key-value pairs to be used for environments in that specific AWS region, allowing region-specific overrides.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.regional_parameters.region: The AWS region (e.g., us-east-1) to which this set of regional blueprint configuration parameters applies.
aws_data_zone_environment_blueprint_conf.updated_at: The timestamp of when this environment blueprint configuration was last updated.

aws_data_zone_environment_profile.user_parameters.name: The name of a user-defined parameter configured in the environment profile, used to match or reference a parameter declared by the associated environment blueprint when provisioning an environment.
aws_data_zone_environment_profile.user_parameters.value: Sets the actual value for a user parameter in the environment profile, which is supplied as the value when the environment is provisioned from this profile.

aws_data_zone_form_type.model.smithy: The Smithy model definition that specifies the structure and validation rules for the form type.

aws_data_zone_owner.owner_type: Indicates whether the owner associated with the DataZone resource is a user or a group, as determined by the service.

aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.add_to_project_member_pool: Configures the ADD_TO_PROJECT_MEMBER_POOL policy grant, determining the settings that allow the grantee to add members to a project's member pool.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.add_to_project_member_pool.includ: Whether the policy grant also applies to child domain units when adding a member to the project member pool.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_asset_type: For an AWS DataZone policy grant, this nested object configures the CreateAssetType policy, where its 'include_child_domain_units' field determines whether the permission to create asset types also applies to child domain units.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_asset_type.include_child_d: Determines whether the permissions granted by this CreateAssetType policy are also applied to child domain units within the parent domain unit.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_domain_unit: Configures the 'Create Domain Unit' policy grant detail, an empty object that, when present, grants the principal permission to create domain units within the DataZone domain.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_domain_unit.include_child_: When creating a domain unit policy grant, this boolean indicates whether the grant applies to child domain units as well as the target domain unit.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_environment_from_blueprint: Specifies the policy grant detail that grants the principal permission to create an environment from a blueprint in Amazon Data Zone.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_environment_profile: This object contains the policy grant details for allowing a principal to create environment profiles in AWS DataZone, including the domain units under which the permission applies.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_environment_profile.domain: The identifier of the DataZone domain unit to which the create environment profile policy grant applies.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_form_type: Specifies the policy grant details for creating form types, including whether the permission also applies to child domain units.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_form_type.include_child_do: Specifies whether the permission to create form types also applies to child domain units within the domain, extending the grant to subdomains.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_glossary: This object defines the policy grant details for creating glossaries in Amazon DataZone, allowing the specified principal to create glossary entries within the target domain or project.
