aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_glossary.include_child_dom: Specifies whether the permission granted to create glossaries also applies to child domain units of the specified domain unit.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_project: The create_project details of the policy grant, used when the policy type is set to CREATE_PROJECT, specifying the permissions for creating projects in Amazon Data Zone.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_project.include_child_doma: When true, the permission to create projects is extended to all child domain units beneath the target domain unit, rather than being limited to that domain unit alone.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.create_project_from_project_profi: The create_project_from_project_profile object defines the policy grant configuration for allowing a principal to create projects from a project profile, typically containing the list of project profile identifiers the grant applies to.
Whether the policy grant for creating a project from a project profile also applies to child domain units, enabling the create-project action to be performed in those child domain units as well.
The list of DataZone project profile identifiers that the policy grant applies to, allowing the grantee to create projects from these specific project profiles.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.delegate_create_environment_profi: When enabled, this flag allows the policy grantee to delegate the ability to create environment profiles to other principals.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.override_domain_unit_owners: This nested object represents the details of an 'override domain unit owners' policy grant, with an `enabled` boolean indicating whether the grant overrides the domain unit's existing owner list.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.override_domain_unit_owners.inclu: A boolean flag that, when true, extends the domain unit owner override to also apply to all child domain units of the specified domain unit.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.override_project_owners: This object contains the detail settings for a policy grant of type OVERRIDE_PROJECT_OWNERS, which grants the principal the ability to override project ownership within AWS DataZone.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.detail.override_project_owners.include_c: When set to true, the project owner override also applies to child domain units, propagating the ownership change down the domain unit hierarchy.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.domain_identifier: The identifier of the Amazon DataZone domain where the policy grant is created.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.entity_identifier: The identifier of the Data Zone entity (such as a project, domain, or user) to which the policy grant applies.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.entity_type: Specifies the type of DataZone entity (such as 'project', 'user', or 'group') that this policy grant targets, used together with the entity identifier to define the grant's scope.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.policy_type: Specifies the type of policy grant being created, such as CREATE_DOMAIN_UNIT or DELETE_DOMAIN_UNIT, which dictates the specific permission granted on the target entity.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal: The user, group, or role to which the policy grant is assigned, specifying the principal type and identifier to control which entity receives the granted permissions.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.domain_unit: Identifies a domain unit as the principal for the policy grant, so that the grant applies to all users and groups within that domain unit.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.domain_unit.domain_unit_design: Specifies the role (owner or member) within the domain unit principal that the policy grant applies to, controlling which users in that domain unit are granted the policy.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.domain_unit.domain_unit_grant_: Defines a filter that specifies whether the policy grant applies to all domain units within the domain unit principal or only to a specific list of domain unit IDs, used to scope the grant for a domain unit principal.
When set to an empty object, this field configures the policy grant to apply to all domain units within the DataZone domain.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.domain_unit.domain_unit_identi: The identifier of the Amazon DataZone domain unit that acts as the principal for this policy grant, determining which domain unit receives the granted permissions.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.group: Specifies the group principal for the policy grant, containing the unique identifier of the AWS DataZone group that receives the granted permissions.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.group.group_identifier: The identifier of the group that is the principal receiving the policy grant in AWS DataZone.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.project: The project object representing the Amazon Data Zone project that will receive the permissions granted by this policy grant.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.project.project_designation: Specifies whether the project principal is identified by its project ID or its project name, enabling the policy grant to reference a project as the grant principal.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.project.project_grant_filter: Configures a domain unit filter that restricts the policy grant to only members of the project who belong to the specified domain unit.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.project.project_grant_filter.d: Specifies a domain unit filter that scopes the project-level policy grant to apply only to the designated domain units within the data zone.
The identifier of the AWS Data Zone domain unit used by the domain unit filter to scope this policy grant for the specified project principal.
Specifies whether the policy grant to the project principal also applies to all child domain units underneath the domain unit selected in this filter.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.project.project_identifier: The identifier of the Amazon DataZone project that serves as the principal for the policy grant, granting permissions to that project.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.user: Defines the user principal to which the policy grant is assigned, specifying the Amazon DataZone user by its unique identifier.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.user.all_users_grant_filter: A boolean flag that, when set to true, grants the policy to all users in the DataZone domain rather than to a specific user identifier.
aws_data_zone_policy_grant.principal.user.user_identifier: Specifies the user identifier of the AWS DataZone user who is the principal receiving this policy grant, determining which user the granted permissions apply to.

aws_data_zone_project.membership_assignments.designation: Specifies the access role (e.g., OWNER or CONTRIBUTOR) granted to the member in the project assignment.
aws_data_zone_project.membership_assignments.member: The member object identifies the user or group in Amazon DataZone that is assigned to the project, specifying the principal's identifier and whether it is a USER or GROUP.
aws_data_zone_project.membership_assignments.member.group_iden: The identifier of the AWS DataZone group that is granted membership in the project.
aws_data_zone_project.membership_assignments.member.user_ident: Specifies the user identifier for a user assigned to the project via a membership assignment, used to grant that user access to project resources in AWS DataZone.
aws_data_zone_project.project_status: The current lifecycle status of the Data Zone project, such as 'ACTIVE' or 'DELETING'.
aws_data_zone_project.resource_tags.key: The key of a resource tag associated with the AWS Data Zone project, specifying the tag name used for identifying and organizing the project resource.
aws_data_zone_project.resource_tags.value: The value component of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS DataZone project, used for organizing and managing project resources.
aws_data_zone_project.user_parameters.environment_configuratio: Specifies the name of the environment configuration in the DataZone project to which this user parameter applies, allowing parameters to be scoped to a specific environment configuration.
aws_data_zone_project.user_parameters.environment_parameters: This field specifies a list of environment parameter objects that define configuration values for AWS Data Zone environments associated with the project, such as resource names or compute settings, which are applied when environments are created from the project's environment profiles.
aws_data_zone_project.user_parameters.environment_parameters.n: The name (key) of an environment parameter configured for the AWS DataZone project's environment, used to pass configuration values when the environment is provisioned.
aws_data_zone_project.user_parameters.environment_parameters.v: The value of an environment parameter in the project's user parameters, which is passed to the DataZone environment when the project is used.

aws_data_zone_project_membership.designation: Designates the role of the member in the DataZone project, determining their access permissions (for example, PROJECT_OWNER or PROJECT_CONTRIBUTOR).
aws_data_zone_project_membership.domain_identifier: The unique identifier of the Amazon DataZone domain in which the project and its membership are defined.
aws_data_zone_project_membership.member: Specifies the member to be added to the project, including the member's identifier and type (USER or GROUP).
aws_data_zone_project_membership.member.group_identifier: Specifies the identifier of the group that is being granted membership to the DataZone project.
aws_data_zone_project_membership.member.user_identifier: The identifier of the user who is being granted membership to the DataZone project, as recognized by the DataZone domain.
aws_data_zone_project_membership.member_identifier: The fully qualified identifier of the AWS principal (such as an IAM user ARN, role ARN, or AWS account ID) that is added as a member to the DataZone project.
aws_data_zone_project_membership.member_identifier_type: Specifies whether the member is a user or a group, determining how the member identifier is interpreted for this DataZone project membership.
aws_data_zone_project_membership.project_identifier: The unique identifier (ID) of the Amazon Data Zone project to which the member (user or group) is granted access.

aws_data_zone_project_profile.allow_custom_project_resource_tags: Indicates whether users are allowed to add custom tags to project resources (such as data assets or environments) when using this project profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.created_at: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when this DataZone project profile was created, assigned by the service and read-only.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.created_by: The identifier of the AWS principal (user or role) who created the DataZone project profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.description: A user-provided description of the project profile, which helps identify and document the purpose or characteristics of the profile within Amazon DataZone.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.domain_id: The unique identifier of the Amazon DataZone domain that this project profile belongs to.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.domain_identifier: The identifier of the Amazon DataZone domain in which the project profile is created.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.domain_unit_id: The service-assigned identifier of the AWS DataZone domain unit that this project profile is scoped to.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.domain_unit_identifier: The unique identifier of the Amazon DataZone domain unit that this project profile is associated with, used to scope the profile to a specific domain unit.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations: A computed list of environment configuration objects for this project profile, each containing the environment blueprint identifier and parameter settings that are applied to projects created from the profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.aws_account: Specifies the AWS account for a per-account environment configuration, controlling which AWS account is used when creating environments for a project in DataZone.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.aws_account.a: The AWS account identifier used when provisioning the environment defined in this project profile's environment configuration.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.aws_region.re: The name of the AWS region (such as us-east-1) where the environment configuration for this DataZone project profile is applied.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.configuration: Overrides the values of configuration parameters for an environment configuration, allowing the project profile to customize environment settings.
Indicates whether the user can edit this parameter override after the project profile has been created, controlling its mutability in the DataZone console or API.
Specifies the name of the environment parameter that this override entry replaces for the project profile's environment configuration.
The override value applied to the specified configuration parameter for the environment configuration of a Data Zone project profile.

The list of resolved environment parameter values for this environment configuration, representing the final effective values after merging the environment blueprint's default parameters with any overrides defined in the project profile.

The name (key) of a resolved environment configuration parameter, identifying which blueprint-defined parameter the corresponding value applies to in the DataZone project profile's environment configuration.
Specifies the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store path that provides the value for this configuration parameter in the environment configuration of the AWS DataZone project profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.deployment_or: The deployment_order specifies the sequential priority of this environment configuration within the project profile, so environments with lower numbers are deployed first when the profile's environment configurations are applied.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.description: Provides a user-defined description for an environment configuration, clarifying the purpose or role of a specific AWS environment (such as its account and region) associated with the DataZone project profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.environment_b: The identifier of the environment blueprint that defines the infrastructure and tools (e.g., a data lake blueprint) to be provisioned for the environment created from this configuration.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.environment_c: The environment_configuration_id uniquely identifies an environment configuration within the project profile, and it is used to reference the configuration that specifies the AWS account, region, and environment type for the environments associated with the profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.environment_configurations.name: The name of an environment configuration, acting as a distinct label for that environment within the AWS Data Zone project profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS DataZone to this project profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.last_updated_at: The timestamp indicating when the project profile was last updated, set automatically by AWS DataZone.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.project_resource_tags.is_value_editable: This boolean indicates whether the value of the project resource tag is editable by project members, so a value of false enforces a fixed tag value across project resources.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.project_resource_tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag applied to resources associated with an Amazon DataZone project profile.
aws_data_zone_project_profile.project_resource_tags.value: The value for a tag key in a project_resource_tags entry, which assigns a tag to the project resources of this AWS Data Zone project profile.

aws_data_zone_subscription_target.subscription_target_config.content: The JSON-encoded configuration payload for a subscription target form, which contains the target-specific parameters (such as the S3 bucket path, Glue database name, or Redshift cluster) required for delivering subscribed data.
aws_data_zone_subscription_target.subscription_target_config.form_name: The name of the metadata form that defines the schema and parameters for this AWS DataZone subscription target configuration.

aws_data_zone_user_profile.details: The computed details of the DataZone user profile, including the IAM or SSO identity information returned by the service.
aws_data_zone_user_profile.details.iam: Specifies the IAM user details for the DataZone user profile, including the ARN of the IAM user.
aws_data_zone_user_profile.details.iam.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM principal (user or role) associated with the DataZone user profile's IAM details.
aws_data_zone_user_profile.details.iam.group_profile_id: The unique identifier of the DataZone group profile associated with this IAM user profile, representing the IAM group membership for the user within the domain.
aws_data_zone_user_profile.details.iam.session_name: The session name that identifies a specific IAM role session when the Data Zone user profile is associated with an IAM role, enabling the profile to correspond to a particular role session.
aws_data_zone_user_profile.details.sso: Contains the IAM Identity Center (SSO) attributes, such as the user's first name, last name, and username, for the Amazon DataZone user profile.
aws_data_zone_user_profile.details.sso.first_name: The first name of the user as provided by the single sign-on (SSO) identity provider in the AWS Data Zone user profile.
aws_data_zone_user_profile.details.sso.last_name: The last name of the user as configured in the external SSO identity provider, used to display the user's name in Amazon DataZone.
aws_data_zone_user_profile.details.sso.username: The SSO username of the user associated with the AWS DataZone user profile.

aws_dax_cluster.arn: The ARN (Amazon Resource Name) of the DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster.
aws_dax_cluster.availability_zones: Specifies the Availability Zones in which the DAX cluster's nodes are placed, allowing you to distribute nodes across multiple AZs for high availability.
aws_dax_cluster.cluster_discovery_endpoint: The endpoint URL (ClusterDiscoveryEndpoint) that DAX client applications use to connect to the cluster, automatically assigned by AWS when the DAX cluster is created.
aws_dax_cluster.cluster_discovery_endpoint_url: The URL of the cluster discovery endpoint that DAX clients use to connect to the cluster.
aws_dax_cluster.cluster_endpoint_encryption_type: Specifies whether client traffic to the DAX cluster endpoint is encrypted with TLS (valid values: TLS or NONE).
aws_dax_cluster.cluster_name: The name of the DAX cluster, which is used as the cluster identifier; if not provided, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique name.
aws_dax_cluster.description: Provides a description of the DAX cluster.
aws_dax_cluster.iamrole_arn: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the DAX cluster uses to access DynamoDB and other required AWS services.
aws_dax_cluster.id: The unique identifier for the DAX cluster, set to the cluster name.
aws_dax_cluster.network_type: Specifies the network type for the DAX cluster, such as IPV4 or DUALSTACK, determining whether the cluster uses IPv4 only or supports both IPv4 and IPv6 addressing.
aws_dax_cluster.node_type: The compute instance type (e.g., dax.r4.large) used for each node in the DAX cluster, determining the memory and CPU capacity of the cluster's cache nodes.
aws_dax_cluster.notification_topic_arn: The ARN of an Amazon SNS topic to which DAX cluster notifications (such as maintenance events) are sent.
aws_dax_cluster.parameter_group_name: The name of the DAX parameter group that applies cluster-wide settings such as query caching and TTL behavior for this DynamoDB Accelerator cluster.
aws_dax_cluster.preferred_maintenance_window: Specifies the daily time range in UTC during which AWS DAX performs maintenance on the cluster, using the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi.
aws_dax_cluster.replication_factor: The total number of nodes (including the primary node) in the DAX cluster, which determines the cluster's read capacity and high availability.
aws_dax_cluster.security_group_ids: The list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the DAX cluster, controlling network access to the cluster.
aws_dax_cluster.ssespecification: Specifies whether server-side encryption is enabled for the DAX cluster by setting an Enabled flag in the SSESpecification object.
aws_dax_cluster.ssespecification.sseenabled: Enables or disables server-side encryption (SSE) for the DAX cluster, using AWS KMS to protect data at rest when enabled.
aws_dax_cluster.subnet_group_name: The name of the subnet group that defines the VPC subnets in which the DAX cluster nodes are launched.

aws_dax_parameter_group.description: A user-specified description that identifies the purpose or contents of this DAX parameter group.
aws_dax_parameter_group.id: The computed unique identifier for the DAX parameter group, which is its parameter group name.
aws_dax_parameter_group.parameter_group_name: The name of this DAX parameter group, which is used when associating the group with a DAX cluster and must be unique in the account and region.
aws_dax_parameter_group.parameter_name_values: Specifies the name-value pairs of DAX parameters to apply to the parameter group, where each key is a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) parameter name and its value is the parameter's configured value.

aws_dax_subnet_group.description: An optional user-provided description that identifies the purpose or context of this DAX subnet group.
aws_dax_subnet_group.id: The name of the DAX subnet group, which uniquely identifies the resource within AWS.
aws_dax_subnet_group.subnet_group_name: The name of this DAX subnet group; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name based on the logical resource ID.
aws_dax_subnet_group.subnet_ids: The list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the DAX cluster will be deployed, defining the network locations for the cluster's nodes.

aws_deadline_budget.actions.description: A human-readable description of a budget action, explaining the action taken when the budget threshold is reached.
aws_deadline_budget.actions.threshold_percentage: The percentage of the budget's usage threshold that, when reached, triggers the corresponding budget action (such as stopping or limiting the farm).
aws_deadline_budget.actions.type: Defines the type of budget action to take when the threshold is reached, such as STOP_SESSION_WORKER or STOP_QUEUE.
aws_deadline_budget.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Deadline budget, used for organizing and managing the budget resource.

aws_deadline_farm.arn: The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the farm, used to reference the farm across AWS services and in IAM policies.
aws_deadline_farm.description: A human-readable description of the Deadline Cloud farm, used to identify the farm's purpose or details.
aws_deadline_farm.display_name: Specifies the human-readable name for the farm, which is used to identify it in the AWS Deadline Cloud console and API operations.
aws_deadline_farm.farm_id: The unique identifier assigned to the farm by AWS Deadline when the farm is created.
aws_deadline_farm.kms_key_arn: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data for the AWS Deadline Cloud farm; if not provided, AWS uses an AWS-managed key.
aws_deadline_farm.tags.key: The user-defined key for a tag attached to the AWS Deadline Cloud farm, used to identify and organize the resource.
aws_deadline_farm.tags.value: Specifies the value of a tag applied to the AWS Deadline Farm, allowing you to categorize and manage the farm with custom metadata such as cost allocation or team identification.

aws_deadline_fleet.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Deadline fleet.
aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities: This read-only object describes the effective resource capabilities of the fleet, such as CPU architecture, CPU count, memory size, and GPU resources, as reported by AWS Deadline Cloud after fleet creation.
aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.amounts: Specifies the list of amount capabilities for the fleet, where each object defines a named resource (e.g. memory or CPU) along with its minimum and maximum amount that a worker can provide.
aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.amounts.max: Specifies the upper bound of a numeric amount capability (e.g., memory or CPU count) that a fleet worker in AWS Deadline Cloud can provide, used to define a valid range alongside the min value.
aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.amounts.min: The minimum numeric amount of a specific capability (e.g., vCPUs or memory) that the Deadline fleet can offer, used to match jobs requiring at least that amount.
aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.amounts.name: The name of the amount capability, which is a string key identifying the resource quantity (e.g., 'gpu' or 'memory') that the fleet advertises in its capabilities.
aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.attributes: Specifies the list of attribute capabilities for the fleet, where each entry defines a custom attribute name and its set of allowed values that workers in the fleet must support.
aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.attributes.name: The name of a single fleet capability attribute (for example, 'GPU' or 'OS') within the attributes list of the fleet's capabilities.
aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.attributes.values: Specifies the list of values for a specific attribute within the fleet's capabilities, enabling job definitions to match fleets based on these attribute values when scheduling jobs in AWS Deadline Cloud.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration: Defines the compute environment for the fleet, selecting either a service-managed Amazon EC2 configuration (specifying instance types, allocation strategy, and capacity) or a customer-managed configuration (specifying worker capabilities such as operating system, CPU, and memory).
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.customer_managed: Specifies the customer-managed configuration for the fleet, including the required worker capabilities (such as CPU architecture, memory, and OS) and the usage mode indicating whether those capabilities are mandatory.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.customer_managed.auto_scal: Configures the minimum and maximum worker count that the customer-managed fleet's auto-scaling uses to scale worker instances in response to job demand.
Specifies the maximum number of worker instances that can be added to the customer-managed fleet per minute during a scale-out event.
Specifies the number of idle workers to maintain as standby capacity, reducing the time jobs wait for worker availability in the auto-scaling fleet.
The number of seconds a worker can remain idle before it is considered idle by the auto-scaling policy and potentially scaled down.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.customer_managed.mode: The operating mode of the customer-managed fleet, set to either RESUME (active and accepting jobs) or PAUSE (suspended and not accepting jobs).
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.customer_managed.storage_p: The unique identifier of the storage profile that defines the file system locations available to this customer-managed fleet.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.customer_managed.tag_propa: Determines whether tags applied to the fleet are propagated to the underlying EC2 worker instances in a customer-managed fleet, with supported values like NONE (no propagation) or TO_EC2 (propagate tags to EC2 instances).
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.customer_managed.worker_ca: Defines the hardware and OS capabilities (CPU architecture, OS type, memory, vCPU count, and accelerator types) that worker instances in a customer-managed AWS Deadline Cloud fleet must have.
Defines the minimum and maximum number of accelerator devices (e.g., GPUs) that must be available on a worker in a customer-managed AWS Deadline fleet.
The maximum number of accelerators (e.g., GPUs) a single worker in the customer-managed fleet can have, serving as the upper bound for the accelerator count range in worker capabilities.
The minimum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that each worker in the customer-managed fleet must have available.
Specifies the minimum and maximum total accelerator memory in MiB for workers in this customer-managed fleet, used by Deadline Cloud to match tasks requiring a certain amount of accelerator memory.
The maximum total accelerator memory in mebibytes (MiB) allowed on a worker for this customer-managed fleet, used to match workers to job requirements.
The minimum total accelerator memory in MiB that a worker must have for the customer-managed fleet to be eligible.
Specifies the GPU accelerator types (e.g., specific GPU model names) available on the worker, which Deadline Cloud uses to match jobs requiring those accelerator types.
Specifies the CPU architecture (x86_64 or arm64) of the worker instances in a customer managed Deadline fleet, used to match jobs that require a specific architecture.

Defines user-defined numeric capability amounts (each with a name and value) that worker instances in a customer-managed fleet advertise, allowing job requirements to match against these custom worker capacity metrics.
The maximum value for a custom worker capability amount in a customer-managed Deadline fleet, capping the upper end of the numeric range that can be reported for that capability.
The minimum value for this custom worker capability amount, used as the lower bound when matching jobs to fleet worker capabilities.
The name of a custom worker capability amount, serving as the identifier or key for the user-defined capability metric on the fleet's worker nodes.
Specifies custom worker attributes as key-value pairs that define the worker's capabilities, allowing Deadline Cloud to match jobs to appropriate customer-managed fleet workers.
Specifies the name (key) of a custom worker capability attribute used to match worker capacity requirements for a customer-managed fleet.
The list of values for a custom attribute that defines a worker's capability, used to match jobs to appropriate workers in a Deadline fleet.
The maximum memory capacity in MiB that a worker in this customer-managed fleet is expected to have, used by Deadline Cloud to match jobs to fleets based on resource requirements.
The minimum amount of memory in MiB that a worker must have to be considered eligible when using customer-managed fleets in AWS Deadline Cloud.
Specifies the operating system family (e.g., Linux or Windows) that workers in a customer-managed fleet must match for task scheduling.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of vCPUs that each worker instance can have in the customer-managed fleet.
The maximum number of vCPUs that a worker in the customer-managed fleet can use.
The minimum number of vCPUs that a worker in the customer-managed fleet must have for the fleet to consider it usable when matching jobs.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.service_managed_ec2: The service-managed EC2 configuration specifies the EC2 instances that AWS Deadline Cloud automatically launches and manages for this fleet, including instance capabilities and instance count limits.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.service_managed_ec2.auto_s: Specifies the minimum and maximum number of worker instances for the service-managed EC2 fleet, enabling automatic scaling within these bounds.
Determines the number of worker instances that are added to the fleet per minute when the service-managed EC2 auto scaling configuration scales out.
Specifies the number of worker instances to keep provisioned and idle as standby capacity, so that the fleet can scale up quickly when new tasks arrive rather than waiting for instances to launch.
The amount of time in seconds that a worker can remain idle before the AWS Deadline Cloud auto scaling configuration scales it down to reduce fleet capacity.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.service_managed_ec2.instan: Defines the service-managed EC2 instance requirements for the fleet, including min/max CPU cores, min/max memory in MiB, CPU architecture type, OS name, and optionally allowed instance types and root volume size.
Defines the required GPU accelerator specifications (including accelerator type and count) for the Amazon EC2 instances provisioned for this Deadline fleet.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of GPU accelerators for the fleet's instances, represented as an object with `Min` and `Max` integer properties, used to filter eligible instance types.
The maximum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that each worker instance in the service-managed EC2 fleet should have.
The minimum number of accelerator cards (e.g., GPUs) that an instance must have in order to be considered for the fleet's instance selection.
Specifies the list of accelerator (GPU) selections available to the fleet's service-managed EC2 instances, including each accelerator's name and runtime (e.g., 'gpu' or 'opt-in').
The name of the accelerator selection (e.g., 'nvidia_a10g') that identifies the specific GPU or accelerator type to be used by the service-managed EC2 instances in the Deadline fleet.
Specifies the runtime (e.g., CUDA) required for the selected GPU accelerator type in a Deadline fleet's service-managed EC2 instances.
Specifies the list of EC2 instance types that the fleet is allowed to use for worker instances.
Specifies the CPU architecture (x86_64 or arm64) for the Amazon EC2 instances that the service-managed fleet will launch.

Specifies a list of custom amount capabilities (each with a name, min, and max) that the Service Managed EC2 fleet advertises, enabling jobs with matching resource amount requirements to be scheduled on the fleet.
The maximum numeric value for a custom instance capability amount, defining the upper bound of the range that Deadline Cloud uses when selecting EC2 instances for the fleet.

For a custom amount in an AWS Deadline Cloud service-managed EC2 fleet's instance capabilities, this min property sets the lower bound (numeric minimum) for the named custom attribute, such as vCPU, memory, or GPU, used when selecting matching EC2 instances.
The name of the custom amount, which must match a custom amount defined on the worker to associate that amount with the fleet's instance capability requirements.

Defines custom key-value pairs (attribute name and value) that worker instances in the fleet advertise as additional capabilities, allowing job requirements to target instances with these specific attributes.
The key of a custom attribute assigned to service-managed EC2 worker instances in the fleet, used for categorizing or matching instances to workload requirements in AWS Deadline Cloud.
Provides the list of string values for a custom attribute that this fleet advertises as a worker capability, used by Deadline Cloud to match jobs that require those attribute values.
Specifies the EC2 instance types that are excluded from the fleet's capacity, preventing these instance types from being used when provisioning worker instances.
Specifies the minimum and maximum memory (in MiB) allowed for instances in the service-managed EC2 fleet, used to constrain eligible instance types.
Specifies the maximum memory in MiB for the service-managed EC2 instances in the fleet, used by AWS Deadline Cloud to determine eligible instance types.
The minimum amount of memory in MiB that a worker instance must have to be eligible for the fleet's service-managed EC2 instances.
Specifies the operating system family (LINUX or WINDOWS) for the service-managed EC2 worker instances in the AWS Deadline Cloud fleet.
Specifies the configuration for the root Amazon EBS volume attached to each service-managed EC2 instance in the Deadline fleet, including settings like volume size, IOPS, throughput, and encryption.
Specifies the provisioned IOPS (I/O operations per second) for the root EBS volume attached to each instance in the AWS Deadline fleet's service-managed EC2 instances.
Specifies the size in GiB of the root EBS volume for the service-managed EC2 instances in the Deadline fleet.
Specifies the throughput in MiB/s for the root EBS volume attached to worker instances in a service-managed EC2 fleet configuration for AWS Deadline Cloud.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of vCPUs allowed for Amazon EC2 instances in this service-managed fleet.
Specifies the maximum number of vCPUs for the service-managed EC2 instances in the AWS Deadline Cloud fleet.
The minimum number of vCPUs an EC2 instance type must provide to be eligible for this Deadline Cloud service-managed fleet's instance capabilities.
Configures the Spot or On-Demand purchase option for the fleet's EC2 instances, including Spot-specific settings like maximum price and allocation strategy.
Specifies the market type for the fleet's EC2 instances, either 'on-demand' or 'spot', determining how the instances are purchased for the Deadline Cloud fleet.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.service_managed_ec2.persis: Specifies the configuration for the persistent EBS volume attached to each worker instance in the service-managed EC2 fleet, including volume size, type, I/O characteristics, and encryption settings.
The provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) for the persistent EBS volume attached to instances in the service-managed EC2 fleet, determining storage performance.
Specifies the absolute file path within the fleet's service-managed EC2 worker instances where the configured persistent volume will be mounted, enabling shared storage access.
The size of the persistent volume attached to the fleet's worker instances, specified in gibibytes (GiB).
Specifies the throughput (in MiB/s) to provision for the persistent EBS volume attached to the fleet's worker instances.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.service_managed_ec2.storag: The ID of the storage profile that defines the file system mounts (e.g., Amazon EFS or FSx) available to the fleet's worker instances.
aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.service_managed_ec2.vpc_co: Specifies the VPC subnets and security groups that the service-managed EC2 instances of the Deadline fleet will use.
Specifies the list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of Deadline Cloud resource configurations to apply to the worker instances launched in the VPC for a service-managed EC2 fleet.
aws_deadline_fleet.description: A human-readable description of the fleet, used to identify the fleet's purpose or configuration in the Deadline Cloud console and APIs.
aws_deadline_fleet.display_name: The human-readable name assigned to the fleet, used for identification within the Deadline Cloud farm.
aws_deadline_fleet.farm_id: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm that this fleet is associated with.
aws_deadline_fleet.fleet_id: The unique identifier assigned by Deadline Cloud to the fleet when it is created, returned as a read-only value.
aws_deadline_fleet.host_configuration: Specifies the network configuration for the worker hosts in the fleet, including the VPC subnet IDs and security group IDs that the EC2 instances for service-managed fleets will launch into.
aws_deadline_fleet.host_configuration.script_body: Specifies the body of a script that runs on each fleet host at startup, enabling custom configuration of the worker environment in AWS Deadline Cloud.
aws_deadline_fleet.host_configuration.script_timeout_second: Specifies the maximum time in seconds that a worker's startup or lifecycle script may run on a host in the Deadline Cloud fleet before the script is considered failed or terminated.
aws_deadline_fleet.max_worker_count: The maximum number of worker instances the fleet can scale up to, setting an upper capacity limit for the fleet's auto-scaling behavior.
aws_deadline_fleet.min_worker_count: Specifies the minimum number of worker instances that must be maintained in the fleet, ensuring baseline capacity for render workloads.
aws_deadline_fleet.role_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the fleet's workers assume to interact with AWS services and perform job tasks.
aws_deadline_fleet.status: The current lifecycle state of the fleet, such as CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS, or DELETING, as reported by the Deadline Cloud service.
aws_deadline_fleet.status_message: The status_message attribute is a read-only string that provides a detailed explanation or reason for the fleet's current status, as reported by AWS Deadline Cloud.
aws_deadline_fleet.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS Deadline Cloud fleet, providing a user-defined label for organizing and managing the fleet through standard AWS tagging practices.
aws_deadline_fleet.tags.value: The value part of a user-defined tag attached to an AWS Deadline Fleet, used to categorize and manage the fleet for cost allocation or operational purposes.
aws_deadline_fleet.worker_count: The current number of active workers in the fleet, as computed and maintained by AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS Deadline Cloud license endpoint.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.dns_name: The DNS name assigned to the license endpoint, used to connect to the endpoint for license management.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.license_endpoint_id: The unique identifier assigned by Deadline Cloud when the license endpoint is created.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.security_group_ids: Specifies the list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the license endpoint's elastic network interface, defining the firewall rules that permit traffic to and from the license endpoint.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.status: Represents the current lifecycle state of the license endpoint, such as CREATING, READY, or DELETING, as tracked by AWS Deadline Cloud.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.status_message: A computed string that provides additional context or error details about the current lifecycle state of the AWS Deadline Cloud license endpoint, such as why it might be in a transitional or failed status.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.subnet_ids: The list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the license endpoint's elastic network interfaces are provisioned to connect to license servers.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Deadline license endpoint, enabling you to categorize and manage the endpoint for cost allocation and access control.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.tags.value: Specifies the value for a user-defined tag on the Deadline license endpoint, used to categorize, track costs, or apply IAM-based access control through resource tags.
aws_deadline_license_endpoint.vpc_id: The ID of the VPC in which the license endpoint is created.

aws_deadline_limit.current_count: The current number of resources that are using this limit, as tracked by AWS Deadline Cloud and updated automatically as usage changes.
aws_deadline_limit.description: Provides an optional human-readable description for the AWS Deadline Cloud limit, clarifying the limit's purpose or scope.
aws_deadline_limit.display_name: A human-readable name for the limit, used to identify and display the limit in the AWS Deadline Cloud console and API.
aws_deadline_limit.farm_id: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm to which this limit belongs.
aws_deadline_limit.limit_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Deadline Cloud to this limit resource when it is created, used to refer to the limit in other resources.
aws_deadline_limit.max_count: The maximum number of resources that the limit permits to be used simultaneously, enforcing a cap on concurrent usage in the Deadline Cloud farm.

aws_deadline_metered_product.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Deadline Cloud metered product.
aws_deadline_metered_product.family: The product family (e.g., 'Arnold' or 'V-Ray') that Deadline Cloud assigns to the metered product, automatically determined and read-only.
aws_deadline_metered_product.license_endpoint_id: The unique identifier of the license endpoint with which the metered product is associated in AWS Deadline Cloud.
aws_deadline_metered_product.port: The network port number on which the metered product's licensing service listens, returned by Deadline Cloud after the product is created.
aws_deadline_metered_product.product_id: The product_id specifies the unique AWS Marketplace product identifier for the software product that is metered and associated with the Deadline farm.
aws_deadline_metered_product.vendor: The vendor of the metered product, representing the company or provider that offers the software, as assigned by AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_monitor.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Deadline Cloud monitor.
aws_deadline_monitor.display_name: A human-readable name for the Deadline Cloud monitor, used to identify it in the AWS console and APIs.
aws_deadline_monitor.identity_center_application_arn: The ARN of the AWS IAM Identity Center application that AWS Deadline Cloud creates and associates with this monitor.
aws_deadline_monitor.identity_center_instance_arn: The ARN of the IAM Identity Center instance used to manage user access and single sign-on for the AWS Deadline Cloud monitor.
aws_deadline_monitor.monitor_id: The unique identifier assigned to the monitor.
aws_deadline_monitor.role_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the Deadline Cloud monitor uses to access the storage resources (such as the S3 bucket and file system) associated with the Deadline Cloud environment.
aws_deadline_monitor.subdomain: Specifies the subdomain that forms part of the monitor's unique web address, used to access the Deadline Cloud monitor endpoint.
aws_deadline_monitor.tags.key: A key for a tag assigned to the AWS Deadline Cloud monitor, used to categorize and identify the resource.
aws_deadline_monitor.url: The URL of the AWS Deadline monitor, used to access the monitor's web-based user interface.

aws_deadline_queue.allowed_storage_profile_ids: Specifies the list of storage profile IDs that are allowed to be used by this Deadline Cloud queue for job attachments.
aws_deadline_queue.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Deadline queue, used for IAM policies and API operations.
aws_deadline_queue.default_budget_action: Specifies the action Deadline takes when the queue's budget limit is exceeded, with valid values NONE and STOP_SCHEDULING_AND_CANCEL_JOBS.
aws_deadline_queue.description: A human-readable description of the queue, used to provide context about the queue's purpose or contents in AWS Deadline Cloud.
aws_deadline_queue.display_name: The user-friendly display name of the Deadline Cloud queue, used to identify it in the AWS console and API.
aws_deadline_queue.farm_id: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm to which this queue belongs and is associated.
aws_deadline_queue.job_attachment_settings: Configures the S3 bucket and root prefix where job attachments for the queue are stored.
aws_deadline_queue.job_attachment_settings.root_prefix: Specifies the S3 key prefix (within the job attachment S3 bucket) that serves as the root location for storing all job attachments for this queue.
aws_deadline_queue.job_attachment_settings.s3_bucket_name: The name of the S3 bucket that AWS Deadline Cloud uses to store job attachments for this queue.
aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user: Specifies the operating system user (and group for POSIX, or Windows user) that jobs submitted to this Deadline queue will run as, along with the run-as mode (USER or WORKER) that determines whether jobs use the queue-defined user or the worker's user.
aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.posix: Configures the POSIX user and group under which jobs in this Deadline queue run.
aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.posix.group: The POSIX group name or ID used to run jobs in the queue.
aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.posix.user: The POSIX user name that jobs in this AWS Deadline queue will run as.
aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.run_as: Specifies whether jobs run as the AWS-managed user or the queue-configured user, with valid values 'AWS_MANAGED_USER' and 'QUEUE_CONFIGURED_USER'.
aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.windows: Specifies the Windows user account settings, including the user name and the ARN of the password stored in AWS Secrets Manager, that Deadline Cloud uses to run jobs on Windows worker nodes in this queue.
aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.windows.password_arn: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the password for the Windows user that jobs will run as on this queue.
aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.windows.user: The Windows user account name that jobs submitted to this AWS Deadline queue will run as on Windows worker nodes.
aws_deadline_queue.queue_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Deadline Cloud to the queue when it is created, used to reference the queue in other operations and resources.
aws_deadline_queue.required_file_system_location_names: Specifies the names of file system locations that must be available and mounted for jobs in this Deadline Cloud queue to run.
aws_deadline_queue.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that the queue assumes to access AWS resources such as S3 buckets.
aws_deadline_queue.scheduling_configuration.priority_balanc: Specifies the priority-balanced scheduling settings for the queue, which allocate worker capacity based on job priority while preventing starvation of lower-priority jobs.
Specifies the number of rendering tasks to buffer in the queue scheduler for workers, helping to minimize idle time and improve rendering throughput.
aws_deadline_queue.scheduling_configuration.priority_fifo: Determines whether the queue schedules jobs using priority-based ordering (true) or first-in, first-out (FIFO) ordering (false).
aws_deadline_queue.scheduling_configuration.weighted_balanc: Specifies the weighted-balanced scheduling mode for the queue, which distributes jobs to workers proportionally based on assigned weights to maintain balanced resource utilization.
Defines the relative weight given to the error rate metric when the weighted balanced scheduling type scores and orders jobs in the queue's scheduling policy.
Specifies the maximum priority value a job can be assigned in the queue's weighted balanced scheduling, overriding any higher priority requested by the job to cap job precedence.
When set to true, ensures that the highest-priority job in the queue is always scheduled first, even under weighted balanced scheduling.
Specifies the relative priority weight that the weighted balanced scheduling configuration uses to determine how jobs in this queue are allocated workers compared to other queues.
For weighted balanced scheduling, the rendering task buffer sets the number of rendering tasks prefetched for each worker to reduce idle time and latency.
Sets the relative scheduling weight for rendering tasks within a weighted-balanced queue scheduling configuration, influencing the proportion of rendering tasks the service assigns.

The submission_time_weight field sets the relative weight applied to a job's submission time when the queue uses weighted balanced scheduling, so a higher value makes older submissions more strongly prioritized.
aws_deadline_queue.tags.key: The key portion of a tag assigned to the AWS Deadline queue, used to categorize, identify, and manage the queue resource.
aws_deadline_queue.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag key attached to the AWS Deadline queue resource.

aws_deadline_queue_environment.farm_id: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm that this queue environment is associated with.
aws_deadline_queue_environment.name: The name of the queue environment, which is derived from the `name` field defined in the environment's template content (YAML or JSON).
aws_deadline_queue_environment.priority: Controls the order in which this queue environment is applied relative to other queue environments associated with the same queue, with the priority value used to rank the environments.
aws_deadline_queue_environment.queue_environment_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Deadline to this queue environment resource.
aws_deadline_queue_environment.queue_id: The unique identifier of the Deadline queue that this environment is associated with, used to scope the environment to a specific queue.
aws_deadline_queue_environment.template: Defines the queue environment's setup as a structured string (typically JSON), specifying environment variables and script actions that run for jobs using this queue environment.
aws_deadline_queue_environment.template_type: Specifies the template format for the queue environment, either JSON or YAML.

aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association.farm_id: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm that contains the queue and fleet being associated.
aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association.fleet_id: The unique identifier of the fleet that is associated with the queue in AWS Deadline Cloud.
aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association.queue_id: The unique identifier of the Deadline queue to associate with the fleet, linking the queue to the specified fleet.

aws_deadline_queue_limit_association.farm_id: The unique identifier of the farm that contains the queue and limit to be associated.
aws_deadline_queue_limit_association.limit_id: The unique identifier of the Deadline Cloud limit to associate with the queue.
aws_deadline_queue_limit_association.queue_id: The unique identifier of the Deadline Cloud queue that is associated with the specified limit.

aws_deadline_storage_profile.display_name: The human-readable name of the storage profile, used to identify it in the Deadline Cloud console and API.
aws_deadline_storage_profile.farm_id: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm to which this storage profile belongs.
aws_deadline_storage_profile.file_system_locations: Defines the list of file system locations (each consisting of a name and a mount path) that this storage profile makes available to worker instances for accessing job data.
aws_deadline_storage_profile.file_system_locations.name: The user-defined name for a file system location in the AWS Deadline Cloud storage profile, used to identify the shared or local storage path.
aws_deadline_storage_profile.file_system_locations.path: The absolute filesystem path (e.g., a mount point or drive letter) on the worker where the file system location referenced by this storage profile entry is accessible.
aws_deadline_storage_profile.file_system_locations.type: In an AWS Deadline Cloud storage profile, each file system location's `type` indicates whether the location represents a shared file system (accessible to all workers) or a local file system (strictly for a single worker).
aws_deadline_storage_profile.os_family: Specifies the operating system family (such as WINDOWS or LINUX) that this AWS Deadline Cloud storage profile is configured for.
aws_deadline_storage_profile.storage_profile_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Deadline Cloud to this storage profile.

aws_deadline_worker.tags.key: The key for a tag to assign to the AWS Deadline Worker resource, allowing you to categorize and manage workers in AWS Deadline Cloud.
aws_deadline_worker.tags.value: The value portion of a tag applied to an AWS Deadline Worker, used to attach custom metadata such as environment or project labels to the worker resource.

aws_detective_graph.tags: The list of tags to attach to the Detective graph, where each tag consists of a key and a value to help organize, identify, and manage the resource.
aws_detective_graph.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Detective graph, used to organize, identify, and manage access to the graph through resource-level permissions and cost allocation.
aws_detective_graph.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Detective graph, used to categorize, manage, and control access to the graph alongside other AWS resources.

aws_dev_ops_agent_agent_space.operator_app.iam: In an AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace, the `operator_app.iam` field defines the IAM role and permission settings the operator application uses to securely access AWS resources on behalf of the agent space.
aws_dev_ops_agent_agent_space.operator_app.idc.idc_instance_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM Identity Center (IdC) instance used by the operator application in the agent space for its identity configuration.
aws_dev_ops_agent_agent_space.operator_app.idc.operator_app_role_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the operator application assumes within the AWS IAM Identity Center (IDC) configuration for the agent space.

aws_dev_ops_guru_notification_channel.config.sns.topic_arn: The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that DevOps Guru publishes notification messages to for this channel.

aws_dev_ops_guru_resource_collection.resource_collection_filter.tags.app_boun: The tag key (AppBoundaryKey) that DevOps Guru uses to define the application boundary for selecting which tagged AWS resources are included in the resource collection.
aws_dev_ops_guru_resource_collection.resource_collection_filter.tags.tag_valu: Specifies the list of tag values for the tag key in the parent `tags` filter, used to match which AWS resources are included in the DevOps Guru resource collection.

aws_direct_connect_connection.tags.value: Specifies the value for a tag assigned to the Direct Connect connection, used to store arbitrary metadata or cost-allocation information.

aws_direct_connect_direct_connect_gatewa.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the Direct Connect gateway, used to categorize and identify the resource.
aws_direct_connect_direct_connect_gatewa.tags.value: Specifies the value of a tag key attached to the Direct Connect gateway, used for identifying and categorizing the gateway resource.

aws_direct_connect_lag.tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag attached to the AWS Direct Connect LAG, used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.
aws_direct_connect_lag.tags.value: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the Direct Connect LAG, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.address_family: The IP address family (ipv4 or ipv6) used for the BGP session on this Direct Connect private virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.amazon_address: Specifies the IP address on the Amazon side of the BGP peering session for this BGP peer.
aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.asn: The autonomous system number (ASN) for the customer's BGP peer on the private virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.auth_key: The MD5 authentication key (BGP password) used for BGP peering on this Direct Connect private virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.bgp_peer_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the BGP peer configured on this Direct Connect private virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.customer_address: The customer_address specifies the IP address on the customer's side of the BGP peering session for a private virtual interface in AWS Direct Connect.
aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Direct Connect private virtual interface, used to identify the tag in a key-value pair.

aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.bgp_peers.address_family: The IP address family (IPv4 or IPv6) to use for the BGP peer on this Direct Connect public virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.bgp_peers.amazon_address: The public IP address assigned to the Amazon side of the BGP session for this peer on the Direct Connect public virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.bgp_peers.asn: The autonomous system number (ASN) of the BGP peer for this Direct Connect public virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.bgp_peers.auth_key: Specifies the BGP MD5 authentication key (BGP password) required for establishing the BGP session with this Direct Connect peer.
aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.bgp_peers.bgp_peer_id: The BGP peer ID is a unique identifier assigned by AWS Direct Connect to this BGP peer when it is created on the public virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.bgp_peers.customer_address: The customer-side IP address for this BGP peer, used as the BGP endpoint on the customer's router for the public virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag to apply to the AWS Direct Connect public virtual interface for managing and categorizing the resource.
aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.tags.value: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS Direct Connect public virtual interface, used to organize or identify the resource.

aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.address_family: The address family (IPv4 or IPv6) used for the BGP session on the transit virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.amazon_address: The IPv4 address on the Amazon side of the BGP peering session for a Direct Connect transit virtual interface, used to establish BGP connectivity with the customer's router.
aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.asn: The autonomous system number (ASN) of the BGP peer used to establish the BGP session for the transit virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.auth_key: The MD5 authentication key used for BGP peering on this transit virtual interface, enabling authenticated BGP sessions with the on-premises router.
aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.bgp_peer_id: The AWS-assigned unique identifier for the BGP peer configured on the transit virtual interface, used to reference the peer in Direct Connect API operations.
aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.bgp_peers.customer_address: The IP address assigned to the customer's side of the BGP session for this transit virtual interface.
aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.tags.key: The key of a tag (e.g., 'Name') applied to the Direct Connect Transit Virtual Interface, used to filter, organize, and control access to the resource.
aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.tags.value: The value component of a tag applied to this AWS Direct Connect transit virtual interface, used for arbitrary metadata such as cost allocation or ownership.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.alias: The DNS alias automatically generated by AWS for the Microsoft Active Directory, used to uniquely identify the directory when connecting to it.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.create_alias: If set to true, AWS Directory Service creates a public alias for the Microsoft AD directory (used in the directory's access URL), and when omitted the default is true.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.dns_ip_addresses: The automatically assigned IP addresses of the DNS servers for the Microsoft Active Directory directory, returned by AWS.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.edition: Specifies the edition of the Microsoft Active Directory, either Standard (default) or Enterprise, which determines the directory's feature set and scaling capabilities.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.enable_sso: Enables single sign-on (SSO) for the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, allowing users to access supported applications using their existing Active Directory credentials.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.id: The unique identifier of the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, assigned by AWS upon creation.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.name: The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the Microsoft Active Directory, such as corp.example.com.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.password: The password for the directory administrator account, which must meet the complexity and length requirements for AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.short_name: Specifies the short name (NetBIOS name) of the Active Directory domain, which is a single-label name that can be used in place of the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) when referring to the domain.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.vpc_settings: Specifies the VPC and subnets (two in different Availability Zones) where the Microsoft AD directory is deployed.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.vpc_settings.subnet_ids: The identifiers of two subnets in different Availability Zones where the directory's domain controllers will be deployed.
aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.vpc_settings.vpc_id: The ID of the VPC in which the Microsoft Active Directory is created.

aws_directory_service_simple_ad.tags: A list of tag objects (each with a Key and Value) to associate with the AWS Directory Service Simple AD directory, enabling cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.
aws_directory_service_simple_ad.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the Simple AD directory resource.
aws_directory_service_simple_ad.vpc_settings: Specifies the VPC configuration for the Simple AD directory, including the VPC ID and the subnets where the directory's domain controllers are deployed.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this DLM lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.copy_tags: Indicates whether to copy tags from the source EBS volume to the snapshots created by this lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.create_interval: The interval (in hours or days) between automatic EBS snapshot creations for a schedule in the DLM lifecycle policy, controlled by the associated interval unit.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.cross_region_copy_targets: Defines the destination regions and their encryption configurations (including optional KMS key ARN) to which snapshots or AMIs created by this DLM lifecycle policy are copied.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.cross_region_copy_targets.target_region: The destination AWS region to which the policy copies snapshots or AMIs as part of its cross-region copy action.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.description: A user-provided descriptive text that identifies the purpose and details of the DLM lifecycle policy, helping to distinguish it from other policies in the AWS account.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.exclusions: Specifies the tags and resource types that exclude matching resources from the lifecycle policy, preventing automatic snapshots or AMI creation for those resources.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.exclusions.exclude_boot_volumes: When true, the lifecycle policy excludes boot volumes from its snapshot schedules, preventing snapshots from being created for EC2 instance boot volumes.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.exclusions.exclude_tags: The list of key-value tag pairs that, when matched on a resource, cause that resource to be excluded from the lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.exclusions.exclude_tags.key: The tag key that, when present on a resource, excludes that resource from the DLM lifecycle policy's actions.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.exclusions.exclude_tags.value: The tag value that, when paired with the corresponding tag key in an exclusion filter, causes matching resources to be excluded from the lifecycle policy's actions.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.exclusions.exclude_volume_types: Specifies the EBS volume types (for example, gp2 or io1) that should be excluded from the lifecycle policy's snapshot or AMI creation actions.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.execution_role_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that AWS Data Lifecycle Manager assumes to create snapshots and manage the lifecycle of the target resources.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the DLM lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details: This object defines the core configuration of the DLM lifecycle policy, specifying the resource type (e.g., EBS snapshots or AMIs), target resource tags, state, and the schedules with their associated actions, such as creating, retaining, and deleting snapshots or AMIs.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.actions: Specifies the list of actions, each containing a name and cross-Region copy settings, that an event-based DLM lifecycle policy executes when its configured event is triggered.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.actions.cross_region_copy: Specifies the cross-Region copy action parameters that define how snapshots or AMIs are copied from the source Region to one or more target Regions as part of the lifecycle policy's action.

Specifies the encryption settings for snapshot copies created by the cross-region copy action, including whether the copied snapshots are encrypted and the ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) to use for encryption.
The ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) used to encrypt snapshots copied to the destination region, defaulting to the region's default EBS encryption key if not specified.
Whether the cross-Region snapshot copies are encrypted, which when true uses the specified KMS key or an AWS managed key.

Specifies the retention rule for snapshots copied to the target region, defining either a retention interval (value and unit such as days, weeks, months, or years) or a maximum count of snapshots to retain.
Specifies the retention period value for cross-region copied snapshots or AMIs, which combined with interval_unit determines how long they are kept in the destination region.
Specifies the unit of time (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) for the retention interval of the cross-region copy action in the lifecycle policy.
The AWS Region to which the resource is copied by this cross-region copy action in the DLM lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.actions.name: Identifies the type of action to be performed by the DLM lifecycle policy, such as 'cross-region-copy', which determines the operation executed on the target resources.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.copy_tags: Indicates whether to copy all user-defined tags from the source snapshot to the target snapshots created by the lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.create_interval: The create_interval determines how often the Data Lifecycle Manager policy creates snapshots or AMIs, specified in hours for EBS snapshot policies (1–24) and in days for EBS-backed AMI policies (1–7).
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.cross_region_copy_targets: Defines the list of destination Regions to which snapshots or AMIs are copied, along with per-target encryption and retention settings.
The AWS region code to which the lifecycle policy copies snapshots as part of a cross-region copy target configuration.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.event_source: Defines the event source that triggers an event-based lifecycle policy, such as a CloudWatch Events rule, including its type (e.g., MANAGED_CWS_EVENT) and parameters like event type and snapshot owner.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.event_source.parameters: The parameters object of an event source in a DLM lifecycle policy, used when the event source type is MANAGED_CWE, contains a description that identifies the CloudWatch Events rule that triggers the event-based policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.event_source.parameters.d: A regular expression used to match the description of snapshots to trigger this event-based DLM lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.event_source.parameters.e: Specifies the type of event that triggers this event-based lifecycle policy, with `shareSnapshot` being the only supported value, meaning the policy runs when a snapshot is shared with your account.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.event_source.parameters.s: Specifies the AWS account IDs of the snapshot owners that can trigger the lifecycle policy when an event occurs (e.g., shared snapshot event) for an event-driven DLM policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.event_source.type: Specifies the type of event source for an event-based DLM lifecycle policy, where the only valid value is MANAGED_CWL to use Amazon CloudWatch Events.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.exclusions: Defines the exclusions for the lifecycle policy, which identify specific resources or resource types (such as volumes with certain tags or specific volume types) that should not be affected by the policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.exclusions.exclude_boot_v: Indicates whether the Data Lifecycle Manager policy excludes boot volumes from all snapshot and AMI creation actions, so that boot volumes are not affected by the policy's lifecycle rules.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.exclusions.exclude_tags: Defines tag key-value pairs that identify resources to exclude from the lifecycle policy's actions, such as snapshot or AMI creation.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.exclusions.exclude_tags.k: The key of a tag that identifies resources to be excluded from the lifecycle policy's actions.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.exclusions.exclude_tags.v: Specifies the tag value for a tag-based exclusion rule, which excludes resources that have this tag value from the lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.exclusions.exclude_volume: Specifies the list of EBS volume types (e.g., 'gp2', 'io1', 'gp3') to exclude from the lifecycle policy, so the policy does not apply to or create snapshots for volumes of those types.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.parameters: Specifies optional parameters, such as ExcludeBootVolume or NoReboot, that modify the behavior of the lifecycle policy's snapshot creation operations.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.parameters.exclude_boot_v: Indicates whether the boot volume of the instance is excluded from the EBS snapshots created by this lifecycle policy when the policy targets instances.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.parameters.exclude_data_v: A list of tag filters (key-value pairs) that identifies data volumes to exclude from the lifecycle policy's snapshot or AMI creation actions.
The tag key used to identify data volumes to exclude from the lifecycle policy's snapshot management.

The value portion of a key-value pair in the exclude data volume tags list, used to match an Amazon EBS volume tag and exclude that volume from the lifecycle policy's snapshot or AMI creation actions.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.parameters.no_reboot: Indicates whether to skip rebooting the instance when creating snapshots, so a value of true prevents the typical reboot that occurs during snapshot creation.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.policy_language: Specifies the policy language format, either SIMPLIFIED or STANDARD, which determines how resource types and actions are expressed in the policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.policy_type: Specifies the type of lifecycle policy, which can be EBS_SNAPSHOT_MANAGEMENT to manage EBS snapshots, IMAGE_MANAGEMENT to manage EBS-backed AMIs, or EVENT_BASED to trigger on Amazon CloudWatch events.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.resource_locations: Specifies the target resource locations for the lifecycle policy, allowing values like 'CLOUD' for resources in the AWS cloud and 'OUTPOST' for resources on an AWS Outpost.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.resource_type: Specifies the type of AWS resource (either 'VOLUME' or 'INSTANCE') that a DLM lifecycle policy targets, determining whether the policy creates EBS snapshots or AMIs.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.resource_types: The types of resources (such as VOLUME or INSTANCE) that this lifecycle policy will manage and snapshot.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules: Defines the schedule(s) that specify when to create Amazon EBS snapshots (or AMIs) and how long to retain them under this lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.archive_rule: Defines the archive rule for this schedule, specifying how long snapshots are retained in the Amazon EBS Archive tier (e.g., the number of days to keep them archived) before deletion.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.archive_rule.re: Specifies the retention duration for archived snapshots created by the containing archive rule, defining how long they are kept before being expired.
Specifies the retention period for snapshots stored in the archive tier, either as a count of snapshots or as an interval with a unit (e.g., days), after which they expire.
The number of snapshots to retain in the archive storage tier.
Specifies the numeric value for how long snapshots are retained in the archive tier before deletion, paired with the interval_unit property to define the unit of time (e.g., days, weeks).
Specifies the unit of time (e.g., DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, YEARS) for the retention period of snapshots in the archive tier, used with the retention_archive_tier.interval value.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.copy_tags: Copies all user-defined tags from the source snapshot to the snapshots created by this schedule.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.create_rule: Defines when the schedule triggers resource creation (e.g., EBS snapshots or AMIs), typically via a recurring interval or a cron expression.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.create_rule.cro: The cron expression that specifies when this create rule triggers snapshot or AMI creation in the DLM lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.create_rule.int: Specifies how often the lifecycle policy creates snapshots; for example, a value of 12 with an interval_unit of 'hours' creates snapshots every 12 hours, and it must be paired with the interval_unit property to define the schedule frequency.
For the create rule of a schedule, this field sets the time unit (HOURS or DAYS) that the interval value uses to control how often AWS Data Lifecycle Manager creates snapshots or AMIs.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.create_rule.loc: Specifies whether the lifecycle policy creates snapshots of resources in the AWS Cloud (CLOUD) or on AWS Outposts (OUTPOST).
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.create_rule.scr: Determines whether the DLM lifecycle policy should proceed with the snapshot creation operation even if this script fails to execute successfully.

Specifies the ARN of the AWS Lambda function or the name of an AWS Systems Manager document that acts as the execution handler for the script configured in this DLM lifecycle policy schedule, enabling custom pre-snapshot or post-snapshot actions.
Specifies the AWS service that executes the script (for example, AWS Systems Manager) when the create rule triggers snapshot creation in a DLM lifecycle policy.

Sets the maximum time in seconds that AWS Data Lifecycle Manager waits for the script (a Systems Manager automation document) to finish executing before declaring the pre/post snapshot action a failure, applied per script in the create rule of the lifecycle policy schedule.
Specifies the maximum number of times AWS DLM will retry a script (defined in the schedule's create rule) after it fails before marking the script execution as failed.
Specifies the stage(s) during the EBS snapshot creation process at which the script should run, with allowed values 'pre' and 'post'.
