aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.create_rule.tim: Specifies the times in UTC (formatted as HH:00) at which the lifecycle policy creates snapshots according to this schedule.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.cross_region_co: Configures the rules for copying snapshots to other AWS Regions as part of this schedule, including destination region, encryption, and retention settings.
The ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) used to encrypt the EBS snapshots or AMIs copied to the target region under this cross-region copy rule in the DLM lifecycle policy.
Indicates whether to copy all user-defined tags from the source EBS snapshot (or AMI) to the cross-region copied snapshot (or AMI).
Specifies the interval and interval unit after which the cross-region copied AMIs are deprecated in the target Region.

The numeric length of the time period (with units set in the sibling `interval_unit` field) after which copied AMIs in the target Region are deprecated according to this cross-region copy deprecate rule.
The unit of time (e.g., days, weeks, months, or years) that, together with the interval value, determines how long the copied AMI is retained in the target region before it is deprecated.
Specifies whether snapshots copied to the target region by this cross-region copy rule are encrypted.

Defines the retention behavior for snapshots copied to the destination region, specifying either a time-based interval (with unit such as days, weeks, months, or years) or a maximum count of snapshots to retain.
The number of interval units (as specified by the associated interval_unit) to retain cross-Region copied snapshots in the target Region before they are deleted.
The unit of time used with the retention interval to specify how long cross-region snapshot copies are retained in the target region, such as days, weeks, months, or years.
The destination AWS Region to which the snapshot or AMI is copied, specified as a Region name (e.g., us-east-1) in the cross-Region copy rule.
The destination AWS Region to which snapshots or AMIs are copied by this cross-Region copy rule.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.deprecate_rule: Defines when AMIs created by this schedule are automatically deprecated, either by specifying a maximum retained count or a time-based interval (e.g., days) after which the AMI is deprecated.
The maximum number of AMIs to retain; when this count is exceeded, the oldest AMIs are deprecated by the lifecycle policy.
The number of time units (as specified by the associated interval_unit field) after which the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is deprecated in this lifecycle policy's deprecation rule.
The unit of time (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used with the interval to determine how long to wait before deprecating the AMI in this schedule's deprecate rule.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.fast_restore_ru: Configures the fast snapshot restore rule for this schedule, specifying the Availability Zones in which to enable fast snapshot restore and the number of snapshots (or time interval) for which fast restore is retained, allowing EBS snapshots to be restored quickly in those zones.
Specifies the list of Availability Zones in which to enable fast snapshot restore for snapshots created by this schedule.
Specifies the Availability Zones in which fast snapshot restore is enabled for snapshots created by this schedule.
The number of snapshots to enable Fast Snapshot Restore on for this schedule's fast restore rule in the DLM lifecycle policy.

Specifies the interval number, paired with the interval unit, that determines how frequently the lifecycle policy enables fast snapshot restore for snapshots taken under this schedule, used as an alternative to the count parameter.
The unit of time (DAYS or WEEKS) for the interval during which snapshots created by this schedule will have fast snapshot restore enabled.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.name: The name of the DLM lifecycle policy schedule, which must be unique among all schedules in the policy and is used to reference the schedule in associated tags and rules.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.retain_rule: Specifies the retention rule for snapshots or AMIs created by this schedule, controlling whether to keep a maximum count or retain for a specific interval (in days or years) before deletion.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.retain_rule.cou: Specifies the maximum number of snapshots to retain for the policy schedule when the retain rule is based on a count, after which the oldest snapshots are deleted.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.retain_rule.int: The number of intervals (measured in the unit specified by the sibling field interval_unit) that snapshots or AMIs are retained by this lifecycle policy schedule before they are deleted.
Specifies the unit of time (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used with the retain rule's interval value to determine how long snapshots created by this schedule are retained.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.share_rules: Specifies the rules for sharing snapshots created by this schedule with other AWS accounts, including target account IDs and the interval for unsharing them.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.share_rules.tar: Specifies the AWS account IDs to which snapshots created by this schedule are shared, as defined in the share rules of the lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.share_rules.uns: Specifies the numeric interval, paired with the associated unit, after which DLM automatically unshares snapshots or AMIs that were shared with the target accounts in this share rule.
The unit of time (DAYS or WEEKS) used with the unshare interval to determine how frequently snapshots are unshared from other accounts in the lifecycle policy's share rule.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.tags_to_add: Specifies the tags to apply to the snapshots or AMIs created by this schedule, allowing you to organize and identify the resources created by the lifecycle policy.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.tags_to_add.key: The key of a tag to be added to resources created by this lifecycle policy schedule, such as snapshots or AMIs, where the corresponding value is specified in the adjacent value field.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.tags_to_add.val: The value for a custom tag that AWS Data Lifecycle Manager applies to the snapshots or AMIs created by this schedule.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.variable_tags: Specifies a list of tags with variable placeholders that are applied to the snapshots or AMIs created when the schedule triggers, where tag values can use DLM-supported variables such as $(instance-id), $(timestamp), or $(uuid) and are replaced with actual resource information at execution time.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.variable_tags.k: The tag key for a variable tag entry that DLM attaches to snapshots or AMIs created by this schedule, where the corresponding value can contain dynamic variables such as $(instance-id) or $(timestamp).
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.schedules.variable_tags.v: This string defines the value of a variable tag applied to snapshots or AMIs created by the schedule, and may contain DLM-supported placeholders such as ${instance-id} or ${timestamp} to dynamically populate the tag value from the source resource or event time.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.target_tags: Tags that identify the resources the lifecycle policy will manage; the policy applies to resources that have all these tags.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.target_tags.key: The tag key used to identify resources that the lifecycle policy should target.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.target_tags.value: The tag value used together with the corresponding key in policy_details.target_tags to identify the resources that the lifecycle policy will manage for snapshot or AMI creation.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.retain_interval: The numeric interval for retaining snapshots in a DLM lifecycle policy schedule, working with `retain_interval_unit` to define the duration (e.g., number of days, weeks, months, or years).
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.state: Specifies whether the lifecycle policy is set to ENABLED or DISABLED, controlling whether the policy is active and can create snapshots.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.tags: This field defines the user-defined tags to attach to the lifecycle policy, which can be used to organize, identify, and manage the policy through cost allocation and resource tagging.
aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.tags.value: The value for a tag key assigned to the Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager lifecycle policy, used to categorize, identify, or manage access to the policy.

aws_dms_data_migration.data_migration_settings: Specifies the execution settings for the data migration, including the number of parallel jobs to run (NumberOfJobs) and the JSON selection rules that determine which database objects are included in the migration.
aws_dms_data_migration.source_data_settings.cdcstart_position: Specifies the position in the source database's transaction log (such as binary log) from which AWS DMS starts reading changes when using change data capture (CDC) for the data migration.
aws_dms_data_migration.source_data_settings.cdcstart_time: The timestamp (in the source database's timezone) from which change data capture (CDC) begins for ongoing replication in the data migration.
aws_dms_data_migration.source_data_settings.cdcstop_time: Specifies the UTC timestamp at which Change Data Capture (CDC) stops collecting incremental changes from the source database for this data migration.
aws_dms_data_migration.source_data_settings.slot_name: Specifies the name of the PostgreSQL replication slot that DMS uses to capture change data for ongoing replication (change data capture) from the source database.
aws_dms_data_migration.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AWS DMS data migration resource, used for categorizing, cost tracking, and access control.
aws_dms_data_migration.tags.value: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the DMS data migration resource, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.doc_db_settings.certificate_arn: The ARN of the certificate used for secure TLS/SSL connection to the Amazon DocumentDB database when the data provider connects.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.doc_db_settings.database_name: The name of the DocumentDB database to which the DMS data provider connects for data migration.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.doc_db_settings.port: The port number used to connect to the DocumentDB instance.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.doc_db_settings.server_name: The hostname or cluster endpoint of the Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) database that this DMS data provider uses to connect for migration.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.doc_db_settings.ssl_mode: Specifies the SSL/TLS mode used when connecting to the DocumentDB cluster, with allowed values including none, require, verify-ca, and verify-full.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2_luw_settings.certificat: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the certificate used to secure connections to the IBM Db2 LUW database for this AWS DMS data provider.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2_luw_settings.database_n: The name of the IBM Db2 LUW database that the data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2_luw_settings.port: TCP port number on which the IBM Db2 LUW database listens for connections, required when configuring an IBM Db2 LUW data provider for AWS DMS.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2_luw_settings.server_nam: The hostname or IP address of the IBM Db2 LUW database server that the data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2_luw_settings.ssl_mode: Defines the SSL encryption and certificate verification mode used when connecting to the IBM Db2 LUW database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2z_os_settings.certificat: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an SSL/TLS certificate that is used to encrypt and verify connections to the IBM Db2 for z/OS database associated with this DMS data provider.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2z_os_settings.database_n: Specifies the database name to use when connecting to the IBM Db2 for z/OS instance for this DMS data provider.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2z_os_settings.port: The TCP port number used to connect to the IBM Db2 for z/OS database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2z_os_settings.server_nam: The host name or IP address of the IBM Db2 for z/OS server that this DMS data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2z_os_settings.ssl_mode: Specifies the SSL/TLS connection mode used when connecting to the IBM Db2 for z/OS database, such as requiring encryption or verifying the server certificate.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.maria_db_settings.certificate_a: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the certificate used for SSL/TLS encryption when connecting to the MariaDB database as a DMS data provider.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.maria_db_settings.port: The TCP port number on which the MariaDB server listens for incoming connections.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.maria_db_settings.server_name: The hostname or IP address of the MariaDB database server that the data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.maria_db_settings.ssl_mode: Specifies the SSL mode used for connections to the MariaDB database, with values such as none, require, verify-ca, or verify-full.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.microsoft_sql_server_settings.c: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SSL/TLS certificate used to encrypt connections to the Microsoft SQL Server database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.microsoft_sql_server_settings.d: Specifies the name of the Microsoft SQL Server database to be used by the data provider.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.microsoft_sql_server_settings.p: Specifies the TCP port number on which the Microsoft SQL Server database is listening for connections.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.microsoft_sql_server_settings.s: The hostname or IP address of the Microsoft SQL Server database that serves as the data provider source.
Specifies the SSL mode used when connecting to the Microsoft SQL Server database, controlling whether the connection is encrypted and whether the server certificate is verified.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_settings.auth_mechanis: Specifies the MongoDB authentication mechanism used when connecting to the database, with valid values including 'default', 'mongodb_cr', and 'scram_sha_1'.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_settings.auth_source: The name of the MongoDB authentication database (authSource) that contains the user credentials used when connecting to the source database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_settings.auth_type: Specifies the authentication type used when connecting to the MongoDB data source, such as NONE or PASSWORD.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_settings.certificate_a: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the certificate used for SSL/TLS encryption when connecting to the MongoDB database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_settings.database_name: The name of the MongoDB database that the DMS data provider uses for connections and migrations.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_settings.port: The TCP port number on which the MongoDB source database is listening for connections.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_settings.server_name: The hostname or IP address of the MongoDB server to connect to for this data provider.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_settings.ssl_mode: Specifies the SSL mode used when connecting to the MongoDB data provider, such as 'none', 'require', 'verify-ca', or 'verify-full'.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.my_sql_settings.certificate_arn: The ARN of a certificate authority (CA) or SSL/TLS certificate used to verify or encrypt the connection to the MySQL database when a secure connection is configured.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.my_sql_settings.port: The TCP port number the MySQL data provider uses to connect to the MySQL database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.my_sql_settings.server_name: The hostname or IP address of the MySQL server that the data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.my_sql_settings.ssl_mode: Defines the SSL/TLS enforcement level for connections to the MySQL data provider, with valid values such as none, require, verify-ca, and verify-full to control encryption and certificate validation.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.oracle_settings.asm_server: Specifies the hostname or IP address of the Oracle Automatic Storage Management (ASM) server that the DMS data provider connects to for Oracle database settings.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.oracle_settings.certificate_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the certificate used to encrypt connections to the Oracle database when SSL/TLS is enabled.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.oracle_settings.database_name: Specifies the Oracle database name (SID or service name) that the AWS DMS data provider uses to connect to the Oracle source database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.oracle_settings.port: The TCP port number used to connect to the Oracle database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.oracle_settings.secrets_manager: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS uses to access Oracle Automatic Storage Management (ASM) credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager for the Oracle data provider.
The identifier of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Oracle ASM credentials used for this data provider's Oracle settings.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS uses to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret storing the Oracle database encryption key, enabling DMS to decrypt the Oracle database data.

Specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret identifier (ARN or name) that stores the Oracle database security encryption password, used by the DMS data provider to authenticate and access the encrypted Oracle data source.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.oracle_settings.server_name: The host name or IP address of the Oracle database server that this data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.oracle_settings.ssl_mode: Specifies the SSL mode (e.g., none, require, verify-ca, verify-full) for connections to the Oracle data provider, controlling whether and how TLS encryption and certificate verification are applied.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.postgre_sql_settings.certificat: The ARN of the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to securely connect to the PostgreSQL database when SSL/TLS is enabled for the data provider.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.postgre_sql_settings.database_n: The name of the PostgreSQL database that this DMS data provider connects to and manages metadata for.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.postgre_sql_settings.port: The TCP port number on which the PostgreSQL database server accepts connections.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.postgre_sql_settings.server_nam: Specifies the host name or IP address of the PostgreSQL server that the data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.postgre_sql_settings.ssl_mode: Specifies the SSL mode to use when connecting to the PostgreSQL database, such as 'none', 'require', 'verify-ca', or 'verify-full'.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.redshift_settings.database_name: The name of the Redshift database that the AWS DMS data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.redshift_settings.port: The TCP port number used to connect to the Amazon Redshift data provider (default is 5439).
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.redshift_settings.server_name: The hostname or IP address of the Amazon Redshift server that the DMS data provider connects to.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.sybase_ase_settings.certificate: The ARN of the certificate used to encrypt connections between the DMS data provider and the Sybase ASE database via SSL/TLS.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.sybase_ase_settings.database_na: The name of the Sybase ASE database to which the data provider connects.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.sybase_ase_settings.encrypt_pas: Indicates whether the password for the Sybase ASE database is encrypted in the data provider settings.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.sybase_ase_settings.port: The TCP port number used to connect to the Sybase Adaptive Server Enterprise database.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.sybase_ase_settings.server_name: The hostname or IP address of the Sybase Adaptive Server Enterprise (ASE) database server to which the data provider connects.
aws_dms_data_provider.settings.sybase_ase_settings.ssl_mode: Determines the SSL mode for the Sybase ASE data provider connection, specifying whether SSL is enforced and how the server certificate is verified.
aws_dms_data_provider.tags.key: The tag key for a tag attached to the AWS DMS data provider, used to categorize and manage the resource.
aws_dms_data_provider.tags.value: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the DMS Data Provider, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_dms_endpoint.tags.key: The key portion of a user-defined tag attached to the DMS endpoint, used for identifying and organizing the resource within AWS.
aws_dms_endpoint.tags.value: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS DMS endpoint.

aws_dms_event_subscription.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS DMS event subscription, used to categorize and identify the resource.
aws_dms_event_subscription.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS DMS event subscription.

aws_dms_migration_project.schema_conversion_application_attributes: The S3 bucket path (prefix) where the AWS DMS Schema Conversion application stores schema conversion artifacts (such as converted schemas and mapping rules) for the migration project.

The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS assumes to access the S3 bucket used by the schema conversion application, enabling it to read and write schema conversion artifacts to the bucket specified by the sibling `s3_bucket_path` attribute.
aws_dms_migration_project.source_data_provider_descriptors.data_pr: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the source data provider used to configure the migration project in AWS Database Migration Service.
Specifies the unique identifier or ARN of the AWS DMS source data provider associated with this migration project.
The name of an existing AWS DMS data provider that acts as the source for this migration project, used within a source data provider descriptor.
aws_dms_migration_project.source_data_provider_descriptors.secrets: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS assumes to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the source data provider's credentials.
Specifies the ARN or name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the credentials for the source database in the migration project.
aws_dms_migration_project.tags.key: The key of a tag that can be assigned to an AWS DMS migration project, used for categorizing, identifying, and managing the project resource within the service.
aws_dms_migration_project.tags.value: The user-defined string value of a tag applied to an AWS DMS migration project, used to store metadata such as project purpose, owner, or environment for resource management and cost tracking.
aws_dms_migration_project.target_data_provider_descriptors.data_pr: The ARN of the AWS DMS data provider that acts as the target endpoint for the migration project.
In the list of target data provider descriptors for the migration project, specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target data provider.
The name of the target data provider that the DMS migration project uses as its destination, referencing an existing AWS DMS data provider resource.
aws_dms_migration_project.target_data_provider_descriptors.secrets: ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS assumes to read the target data provider's connection credentials from AWS Secrets Manager.

The secrets_manager_secret_id within a target data provider descriptor specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret (by name or ARN) that stores the connection details for the target database endpoint used by the DMS migration project.

aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.availability_zone: Specifies the Availability Zone (AZ) in which the AWS DMS replication instance associated with this replication config will be provisioned.
aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.dns_name_servers: Specifies the custom DNS name servers (as a comma-separated list of IP addresses) that the AWS DMS replication instance uses for name resolution.
aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.kms_key_id: The ARN or ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data on the storage attached to the AWS DMS replication instance.
aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.max_capacity_units: The maximum number of DMS capacity units that the replication can scale to, defining the upper limit of compute capacity for the AWS DMS replication config.
aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.min_capacity_units: Sets the minimum number of DMS capacity units to provision for a serverless replication, defining the lower bound for automatic scaling of compute resources.
aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.multi_az: Specifies whether to enable Multi-AZ deployment for the AWS DMS replication config's compute environment, providing high availability by provisioning a standby replica in a different Availability Zone.
aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.preferred_maintenance_win: Specifies the preferred weekly maintenance window (in UTC, format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi) during which AWS Database Migration Service can perform maintenance on the replication services associated with this replication config.
aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.replication_subnet_group_: The identifier of the AWS DMS replication subnet group in which the replication instance for this replication config is deployed.
aws_dms_replication_config.compute_config.vpc_security_group_ids: Specifies the VPC security group IDs to associate with the compute configuration for the AWS DMS replication, controlling network access to the replication environment.
aws_dms_replication_config.tags.key: The key of a key-value tag that can be attached to the DMS replication configuration for resource management and cost allocation.
aws_dms_replication_config.tags.value: The value portion of a tag assigned to the AWS DMS replication configuration, used for metadata, identification, and cost allocation.

aws_dms_replication_instance.allocated_storage: Specifies the amount of storage (in gigabytes) to allocate for the AWS DMS replication instance.
aws_dms_replication_instance.allow_major_version_upgrade: Indicates whether major version upgrades are allowed for the replication instance, and must be set to true to permit such upgrades when the engine version is changed.
aws_dms_replication_instance.auto_minor_version_upgrade: Indicates whether minor engine version upgrades are applied automatically to the replication instance during the maintenance window.
aws_dms_replication_instance.availability_zone: Specifies the Availability Zone (AZ) in which the AWS DMS replication instance is created, influencing placement and failover behavior for Multi-AZ deployments.
aws_dms_replication_instance.dns_name_servers: Specifies a comma-separated list of DNS name servers that the AWS DMS replication instance uses to resolve domain names for source and target endpoints.
aws_dms_replication_instance.engine_version: Specifies the DMS engine version number to use for the replication instance, such as '3.4.4'.
aws_dms_replication_instance.id: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DMS replication instance, generated by AWS and used as the unique Terraform resource identifier.
aws_dms_replication_instance.kms_key_id: This field specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or ID of an AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) used to encrypt the storage and data on the DMS replication instance, instead of the default AWS-managed key.
aws_dms_replication_instance.multi_az: Specifies whether the replication instance is deployed across multiple Availability Zones for high availability.
aws_dms_replication_instance.network_type: Specifies whether the replication instance uses IPv4 only (ipv4) or dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 (dual) for network connectivity.
aws_dms_replication_instance.preferred_maintenance_window: Specifies the preferred time window (in the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi, e.g., 'sun:01:00-sun:02:00') during which AWS may perform maintenance on the replication instance.
aws_dms_replication_instance.publicly_accessible: Whether the DMS replication instance is publicly accessible, meaning it receives a public IP address and can be reached from the internet, as opposed to being private within the VPC.
aws_dms_replication_instance.replication_instance_class: The compute and memory capacity class for the replication instance, such as dms.t2.small or dms.c4.large, which determines the performance and cost of the instance.
aws_dms_replication_instance.replication_instance_identifier: Specifies a user-defined name for the replication instance, which must be unique within the AWS account and region and can include letters, numbers, and hyphens.
aws_dms_replication_instance.replication_instance_private_ip_addresse: The list of private IP addresses assigned to the AWS Database Migration Service replication instance.
aws_dms_replication_instance.replication_instance_public_ip_addresses: The public IP addresses assigned to the DMS replication instance when it is configured for public accessibility.
aws_dms_replication_instance.replication_subnet_group_identifier: The identifier of an existing DMS replication subnet group that determines the VPC and subnets where the replication instance's network interfaces are placed.
aws_dms_replication_instance.tags: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the DMS replication instance, which are used for cost allocation, access control, and identifying the resource in AWS.
aws_dms_replication_instance.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS DMS replication instance, used to associate arbitrary metadata (e.g., environment, owner, or cost center) with the resource for management and cost allocation purposes.
aws_dms_replication_instance.vpc_security_group_ids: Specifies the VPC security group IDs to be associated with the DMS replication instance.

aws_dms_replication_subnet_group.tags.value: The value portion of a tag (key-value pair) assigned to the DMS replication subnet group, used to categorize and manage the resource for cost allocation and operational purposes.

aws_dms_replication_task.cdc_start_position: Specifies the native source database position (such as a log file number or LSN) from which AWS DMS begins reading change data capture (CDC) changes when starting the replication task.
aws_dms_replication_task.cdc_start_time: The Unix timestamp in seconds that specifies when Change Data Capture (CDC) should begin for the replication task, defining the starting point for capturing ongoing data changes.
aws_dms_replication_task.cdc_stop_position: Specifies the point in time (as a Unix timestamp) or LSN (log sequence number) up to which the change data capture (CDC) portion of the replication task should process changes, after which the task stops.
aws_dms_replication_task.id: The ARN of the DMS replication task, which uniquely identifies it within AWS.
aws_dms_replication_task.migration_type: Specifies the migration type for the replication task, which can be one of 'full-load', 'cdc', or 'full-load-and-cdc'.
aws_dms_replication_task.replication_instance_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS DMS replication instance that will run the replication task.
aws_dms_replication_task.replication_task_identifier: A user-supplied unique identifier for the DMS replication task within an AWS account, used to reference and manage the task in AWS DMS.
aws_dms_replication_task.replication_task_settings: A JSON-format string that configures the AWS DMS replication task's operational settings, such as target table preparation mode, full load behavior, and error handling options.
aws_dms_replication_task.source_endpoint_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the source database endpoint that the DMS replication task reads data from during migration.
aws_dms_replication_task.table_mappings: JSON string that specifies table mapping rules, including selection and transformation rules, for a DMS replication task.
aws_dms_replication_task.tags: Assigns metadata key-value pairs to the DMS replication task for resource categorization and cost tracking.
aws_dms_replication_task.tags.key: Specifies the key of a tag attached to the AWS DMS replication task, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.
aws_dms_replication_task.target_endpoint_arn: The ARN of the target database endpoint that the replication task connects to for writing migrated data.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.availability_zones: The list of Availability Zones where the cluster's instances are distributed, enabling multi-AZ deployment for high availability.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.backup_retention_period: The number of days for which automated backups of the DocumentDB cluster are retained.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.cluster_resource_id: The unique cluster resource identifier assigned by AWS when the DocDB cluster is created, used to construct the cluster ARN.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.copy_tags_to_snapshot: Indicates whether to copy all tags from the DB cluster to snapshots of the cluster, so that the snapshots inherit the cluster's tags.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.dbcluster_identifier: Specifies a unique identifier for the DB cluster, which is stored as a lowercase string and used as the cluster's name.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.dbcluster_parameter_group_name: The name of the DocumentDB cluster parameter group to associate with this DB cluster, which contains engine configuration values applied to all instances in the cluster.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.dbsubnet_group_name: The name of the DB subnet group the DocumentDB cluster uses, which must contain subnets in at least two Availability Zones.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.deletion_protection: When set to true, deletion protection is enabled for this DocumentDB cluster, preventing the cluster from being deleted via the AWS Management Console or API until deletion protection is explicitly disabled.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.enable_cloudwatch_logs_exports: Specifies the log types (for example, 'audit' or 'profiler') that the DocumentDB cluster exports to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.endpoint: The endpoint is the read-only primary connection hostname for the DocumentDB cluster, used to connect applications to the cluster's primary instance.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.engine_version: Specifies the version number of the database engine (e.g., '4.0', '5.0') to use for the DocumentDB cluster.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.global_cluster_identifier: The identifier of the Amazon DocumentDB global cluster to which this DB cluster belongs, used to join a cluster to a global cluster that spans multiple regions.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.id: The cluster's unique identifier, which corresponds to the DB cluster's name as specified at creation time.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.kms_key_id: The AWS KMS key ID or ARN used to encrypt the storage for this DocumentDB cluster.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.manage_master_user_password: Indicates whether the master user password is managed by AWS Secrets Manager, enabling automatic rotation and secure retrieval.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.master_user_password: The password for the master database user used to authenticate and manage the Amazon DocumentDB cluster, required when creating a new cluster unless you are restoring from a snapshot.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.master_user_secret_kms_key_id: The AWS KMS key identifier used to encrypt the master user password stored as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager, where omitting it defaults to the aws/secretsmanager key.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.master_username: The master username for the DocumentDB cluster, used to authenticate as the administrative user.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.network_type: Specifies the network type for the cluster, either IPV4 for IPv4 only or DUAL to support both IPv4 and IPv6 addressing.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.port: The port number on which the DocumentDB DB cluster accepts connections, defaulting to 27017.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.preferred_backup_window: The daily time range, in UTC and 24-hour format (HH24:MI-HH24:MI), during which automated backups are created for the DocumentDB cluster.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.preferred_maintenance_window: The weekly time range (in UTC) during which system maintenance, such as patching, may occur on the Amazon DocumentDB cluster, specified in the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi (e.g., Mon:00:00-Mon:03:00).
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.read_endpoint: The reader endpoint for the DocumentDB cluster, which routes read connections to available replica instances.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.restore_to_time: Specifies the UTC time (in ISO 8601 format) to restore the DB cluster to, when performing a point-in-time restore.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.restore_type: Specifies the type of restore to perform when creating the DB cluster from a snapshot or point-in-time backup, with allowed values typically being 'full' or 'copy-on-write'.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.rotate_master_user_password: Indicates whether to rotate the master user password for the DocumentDB cluster; enabling this triggers generation of a new password stored as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.serverless_v2_scaling_configuration: Configures the minimum and maximum Amazon DocumentDB capacity units (ACUs) for a DocumentDB cluster running in Serverless v2 mode.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.serverless_v2_scaling_configuration.max_: The maximum number of DocumentDB capacity units (DCUs) that the serverless v2 cluster can scale up to, setting the upper bound for compute and memory capacity.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.serverless_v2_scaling_configuration.min_: The minimum capacity in Amazon Capacity Units (ACUs) that the DocumentDB Serverless v2 cluster can scale down to.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.snapshot_identifier: The identifier of an existing DB cluster snapshot to restore the cluster from when creating it.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.storage_encrypted: Indicates whether the DB cluster's storage is encrypted at rest, using AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.storage_type: Selects the storage configuration for the DocumentDB cluster, where 'standard' uses general-purpose SSD storage and 'iopt1' uses I/O-Optimized storage with dedicated IOPS pricing.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.tags: A list of key-value tags to attach to the DocumentDB cluster for identification and resource management.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.use_latest_restorable_time: When performing a point-in-time restore, this boolean determines whether to restore the DB cluster to the latest restorable time; if true, `restore_to_time` must be omitted, and a source cluster identifier is required.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster.vpc_security_group_ids: The list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the DocumentDB cluster, controlling which network security groups can access the cluster.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.description: A user-supplied description of the DB cluster parameter group, which is required when creating the group and helps identify its purpose.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.family: The database engine family that this DocDB cluster parameter group applies to (e.g., 'docdb3.6' or 'docdb4.0'), which determines the set of parameters available for the cluster.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.id: The name of the DocumentDB cluster parameter group, which serves as its unique identifier.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.name: The name of the DB cluster parameter group; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name for the group.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.parameters: The parameters block defines the individual parameters (name, value, and apply method) to associate with the DocumentDB cluster parameter group.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.tags: A list of key-value pairs (tags) to assign to the DocumentDB DB cluster parameter group for resource categorization and management.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.tags.key: The key of a key-value tag attached to the DocumentDB cluster parameter group, used to identify and categorize the resource within AWS.
aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.tags.value: The value portion of a tag attached to the DocumentDB cluster parameter group, which together with the tag key forms a key-value label used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.auto_minor_version_upgrade: Indicates whether minor engine version upgrades are applied automatically to the DB instance during its maintenance window.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.availability_zone: Specifies the Availability Zone (AZ) where the Amazon DocumentDB DB instance is provisioned, for example, us-east-1a.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.cacertificate_identifier: Specifies the identifier of the CA certificate used for the DocumentDB DB instance's server certificate, allowing you to rotate the certificate used for TLS connections.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.certificate_rotation_restart: Whether the DocumentDB instance is restarted automatically when the CA certificate for the instance is rotated, allowing the new certificate to take effect without manual action.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.dbcluster_identifier: The identifier of the DocumentDB cluster this instance will belong to, defining the cluster in which the instance is created and replicated.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.dbinstance_class: The compute and memory capacity class of the Amazon DocumentDB instance (e.g., db.r5.large), which determines its performance characteristics and pricing.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.dbinstance_identifier: The user-supplied unique identifier for the DocumentDB DB instance, which must be unique within an AWS account and Region; if not provided, CloudFormation generates one automatically.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.enable_performance_insights: A boolean flag that when true enables Performance Insights, a database performance monitoring and tuning feature, for the Amazon DocumentDB DB instance.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.endpoint: The endpoint address of the DocumentDB instance, providing the hostname used to connect to the database.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.id: The unique identifier of the DocumentDB DB instance, matching the DB instance identifier.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.port: The TCP port number, assigned by AWS, on which the DocumentDB instance accepts connections (for example, 27017).
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.preferred_maintenance_window: Specifies the weekly time range (in UTC) during which Amazon DocumentDB performs system maintenance on this DB instance, using the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi (e.g., sun:05:00-sun:06:00).
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.tags: Specifies a list of tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the DocumentDB DB instance for categorization and access control.
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.tags.key: The key of a tag to assign to the DocumentDB DB instance, used for identifying and organizing the resource (for example, 'Name' or 'Environment').
aws_doc_db_dbinstance.tags.value: The user-defined value of a tag applied to the DocumentDB DB instance, used to store arbitrary metadata such as environment, cost center, or project for resource organization and management.

aws_doc_db_dbsubnet_group.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon DocumentDB DB subnet group, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource (e.g., via cost allocation or access control).
aws_doc_db_dbsubnet_group.tags.value: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the DocumentDB DB subnet group, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_doc_db_global_cluster.tags.key: The key portion of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon DocumentDB global cluster, used for metadata, cost allocation, and access control.
aws_doc_db_global_cluster.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the DocumentDB global cluster.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.admin_user_name: The administrative (master) username for the DocumentDB elastic cluster, used as the initial admin user for authentication.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.admin_user_password: Password for the admin user account that is created to access the elastic cluster's database.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.auth_type: Specifies the authentication type for the cluster, indicating whether the admin password is supplied as plain text (PLAIN_TEXT) or via a Secrets Manager secret ARN (SECRET_ARN).
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.backup_retention_period: Specifies the number of days that automatic backups of the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster are retained.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.cluster_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the DocumentDB elastic cluster.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.cluster_endpoint: The connection endpoint for the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, used by applications to connect to the cluster.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.cluster_name: Specifies the name of the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, which is used as a unique identifier for the cluster within your AWS account and region.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.kms_key_id: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data at rest in the DocumentDB elastic cluster.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.preferred_backup_window: Specifies the preferred daily time range, in UTC (format HH24:MI-HH24:MI), during which AWS automatically creates backups for the Amazon DocumentDB Elastic Cluster.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.preferred_maintenance_window: The weekly time range (in UTC) during which system maintenance may occur for the DocumentDB elastic cluster, specified in the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi (e.g., Mon:01:00-Mon:02:00).
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.shard_capacity: The number of vCPUs allocated to each shard in the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, defining the compute capacity per shard.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.shard_count: The desired number of shards for the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, where each shard is an independent partition of the cluster's data and this value directly determines the cluster's storage and compute capacity.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.shard_instance_count: Specifies the number of instance nodes to provision for each shard in the DocumentDB elastic cluster, affecting shard high availability and failover behavior.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.subnet_ids: Specifies the VPC subnet IDs in which the Amazon DocumentDB Elastic Cluster's instances are deployed, determining the cluster's network placement within a VPC.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.tags: Specifies the key-value tags to associate with the DocumentDB Elastic Cluster for resource identification and management within AWS.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon DocumentDB Elastic Cluster, enabling the resource to be categorized, identified, and filtered by user-defined metadata.
aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.vpc_security_group_ids: A list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the cluster, controlling inbound and outbound network access.

aws_drs_source_network.tags.key: A user-defined key for a tag on the AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) Source Network, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_dsql_cluster.multi_region_properties.clusters: Specifies the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the linked regional DSQL clusters that form the multi-region cluster.
aws_dsql_cluster.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the DSQL cluster, used to organize and identify the cluster for management and cost allocation.
aws_dsql_cluster.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the DSQL cluster, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the DynamoDB global table, assigned by AWS upon creation.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.attribute_definitions: Defines the name and type of each attribute used in the key schema (partition key and optional sort key) for the DynamoDB global table, where each item specifies an AttributeName and AttributeType.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.attribute_definitions.attribute_name: The name of the attribute to be used in the global table's key schema or secondary indexes, matching the attribute names in the table's item definitions.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.attribute_definitions.attribute_type: The data type of the attribute in the DynamoDB Global Table's attribute definition, which must be one of 'S' (string), 'N' (number), or 'B' (binary).
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.billing_mode: Specifies how read and write throughput is billed for the global table, either PROVISIONED (with provisioned capacity) or PAY_PER_REQUEST (on-demand).
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes: Specifies the global secondary indexes (GSIs) for the DynamoDB global table, defining each index's name, key schema, projection, and provisioned throughput settings that are replicated across all regional replicas.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.index_name: The name of the global secondary index for the DynamoDB global table, which must be unique within the table and is used to query the indexed data.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.key_schema: Key schema for the global secondary index, defining the partition (HASH) and optional sort (RANGE) key attributes that determine the index's data organization.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.key_schema.attr: The name of the attribute that serves as the partition key or sort key in the global secondary index's key schema, which must match an attribute defined in the table's attribute definitions.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.key_schema.key_: Specifies whether the key attribute is a HASH (partition) key or RANGE (sort) key for the global secondary index's key schema in a DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.projection: Specifies the set of attributes that are projected into the global secondary index, including the projection type (e.g., ALL, KEYS_ONLY, or INCLUDE) and any non-key attributes to include when the type is INCLUDE.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.projection.non_: Specifies the list of non-key attribute names to include in the global secondary index's projection, used only when the projection type is set to INCLUDE.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.projection.proj: Specifies the set of attributes that are projected into the global secondary index, allowing values such as KEYS_ONLY, INCLUDE, or ALL to control which table attributes are copied to the index.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.read_on_demand_: Configures the on-demand read throughput settings for this global secondary index, setting the maximum read request units so the index scales automatically with DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode.
Sets the maximum number of read request units that the global secondary index can consume in on-demand capacity mode, capping its read throughput within the read on-demand throughput settings.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.read_provisione: Configures the read capacity units or auto scaling settings for read throughput of the specified global secondary index in this DynamoDB global table.
For each global secondary index on the DynamoDB global table, this specifies the maximum number of strongly consistent reads consumed per second before DynamoDB returns a ThrottlingException.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.warm_throughput: Specifies the warm throughput settings (read and write units per second) for the global secondary index of the DynamoDB global table.
The number of warm read units per second for the global secondary index, used to pre-provision read capacity for on-demand DynamoDB tables to prevent throttling during sudden traffic spikes.
Specifies the number of warm write throughput capacity units to allocate for this global secondary index of the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.write_on_demand: Specifies the maximum write request units that this global secondary index can consume when the table is set to on-demand capacity mode.
Specifies the maximum number of write request units that the global secondary index can consume per second when the DynamoDB global table is set to on-demand capacity mode.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_secondary_indexes.write_provision: Specifies the write capacity settings (either fixed write capacity units or auto-scaling configuration) for the global secondary index of the DynamoDB global table.
Configures auto scaling settings (minimum/maximum write capacity units and target utilization) for the write capacity of the global secondary index in a DynamoDB global table.

The maximum number of write capacity units that Application Auto Scaling can scale the global secondary index's write capacity up to under the associated scaling policy, as defined in the write capacity auto scaling settings of a DynamoDB global table.
The minimum number of write capacity units that the auto scaling policy can scale down to for the global secondary index.
The initial number of write capacity units to allocate for the global secondary index before DynamoDB auto scaling adjusts capacity based on actual utilization.

Configuration for the target-tracking scaling policy that DynamoDB Auto Scaling uses to manage the write capacity of this global secondary index, including the target utilization percentage (TargetValue) and whether scale-in is disabled.
When set to true, prevents the target tracking scaling policy from scaling in (decreasing) the write capacity of the global secondary index.
The scale-in cooldown period, in seconds, for the write capacity auto scaling of this global secondary index, during which DynamoDB suppresses scaling-in actions.

Scale-out cooldown, in seconds, for the write capacity auto scaling target tracking policy of the global secondary index, controlling how long to wait after a scale-out activity before another can start.

Specifies the target utilization percentage (e.g., 70 for 70%) that the target tracking scaling policy for write capacity of this global secondary index will maintain, triggering scaling when actual utilization deviates.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_table_source_arn: The ARN of an existing DynamoDB table whose data is used to populate the global table when it is created.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_table_witnesses: Configures the witness regions for the DynamoDB global table, which participate in quorum for multi-Region strong consistency without storing a full replica of the table data.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.key_schema: Determines the primary key for the global table by listing the attributes that form the partition key and optional sort key, each with a KeyType of HASH or RANGE.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.key_schema.attribute_name: Specifies the name of an attribute that is part of the primary key (partition key or sort key) of the DynamoDB global table's key schema.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.key_schema.key_type: Specifies whether the attribute named in this key schema element serves as the hash (partition) key or range (sort) key of the DynamoDB table's primary key.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_secondary_indexes: A list of local secondary indexes (LSIs) for the global table, each specifying an alternate sort key to enable querying by a non-key attribute within a partition.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_secondary_indexes.index_name: The unique name of the local secondary index, which is required to define the index and is used to reference it in DynamoDB queries and operations.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_secondary_indexes.key_schema: Defines the partition key and optional sort key for the local secondary index, using AttributeName and KeyType pairs that must reference attributes declared in the parent table's AttributeDefinitions.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_secondary_indexes.key_schema.attri: Specifies the name of a key attribute in the key schema of a local secondary index, which must match an attribute defined in the global table's attribute definitions.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_secondary_indexes.key_schema.key_t: Specifies whether the key is a partition key (HASH) or a sort key (RANGE) in the key schema of a local secondary index for the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_secondary_indexes.projection: Specifies which table attributes are copied into the local secondary index, defined by a ProjectionType (ALL, KEYS_ONLY, or INCLUDE) and optional NonKeyAttributes for the INCLUDE type.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_secondary_indexes.projection.non_k: Specifies the non-key attribute names to include in the projection of the local secondary index when ProjectionType is set to INCLUDE.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_secondary_indexes.projection.proje: Determines which attributes are projected into the local secondary index, valid values are KEYS_ONLY, INCLUDE, or ALL, controlling whether only the key attributes, a specified set of non-key attributes, or all attributes are copied into the index.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.multi_region_consistency: Specifies the multi-region consistency mode for the DynamoDB global table, with allowed values of 'EVENTUAL' or 'STRONG', controlling whether strongly consistent reads are available across all replica regions.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.read_on_demand_throughput_settings: Specifies the read on-demand throughput settings for a replica in the global table, including the maximum read request units allowed when the table uses on-demand capacity mode.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.read_on_demand_throughput_settings.max_r: Sets the maximum read capacity, in read request units, that the global DynamoDB table can scale up to when using on-demand capacity mode.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.read_provisioned_throughput_settings: Specifies the read capacity provisioning settings for a replica of the DynamoDB global table, including a fixed read capacity unit count or auto-scaling configuration.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.read_provisioned_throughput_settings.rea: Sets the maximum number of strongly consistent read operations per second consumed per replica for a DynamoDB global table, used to configure the provisioned capacity for the replica's read throughput.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas: Defines the AWS Regions in which replicas of the DynamoDB global table are created, along with per-replica settings such as point-in-time recovery and contributor insights.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.contributor_insights_specificat: Specifies the Contributor Insights configuration for this replica, including whether Contributor Insights is enabled on the replica table.
Specifies whether CloudWatch Contributor Insights is enabled for this replica of the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.deletion_protection_enabled: When true, deletion protection is enabled for this replica table in the DynamoDB global table, preventing the replica from being successfully deleted via a DeleteTable operation.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.global_secondary_indexes: Specifies the global secondary indexes to be configured on a specific replica of the DynamoDB global table, allowing per-replica provisioning overrides (such as read/write capacity) for those indexes in that region.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.global_secondary_indexes.contri: Configures whether CloudWatch Contributor Insights is enabled for a specific global secondary index on a replica table of a DynamoDB global table.
Determines whether CloudWatch Contributor Insights is enabled for the global secondary index on this replica of the DynamoDB global table.
This field sets the CloudWatch Contributor Insights mode for the specified global secondary index within a replica of the DynamoDB global table, with allowed values ENABLED and DISABLED.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.global_secondary_indexes.index_: The name of the global secondary index in the replica's configuration that the GSI override settings apply to, matching an index defined on the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.global_secondary_indexes.read_o: Specifies the on-demand (pay-per-request) read throughput settings for the global secondary index replica, including the maximum read request units that can be consumed per second.
Specifies the maximum number of read request units for the global secondary index in a replica of a DynamoDB global table when it uses on-demand capacity mode.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.global_secondary_indexes.read_p: Specifies the read capacity settings for a global secondary index in a specific replica of a DynamoDB global table.

Configures the application auto-scaling settings for the read capacity of the global secondary index in the replica, including minimum and maximum read capacity and the target tracking scaling policy.
The maximum number of read capacity units that auto scaling can scale the global secondary index to for this replica in a DynamoDB global table.
The minimum number of read capacity units that Application Auto Scaling can scale down to for this global secondary index replica's read capacity.
Seed capacity for the global secondary index's read auto scaling in this replica, representing the initial read capacity units DynamoDB provisions before scaling adjusts.

This object configures the target tracking scaling policy for Application Auto Scaling on the read capacity of a global secondary index in a DynamoDB global table replica, specifying the target utilization value that triggers scaling adjustments.

When set to true, prevents the DynamoDB read capacity auto scaling target tracking policy from scaling in (reducing) the provisioned read capacity for the global secondary index, while still allowing scale-out to increase capacity.
The scale-in cooldown period (in seconds) that DynamoDB waits after a scale-in activity before it can trigger another scale-in for read capacity of a global secondary index replica.
The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-out activity completes before another scale-out activity can start for the global secondary index read capacity of this replica.

The target utilization percentage for the read capacity auto scaling policy, representing the desired ratio of consumed read capacity to provisioned read capacity for the global secondary index in the replica's read capacity autoscaling configuration.
The number of read capacity units to provision for the global secondary index in the specified replica, controlling the read throughput for that index in that region.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.global_table_settings_replicati: Sets the replication mode for the global table, within a replica's global table settings, to either STANDARD (no cross-region replication) or REMOTE (cross-region global table).
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.kinesis_stream_specification: Specifies the Kinesis Data Streams configuration for a replica of the DynamoDB global table, controlling whether a stream is enabled and optionally referencing an existing stream ARN.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.kinesis_stream_specification.ap: Specifies the precision of the ApproximateCreationDateTime value in the Kinesis stream for a replica, either MILLISECOND or MICROSECOND.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.kinesis_stream_specification.st: Specifies the ARN of the Amazon Kinesis Data Stream that receives item-level updates for this replica in the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.point_in_time_recovery_specific: Configuration for point-in-time recovery (PITR) settings on a specific replica of the DynamoDB global table, containing a boolean flag that enables or disables PITR for that replica.
Enables or disables point-in-time recovery for the corresponding replica of the DynamoDB global table, allowing the replica to be restored to any point in time within the backup window.
Specifies the number of days for which point-in-time recovery data is retained for the given replica of the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.read_on_demand_throughput_setti: Configures the read on-demand throughput settings for a replica in a DynamoDB global table, including the maximum read request units for on-demand capacity mode.
Specifies the maximum number of read request units that a replica of the DynamoDB global table can consume on-demand, setting an upper bound on its read throughput.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.read_provisioned_throughput_set: Defines the provisioned read capacity settings for a specific replica of the DynamoDB global table, including either a fixed read capacity unit count or auto scaling read settings.

Specifies the read capacity auto scaling settings for a replica, including the minimum and maximum provisioned capacity, optional seed capacity, and the target tracking scaling policy configuration that DynamoDB uses to adjust read capacity.
The maximum provisioned read capacity units that the auto scaling policy is allowed to scale up to for this replica.
The minimum number of read capacity units that DynamoDB auto scaling can scale down to for the replica's read capacity.
Specifies the initial read capacity units for the replica that are provisioned before auto scaling begins, serving as the starting point for the auto scaling group.

Specifies the target tracking scaling policy configuration for read capacity auto scaling on a DynamoDB Global Table replica, controlling target utilization, scale-in/scale-out cooldowns, and whether scale-in is disabled.
DisableScaleIn determines whether the target tracking scaling policy for read capacity auto scaling on this replica is prevented from scaling in (reducing provisioned read capacity).

The number of seconds for the scale-in cooldown period, during which App Auto Scaling suppresses additional scale-in activities for the read capacity of this replica after a scale-in activity completes.
The amount of time, in seconds, to wait after a scale-out activity before another scale-out activity can occur, controlling how quickly read capacity increases for this replica.
The target utilization percentage for the read capacity auto scaling policy on this global table replica, representing the desired fraction of provisioned read capacity to consume.
Specifies the maximum number of strongly consistent reads per second for the replica table in a DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.region: The AWS Region in which a replica of the DynamoDB global table is created.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.replica_stream_specification: Configures DynamoDB Streams for a specific replica in the global table, including whether streaming is enabled and the stream view type (e.g., NEW_IMAGE, OLD_IMAGE) that determines which data changes are written.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.replica_stream_specification.re: Specifies a resource-based policy that controls access to the DynamoDB stream associated with the replica, enabling cross-account stream sharing and read access.
Specifies the JSON policy document that defines the resource-based permissions for the DynamoDB stream attached to this replica, controlling cross-account or cross-region access to the stream data.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.replica_stream_specification.ta: The key of a tag to be applied to the stream specification of a replica in a DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.resource_policy: Defines the IAM resource-based policy (JSON) applied to the DynamoDB replica table in the corresponding region, allowing replica-specific access control separate from the global table's default policy.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.resource_policy.policy_document: The IAM policy document (in JSON format) that defines the resource-based permissions policy for the replica table, allowing you to grant cross-account or cross-service access to that specific replica in the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.ssespecification: Configures the server-side encryption (SSE) for a specific replica of a DynamoDB global table, allowing you to specify an AWS KMS key (via KMSMasterKeyId) for encrypting data in that replica.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.ssespecification.kmsmaster_key_: The KMS key ID or ARN used for server-side encryption in the SSE specification of a specific replica of the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.table_class: Specifies the table class for a replica, either STANDARD or STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS, which determines the storage and throughput cost tier for that regional table copy.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.tags: Specifies the list of tags to associate with each replica table in the DynamoDB global table, allowing you to apply different tags per replica region.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to a specific replica (Region) of the global DynamoDB table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.ssespecification: Specifies the server-side encryption (SSE) configuration for the DynamoDB global table, including whether encryption is enabled and the encryption key type (such as AWS owned or customer-managed KMS) to use.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.ssespecification.sseenabled: Specifies whether server-side encryption (SSE) is enabled for the DynamoDB global table, with true enabling encryption using AWS Key Management Service (KMS).
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.ssespecification.ssetype: Specifies the server-side encryption type for the global table, either AES256 (DynamoDB-managed key) or KMS (AWS KMS customer-managed key).
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.stream_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DynamoDB stream for the global table, automatically generated when stream specification is configured.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.stream_specification: The stream specification object configures Amazon DynamoDB Streams for the global table, including the stream enabling flag and stream view type that determines which item changes (keys only, new image, old image, or both) are written to the stream.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.stream_specification.stream_view_type: Specifies which item changes (keys only, new image, old image, or both) are captured in the DynamoDB stream for the global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.table_id: The read-only DynamoDB table ID that uniquely identifies this global table, assigned by AWS when the table is created.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.table_name: The name to assign to the DynamoDB global table; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.time_to_live_specification: Configures Time to Live (TTL) settings for the global table, including whether TTL is enabled and the attribute name that stores the expiration timestamp.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.time_to_live_specification.attribute_nam: Specifies the name of the item attribute that stores the expiration timestamp, enabling DynamoDB to automatically delete expired items from the global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.time_to_live_specification.enabled: Whether time-to-live (TTL) is enabled for the global table, allowing DynamoDB to automatically delete items after a specified expiry timestamp.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.warm_throughput: Specifies the warm throughput (pre-allocated read/write capacity units per second) for the global table to sustain high traffic without throttling.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.warm_throughput.read_units_per_second: Sets the number of warm read capacity units per second for the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.warm_throughput.write_units_per_second: Specifies the number of write capacity units per second to provision for warm throughput on the DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.write_on_demand_throughput_settings: Specifies the optional on-demand write capacity cap (MaxWriteRequestUnits) for the DynamoDB global table, applying this write throughput limit uniformly across all replicas.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.write_on_demand_throughput_settings.max_: Sets the maximum number of write request units for on-demand capacity mode of a replica in a DynamoDB global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.write_provisioned_throughput_settings: Configures the write capacity (provisioned throughput) for the AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable, specifying either a fixed number of write capacity units or auto-scaling settings for each replica in the global table.
aws_dynamo_db_global_table.write_provisioned_throughput_settings.wr: Defines the application auto scaling settings for write capacity on each replica of the DynamoDB global table, including scaling limits and target utilization.
Specifies the maximum number of write capacity units that the write auto scaling policy can scale the global table's write throughput up to.
The minimum number of write capacity units that DynamoDB can scale down to for a replica's write capacity auto scaling in a global table.
The initial number of write capacity units to provision for a new replica table in a DynamoDB global table, applied only when the replica is created before auto scaling adjusts it.
Configuration for the target tracking policy that DynamoDB uses to automatically adjust write capacity, including the target utilization percentage and whether scale-in is disabled.
Indicates whether scale-in by the target tracking policy is disabled for the write capacity auto scaling of this replica in the DynamoDB global table.
The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-in activity completes before another scale-in activity can begin for the DynamoDB write capacity auto scaling target tracking policy.
The amount of time, in seconds, to wait after a scale-out activity completes before another scale-out activity can begin, allowing DynamoDB write capacity to stabilize for the global table.
The target utilization percentage (0-100) for the write capacity auto scaling target tracking policy on the DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_table.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DynamoDB table, automatically assigned by AWS when the table is created.
aws_dynamo_db_table.attribute_definitions.attribute_name: The name of an attribute in the DynamoDB table's attribute definitions, which must correspond to a key schema attribute (partition key, sort key, or index key) for the table or its secondary indexes.
aws_dynamo_db_table.attribute_definitions.attribute_type: Specifies the data type for the attribute, which must be one of S (string), N (number), or B (binary).
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.contributor_ins: Configures CloudWatch Contributor Insights for the global secondary index, with an `Enabled` setting to enable or disable Contributor Insights on that index.
Whether CloudWatch Contributor Insights are enabled for this global secondary index.
Enables or disables CloudWatch Contributor Insights for this global secondary index, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.index_name: The name of the global secondary index, which must be unique within the DynamoDB table and is used to query data through that index.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.key_schema: Specifies the attribute names and key types (HASH or RANGE) that form the partition key and optional sort key for each global secondary index, determining how items are indexed in that GSI.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.key_schema.attr: The name of the table attribute that serves as the partition or sort key for this global secondary index, which must match an attribute declared in the table's AttributeDefinitions.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.key_schema.key_: Specifies whether the key element is a HASH (partition) key or a RANGE (sort) key in the key schema of the global secondary index.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.on_demand_throu: Specifies the maximum read and write request units for a global secondary index when the table is configured for on-demand capacity mode, allowing fine-grained control over the index's throughput limits.
The maximum number of read request units that can be consumed per second by this global secondary index when the table is in on-demand capacity mode.
Sets the maximum number of write request units that this global secondary index can use when it operates in on-demand (pay-per-request) capacity mode, capping its write throughput.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.projection: Configures which table attributes are copied to the global secondary index, including the projection type (ALL, KEYS_ONLY, or INCLUDE) and optional non-key attributes.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.projection.non_: Lists the additional (non-key) table attributes that are copied into the global secondary index when its projection type is INCLUDE.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.projection.proj: Determines which table attributes are copied to the global secondary index: ALL copies every attribute, KEYS_ONLY copies only the table and index keys, and INCLUDE copies only the attributes listed in the projection's NonKeyAttributes.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.provisioned_thr: Configures the read and write capacity units for a global secondary index when the DynamoDB table uses provisioned billing mode.
The number of read capacity units to provision for the global secondary index, controlling the index's throughput for strongly consistent reads when using provisioned billing mode.
The maximum number of write capacity units consumed per second for the global secondary index's provisioned throughput.
aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_indexes.warm_throughput: Specifies the warm throughput capacity (read and write units per second) for the global secondary index when the table uses the Standard-IA (Infrequent Access) storage class, allowing throughput to be set separately for data in the warm storage tier.
The number of read capacity units per second for warm throughput of the global secondary index.
The maximum number of write operations per second for the global secondary index's warm throughput, setting a capacity limit for writes to data in the warm storage tier of the DynamoDB table.
aws_dynamo_db_table.local_secondary_indexes.index_name: The name of the local secondary index, which must be unique within the table and is used to query the table using an alternate sort key.
aws_dynamo_db_table.local_secondary_indexes.key_schema: Defines the key schema for the local secondary index, specifying the partition key (which must be the same as the table's partition key) and a distinct sort key, each with an attribute name and key type (HASH or RANGE).
aws_dynamo_db_table.local_secondary_indexes.key_schema.attri: The name of the attribute that serves as either the required partition key (matching the table's primary key) or the optional sort key in the local secondary index's key schema, and must correspond to an attribute defined in the table's attribute definitions.
