aws_dynamo_db_table.local_secondary_indexes.key_schema.key_t: Specifies whether the corresponding attribute in the local secondary index's key schema is the partition key (HASH) or the sort key (RANGE), which for a local secondary index must be the table's partition key plus an additional attribute for the sort key.
aws_dynamo_db_table.local_secondary_indexes.projection: Specifies which table attributes are copied into the local secondary index, using ALL, KEYS_ONLY, or INCLUDE modes, with INCLUDE requiring an explicit list of non-key attributes to project.
aws_dynamo_db_table.local_secondary_indexes.projection.non_k: A list of non-key attributes that are projected into the local secondary index, in addition to the table's primary key attributes.
aws_dynamo_db_table.local_secondary_indexes.projection.proje: Specifies which attributes are copied from the table to the local secondary index: KEYS_ONLY (only index and table keys), INCLUDE (only the specified non-key attributes), or ALL (all table attributes).
aws_dynamo_db_table.stream_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DynamoDB stream associated with the table, available when a stream specification is enabled on the table.
aws_dynamo_db_table.tags.value: The value of a tag key-value pair assigned to the DynamoDB table, used for resource categorization and identification.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.availability_zone: The Availability Zone where the capacity reservation is created, used to reserve compute capacity in that specific zone for EC2 instances.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.availability_zone_id: Specifies the ID of the Availability Zone (such as use1-az1) in which to create the Capacity Reservation, serving as an alternative to specifying the Availability Zone by name.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.available_instance_count: The number of instances that remain available for use in the Capacity Reservation, reflecting unused capacity that can still be used to launch instances.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.capacity_allocation_set: A computed list of objects that describes how the total instance capacity of the reservation is allocated among different allocation types (e.g., 'used' or 'future'), as reported by the EC2 DescribeCapacityReservations API.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.capacity_allocation_set.allocation_type: Indicates whether the allocated capacity is for 'used' (currently running instances) or 'future' (reserved but not yet running) usage, with allowed values of 'used' or 'future'.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.capacity_allocation_set.count: The number of EC2 instances of the specified instance type to reserve in this capacity reservation allocation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.capacity_reservation_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the EC2 Capacity Reservation, used to uniquely identify the reservation across AWS services.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.capacity_reservation_fleet_id: The ID of the Capacity Reservation Fleet that this capacity reservation belongs to, if it was created as part of a fleet; this value is only set when the reservation is managed by a fleet.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.commitment_info: commitment_info is a computed object that exposes the commitment duration and commitment end date for this EC2 Capacity Reservation, reflecting the reserved capacity's committed term details.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.commitment_info.commitment_end_date: The timestamp indicating when the committed term of the EC2 Capacity Reservation ends, marking the expiration of a reserved capacity commitment.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.commitment_info.committed_instance_count: The number of EC2 instances you are committed to running as part of this Capacity Reservation's commitment, which underpins the capacity reservation's usage commitment and corresponding billing discount.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.create_date: The date and time at which the Capacity Reservation was created.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.ebs_optimized: Indicates whether the capacity reservation is EBS-optimized, which provides dedicated throughput for Amazon EBS I/O.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.end_date: The date and time (in ISO 8601 format) when the Capacity Reservation expires, after which the reserved capacity is released and any instances running in the reservation are automatically stopped or terminated.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.end_date_type: Determines whether the Capacity Reservation has a specific end date/time (limited) or persists indefinitely (unlimited).
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.ephemeral_storage: A Boolean value indicating whether the Capacity Reservation supports instances that use ephemeral (instance store) storage.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.id: The unique capacity reservation identifier (e.g., cr-1234567890abcdef0) assigned by AWS when the reservation is created, used to reference this reservation in API calls and other resources.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.instance_count: The number of instances for which to reserve capacity in the Capacity Reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.instance_match_criteria: Determines how the capacity reservation matches instances: 'open' allows any matching instance to use the reservation automatically, while 'targeted' requires instances to explicitly specify the reservation ID to use it.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.instance_platform: Specifies the operating system platform (e.g., Linux/UNIX, Windows, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, SUSE Linux) that the capacity reservation will support, matching the platform of the AMI used to launch instances.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.instance_type: The EC2 instance type for which to reserve capacity, such as m5.large or c5.xlarge.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.out_post_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Outpost on which to create the Capacity Reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.owner_id: The ID of the AWS account that owns the Capacity Reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.placement_group_arn: The ARN of the cluster placement group in which to create the capacity reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.reservation_type: The type of the Capacity Reservation, either 'default' for on-demand reservations or 'capacity-block' for future-dated reservations.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.start_date: The date and time at which the capacity reservation was started, as reported by the AWS EC2 API.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.state: The current lifecycle state of the capacity reservation, such as 'active', 'pending', 'failed', 'expired', or 'cancelled', as reported by AWS.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.tag_specifications: Specifies one or more tag specifications, each defining a resource type (such as 'capacity-reservation') and a set of tags to apply to the capacity reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.tag_specifications.resource_type: Specifies the type of resource to tag, which for an EC2 Capacity Reservation must be set to `capacity-reservation` to apply the associated tags to that reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.tag_specifications.tags: The list of tags to associate with the EC2 Capacity Reservation, as part of the tag specifications for the resource.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.tag_specifications.tags.key: The key of a tag to apply to the EC2 Capacity Reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.tag_specifications.tags.value: The value of a tag to assign to the EC2 Capacity Reservation, used to categorize or identify the reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.tenancy: The tenancy of the Capacity Reservation, either 'default' for shared hardware or 'dedicated' for a single physical server.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.total_instance_count: The total number of instances for which this Capacity Reservation reserves capacity, reported by EC2 as a read-only attribute that cannot be modified.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.unused_reservation_billing_owner_id: Specifies the AWS account ID that will be billed for unused capacity in this EC2 Capacity Reservation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.allocation_strategy: Determines how the Capacity Reservation Fleet allocates capacity across the specified instance types, either by spreading evenly across them (diversified) or by honoring the priority order you set (prioritized).
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.capacity_reservation_fleet_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the EC2 Capacity Reservation Fleet.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.end_date: Specifies the date and time at which the Capacity Reservation Fleet expires.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.instance_match_criteria: Determines how instances are matched to the capacity reservation fleet: 'open' (default) allows any matching instance to use the reserved capacity, while 'targeted' requires instances to explicitly target the fleet.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.instance_type_specifications: Defines the list of instance type specifications for the capacity reservation fleet, each indicating an instance type, the number of instances to reserve, and the weight used to calculate total capacity.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.instance_type_specifications.availabilit: The Availability Zone in which the capacity reservation for this instance type specification is allocated, enabling the fleet to target capacity across specific zones.
Specifies the unique identifier of the Availability Zone where capacity for the given instance type is reserved, allowing the fleet to target an AZ by its ID rather than its name.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.instance_type_specifications.ebs_optimiz: Specifies whether instances launched in this capacity reservation are EBS-optimized for enhanced performance.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.instance_type_specifications.instance_pl: The operating system platform (e.g., Linux/UNIX, Windows, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, SUSE Linux) for the instance type specification within the EC2 Capacity Reservation Fleet.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.instance_type_specifications.instance_ty: Specifies the EC2 instance type (e.g., `m5.large`, `c5.xlarge`) for which this individual capacity reservation specification within the fleet will reserve capacity.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.instance_type_specifications.priority: The priority of this instance type in the capacity reservation fleet, where lower values indicate higher priority for fulfilling the reservation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.instance_type_specifications.weight: The weight value for an instance type in a Capacity Reservation Fleet determines how much of the fleet's total target capacity each instance of that type consumes when calculating the number of instances needed.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.no_remove_end_date: Setting this to true indicates the Capacity Reservation Fleet has no end date, so it does not expire and automatically release its capacity reservations, remaining active until explicitly deleted.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.remove_end_date: When set to true, this removes the configured end date for the capacity reservation fleet, causing it to remain active indefinitely.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.tag_specifications: Specifies the tags to apply to the Capacity Reservation Fleet during creation, enabling resource management and cost allocation through key-value pairs.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.tag_specifications.resource_type: Specifies the type of resource to tag; for a Capacity Reservation Fleet the only valid value is `capacity-reservation-fleet` (the fleet itself).
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.tag_specifications.tags: The list of tags to apply to the resources identified by the parent tag specification, such as the capacity reservation fleet itself, when creating or managing the fleet.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.tag_specifications.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag applied to an EC2 Capacity Reservation Fleet for identification and management.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.tag_specifications.tags.value: The tag value to associate with the Capacity Reservation Fleet, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the fleet through resource grouping and cost allocation.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.tenancy: The tenancy of the Capacity Reservation Fleet, which indicates whether instances launched in the fleet run on shared (default) or dedicated hardware.
aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.total_target_capacity: The total amount of capacity, in units (each instance counts as one unit unless you apply instance type weights), that the Capacity Reservation Fleet aims to reserve across all instance types and Availability Zones.

aws_ec2_carrier_gateway.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag associated with this EC2 Carrier Gateway, used for identifying, organizing, and cost allocation of the resource.
aws_ec2_carrier_gateway.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the AWS EC2 Carrier Gateway, used for metadata, organization, and cost tracking alongside its corresponding tag key.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.access_group_id: The ID of the Active Directory group that is allowed access to the network; if omitted, all users in the directory are permitted.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.authorize_all_groups: Indicates whether to authorize access to all groups, so when set to true, the rule applies to every Active Directory group, and when false, you must specify target groups via the GroupId field.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.client_vpn_endpoint_id: The ID of the Client VPN endpoint to which this authorization rule applies.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.description: A brief, optional description that identifies the purpose of the Client VPN authorization rule.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.target_network_cidr: The CIDR block of the target network that this authorization rule grants access to for the specified clients or groups.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.authentication_options: Specifies the authentication methods (certificate-based, directory service, or federated/SAML) that clients must use to authenticate to the Client VPN endpoint.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.authentication_options.active_directory: Defines the Active Directory (AWS Directory Service) authentication settings for the Client VPN endpoint, including the directory ID used to authenticate clients.
The ID of the AWS Managed Microsoft Active Directory used for client authentication.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.authentication_options.federated_authent: Specifies the SAML-based federated authentication configuration for the Client VPN endpoint, including the IAM SAML provider ARN(s) used to authenticate users.
The ARN of the IAM SAML identity provider that the Client VPN endpoint uses to authenticate users via federated SAML-based authentication.
The ARN of the IAM SAML identity provider used to authenticate users accessing the self-service portal (where clients can manage their own certificates) for this AWS Client VPN endpoint.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.authentication_options.mutual_authentica: Configures mutual authentication (client certificate) for the Client VPN endpoint, requiring the ARN of the client root certificate chain to verify client certificates.
The ARN of the client root certificate chain that is used for mutual authentication with the AWS Client VPN endpoint.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.authentication_options.type: Specifies the authentication method to use for the Client VPN endpoint, which can be one of certificate-authentication, directory-service-authentication, or federated-authentication.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_cidr_block: The IPv4 CIDR range from which client IP addresses are allocated when they connect to the VPN.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_connect_options: Specifies the client connect options for the Client VPN endpoint, including the Lambda function used for connection authorization and post-connection feedback.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_connect_options.enabled: Specifies whether to enable Client Connect for the Client VPN endpoint, which allows an AWS Lambda function to handle custom authentication and authorization of client connections.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_connect_options.lambda_function_a: The ARN of the Lambda function that handles client connection authorization for the Client VPN endpoint, used when client connect options are enabled.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_login_banner_options: Configures the optional client login banner for the VPN endpoint, specifying whether a banner is enabled and the banner text that clients see during authentication.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_login_banner_options.banner_text: The customizable text displayed in the banner on the AWS-provided client VPN client during a connection session, with a maximum length of 1400 characters.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_login_banner_options.enabled: Specifies whether the Client VPN endpoint shows a customizable login banner to clients before they authenticate.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_route_enforcement_options: Configures the automatic addition of a default route (0.0.0.0/0) for client VPN connections, controlling whether egress-only internet traffic is routed through the VPN tunnel (when set to true) or excluded (when set to false).
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_route_enforcement_options.enforce: When set to true, this enforces that client traffic only uses routes advertised through the Client VPN endpoint, preventing clients from using other local network routes; when false, clients may also use their own local routes.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.connection_log_options: Configures whether client connection logs are enabled and, if so, the CloudWatch Logs log group and log stream to which they are published.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.connection_log_options.cloudwatch_log_gr: The name of the CloudWatch log group where AWS Client VPN publishes connection logs when connection logging is enabled.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.connection_log_options.cloudwatch_log_st: The name of the CloudWatch Logs stream to which the Client VPN endpoint publishes connection logs; if not specified, a default stream under the configured log group is used.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.connection_log_options.enabled: Specifies whether connection logging is enabled for the Client VPN endpoint, which determines if detailed logs of client connections are sent to the specified CloudWatch Logs group.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.description: A user-specified description for the Client VPN endpoint, used to identify it.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.disconnect_on_session_timeout: Specifies whether to disconnect a client after the session timeout period expires for the Client VPN endpoint.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.dns_servers: Specifies the IPv4 addresses of DNS servers that are used by clients for DNS resolution when connected to the AWS Client VPN endpoint.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.endpoint_ip_address_type: Specifies whether the Client VPN endpoint uses IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, which must match the IP version of the client CIDR block.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.id: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the Client VPN endpoint, such as cvpn-endpoint-1234567890abcdef0.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.security_group_ids: Specifies the IDs of the security groups to be associated with the Client VPN endpoint to control inbound and outbound traffic to the VPC.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.self_service_portal: Specifies whether the self-service portal is enabled for the Client VPN endpoint, allowing clients to request and manage their own client certificates.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.server_certificate_arn: The ARN of the server certificate that the Client VPN endpoint uses for TLS authentication with clients.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.session_timeout_hours: The maximum duration in hours that a client connection can remain active before being terminated, valid values are from 1 to 24.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.split_tunnel: Controls whether the Client VPN endpoint routes only traffic destined for the VPC through the tunnel (split-tunnel, true) or all traffic from the client (full-tunnel, false).
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.tag_specifications: Specifies the tags to apply to the Client VPN endpoint at creation, by providing a list of tag specifications that each include a resource type (client-vpn-endpoint) and tag key-value pairs.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.tag_specifications.resource_type: Specifies the type of AWS resource the tags apply to, which must be the string `client-vpn-endpoint` for a Client VPN endpoint.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.tag_specifications.tags: Specifies the key-value tags to attach to the resource identified by the parent tag_specifications resource_type during Client VPN endpoint creation.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.tag_specifications.tags.value: The value portion of a key-value tag assigned to the AWS Client VPN endpoint, used to organize and identify the resource for management and billing purposes.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.traffic_ip_address_type: Specifies whether the Client VPN endpoint routes IPv4 or IPv6 traffic, with valid values 'ipv4' or 'ipv6'.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.transit_gateway_configuration.availabili: Specifies the IDs of the Availability Zones where the VPC attachment for the Client VPN endpoint is created when using a transit gateway.

For Client VPN endpoints that use a transit gateway, this list specifies the Availability Zones (e.g., us-east-1a) where the VPC attached to the transit gateway must have subnets, so the transit gateway attachment can route traffic.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.transit_gateway_configuration.transit_ga: The unique identifier of the transit gateway to which the Client VPN endpoint attaches for routing client traffic through a transit gateway.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.transport_protocol: Specifies the transport protocol (TCP or UDP) used by the Client VPN endpoint for the VPN session.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.vpc_id: The ID of the VPC to associate with the Client VPN endpoint, which determines the VPC in which the endpoint's network interfaces are created and is needed to attach subnets via association resources.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.vpn_port: Specifies the port number (either 443 or 1194) that the Client VPN endpoint will use for the VPN tunnel, controlling whether the tunnel uses TCP (443) or UDP (1194).

aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.client_vpn_endpoint_id: The ID of the Client VPN endpoint to which this route is associated.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.description: A user-defined description for the route, often used to identify its purpose or destination in the Client VPN endpoint.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.destination_cidr_block: The IPv4 CIDR block (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16) of the destination network that this Client VPN route forwards traffic through the VPN tunnel.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.id: The computed unique identifier for the Client VPN route, formatted as the client VPN endpoint ID, destination CIDR block, and target subnet ID separated by colons.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.target_vpc_subnet_id: The ID of the VPC subnet to which the Client VPN endpoint routes traffic for the destination CIDR block.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_target_network_associ.availability_zone: The availability zone of the subnet that the Client VPN endpoint is associated with, automatically derived from the specified subnet.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_target_network_associ.availability_zone_id: This field contains the unique identifier of the Availability Zone where the target network's subnet resides; it is automatically populated from the associated subnet and cannot be independently set.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_target_network_associ.client_vpn_endpoint_id: The ID of the Client VPN endpoint to which the target network is associated.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_target_network_associ.id: The unique association ID assigned by AWS to the target network (subnet) when it is associated with the Client VPN endpoint.
aws_ec2_client_vpn_target_network_associ.subnet_id: The ID of the subnet to associate with the Client VPN endpoint, enabling the endpoint to route traffic to and from that subnet's network.

aws_ec2_dhcpoptions.dhcp_options_id: The unique identifier (DHCP options ID) that AWS assigns to the DHCP options set when it is created, and which is used to associate the set with a VPC or subnet.
aws_ec2_dhcpoptions.tags.key: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the DHCP options set, used to identify and organize the resource within AWS.
aws_ec2_dhcpoptions.tags.value: The value portion of a user-defined tag attached to the DHCP options set, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_ec2_eipassociation.eip: The Elastic IP address (IPv4) to associate with the specified instance or network interface; this can be an IP string or a reference to an EIP resource.
aws_ec2_eipassociation.id: The unique identifier of the Elastic IP association, which is the association ID (e.g., eipassoc-...) returned by AWS.

aws_ec2_fleet.context: The `context` field specifies a string that AWS reserves for future use in the EC2 Fleet, and it does not currently alter fleet behavior.
aws_ec2_fleet.excess_capacity_termination_policy: Controls whether excess instances are terminated when the EC2 Fleet's target capacity is reduced below its current running capacity, accepting values 'termination' (default) or 'no-termination'.
aws_ec2_fleet.fleet_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the EC2 Fleet, used to reference the fleet in API calls and other resources.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs: Specifies the launch template configurations (including launch template ID/name and overrides for instance type, subnet, etc.) that the EC2 Fleet uses to launch instances.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.launch_template_: Specifies the launch template ID or name and its version, which the EC2 Fleet uses as the base configuration for launching instances in this fleet.

Specifies the ID of the EC2 launch template that defines the instance configuration (such as AMI, instance type, and network settings) for the instances launched by the EC2 Fleet from this launch template config.
The name of the EC2 launch template to use for instances launched in this fleet's launch template configuration.
The version of the launch template (e.g., a specific version number, $Latest, or $Default) that the EC2 Fleet uses when launching instances for this launch template configuration.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides: Specifies the instance types, subnets, and other parameters that override the associated launch template when EC2 Fleet selects them for launching instances.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.availa: Specifies the Availability Zone in which to launch the instances for this fleet, overriding the placement specified in the launch template.
Specifies the ID of the Availability Zone (e.g., use1-az1) in which the EC2 Fleet launches instances for this override, replacing any Availability Zone from the launch template.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.block_: Defines the block device mapping overrides applied to instances launched using this launch template override, such as attaching additional EBS volumes or modifying root volume settings.

The device name (e.g., /dev/xvda or /dev/sdh) exposed to the instance for a block device mapping override applied to a launch template configuration in the EC2 Fleet, determining where the attached volume or instance store volume appears within the guest OS.
Specifies the EBS volume settings (e.g., volume size, type, IOPS, encryption, and delete-on-termination behavior) for a block device in an EC2 Fleet launch template override.
Indicates whether the EBS volume created by this block device mapping is automatically deleted when the EC2 instance terminates.
Specifies whether the EBS volume for this block device mapping in the EC2 Fleet launch template override should be encrypted, allowing enforcement of encryption on launched instances.

Specifies the provisioned IOPS (I/O operations per second) for the EBS volume in a launch template override's block device mapping, used when configuring an EC2 Fleet with volume types that support custom IOPS (io1, io2, or gp3).
The ID or ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the EBS volume created by this block device mapping override in the EC2 Fleet launch template configuration.
The ID of the snapshot from which to create the EBS volume, used to initialize the volume with the data from that snapshot.
Specifies the size of the EBS volume in GiB for the block device mapping override in the EC2 Fleet launch template configuration.
Specifies the EBS volume type (e.g., gp2, gp3, io1) to use for the block device in the launch template override when the EC2 Fleet launches instances.
Indicates that the specified device name should not be mapped to a block device on the launched instance, effectively suppressing that device from the instance's block device mapping.
Specifies the virtual device name (e.g., ephemeral0) for an ephemeral instance store volume in the block device mapping of a launch template override used by the EC2 Fleet.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.iam_in: Specifies the IAM instance profile to associate with instances launched according to this launch template override, which overrides any IAM instance profile set in the launch template.
The ARN of the IAM instance profile to associate with the instances launched from this EC2 Fleet override.
Specifies the name of the IAM instance profile assigned to instances launched from this fleet override, providing them with the permissions of the associated IAM role.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.instan: Defines the hardware requirements (such as vCPU count and memory) that an instance type must meet for EC2 Fleet to select it for this launch template override.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that an instance must have to be considered for the fleet.
The maximum number of accelerators (such as GPUs or FPGAs) that an instance type can have in order to match the instance requirements for the EC2 Fleet override.
The minimum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that an instance type must have to satisfy the instance requirements for the EC2 Fleet.
Defines which accelerator (GPU) manufacturers are acceptable for instance types that match this launch template override, filtering by vendors such as NVIDIA or AMD.
Lists the accelerator names (e.g., 'a100', 'v100') that instance types must have, so the EC2 Fleet only selects instances with those accelerators when using this launch template override.
Defines the minimum and maximum total memory (in MiB) required for accelerators (such as GPUs) on instance types that the EC2 Fleet can launch.
The maximum total accelerator memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to match the instance requirements.
The minimum total accelerator (GPU) memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to be considered for the EC2 Fleet.

Specifies the types of hardware accelerators (such as GPU, FPGA, or inference) that instances must have to meet the instance requirements, filtering which instance types are eligible for the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies a list of instance types that are allowed for the fleet to use, ensuring that the fleet launches instances only on these permitted types.
Specifies whether the instance type must be a bare metal instance, with allowed values included, excluded, or required.
Specifies the minimum and maximum baseline EBS bandwidth (in Mbps) that an instance type must meet to be eligible for the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies the maximum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps that an instance type must have to be considered for the EC2 Fleet, used as a filter in the instance requirements overrides.
Specifies the minimum baseline EBS bandwidth (in Mbps) that an instance must meet to be considered for the EC2 Fleet's instance requirements.
Specifies the baseline performance requirements for CPU and memory of instance types that the EC2 Fleet can launch, enabling filtering based on a minimum performance threshold.

Specifies the CPU baseline performance factor, which uses a set of reference instance families to define the minimum expected CPU performance that instance types must meet for the fleet's launch configuration overrides.
A list of CPU performance factor references, each defining an instance family (e.g., m5, c5) that serves as the baseline for CPU performance when selecting instance types for the EC2 Fleet.
The instance family name (e.g., c5, m5) used as a baseline CPU performance reference when specifying instance requirements for the EC2 Fleet.

Specifies whether to include, require, or exclude burstable performance instance types (such as T3, T4g) in the EC2 Fleet's instance requirements, with valid values 'included', 'required', or 'excluded'.
A list of CPU manufacturers (such as Intel, AMD, and Amazon Web Services) that the instance requirements will accept when selecting instance types for the EC2 Fleet to launch.
List of EC2 instance types that are explicitly excluded from consideration when the fleet launches instances under these instance requirements.
Specifies the list of instance generations (for example, 'current' or 'previous') that the instance types must belong to in order to be used for this fleet's launch template override.
Specifies whether the instance types selected for the fleet must have local storage (such as NVMe) or not, with values like `required`, `preferred`, or `excluded`.
Filters candidate instances for the fleet to those whose local storage type matches the specified values (hdd and/or ssd), so only instances with that kind of local storage are considered.

Specifies the maximum Spot Instance price you are willing to pay as a percentage of the optimal On-Demand price for that instance type, used as a price protection threshold to filter candidate instance types in the fleet's instance requirements.
Specifies the minimum and maximum memory in GiB per vCPU for an instance type to be considered when fulfilling the fleet's launch template overrides.
The maximum memory per vCPU (in GiB) that an instance must have to match the specified instance requirements in the EC2 Fleet launch template override.
The minimum amount of memory (in GiB) per vCPU that an instance type must have to match the instance requirements when launching an EC2 Fleet.
Defines the range of memory (in MiB) for instance types that the EC2 Fleet can select, with minimum and maximum values.
The maximum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to be eligible for the fleet.
The minimum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to be included in the fleet's selection.
Defines the minimum and maximum network bandwidth in gigabits per second (Gbps) that an instance type must offer to be considered a match for the EC2 Fleet's overrides.
Sets the maximum network bandwidth (in Gbps) that an instance type must offer to be selected by the EC2 Fleet when using this launch template override's instance requirements.
The minimum network bandwidth in gigabits per second that instances must meet to be considered by the EC2 Fleet's launch template override instance requirements.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of network interfaces that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements for an EC2 Fleet launch template override.
The maximum number of network interfaces that an instance type must support for it to be considered by the EC2 Fleet.
The minimum number of network interfaces that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements in an EC2 Fleet launch template override.

Sets the maximum price for On-Demand instances as a percentage above the lowest-priced instance type that meets the specified requirements, used to control costs when EC2 Fleet selects instance types.
When set to true, only instance types that support encryption in transit are considered when fulfilling the fleet's launch template overrides.
Indicates whether the instance types must support hibernation; when set to true, only instance types that can hibernate are considered for the fleet.

Specifies the maximum price you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance as a percentage above the lowest Spot price among the eligible instance types, used within a launch template override's instance requirements to control Spot selection in the fleet.
Defines the minimum and maximum amount of local storage (in GB) that an instance type must provide for the fleet to consider it, filtering candidate instance types.
The maximum amount of local storage (in GB) that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements for this launch template override in the EC2 fleet.
The minimum total amount of local storage (in GB) that an instance type must have to be considered for the EC2 Fleet.
Defines the minimum and maximum number of vCPUs that an instance type must have to be eligible for the EC2 Fleet.
The maximum number of vCPUs an instance type can have to be eligible for the launch template override.
The minimum number of vCPUs that an instance type must offer to be eligible for the EC2 Fleet's capacity.
The EC2 instance type to launch in this override of the launch template configuration for the EC2 Fleet.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.key_na: Specifies the EC2 key pair name to associate with instances launched by this launch template override.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.max_pr: The maximum price per unit hour that you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance in this EC2 Fleet, which overrides the max price set in the associated launch template.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.metada: Sets the instance metadata service (IMDS) options—such as requiring token usage with HttpTokens and controlling the HTTP endpoint with HttpEndpoint—for EC2 instances launched by this specific fleet override.
Indicates whether the IPv4 instance metadata endpoint (enabled or disabled) is enabled for instances launched from this launch template override in the EC2 Fleet.
Determines whether HTTP tokens are required for accessing the instance metadata service for instances launched with this override, enforcing the use of IMDSv2 when set to 'required'.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.networ: Indicates whether to automatically assign a public IPv4 address to the primary network interface of an instance launched using this launch template override.
Indicates whether this network interface is deleted when the EC2 instance is terminated.
Provides a text description for the network interface created for the fleet's instances, overriding the description in the launch template if provided.

The zero-based position of the network interface on the instance (e.g., 0 for the primary interface) for this launch template override, which determines the attachment order when multiple interfaces are specified.
The list of security group IDs to attach to the network interface defined by this override in the EC2 Fleet launch template configuration.

Specifies the type of network interface for the override, with valid values being 'interface' for a standard VPC network interface, 'efa' for an Elastic Fabric Adapter, or 'trunk' for a trunk network interface.
Specifies the number of IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface for instances launched using this EC2 Fleet launch template override.
The IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface when overridden for a launch template configuration in the EC2 Fleet.
The specific IPv6 address to assign to the network interface for the EC2 Fleet instance override, enabling a static address from the subnet's IPv6 range.
The index of the network card on the instance, which associates the network interface with a specific network card for instance types that support multiple network cards.
The ID of an existing Elastic Network Interface (ENI) that overrides the network interface configuration from the launch template for instances launched by this fleet override.
Specifies the primary private IPv4 address to assign to the network interface; if omitted, AWS automatically selects an available address from the subnet's range.
Defines private IPv4 addresses to assign to the network interface for instances launched by the EC2 Fleet, where each entry specifies the IP address and whether it is the primary private IP.
Indicates whether the specified private IP address is the primary private IP address for the network interface.
The private IPv4 address to assign to a network interface in the EC2 Fleet launch template override, where each entry in the private_ip_addresses list specifies one such address.
Sets the number of secondary private IPv4 addresses to automatically assign to the network interface when an EC2 Fleet instance is launched with this launch template override.
The ID of the subnet in which the instances will be launched when applying this network interface override.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.placem: Overrides the EC2 placement settings (e.g., Availability Zone, Affinity, Tenancy) for instances launched with this launch template override in the EC2 Fleet.

The affinity setting (such as 'host' or 'default') that determines whether instances launched with this placement override are associated with a dedicated host in the EC2 Fleet's launch template configuration.
Specifies the Availability Zone in which to launch the instances for this fleet override, overriding the placement setting from the launch template.
The name of the placement group in which to launch the instances for this fleet launch template override.
The ID of the Dedicated Host on which to launch the instances in this fleet override.
The ARN of the host resource group in which to launch the instances, used to place instances on a group of dedicated hosts for the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies the partition number within a partition placement group where the instances launched from this launch template override should be placed.
Specifies a specific spread domain within a spread placement group for the instance overrides, controlling which fault-isolated partition the fleet-launched instances are placed into.
Specifies the tenancy (default, dedicated, or host) for instances launched using this placement override in the EC2 Fleet.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.priori: Defines the order in which EC2 Fleet prioritizes this instance type override when fulfilling capacity, where lower numbers indicate higher priority.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.subnet: The ID of the subnet in which to launch the instances, overriding any subnet specified in the associated launch template.
aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.overrides.weight: The number of capacity units that each instance of this instance type contributes to the fleet's target capacity, enabling instance weighting for mixed instance types in the EC2 Fleet.
aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options: Specifies the allocation strategy and other options for On-Demand Instances in the EC2 Fleet, such as how capacity is prioritized and whether to use capacity reservations.
aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.allocation_strategy: Determines the order in which On-Demand Instances are launched across instance types in the fleet, with 'lowest-price' selecting the lowest-priced type first (default) and 'prioritized' following the priority order defined in the launch template.
aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.capacity_reservation_o: Specifies whether to use unused Capacity Reservations to fulfill On-Demand Instance capacity in the EC2 Fleet, including the usage strategy (e.g., use-capacity-reservations-first).

Determines whether the EC2 Fleet uses unused Capacity Reservations first to fulfill On-Demand capacity before launching new On-Demand Instances, with the only valid value being 'use-capacity-reservations-first'.
aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.max_total_price: Specifies the maximum amount per hour (in USD) you are willing to pay for all On-Demand Instances launched by the EC2 Fleet.
aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.min_target_capacity: The minimum number of On-Demand Instances that the EC2 Fleet must maintain, ensuring a baseline of On-Demand capacity within the fleet's total target capacity.
aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.single_availability_zo: Indicates whether the fleet launches all On-Demand Instances into a single Availability Zone.
aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.single_instance_type: When enabled, this makes the On-Demand portion of the EC2 Fleet launch only a single instance type (as specified in the launch template or its overrides) rather than multiple types chosen by the allocation strategy.
aws_ec2_fleet.replace_unhealthy_instances: Indicates whether EC2 Fleet automatically replaces instances that become unhealthy, launching new instances to maintain the fleet's target capacity.
aws_ec2_fleet.reserved_capacity_options.reservation_ty: Specifies the types of reserved capacity (e.g., capacity-reservation or capacity-block) that the EC2 Fleet can use to fulfill On-Demand capacity.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options: Configures the Spot Instance purchasing behavior for the fleet, including allocation strategy, instance interruption behavior, and maximum price per hour.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.allocation_strategy: Determines how the EC2 Fleet allocates Spot Instance capacity across Spot pools, using strategies such as lowest-price, diversified, or capacity-optimized.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.instance_interruption_behav: Controls the behavior of Spot Instances in the fleet when they are interrupted by EC2, allowing values such as 'terminate', 'stop', or 'hibernate' to specify whether instances are terminated, stopped, or hibernated.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.instance_pools_to_use_count: Specifies the number of Spot capacity pools across which the EC2 Fleet distributes its target Spot capacity, and is only used when the Spot allocation strategy is set to 'lowestPrice'.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.maintenance_strategies: Specifies the maintenance strategies for the Spot Instances in the fleet, such as enabling capacity rebalancing to automatically replace instances that are at risk of interruption.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.maintenance_strategies.capa: Configures the capacity rebalance behavior for the fleet's Spot Instances, allowing EC2 Fleet to attempt to launch a replacement instance before an existing Spot Instance is interrupted, with a configurable replacement strategy.

Determines whether EC2 Fleet launches a replacement Spot Instance when the current instance is at risk of interruption (launch) or launches a replacement before terminating the current instance (launch-before-terminate).
The number of minutes to wait after receiving a Spot Instance rebalance notification before terminating the instance, allowing proactive replacement during capacity rebalancing.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.max_total_price: The maximum hourly price you are willing to pay for Spot Instances in the EC2 Fleet, specified as a string representing a dollar amount (e.g., '0.50').
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.min_target_capacity: Specifies the minimum target capacity for Spot Instances in the fleet; if the fleet cannot reach this capacity, it launches no instances.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.single_availability_zone: When set to true, the Spot Fleet launches all instances in the same single Availability Zone, instead of potentially spreading across multiple, to keep them co-located for low latency.
aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.single_instance_type: Indicates whether the Spot Fleet will launch a single instance type to fulfill the entire target capacity, rather than diversifying across multiple instance types.
aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications: The list of tag specifications that define the tags to apply to the EC2 Fleet resource itself, typically using the resource type 'fleet'.
aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.resource_type: Specifies the type of resource to tag, such as an instance or the fleet itself, within a tag specification for the EC2 Fleet.
aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.tags: Specifies the list of tags (key-value pairs) to apply to the fleet's launched resources, such as instances or volumes, as part of the parent tag specification.
aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.tags.key: The tag key (e.g., 'Name') of a tag to apply to EC2 instances that the fleet launches, as defined in this tag specification.
aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.tags.value: Specifies the value of a tag assigned to the EC2 Fleet, used to categorize and identify the fleet among your AWS resources.
aws_ec2_fleet.target_capacity_specification: Configures the overall target capacity for the EC2 Fleet, including total, On-Demand, and Spot capacity values, the default capacity type for provisioning, and the unit type (instances or vCPU) used for measurement.
aws_ec2_fleet.target_capacity_specification.default_ta: Sets the default purchase type (on-demand or spot) for the EC2 Fleet's target capacity when individual capacity types are not otherwise specified.
aws_ec2_fleet.target_capacity_specification.on_demand_: The number of On-Demand units to request as the target capacity for the EC2 Fleet.
aws_ec2_fleet.target_capacity_specification.spot_targe: Specifies the number of units to request for Spot Instance capacity in the EC2 Fleet's overall target capacity.
aws_ec2_fleet.target_capacity_specification.target_cap: The unit of measure for the target capacity of the EC2 Fleet, either 'vcpu' or 'memory-mib'.
aws_ec2_fleet.target_capacity_specification.total_targ: The total number of capacity units (instances or other units) that the EC2 Fleet aims to launch and maintain across all specified capacity reservation and instance type options.
aws_ec2_fleet.terminate_instances_with_expiration: Indicates whether running instances should be terminated when the EC2 Fleet reaches its expiration time (validUntil); if false, instances continue to run beyond expiration.
aws_ec2_fleet.type: Specifies the type of EC2 Fleet (maintain, request, or instant), which controls whether the fleet maintains a target capacity over time, fulfills a one-time request, or launches the capacity immediately.
aws_ec2_fleet.valid_from: The timestamp (in UTC) at which the EC2 Fleet request becomes valid, after which the fleet can begin launching instances.
aws_ec2_fleet.valid_until: The date and time when the EC2 Fleet request expires, and after which AWS will not launch any new instances for the fleet.

aws_ec2_host.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag assigned to the EC2 Dedicated Host.
aws_ec2_host.tags.value: The value portion of a tag attached to the EC2 Dedicated Host.

aws_ec2_instance_connect_endpoint.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, used to identify, categorize, and filter the resource within AWS.

aws_ec2_ipam.default_resource_discovery_organizationa: Sets the AWS Organizations entity path (the OU path, e.g., 'ou-1234-abcdefgh') for an organizational unit to exclude from the IPAM default resource discovery, preventing resources in that OU from being automatically discovered.
aws_ec2_ipam.description: A user-specified, free-form text description of the IP address manager (IPAM) used to identify it in the AWS console and APIs.
aws_ec2_ipam.operating_regions.region_name: The name of the AWS Region in which the IPAM operates, defining one of the operating regions for the IPAM.
aws_ec2_ipam.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the EC2 IPAM resource, used to categorize or identify the IPAM with custom metadata (e.g., 'Name' or 'Environment').
aws_ec2_ipam.tags.value: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag key assigned to the EC2 IPAM resource for organizational or management purposes.

aws_ec2_ipamallocation.description: A user-defined free-form text description that annotates the IPAM allocation, typically used to record the purpose, owner, or other identifying information for the allocated CIDR block.

aws_ec2_ipampool.allocation_resource_tags.key: The key of a tag that is automatically applied to resources allocated from this IPAM pool, as part of the allocation_resource_tags map.
aws_ec2_ipampool.allocation_resource_tags.value: The value of a tag that will be applied to resources that receive CIDR allocations from this IPAM pool.
aws_ec2_ipampool.description: Sets a user-defined descriptive text for the EC2 IPAM pool, used to identify the pool's purpose and displayed in IPAM management views and API responses.
aws_ec2_ipampool.provisioned_cidrs.cidr: The CIDR block (in CIDR notation) that is provisioned to the IPAM pool, defining a specific address range added to the pool's managed address space.
aws_ec2_ipampool.source_resource.resource_id: The resource ID of the source resource (such as a VPC) that provides CIDRs to be allocated to the IPAM pool.
aws_ec2_ipampool.source_resource.resource_owner: The AWS account ID of the source resource (such as a VPC or another IPAM pool) that this IPAM pool uses as the origin for its CIDR provisioning, required when defining a source resource for the pool.
aws_ec2_ipampool.source_resource.resource_region: Specifies the AWS region in which the source resource (such as a VPC or subnet) that provides the CIDR block for this IPAM pool resides.
aws_ec2_ipampool.source_resource.resource_type: The type of the source resource being admitted into the IPAM pool, such as 'vpc' or 'subnet', which is paired with the source resource ID to identify the originating VPC or subnet.
aws_ec2_ipampool.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag to associate with the IPAM pool, used for identifying and organizing the pool.

aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver.rules.conditions.resource_id: Limits the rule to prefix list entries that are associated with the given AWS resource ID, such as a VPC or subnet.
aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver.rules.ipam_scope_id: The ID of the IPAM scope that this resolver rule is associated with, used to determine which IPAM-managed prefix list the rule selects during resolution.
aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver.rules.resource_type: Specifies the type of AWS resource (e.g., VPC, subnet) that a rule matches when resolving resources into the prefix list.
aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver.rules.static_cidr: Specifies the static CIDR block included in a rule entry for the prefix list resolver, defining the IP address range used to match traffic.

aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver_target.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag assigned to the IPAM prefix list resolver target, used for organizing and managing the resource in AWS.

aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery.description: Specifies a custom description for the IPAM resource discovery, which is used to provide human-readable context or identification for the discovery resource within the AWS EC2 IPAM service.
aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery.operating_regions.region_name: Specifies the AWS Region (e.g., us-east-1) in which the IPAM resource discovery operates.
aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery.organizational_unit_exclusions.organizat: Defines the AWS Organizations entity path (e.g., 'o-1234567890abcdef0') of an organizational unit to exclude from IPAM resource discovery, preventing resources in that OU from being discovered.
aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery.tags.value: The value for a tag key attached to the IPAM resource discovery, which is a user-defined string for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery_associati.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the IPAM resource discovery association, used to organize and identify the resource within AWS.
aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery_associati.tags.value: Specifies the value of a tag key attached to the IPAM resource discovery association, used to organize and identify the association for purposes like cost allocation and access management.

aws_ec2_ipamscope.description: A user-defined description for the IPAM scope.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table.tags: A list of key-value pairs to associate with the local gateway route table for identification and categorization, where each object consists of a Key and a Value string.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag that can be attached to an EC2 Local Gateway Route Table for resource identification and management.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_virtua.tags.key: A user-defined key for a tag on this AWS Local Gateway Route Table Virtual Interface Group Association, used to categorize, organize, or filter the resource in AWS.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_virtua.tags.value: The value of a tag key attached to the Local Gateway Route Table Virtual Interface Group Association, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_vpcass.tags: Tags are user-defined key-value pairs that label and identify the VPC association with the local gateway route table, enabling cost allocation and resource management.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_vpcass.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Local Gateway Route Table VPC Association, serving as the name portion of a user-defined metadata label for the association.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_vpcass.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the association between a local gateway route table and a VPC.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface.tags.key: The user-defined key for a tag attached to the EC2 Local Gateway Virtual Interface, used to organize and identify the resource.
aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the Local Gateway Virtual Interface, used to categorize or identify the resource.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface_.tags.value: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the Local Gateway Virtual Interface Group, enabling you to assign custom metadata for identification and management.

aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.icmp: Specifies the ICMP type and code for the network ACL rule when the protocol is ICMP or ICMPv6, used to match specific ICMP traffic patterns.
aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.icmp.code: The ICMP code number, used to filter ICMP traffic in a network ACL entry, where it must be specified when the ICMP type is set to a specific value (e.g., 0 for echo request) rather than -1.
aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.icmp.type: The ICMP type number for the ICMP protocol, used when the protocol is set to ICMP (e.g., 8 for echo request).
aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.id: A computed identifier that combines the network ACL ID and rule number to uniquely represent this network ACL entry.
aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.port_range: Specifies the inclusive lower and upper bounds of the port range to match for the network ACL rule, typically used when the protocol is TCP or UDP.
aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.port_range.from: The starting (lower) port number of the TCP or UDP port range that this network ACL entry rule applies to, used together with the 'to' value to define the range of allowed or denied destination ports.
aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.port_range.to: Specifies the highest port number in the inclusive range of ports that this network ACL entry applies to, paired with the port_range.from value to define the upper boundary of allowed or denied traffic.

aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.created_date: The ISO 8601 formatted timestamp when the network insights access scope was created.
aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.exclude_paths: Specifies a list of network path statements to exclude from the access scope, so that traffic matching any of these paths is not analyzed.
aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.exclude_paths.destination: Specifies the destination endpoint (such as an IP address, resource ID, or ARN) of a network path that is excluded from the access scope.
aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.exclude_paths.destination.packet_header_: Specifies the packet header fields (such as source/destination IP addresses, ports, and protocols) that the destination of an excluded path must match in the Network Insights Access Scope.
Specifies the destination IP addresses or CIDR ranges that a packet must match to be considered part of the excluded path's destination traffic, used as filters in the packet header statement.
Specifies the destination ports or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '1000-1024') that a packet must match for its path to be considered for exclusion in the network access scope.

For the excluded path's destination component, this list specifies the destination prefix list IDs (e.g., pl-0123456789abcdef0) that the packet header statement matches, causing traffic destined to any of these prefix lists to be excluded from the access scope.
Specifies the list of network protocols (e.g., tcp, udp, icmp) that the destination packet header statement matches for traffic to be excluded from the access scope.
The list of source IP address CIDR ranges that the packet header statement matches for the destination of an exclusion path in the Network Insights access scope.
Specifies the source port or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '1-1024') that the packet header statement matches on to define excluded traffic in the Network Insights Access Scope.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.explanations.sub: Provides details about the subnet involved at this point in the analyzed network path, such as its ID and ARN, as part of the explanation for the path component's behavior.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the subnet involved in this explanation step of the network path analysis.
The ID of the subnet that is part of the explanation for this forward path component in the analyzed network path.
Represents the subnet route table that was used for routing in the network path explanation, including the route table ID and the VPC in which it resides.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the subnet route table referenced in this explanation of the network path analysis.
The ID of the subnet route table that explains the routing decision for this step in the network path analysis.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.explanations.tra: Provides the transit gateway's identifying information (such as its ARN and ID) as part of the explanation for how traffic traversed the analyzed network path.
The ARN of the transit gateway involved in the network path explanation component.
The unique identifier of the transit gateway associated with this network path explanation step.
Contains details about the transit gateway attachment (e.g., its attachment ID and associated transit gateway ID) that explains how traffic flows through the component in the network path.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the transit gateway attachment associated with this explanation in the network path analysis.
The ID of the transit gateway attachment that this explanation component refers to in the network path analysis.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the transit gateway route table that explains the network path component.
The ID of the transit gateway route table that the network insights analysis evaluated as part of the path explanation.

The ID of the transit gateway attachment (such as a VPC or VPN connection) that serves as the target for the route in the transit gateway route table analyzed by the network insights path.
The destination CIDR block associated with the transit gateway route table route in the path explanation, indicating the prefix that the route entry matches during network path analysis.
The ID of the prefix list matched by this transit gateway route table route in the network path explanation.
The ID of the AWS resource (such as a VPC attachment or VPN attachment) that provides the route in the transit gateway route table explanation for this path component.
The type of the resource that serves as the target for this transit gateway route table route, as identified in the network insights analysis explanation.
Indicates whether the transit gateway route that explains this forward path hop was created statically or propagated (values are 'static' or 'propagated').
The state of the transit gateway route table route (e.g., active, blackhole) that the network insights analysis identified as part of the explanation.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.explanations.vpc: Represents the VPC component in the analysis explanation, identifying the VPC by its Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and ID.
The ARN of the VPC that this explanation step refers to within the forward path component of the network insights analysis.
The unique identifier (ID) of the VPC referenced by this explanation, identifying the VPC that contains the network component being analyzed.
Details about the VPC endpoint that is part of the network path explanation, such as its ID, type, and the VPC in which it resides.
The ARN of the VPC endpoint involved in this step of the network path analysis, identifying the specific endpoint resource.
The ID of the VPC endpoint (e.g., vpce-0123456789abcdef0) involved in the network path explanation.
The VPC peering connection involved in this explanation of a network path component, populated when the analysis explains traffic traversal through a VPC peering connection.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC peering connection that this explanation refers to, identifying the peering link used in the analyzed network path.
The ID of the VPC peering connection whose explanation is included in the forward path component analysis, identifying the specific peering connection involved in the network path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.explanations.vpn: Specifies the VPN connection referenced in a path explanation, including its identifier and state, when the analyzed traffic traverses a VPN tunnel.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPN connection associated with this explanation in the forward path of the network insights analysis.
The ID of the VPN connection that this explanation references, identifying the VPN resource involved in the analyzed network path component.
Contains the properties of the virtual private gateway (VPN gateway) that is referenced in this explanation, such as its ID, state, type, and availability zone.
The ARN of the VPN gateway that explains this step of the analyzed network path.
The ID of the VPN gateway involved in this explanation of the network path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.inbound_header: Describes the packet header (source/destination IP addresses, ports, and protocol) for inbound traffic at this component of the analyzed network path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.inbound_header.d: The list of destination IP addresses in the inbound packet header for this forward path component, showing where the captured traffic is destined.
Specifies the destination port ranges in the inbound header of a forward path component, representing the destination port values that the analyzed traffic matched.
The inclusive lower bound of a destination port range in the inbound header of a path component, used to match traffic in an EC2 Network Insights Analysis.
The inclusive upper bound of a destination port range in the inbound header, specifying the end of the range of destination ports for the network path component.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.inbound_header.p: The IP protocol number (e.g., '6' for TCP, '17' for UDP) carried in the inbound packet header at this point in the analyzed network path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.inbound_header.s: The list of source IP addresses contained in the inbound traffic header of this forward path component, indicating the origins of the traffic analyzed at this point.

The list of source port ranges (each with a from/to value) in the inbound packet header for this path component, indicating which TCP/UDP source ports the analyzed traffic matched during the network insights analysis.
The inclusive start (lower bound) of the source port range in the inbound header of a path component in the network insights analysis.
The inclusive upper bound of the source port range in the inbound header of the network path component.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.outbound_header: The outbound_header object captures the IP header details (such as source and destination addresses and ports) for the outgoing packet of this forward path component.
The destination IP addresses of the packet's outbound header as it exits this component of the analyzed network path.
Specifies the list of destination port ranges in the outbound header of a forward path component, indicating the ranges of destination ports used for the analyzed traffic at that hop.
The inclusive starting port of the destination port range in the outbound header for this path component.
The ending port number (inclusive) of the destination port range in the outbound header of a forward path component.
The IP protocol number (e.g., 6 for TCP, 17 for UDP) used in the outbound packet header of this path component.
The source IP addresses in the outbound packet header for this path component, representing the packets' originating addresses as they leave this component.

Represents the list of source port ranges in the outbound packet header for this forward path component, where each range includes the From and To port values captured during the network insights analysis.
The inclusive lower bound of a source port range in the outbound header of a forward path component in an AWS EC2 Network Insights analysis, used to match traffic for the analysis.
The inclusive upper bound of a source port range in an outbound header of a path component in a network insights analysis.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.route_table_rout: Describes the route table route that was used to forward traffic at this component of the analyzed network path, including routing details such as destination CIDR block, target gateway, or instance.
The destination CIDR block of the route table entry that directs traffic along the analyzed network path.
The ID of the destination prefix list for this route table route in the forward path of the network insights analysis.
The ID of the egress-only internet gateway that is the target of the route table route in the forward path of the network insights analysis.
The ID of the internet gateway or virtual private gateway targeted by the route in the analyzed path component.
The ID of the EC2 instance that serves as the target of this route table route in the analyzed network path.
The ID of the NAT gateway that is the target of the route table entry used to forward traffic along the analyzed network path.
The ID of the network interface (ENI) that the route table entry targets as the next hop, as encountered in the forward path of the network insights analysis.

The state of the route table route (e.g., active or blackhole) as observed for the analyzed path component.
The ID of the transit gateway targeted by a route in the route table that the analyzed packet follows, when the route uses a transit gateway as its target.
The ID of the VPC peering connection that serves as the target of the route table route traversed during the network insights analysis.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.security_group_r: Describes the security group rule matched at this component of the analyzed forward network path, including the rule's security group ID, direction, protocol, port range, and source/destination CIDR or prefix list.
The IPv4 CIDR block associated with the security group rule that matched in this path component.
The direction of traffic for the security group rule, either 'ingress' (inbound) or 'egress' (outbound).
Port range (inclusive start and end ports) specified in the security group rule that the path component represents.

The inclusive upper bound of the port range in the security group rule that matched the path component, representing the highest port permitted or used.
The ID of the managed prefix list referenced by the security group rule that applies to this forward path component.
The IP protocol number or name (e.g., tcp, udp, icmp) used by the security group rule in the forward path component of the network insights analysis.
The ID of the security group that owns the security group rule affecting traffic at this component of the analyzed network path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.sequence_number: The order of this component within the analyzed network path, used to sequence the path components.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.service_name: The name of the AWS service that the path component is associated with, such as VPC, Subnet, Internet Gateway, or VPC Endpoint.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.source_vpc: The source VPC for this network path component, represented as a component object that includes the VPC's ARN, ID, and related metadata to show where traffic originates at this hop.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.source_vpc.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the source Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) for this component in the analyzed network path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.source_vpc.id: The AWS VPC identifier of the source VPC from which traffic originates in this forward path component of the network insights analysis.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.subnet: Represents the subnet resource that is a component of the forward path in an EC2 Network Insights Analysis, including its identifying details such as ARN and subnet ID.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.subnet.arn: The ARN of the subnet that appears as a component in the forward path of the network insights analysis.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.subnet.id: The ID of the subnet that is part of this hop in the analyzed network path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.transit_gateway: Describes the transit gateway involved in this forward path component, including its ARN, ID, name, and associated route table ID.

The unique identifier of the transit gateway that appears as a component in the forward path of the network insights analysis.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.transit_gateway_: Information about the transit gateway route table route that was used to forward traffic at this component of the analyzed forward path.

The ID of the transit gateway attachment (such as a VPC, VPN, or peering connection) that serves as the next hop for the route in the transit gateway route table, as observed in the analyzed network path.
The CIDR block that the transit gateway route table route matches as the destination for traffic analysis.
The ID of the prefix list used as the destination of the transit gateway route table route.
The ID of the resource (such as a VPC attachment or peering connection) that the transit gateway route table route targets in the analyzed network path.
The type of resource that the transit gateway route table route targets, such as 'vpc', 'vpn', or 'direct-connect-gateway'.
The origin of the transit gateway route table route (e.g., static or propagated) that was used to forward traffic along the analyzed path.
The state of the transit gateway route table route encountered in the forward path, such as 'active' or 'blackhole'.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.vpc: The VPC that contains this component in the analyzed network path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.vpc.arn: The ARN of the VPC through which the analyzed network path traverses in this forward path component.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.forward_path_components.vpc.id: The unique identifier of the VPC that is identified as a component in the forward path of the network insights analysis.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.network_insights_analysis_id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Network Insights Analysis resource.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.network_insights_path_id: The ID of the network insights path that this analysis will run against.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.network_path_found: Indicates whether a network path was found between the source and destination in the network insights analysis.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components: The list of network components that constitute the return path of the analyzed network journey, detailing each hop's resource type and identifiers.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.acl_rule: The network ACL rule that matched the analyzed return path, containing details such as rule number, allow/deny action, protocol, port range, and CIDR block.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.acl_rule.cidr: The IPv4 CIDR range that the network ACL rule applies to for this component of the return path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.acl_rule.egress: Indicates whether this network ACL rule is an egress (outbound) rule, as opposed to an ingress (inbound) rule, in the analyzed return path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.acl_rule.port_ran: The inclusive port range (from and to) of the network ACL rule that matched the traffic on the return path of the network insights analysis.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.acl_rule.protocol: The IP protocol (e.g., TCP, UDP, ICMP, or a numeric protocol number) that the network ACL rule applies to in the analyzed return path.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.acl_rule.rule_act: Indicates whether the network ACL rule action is 'allow' or 'deny' for the analyzed traffic path component.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.acl_rule.rule_num: Indicates the rule number of the network ACL entry that was evaluated for the traffic in this path component, identifying which ACL rule allowed or denied the packet.
aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.additional_detail: Returns a list of additional detail objects for each return path component in the analyzed network path, where each object includes the type of detail (e.g., a security group rule) and the associated AWS resource component.

The ID of the AWS resource component that the additional detail refers to in a return path component of a Network Insights analysis.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.component.id: The unique identifier of the network component (such as a subnet or security group) that appears in the return path of the analyzed traffic.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.return_path_components.destination_vpc.i: The ID of the VPC that serves as the destination in this analyzed return path component of a network insights analysis.
