aws_ecs_capacity_provider.auto_scaling_group_provider.managed_scal: Sets the number of seconds that a newly launched EC2 instance must warm up before its capacity counts toward the managed scaling target of the capacity provider, allowing it to initialize and start accepting tasks.
The maximum number of container instances that can be added to or removed from the Auto Scaling group during a single managed scaling activity for the ECS capacity provider.
Specifies the minimum number of instances that the managed scaling operation can add or remove in a single scaling activity for the Auto Scaling group used by this capacity provider.
Specifies whether managed scaling for the Auto Scaling Group is enabled or disabled, controlling ECS's automatic adjustment of the group's capacity.
The target capacity percentage for the Auto Scaling group, used by managed scaling to determine when to scale out or in, with a default of 100.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.auto_scaling_group_provider.managed_term: Enables or disables ECS-managed termination protection for the Auto Scaling group, which prevents ECS-managed instances from being terminated during scale-in events.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.managed_instances_provider.auto_repair_c: Configuration that enables or disables automatic repair (replacement) of unhealthy managed EC2 instances for the ECS capacity provider, controlled by the nested 'enabled' flag.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.managed_instances_provider.infrastructur: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon ECS uses to manage the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group associated with this capacity provider.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.managed_instances_provider.instance_laun: Specifies the EC2 launch template that the capacity provider uses to launch instances into the Auto Scaling group it manages.
Determines whether the capacity provider launches On-Demand or Spot instances for the managed instances using this launch template.
The ARN of the EC2 Capacity Reservation Group that the launch template targets, ensuring instances launched by the capacity provider use capacity from that reservation group.

Specifies the capacity reservation preference for the instance launch template, with valid values 'open' (automatically match any open Capacity Reservation) and 'none' (do not use Capacity Reservations).
The ARN of the IAM instance profile that the EC2 instances launched by this capacity provider's managed instances will use to interact with AWS services.
Boolean flag that enables FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules on the container instances launched using this capacity provider's managed instance launch template.

Controls whether instance tags are propagated to the instance metadata service (IMDS) on EC2 instances launched from the launch template specified in the managed instances provider of the ECS capacity provider.

Defines the instance requirements (e.g., vCPU count, memory, and other attributes) that the Auto Scaling group uses to automatically select EC2 instance types for the managed instances of the ECS capacity provider.

Specifies the minimum and maximum number of GPU accelerators (e.g., for compute-intensive workloads) that instances must have to match the instance requirements for the Auto Scaling group used by this ECS capacity provider.
Specifies the maximum number of GPU accelerators (e.g., GPUs) that an instance must have to be selected for the capacity provider's managed instance fleet.
Specifies the minimum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements for the capacity provider's managed instance launch template.

Specifies the acceptable manufacturers of hardware accelerators (GPUs) for the EC2 instance types that the capacity provider's managed instances can launch, restricting eligible instance types to those with accelerators from the listed manufacturers.
Specifies the names of GPU accelerators (e.g., 'a100', 'v100') that the instance types must have to be considered for the capacity provider's managed instances.

Specifies the minimum and maximum total memory (in MiB) across all accelerators (e.g., GPUs) that an instance type must have to be eligible for use in the managed Auto Scaling group for this ECS capacity provider, filtering the instance types that can be launched.
The maximum total accelerator memory, in MiB, that an instance can have to satisfy the instance requirements when ECS launches instances for the capacity provider's managed scaling.
The minimum total accelerator memory in MiB that an instance type must have to be considered for the managed instance requirements of the ECS capacity provider's launch template.

Specifies the types of hardware accelerators (such as gpu, fpga, or inference) that the EC2 instances must have when using instance requirements to select instance types for the capacity provider's managed instances.
Restricts the eligible EC2 instance types for the capacity provider's managed instances to the explicitly listed instance types within the launch template's instance requirements.

Specifies whether the launch template's instance requirements must target bare metal instances, with values `included`, `excluded`, or `required` to indicate whether bare metal instance types are allowed, disallowed, or required.

Specifies the minimum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps that an instance type must offer for the capacity provider's managed EC2 instances, used as part of the instance requirements to filter eligible instance types.
The maximum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps that an instance type must not exceed when matching the instance requirements for the capacity provider's managed instances.
The minimum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps that the instance type must support.
Specifies whether instances with burstable performance (e.g., T2, T3 families) are included or excluded when the capacity provider selects instance types for its managed instances.

Restricts the EC2 instance types eligible for the capacity provider's managed instances to those with a CPU manufacturer listed (e.g., 'intel', 'amd', or 'amazon-web-services' for AWS Graviton processors).
Specifies a list of EC2 instance types to explicitly exclude from the capacity provider's managed Auto Scaling group when instance requirements are used to automatically select compute resources.
Specifies the instance generations (e.g., '5' for fifth-generation instances) that are allowed when selecting eligible EC2 instance types under the instance requirements.
Specifies whether the instance types used by the ECS capacity provider's Auto Scaling group must include local instance storage, with allowed values of included, excluded, or required.

Specifies the local storage types (e.g., hdd or ssd) that an instance must support to be eligible for the capacity provider's managed instance fleet, as defined in the instance requirements of the launch template.

The maximum spot price as a percentage of the optimal On-Demand price for the instance, used to set a ceiling on Spot Instance pricing within the Auto Scaling group managed by the ECS capacity provider.
Defines the minimum and maximum amount of memory (in GiB) per vCPU that the EC2 instances used by the capacity provider's managed instance launch template must have.
The maximum amount of memory per vCPU (in GiB) that an instance type must have to be included in the instance requirements for the capacity provider's managed instances.
Defines the minimum amount of memory per vCPU (in GiB) that an instance must provide to be selected by the Auto Scaling group created for the ECS capacity provider's managed instance provisioning.
Specifies the minimum and maximum memory (in MiB) that instances must have to be selected for the capacity provider, using the min and max sub-fields of this object.
The maximum memory, in MiB, that an instance must have to be considered for use by this ECS capacity provider's managed instance fleet.
The minimum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements for the ECS capacity provider's managed instance launch template.

Specifies the minimum and maximum network bandwidth (in gigabits per second) that an instance must meet when the capacity provider launches managed instances, used to filter eligible EC2 instance types.
The maximum network bandwidth in gigabits per second that an instance type must support to be considered eligible for the ECS capacity provider's managed instance pool.
Defines the minimum network bandwidth (in Gbps) that an instance must offer to be selected for the capacity provider's managed instance launch template.
The minimum and maximum number of network interfaces that an instance type must support, used to filter eligible instance types when the capacity provider launches instances.
The maximum number of network interfaces that an instance type must have for it to be considered for the capacity provider's managed instances.
Sets the minimum number of network interfaces required on an EC2 instance type for the capacity provider to consider it when launching managed instances via the instance launch template.

For the managed EC2 Auto Scaling group behind this ECS capacity provider, this sets the maximum price you are willing to pay for On-Demand instances as a percentage above the lowest On-Demand price among the instance types that meet the specified requirements, influencing instance selection.
Indicates whether the ECS capacity provider's managed instances must be of a type that supports EC2 hibernation.

Sets the maximum price you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance as a percentage of the lowest-priced Spot Instance, allowing you to bid above the baseline Spot price to increase the chance of instance fulfillment.
Configures the minimum and maximum total local storage (in GiB) that an instance type must have for the capacity provider's managed instance launch template.
Sets the maximum total local storage (in GB) that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements for the ECS capacity provider's managed instances.
The minimum total local storage in GiB that an instance type must offer, used to filter which instance types are considered for the capacity provider.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of vCPUs that the instance type must have, used to filter EC2 instances for the capacity provider's managed instance fleet.
Specifies the maximum number of vCPUs for the EC2 instance types that can be used by the managed instance provisioning of the ECS capacity provider.
The minimum number of vCPUs that an instance type must have to be considered for launching managed instances in the ECS capacity provider.
Indicates whether to enable the use of local ephemeral storage on the managed EC2 instances for tasks running in this ECS capacity provider.

Specifies the VPC networking configuration for the EC2 instances launched by the capacity provider, including subnets, security groups, and whether to assign a public IP address, as part of the instance launch template in the managed instances provider.

The list of security group IDs to assign to the EC2 instances launched by the managed instance provider's instance launch template, used as part of the network configuration for the ECS capacity provider.
The list of subnet IDs in which the ECS capacity provider's container instances are launched, specified within the network configuration of the instance launch template.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.managed_instances_provider.propagate_tag: Determines whether tags from the Auto Scaling group are propagated to the container instances launched by the capacity provider's managed instance provider; accepts values like `TAG_FROM_AUTO_SCALING_GROUP` and `NONE`.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.name: Specifies the name of the capacity provider, which must be unique within the account and Region and contain only letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens (up to 255 characters); if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.tags: Specifies the metadata tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the ECS capacity provider for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.tags.key: Specifies the key for a user-defined tag attached to the ECS capacity provider, which can be used for cost allocation, resource organization, and IAM-based access control.
aws_ecs_capacity_provider.tags.value: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag applied to the ECS capacity provider, used for metadata organization and cost tracking.

aws_ecs_cluster.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this ECS cluster.
aws_ecs_cluster.cluster_settings.name: The name of the cluster setting, which identifies the specific setting (such as 'containerInsights') that the corresponding value applies to.
aws_ecs_cluster.cluster_settings.value: The value for the ECS cluster setting, such as 'enabled' or 'disabled' for the common 'containerInsights' setting.
aws_ecs_cluster.default_capacity_provider_strategy.base: Base specifies the minimum number of tasks that run on this capacity provider within the cluster's capacity provider strategy.
aws_ecs_cluster.default_capacity_provider_strategy.capac: Specifies the name of the capacity provider (such as FARGATE, FARGATE_SPOT, or a custom Auto Scaling group-based provider) to include in the default capacity provider strategy that Amazon ECS applies when running tasks without an explicit strategy.
aws_ecs_cluster.default_capacity_provider_strategy.weigh: Weight is the relative proportion of tasks that should be placed on this capacity provider, used for spreading tasks across providers in the cluster's default capacity provider strategy.
aws_ecs_cluster.tags.value: The value of an arbitrary tag assigned to the ECS cluster, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_provider_associ.default_capacity_provider_strategy.base: The base setting defines the minimum number of tasks that must run on the specified capacity provider before other providers in the default strategy are used, ensuring baseline capacity for the cluster.
aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_provider_associ.default_capacity_provider_strategy.capac: The name of the capacity provider to be used for this entry in the default capacity provider strategy.
aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_provider_associ.default_capacity_provider_strategy.weigh: Determines the relative proportion of tasks that should be placed on this capacity provider as part of the default strategy, where a higher value increases the share of tasks routed to it.

aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.command: Specifies the command to pass to the container, which overrides the default command set in the container image.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.cpu: The number of CPU units reserved for the container, where 1024 CPU units equal one vCPU.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.depends_on: Specifies the container dependencies for this container, where each dependency defines a container name and a condition (START or COMPLETE) that must be satisfied before this container can start.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.depends_on.conditi: Specifies the condition (START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, or HEALTHY) that must be satisfied by the referenced dependency container before this container can start.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.depends_on.contain: The name of the container that this container definition depends on, used in a dependsOn entry to specify the target container for a dependency condition.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.entry_point: Overrides the default entry point for the container, specified as a list of command-line arguments that form the ENTRYPOINT instruction (e.g., ['/bin/sh', '-c']).
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.environment: Defines the environment variables to pass to the container, as a list of key-value pairs (name and value) that the container can access at runtime.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.environment.name: The `name` attribute of an environment variable entry defines the variable name that will be set inside the container's environment.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.environment.value: The value of the environment variable to pass to the container.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.environment_files: Specifies a list of files (such as those stored in Amazon S3 or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store) from which environment variables are loaded for the container.
Specifies the source type of the environment file, either 's3' for an Amazon S3 object or 'ssm' for an AWS Systems Manager parameter.
For each environment file entry, this is the ARN of the Amazon S3 object that contains the environment variable definitions to be injected into the container.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.essential: Indicates whether the container is marked as essential; if an essential container stops or fails, the entire task is stopped.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.firelens_configura: Configures the FireLens log router for this container, specifying the log driver type (fluentd or fluentbit) and its associated options for routing container logs to a downstream processor.
A map of configuration options (e.g., enable-ecs-log-metadata, config-file-type, config-file-value) passed to the Fluent Bit or Fluentd log router when FireLens is configured for the container.
Sets which log router (fluentd or fluentbit) the Firelens configuration uses to deliver container logs to the configured destination.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check: Configures the Docker health check for the container, specifying the command and parameters such as interval, timeout, retries, and start period that Amazon ECS uses to monitor container health.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.comma: The command to run inside the container to check its health, typically a list starting with 'CMD-SHELL' or 'CMD' followed by the executable or shell command and its arguments.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.inter: Specifies the time period in seconds between each container health check execution for this task definition.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.retri: Number of consecutive failed health checks required before the container is considered unhealthy.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.start: The number of seconds after the container starts during which failed health checks do not count toward the maximum number of retries, allowing the container to initialize before health check evaluation begins.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.timeo: The number of seconds to wait for a health check to return a response before marking the container as unhealthy, with a valid range of 2 to 60 seconds.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.image: Specifies the Docker image name and optionally tag or digest (e.g., 'nginx:latest' or '123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/my-app:1.0') that the container will run from in the ECS task definition.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.interactive: Specifies whether the container's standard input remains open, equivalent to the Docker interactive (-i) flag.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters: Configures Linux-specific container settings such as kernel capabilities, devices, tmpfs mounts, shared memory size, and whether to run an init process inside the container.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.c: Specifies the Linux capabilities to add or remove from the container's default set, using add and drop lists.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to add to the container, granting additional kernel permissions beyond the default set.
Defines the Linux kernel capabilities that should be removed (dropped) from the container's capability set, reducing its privileges.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.d: Specifies the list of host devices to expose to the container within its Linux parameters, where each device object defines the hostPath, containerPath, and permissions for that device.
The path inside the container at which the host device is exposed, as specified in the devices list of LinuxParameters for the container definition.
The path on the host instance of the device to expose to the container.
Specifies the cgroup permissions (read, write, mknod) to apply to the container device for this device entry in the ECS task definition's Linux parameters.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.i: Enables the init process (PID 1) inside the container, ensuring that it properly reaps zombie processes and handles signals within the container's namespace.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.t: Defines the tmpfs mount configurations for the container, specifying the container path and mount options (such as size and permissions) for each tmpfs volume.
The absolute file path inside the container where the tmpfs volume is mounted.
Specifies the mount options (such as 'ro' or 'noexec') for the tmpfs mount in the container's Linux parameters.
The size (in MiB) of the tmpfs mount to be used in the container's ephemeral storage.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.log_configuration: Specifies the logging configuration for the container, including the log driver to use, its options, and optional secret options.
Specifies the log driver to use for the container (e.g., awslogs, fluentd, gelf, json-file, journald, logentries, syslog, splunk, awsfirelens), which determines how logs are collected and sent to a destination.
Specifies the key-value map of configuration options to pass to the container's log driver, such as awslogs-group, awslogs-region, and awslogs-stream-prefix for the awslogs driver.

Specifies a list of secrets to pass to the container's log driver, where each entry consists of the name of the log driver option (as the secret key) and the valueFrom ARN that references the secret in AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

The name (configuration key) of a secret passed to the container's logging driver, whose actual value is retrieved from the AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store secret specified in the corresponding valueFrom field.
Specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or SSM Parameter Store parameter from which the container's log driver retrieves the secret value for the given log configuration secret option.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.memory: The hard memory limit in MiB for the container; if the container exceeds this memory usage, the ECS agent may stop the container.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.memory_reservation: Specifies the soft memory limit (in MiB) for the container, which may be exceeded if the host has spare memory but triggers OOM or task-idle behavior under memory pressure.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.mount_points: Specifies which volumes from the task definition to mount into the container, including the container path, source volume, and whether the mount is read-only within each container definition.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.mount_points.conta: The path inside the container at which the volume is mounted, as specified in a mount point for an ECS task definition.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.mount_points.read_: Indicates whether the container's mount point is read-only; when true, the container can only read from the volume, and when false, it has read-write access.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.mount_points.sourc: Specifies the name of the volume to mount, which must correspond to a volume defined in the task definition's volumes section.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.name: The name of the container, used to uniquely identify it within the task definition and required for each container definition.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.privileged: Determines whether the container runs in privileged mode, giving it full access to host devices and extended Docker capabilities (equivalent to Docker's --privileged flag).
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.pseudo_terminal: Allocates a pseudo-TTY to the container, providing an interactive terminal session (corresponding to Docker's tty option).
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.readonly_root_file: When set to true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing the container from writing to its root filesystem.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.repository_credent: Provides the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the private repository credentials used to pull the container image.
Specifies the ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret or SSM parameter that stores the private repository credentials (username and password) used to authenticate when pulling the container image.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.restart_policy: Defines the restart policy for the container in the ECS task definition, specifying whether the container is automatically restarted when it exits and the maximum number of restart attempts allowed.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.restart_policy.ign: The list of container exit codes that are ignored by the restart policy, meaning if the container exits with one of these codes, it will not be automatically restarted.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.restart_policy.res: In the restart policy for an ECS container definition, this field sets the time window, in seconds, during which Amazon ECS counts restart attempts against the configured maximum before stopping the container.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.secrets: Specifies the secrets to inject into the container as environment variables, referencing AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store or AWS Secrets Manager secrets via the valueFrom ARN or name.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.secrets.name: The name of the environment variable in the container that will be set to the secret value retrieved from the referenced AWS Secrets Manager secret or SSM Parameter Store parameter.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.secrets.value_from: The ARN of the secret in AWS Secrets Manager or the Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter to be injected as an environment variable when the container is started.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.start_timeout: The maximum time in seconds ECS waits for this container to transition from CREATED to RUNNING before stopping the container and failing the task.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.stop_timeout: Specifies the time (in seconds) to wait for the container to stop gracefully after a stop signal before force-stopping it, overriding the default Docker stop timeout in this container definition.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.system_controls: Specifies a list of Linux kernel system controls (sysctl) for the container, where each entry defines a namespace (e.g., net.core.somaxconn) and a corresponding value to tune kernel parameters.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.system_controls.na: The namespaced kernel parameter path (e.g., net.ipv4.ip_forward) that this system control entry sets inside the container.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.system_controls.va: The value of the kernel parameter (sysctl setting) to apply inside the container, paired with the namespace in the same system_controls block to customize runtime container networking or other kernel defaults.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.ulimits: Configures ulimit settings for each container in an ECS daemon task definition, specifying the resource name (e.g., nofile, nproc) and its soft and hard limits.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.ulimits.hard_limit: The hard limit (maximum value) for the specified ulimit in the container definition, corresponding to the `rlim_max` value used by Docker's `--ulimit` flag.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.ulimits.name: The name of the resource limit to set, such as nofile, nproc, or cpu, defining which ulimit is applied to the container.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.ulimits.soft_limit: The soft limit for the specified ulimit, which is the value the kernel enforces for the resource (e.g., file size, open files) in the container.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.user: Specifies the user name or UID (and optionally group name or GID) to run the container's process as, overriding the default user defined in the container image.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.container_definitions.working_directory: Sets the working directory inside the container from which the container's default command is executed.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.daemon_task_definition_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this ECS daemon task definition within your AWS account and region.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.tags: Specifies a list of key-value tag pairs to attach to the ECS task definition, enabling cost allocation and resource grouping.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the ECS daemon task definition, used to identify, categorize, and manage the resource.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.volumes.host: For each volume defined in the task definition, the host object configures an Amazon ECS host volume, with the optional sourcePath property specifying the path on the container instance host to mount the volume from.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.volumes.host.source_path: Specifies the absolute path on the container instance host where a bind-mount volume is sourced, used for EC2 launch type tasks when the volume type is 'bind'.
aws_ecs_daemon_task_definition.volumes.name: Specifies the name of the volume, which is used to reference this volume from a container definition's mountPoints sourceVolume in the ECS task definition.

aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.active_configurations.network_configurat: Specifies the VPC subnets to use for the network configuration of an active configuration, controlling where the ECS Express Gateway service places its elastic network interfaces.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where container logs are delivered when using the awslogs log driver.
For the awslogs log driver, this prefix is prepended to the container name to define the CloudWatch log stream name, enabling organized log grouping.
Specifies the string value for an environment variable set on the primary container in the active ECS Express Gateway service configuration.
Specifies the credentials used to authenticate to a private container registry, typically containing a credentialsParameter ARN that references a Secrets Manager secret or SSM parameter.
Specifies the ARN or name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter that stores the private repository authentication credentials for the primary container.

The ARN or full name (in the form of a Systems Manager parameter name or Secrets Manager secret ARN) of the external source that stores the secret value to be injected into the container as an environment variable or referenced in the task definition.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.active_configurations.service_revision_a: Uniquely identifies the version of the service configuration that is among the currently active configurations for the ECS Express Gateway service.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.network_configuration.subnets: Specifies the list of subnet IDs in which the ECS service's tasks are placed, defining the VPC subnets for the service's network configuration.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.primary_container.aws_logs_configuration: Configures how the primary container sends logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs by specifying the log group, region, and log stream prefix options for the awslogs driver.
The CloudWatch Logs log group that receives the primary container's logs when the container is configured with the awslogs log driver.
This field specifies the prefix for the CloudWatch log stream that the container's logs are sent to, where the full log stream name is formed by concatenating this prefix with the container name.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.primary_container.command: Specifies the command to run in the primary container of the Express Gateway service, as a list of string arguments that override the container image's default command.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.primary_container.environment: Defines a list of environment variables (key-value pairs) to pass to the primary container of the ECS Express Gateway service, allowing you to configure the container's runtime settings without modifying its image.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.primary_container.image: The container image (e.g., 'nginx:latest') that the primary container of the ECS Express Gateway service will run, as a required property of the primary container's configuration.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.primary_container.repository_credentials: Specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret ARN containing credentials used to authenticate the primary container to a private image repository, enabling the container to pull images that require authentication.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.primary_container.secrets: Specifies the list of secret references to be injected as environment variables into the primary container, each mapping a container environment variable name to a secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager or a parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
aws_ecs_express_gateway_service.primary_container.secrets.value_from: Provides the ARN or name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter from which the primary container's environment variable value is retrieved.

aws_ecs_service.capacity_provider_strategy.base: The base value designates the minimum number of tasks to run on the specified capacity provider; only one capacity provider in a strategy can have a base defined.
aws_ecs_service.capacity_provider_strategy.capacity_prov: Specifies the name of the capacity provider (e.g., FARGATE, FARGATE_SPOT, or a custom capacity provider) to use for placing tasks in the ECS service cluster.
aws_ecs_service.capacity_provider_strategy.weight: The relative weight of the capacity provider in the strategy, which determines the proportion of tasks that are placed on that provider.
aws_ecs_service.deployment_configuration.lifecycle_hooks: The ARN of the Lambda function or Amazon ECS task that the deployment lifecycle hook invokes during an Amazon ECS service deployment.
Lists the deployment lifecycle stages (e.g., PENDING or PRIMARY) during which the ECS service lifecycle hook is invoked.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon ECS assumes to invoke the target of this deployment lifecycle hook during a service deployment.
Determines whether the lifecycle hook applies to the task level or the service level, with valid values of TASK and SERVICE, controlling the target scope of the hook during an Amazon ECS deployment.
Defines the maximum time ECS will wait for the associated lifecycle hook to complete before considering the hook failed and proceeding with the deployment.

The maximum number of minutes that an Amazon ECS deployment lifecycle hook can remain running before the deployment is considered failed and rolled back, as part of the service's deployment configuration.
aws_ecs_service.load_balancers.container_name: Specifies the name of the container (as defined in the task definition) that the load balancer routes traffic to, used together with containerPort to register targets in the target group.
aws_ecs_service.load_balancers.container_port: The port on the container that the load balancer forwards traffic to, used by the associated target group to route requests to the ECS service's container.
aws_ecs_service.load_balancers.load_balancer_name: The name of the Classic Load Balancer to associate with the ECS service, used when the load balancer type is classic rather than an Application or Network Load Balancer target group.
aws_ecs_service.load_balancers.target_group_arn: The ARN of the target group to which the ECS service's tasks are registered for the specified load balancer.
aws_ecs_service.monitoring.metric_configurations.metric_: Specifies the names of the metrics (such as CPUUtilization or MemoryUtilization) that the Amazon ECS service will emit to CloudWatch as part of its monitoring configuration.
aws_ecs_service.monitoring.metric_configurations.resolut: The number of seconds between aggregation periods for the ECS service's CloudWatch metric, determining the metric's resolution granularity.
aws_ecs_service.name: The unique name of the ECS service within its cluster; when omitted, this is auto-generated by ECS, and this attribute holds the final name after creation.
aws_ecs_service.placement_constraints.expression: A cluster query language expression that defines the placement constraint for the service when the constraint type is 'memberOf', using the Amazon ECS placement constraint syntax.
aws_ecs_service.placement_constraints.type: Specifies the type of placement constraint, either 'distinctInstance' to place each task on a distinct container instance, or 'memberOf' to apply a cluster query language expression.
aws_ecs_service.placement_strategies.field: The field to apply the placement strategy against; for spread strategies this is often a custom attribute like attribute:ecs.availability-zone, for binpack it is cpu or memory, and it is not used for random strategies.
aws_ecs_service.placement_strategies.type: The type of placement strategy to use, such as spread, binpack, or random, for distributing tasks across container instances in the ECS service.
aws_ecs_service.service_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the ECS service.
aws_ecs_service.service_connect_configuration.log_config: Specifies the name of the secret option, which serves as the key for the log driver configuration and pairs with the valueFrom ARN to retrieve the secret value from AWS Secrets Manager.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or SSM Parameter Store parameter that supplies the value for the named log configuration option in the ECS Service Connect log configuration.
aws_ecs_service.service_connect_configuration.services.c: The list of client aliases for each Service Connect service, which define alternative names and ports for the service to be discovered within the Cloud Map namespace.
The custom DNS hostname that clients use to access the service through AWS ECS Service Connect, which overrides the default service discovery name within the namespace.
The port number that clients use to connect to the service through this Service Connect client alias.
The name of the HTTP header that identifies test traffic for routing through this client alias, enabling Service Connect canary deployments.
aws_ecs_service.service_connect_configuration.services.d: The discovery name for this service in Amazon ECS Service Connect, which is used as the DNS hostname for service-to-service communication within the Service Connect namespace.
aws_ecs_service.service_connect_configuration.services.i: Overrides the port that the Amazon ECS Service Connect service uses to accept inbound traffic, so you can map a different ingress port than the default one determined by the service's port configuration.
aws_ecs_service.service_connect_configuration.services.p: Specifies the name of the port mapping in the task definition that ECS Service Connect uses to route traffic to this service.
aws_ecs_service.service_connect_configuration.services.t: Configures the idle and request timeouts (in seconds) for the Service Connect service, with fields for `idleTimeoutSeconds` and `requestTimeoutSeconds`.
Specifies the idle timeout in seconds for a service in the Amazon ECS Service Connect configuration, during which a connection must have activity to remain open, otherwise it is closed.
Defines the maximum time in seconds that an individual request can stay in flight before the Service Connect proxy times it out, enforcing request-level timeout for the ECS Service Connect service.
Configures TLS for an individual Service Connect service, specifying the certificate authority (via ARN) that issues client certificates and the optional KMS key used to encrypt the CA's private key.
Specifies the ARN of the private certificate authority (such as AWS Private CA) that issues the TLS certificates used for the Service Connect service's mutual TLS encryption.
The ARN of the AWS Private Certificate Authority (ACM PCA) that issues the TLS certificate for the ECS Service Connect service.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the private key of the TLS certificate for this Service Connect service.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon ECS assumes to create the certificate used for the service's Service Connect TLS configuration.
aws_ecs_service.service_registries.container_name: The name of the container (as specified in the task definition) whose port is used for service discovery with the Cloud Map registry.
aws_ecs_service.service_registries.container_port: The port on the container that AWS Cloud Map service discovery uses to route traffic to the ECS service; if omitted, the container's first assigned port is used.
aws_ecs_service.service_registries.port: The port number to register with the service registry, overriding the container port from the task definition for service discovery purposes.
aws_ecs_service.service_registries.registry_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Cloud Map service registry that this ECS service uses for service discovery.
aws_ecs_service.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the ECS service, used for organizing and identifying the service within AWS.
aws_ecs_service.tags.value: Sets the value of a metadata tag on the ECS service, which can be used for cost allocation, resource lifecycle management, and IAM-based access control.
aws_ecs_service.volume_configurations.managed_ebsvolume: Defines the configuration for an Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume that is managed by Amazon ECS for use as a service-managed volume in an ECS service, including settings such as size, volume type, file system type, and encryption.
Specifies whether the managed Amazon EBS volume used by the ECS service task should be encrypted.
The filesystem type (e.g., ext4, xfs) to format the managed EBS volume with, used when the ECS service creates and attaches the volume.
Specifies the provisioned IOPS for the managed Amazon EBS volume attached to the ECS service, controlling the volume's input/output performance.
The customer-managed KMS key ARN or ID used to encrypt the managed EBS volume attached to the ECS service's tasks.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon ECS assumes to create, attach, and detach the managed EBS volume for the service, falling back to the service-linked role if not provided.
Specifies the size in GiB of the Amazon EBS volume that is created and attached to the container instances when the ECS service uses a managed EBS volume configuration.
Specifies the snapshot ARN or ID from which the Amazon EBS volume is created, allowing the ECS service's managed volume to be initialized with data from an existing snapshot.
Defines the tag specifications for the Amazon EBS volume that this ECS service creates and manages, specifying which tags are applied to the volume resource when it is provisioned.
Determines which source of tags (either the ECS task definition or the ECS service) should be propagated to the managed EBS volume, with valid values of TASK_DEFINITION or SERVICE.
The type of Amazon EBS resource (either 'volume' or 'snapshot') to which the tags in this tag specification apply, used when tagging a managed EBS volume attached to an ECS service.
Specifies the list of tag key-value pairs to be applied to the managed EBS volume when it is provisioned for the ECS service.
Specifies the tag key to assign to the managed Amazon EBS volume attached to the Amazon ECS service.
The tag value assigned to a tag key for the managed EBS volume configured for the ECS service.
Sets the throughput in MiB/s for the managed EBS volume when the volume type is gp3, controlling the performance throughput of the volume.

Sets the rate (in GiB per minute) at which the managed EBS volume is initialized, used when restoring from a snapshot to pre-warm blocks and avoid I/O performance degradation before the task accesses them.
Specifies the Amazon EBS volume type (e.g., gp3, io2) for the managed EBS volume attached to tasks in this ECS service.
aws_ecs_service.volume_configurations.name: The name of the EBS volume attached at the ECS service level, which must match the volume name referenced by container mount points as sourceVolume in the task definition.
aws_ecs_service.vpc_lattice_configurations.port_name: Specifies the name of the port mapping in the task definition that VPC Lattice uses to route traffic to the service.
aws_ecs_service.vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon ECS assumes to register and deregister the service with the associated VPC Lattice target group.
aws_ecs_service.vpc_lattice_configurations.target_group_: The ARN of the VPC Lattice target group that this ECS service registers with as a target.

aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.command: The command to run in the container, which overrides the default command specified in the container image.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.cpu: The number of CPU units reserved for this container, which determines the relative CPU share allocated to it within the task.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.credential_specs: A list of ARNs for Windows credential specification files (used for gMSA or domain-joined containers) that are applied to this container definition, either stored in an S3 bucket or in the ECS service-linked role.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.depends_on: Specifies dependencies on other containers in the same task, controlling startup and shutdown order by requiring a container to reach a certain condition (e.g., START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, HEALTHY) before this container starts.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.depends_on.conditi: Specifies the state that the container named in depends_on must reach for this container to start, such as START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, or HEALTHY.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.depends_on.contain: Specifies the name of the container that this container depends on, as part of the container's dependency conditions within the same task definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.disable_networking: When set to true, disables networking for the container, meaning it does not receive a network interface and has no network access within the task.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.dns_search_domains: A list of DNS search domain names that are passed to the container's resolver configuration, allowing the container to search these domains when resolving hostnames.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.dns_servers: Specifies the DNS servers for the container, which are written to the container's /etc/resolv.conf file as nameserver entries.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.docker_labels: Specifies the custom Docker labels to add to the container as key-value pairs, which can be used for organizing or identifying the container.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.docker_security_op: Specifies the Docker security options (a list of strings) that are passed to the container runtime, such as 'no-new-privileges', to enforce additional security constraints on the container.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.entry_point: Specifies the entry point for the container as a list of strings, overriding the default ENTRYPOINT defined in the container image, where the first string is the executable and the rest are arguments.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.environment: The environment variables to pass to the container, as a list of objects each containing a name and a value.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.environment.name: The name of the environment variable to configure in the container as part of the task definition's container environment list.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.environment.value: The value of the environment variable defined for the container in the ECS task definition, paired with the corresponding name in the environment key-value list.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.environment_files: A list of environment files (S3 objects) whose contents define environment variables that are injected into the container at task launch.
Specifies the type of the environment file, where the only supported value is 's3', indicating the file is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket.
The Amazon S3 object ARN (e.g., arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/key-name) of the environment variables file that ECS loads into the container environment.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.essential: Specifies whether this container is essential to the task; if an essential container stops or fails, all other containers in the task are stopped and the task is considered failed.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.extra_hosts: Specifies additional hostname-to-IP address mappings to add to the container's /etc/hosts file, allowing the container to resolve those hostnames.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.extra_hosts.hostna: The hostname to add to the container's /etc/hosts file, paired with its IP address in the same extra_hosts entry.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.extra_hosts.ip_add: The IP address to which the corresponding hostname in the extra_hosts entry is resolved inside the container's network configuration (e.g., appended to /etc/hosts).
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.firelens_configura: Specifies the FireLens configuration for a container in the ECS task definition, enabling log routing to destinations like Fluentd or Fluent Bit via a configurable type and options such as log metadata and config file delivery.
Configures FireLens log routing by providing settings such as config-file-type, config-file-value, and enable-ecs-log-metadata.
Specifies the log router to use for Firelens, either 'fluentd' or 'fluentbit' (required).
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check: Defines the container health check configuration, including the command to run and parameters such as interval, timeout, retries, and start period, which ECS uses to determine container health.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.comma: The command (as a list of strings, e.g., ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost/"]) that the container runs to perform its health check, corresponding directly to the Docker HEALTHCHECK instruction's command portion.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.inter: The time period in seconds between each container health check execution, as part of the ECS task definition container health check configuration.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.retri: Specifies the number of times to retry a failed health check before the container is considered unhealthy, with a default of 3.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.start: Specifies the duration in seconds that Amazon ECS waits after the container starts before it begins counting failed health check results, providing a grace period for containers that need time to initialize before being marked unhealthy.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.health_check.timeo: The number of seconds to wait for a health check to succeed before considering the container unhealthy.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.hostname: Sets the hostname of the container, which other containers in the same task definition can use for DNS resolution.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.image: The Docker image (e.g., a repository URL or image name:tag) to run for this container in the ECS task definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.interactive: When set to true, this enables the container's interactive mode, keeping STDIN open and allowing a shell or other process to interact with the container, equivalent to Docker's `--interactive` flag.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.links: Specifies a list of container names to link, enabling network connectivity and injecting environment variables for inter-container communication.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters: Specifies Linux-specific container configuration options such as kernel capabilities, device mappings, init process enablement, shared memory size, tmpfs mounts, and swap settings for a container in an ECS task definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.c: Specifies the Linux capabilities to add or remove from the container's default set, with 'add' and 'drop' lists of capability names.
Specifies additional Linux capabilities to grant the container, such as SYS_ADMIN or NET_ADMIN, in the task definition's Linux parameters.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to remove from the container's default set, such as SYS_ADMIN or NET_RAW, to restrict its privileges at runtime.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.d: A list of host devices to expose to the container, each specifying the host path, optional container path, and access permissions (read, write, mknod).
The path inside the container at which the host device is mounted and exposed.
The absolute path on the host of the device to expose to the container, used in a Linux container's devices configuration to grant access to host devices.

Specifies the device permissions (e.g., read, write, mknod) that grant the container access to each host device listed in the devices block, controlling what operations the container can perform on those devices.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.i: When true, runs an init process as PID 1 inside the container to reap zombie processes and properly forward signals, such as SIGTERM, to the main application.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.m: The maximum amount of swap memory (in MiB) the container can use, overriding the host's default swap settings for this container.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.s: Specifies the size in MiB of the shared memory (/dev/shm) volume to allocate for the container, overriding the default 64 MiB.
The swappiness parameter controls the relative weight of swapping out anonymous pages versus page cache in the container, accepting an integer from 0 to 100 that is passed as a kernel tuning option.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.linux_parameters.t: Configures temporary file system (tmpfs) mounts for the container, listing each mount's container path, size in MiB, and optional mount options as defined under LinuxParameters in the ECS task definition.
The absolute file path inside the container where the tmpfs volume is mounted.
Specifies the mount options (e.g., size, mode, ro) passed to the tmpfs mount for the container.
The size of the tmpfs mount in MiB, specifying the maximum capacity of the temporary filesystem mounted at the container's path.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.log_configuration: This object configures the logging driver for the container (e.g., awslogs, json-file, syslog) and its options, such as awslogs-group and awslogs-region, controlling how container logs are captured and delivered to the specified destination.
Specifies the logging driver used by the container, such as awslogs for CloudWatch Logs, fluentd, syslog, json-file, or splunk, which determines how and where container logs are delivered.
The options map provides the key-value configuration parameters for the container's chosen log driver (for example, awslogs-group and awslogs-region for the awslogs driver).
Specifies the secrets to pass to the log driver configuration, allowing you to reference sensitive information from AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store.
The name (key) of the log driver option for which the referenced secret's value is used, such as 'splunk-token' or 'project' in the log configuration.
The ARN of the secret (from AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store) that provides the value for the corresponding log driver option in the ECS task definition's log configuration.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.memory: Specifies the hard limit (in MiB) of memory available to the container; when the container's memory usage reaches this limit, the container is killed.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.memory_reservation: The soft memory limit in MiB for the container, which ECS uses for placement and scheduling, allowing the container to burst above this value when the host has spare memory.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.mount_points: Specifies the mount points for data volumes in the container, including the source volume name and the container path where the volume is mounted.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.mount_points.conta: The container_path specifies the absolute path inside the container where the volume is mounted.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.mount_points.read_: Determines whether the container has read-only access to the mounted volume; when set to true, writes to the volume are rejected, and when false, read/write access is permitted.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.mount_points.sourc: Name of the volume to mount, which must match the name of a volume defined in the task definition's volumes block.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.name: The name of the container definition, which must be unique among all container definitions in the task definition and is used to reference the container from other definitions (e.g., links, dependsOn, and volume mounts).
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.port_mappings: Defines the port mappings for a container, specifying container port, host port, and protocol (tcp/udp), which controls how traffic is routed to the container in the ECS task.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.port_mappings.app_: Specifies the application protocol (e.g., http, http2, grpc) for this port mapping, which is used by AWS App Mesh and Amazon ECS Service Connect to route traffic to the container.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.port_mappings.cont: The port number on the container that receives inbound traffic, paired with a host port to map a container port to a port on the host for ECS task definition port mappings.
Specifies the inclusive range of container ports to map to the host, using the format 'startPort-endPort' (for example, '8000-8080'), enabling the task to expose multiple ports in one definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.port_mappings.host: The port number on the container instance (host) that receives inbound traffic and forwards it to the container's `containerPort`, used with bridge and host network modes; it can be left empty to map directly to the container port.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.port_mappings.name: The name that identifies this port mapping, used when configuring Service Connect for the ECS service.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.port_mappings.prot: The transport protocol (tcp, udp, or tcpudp) that this port mapping uses for communication in the container definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.privileged: When set to true, the container runs in privileged mode, granting it elevated permissions on the host container instance (similar to Docker's --privileged flag).
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.pseudo_terminal: Indicates whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY (teletypewriter) for the container, enabling an interactive terminal session, similar to the Docker `--tty` flag.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.readonly_root_file: Specifies whether the container's root filesystem is mounted in read-only mode, preventing the container from writing to its root filesystem while still permitting writes to attached volumes.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.repository_credent: Specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret or SSM parameter ARN that holds the credentials needed to pull the container image from a private registry.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter that stores the authentication credentials for the private container repository used by this container definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.resource_requireme: Specifies the type and amount of a resource (such as GPU or InferenceAccelerator) that the container requires, used to request hardware accelerators like NVIDIA GPUs or AWS Inferentia chips.
Specifies the type of resource to reserve for the container, such as GPU or InferenceAccelerator, in the ECS task definition's container definition resource requirements.
The value of the resource requirement, which specifies the number of GPUs for the 'GPU' type or the device name for the 'InferenceAccelerator' type.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.restart_policy: Specifies the restart policy for the container, including whether it is enabled and the attempt period, allowing the container to automatically restart after a failure or exit; it is only supported for tasks using the Fargate launch type.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.restart_policy.ena: Whether the container's restart policy is enabled, allowing ECS to automatically restart the container if it exits or fails.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.restart_policy.ign: Specifies a list of container exit codes that are ignored by the ECS restart policy, so the container is not restarted when it exits with any of these codes.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.restart_policy.res: The number of seconds to wait after a container exits before attempting to restart it, as part of the ECS restart policy to control the frequency of restart attempts.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.secrets: Specifies the secrets to pass to the container, referencing either AWS Secrets Manager secrets or SSM Parameter Store parameters, each containing a name and a valueFrom ARN or full SSM parameter name.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.secrets.name: The name of the environment variable that will be set on the container, with its value securely supplied from the secret specified in the corresponding valueFrom field.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.secrets.value_from: Specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or the name/ARN of the SSM parameter that supplies the secret value to be injected into the container.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.start_timeout: Specifies the time duration in seconds to wait for the container to become healthy after it starts, after which the container is considered failed if it has not reached a healthy state.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.stop_timeout: The time in seconds to wait for the container to stop after sending SIGTERM before the system sends SIGKILL, overriding the Docker daemon's default stop timeout.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.system_controls: Specifies a list of system control (sysctl) settings to apply to the container, allowing you to modify kernel parameters such as network stack settings (e.g., net.ipv4.ip_forward) as defined in the container definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.system_controls.na: The sysctl namespace (kernel parameter name) to configure for the container, such as `kernel.msgmax` or `net.ipv4.ip_forward`.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.system_controls.va: The value assigned to the Linux kernel system control (sysctl) specified by the `namespace` field, such as `1` to enable IP forwarding in the container's network namespace.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.ulimits: Defines a list of ulimit settings for the container that override Docker defaults, each specifying a resource type (such as 'nofile' or 'cpu') along with soft and hard limits.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.ulimits.hard_limit: The hard limit (maximum value) for the ulimit setting on the container, which the container cannot exceed.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.ulimits.name: Specifies the type of ulimit to apply to the container, such as 'cpu', 'nofile', 'nproc', or other valid Linux resource limit names.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.ulimits.soft_limit: The lower boundary (soft limit) for the container's ulimit value, specifying the resource limit that can be raised by the process up to the hard limit.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.user: The user name or numeric UID (and optionally group) to run the container process as, overriding the image's default user.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.version_consistenc: Specifies whether ECS version consistency is enabled for this container definition, accepting values 'enabled' or 'disabled' to control whether the container image is pinned to an exact digest for immutable deployments.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.volumes_from: Specifies the volumes to mount from other containers in the same task definition, including the source container name and whether the mount is read-only.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.volumes_from.read_: If true, the container mounts the volume from the source container as read-only.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.volumes_from.sourc: The name of the source container from which this container mounts volumes, as defined in the containerDefinitions.
aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions.working_directory: The working directory inside the container where the container's entrypoint command is run.
aws_ecs_task_definition.inference_accelerators: Configures the Amazon Elastic Inference accelerators to attach to the task, where each accelerator is specified by a device name and device type.
aws_ecs_task_definition.inference_accelerators.device_name: The name of the inference accelerator device, which the container uses to access the accelerator (e.g., 'device1').
aws_ecs_task_definition.inference_accelerators.device_type: Specifies the Elastic Inference accelerator type (e.g., eia2.medium or eia1.large) to attach to the task.
aws_ecs_task_definition.placement_constraints.expression: The cluster query language expression that defines the placement constraint when the type is 'memberOf', specifying which container instances the task can be placed on.
aws_ecs_task_definition.placement_constraints.type: The placement constraint type, which must be either 'distinctInstance' (place each task on a distinct container instance) or 'memberOf' (use a cluster query language expression defined in the expression field).
aws_ecs_task_definition.proxy_configuration.proxy_configuration_: This is the name (key) of a key-value pair in the ECS task definition's proxy configuration properties, identifying which proxy setting (e.g., ProxyIngressPort, ProxyEgressPort, IgnoredUID, or AppPorts) the corresponding value applies to.
The string value of a key in the proxy configuration properties map, defining parameters such as AppPorts, EgressIgnoredPorts, or IgnoredUIDs for the AWS App Mesh proxy in the ECS task definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.tags.key: The key (name) of a key-value tag attached to the ECS task definition, used for resource identification and cost allocation.
aws_ecs_task_definition.task_definition_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this task definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.configured_at_launch: When set to true, indicates that the volume is configured on the container instance at launch time rather than being fully specified in the task definition, enabling dynamic volume configuration (such as for Docker volumes) at runtime.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.docker_volume_configuration: Specifies the Docker volume configuration for a volume in the task definition, including the volume scope, autoprovision setting, driver, driver options, and labels when the volume type is 'docker'.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.docker_volume_configuration.auto: When true, ECS automatically creates the named Docker volume if it does not already exist when the task is launched.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.docker_volume_configuration.driv: Specifies the Docker volume driver to use, such as 'local' or a third-party driver (e.g., 'rexray'), for the volume configured in the task definition.
Specifies a map of Docker driver-specific options passed to the volume driver when configuring a Docker volume in an ECS task definition.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.docker_volume_configuration.labe: Specifies key-value pairs that are assigned as Docker volume labels, which serve as metadata for organizing and identifying the volume and are passed to the Docker volume driver.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.docker_volume_configuration.scop: Determines the lifecycle of the Docker volume, where 'task' auto-provisions and deletes the volume when the task stops, and 'shared' allows the volume to exist independently of any single task.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.efsvolume_configuration: Configures an Amazon EFS volume for the task definition, specifying the EFS filesystem ID, root directory path, transit encryption and port, and optional IAM authorization via an access point.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.efsvolume_configuration.authoriz: The authorization configuration for an Amazon EFS volume, specifying the EFS access point ID and IAM role to use for the volume's file system access.
The access point ID of the EFS file system that Amazon ECS uses to mount the volume, applying the access point's root directory and POSIX user/group permissions to the task's container.
Specifies whether to use IAM authorization for the EFS volume's access point, with a value of 'ENABLED' to enable IAM authentication or 'DISABLED' to use the default EFS security settings.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.efsvolume_configuration.filesyst: The ID of the Amazon EFS file system that this volume mounts, identifying the target file system for the container's persistent storage.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.efsvolume_configuration.root_dir: The path on the Amazon EFS file system to mount as the root directory for the container, defaulting to '/' if not specified.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.efsvolume_configuration.transit_: Indicates whether Amazon EFS uses encryption for data in transit when the volume is mounted in the task, accepting 'ENABLED' to enable encryption or 'DISABLED' to disable it.
Specifies the port on the EFS file system to use for transit encryption, required when transit encryption is enabled.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.fsx_windows_file_server_volume_c: Specifies the configuration for using an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server volume as a data volume in the ECS task definition, including the file system ID, root directory, and authorization configuration.
Specifies the domain and the AWS Secrets Manager credential secret that the container uses to mount the FSx for Windows File Server volume.
Specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter that stores the Microsoft Active Directory domain credentials for mounting the FSx Windows file server volume.
The domain field specifies the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the Active Directory domain to use for authentication when accessing the FSx Windows File Server volume.
The ID of the Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system to mount for this volume in the ECS task definition.
The root directory on the FSx Windows File Server file system to mount as the root for the container's volume.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.host: The host object defines the source path on the container instance for a bind mount volume, with its `sourcePath` property specifying the exact host directory to mount.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.host.source_path: Specifies the path on the host container instance (EC2) that is mounted into the container when the volume type is 'host'.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.name: The name of the volume, which is referenced by container definitions in the mountPoints.sourceVolume property.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.s3_files_volume_configuration: Configuration for an Amazon S3 file volume within an ECS task definition, specifying the S3 bucket, key (object path), and optional object version used to mount a single S3 object as a file into the container.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.s3_files_volume_configuration.ac: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 access point that ECS uses to access the S3 bucket for this volume configuration.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.s3_files_volume_configuration.fi: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket that ECS mounts as a file system volume to tasks using the S3 file volume configuration.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.s3_files_volume_configuration.ro: Specifies the subdirectory within the S3 bucket that is mounted as the root of the ECS volume, determining the base path for files exposed via this volume configuration.
aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.s3_files_volume_configuration.tr: Specifies the custom port used for encrypted (TLS) communication with Amazon S3 when the S3 volume's transit encryption is enabled.

aws_ecs_task_set.capacity_provider_strategy: Specifies the capacity provider strategy for the task set, defining which capacity providers to use and the weights and base values that govern how tasks are distributed among them.
aws_ecs_task_set.capacity_provider_strategy.base: The minimum number of tasks to run on this capacity provider before the task set's weight-based scaling applies.
aws_ecs_task_set.capacity_provider_strategy.capacity_prov: The name of the capacity provider, as registered in the ECS cluster, that this task set should use for running tasks.
aws_ecs_task_set.capacity_provider_strategy.weight: The relative weight assigned to a capacity provider in the strategy, determining what proportion of tasks from the task set are placed on that provider.
aws_ecs_task_set.load_balancers: Configures the load balancer or target groups that route traffic to the tasks in this ECS task set, specifying the container and port to receive traffic.
aws_ecs_task_set.load_balancers.container_name: The name of the container, as defined in the task definition, to which the load balancer routes traffic for this task set.
aws_ecs_task_set.load_balancers.container_port: The container port on which the task set's containers receive traffic from the associated load balancer or target group, used to route incoming requests to the correct container port.
aws_ecs_task_set.load_balancers.target_group_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target group to which the ECS task set's tasks are registered for load balancing.
aws_ecs_task_set.scale: Specifies the scaling configuration for the task set, including the unit (e.g., PERCENT) and value that determine the target number of tasks for the task set.
aws_ecs_task_set.service_registries.container_name: Specifies the container name from the task definition to use for the service discovery (Cloud Map) registry, and if not provided, the default container in the task definition is used.
aws_ecs_task_set.service_registries.container_port: Specifies the container port that the Amazon ECS task set's service registry uses for service discovery with AWS Cloud Map.
aws_ecs_task_set.service_registries.port: The port number that the service discovery service uses for the task's registry entry, which overrides the container's port mapping if specified.
aws_ecs_task_set.service_registries.registry_arn: The ARN of the AWS Cloud Map service registry in which the task set's tasks are registered for service discovery.
aws_ecs_task_set.tags.key: The key of a tag that can be assigned to the ECS task set for organizational or identification purposes.
aws_ecs_task_set.tags.value: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag attached to the ECS task set, which can be used for resource categorization, cost allocation, and operational management.

aws_efs_access_point.access_point_id: The AWS-assigned unique identifier for the EFS access point, used to reference the access point in other resources or APIs.
aws_efs_access_point.access_point_tags.key: The key of a tag in the access_point_tags list on the EFS access point, corresponding to the Key property of the CloudFormation AccessPointTags tag objects.
aws_efs_access_point.access_point_tags.value: The value of a tag applied to the EFS access point, used for metadata and resource categorization.
aws_efs_access_point.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the EFS access point, which uniquely identifies the access point within AWS.

aws_efs_file_system.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this EFS file system, used to reference it in IAM policies and other AWS services.
aws_efs_file_system.file_system_id: The unique AWS-assigned identifier (e.g., fs-12345678) for the EFS file system, returned by AWS and used to reference the file system in other resources.
aws_efs_file_system.file_system_tags.key: The key of a tag applied to the EFS file system, used to organize and identify the resource within AWS.
aws_efs_file_system.file_system_tags.value: The value portion of a tag assigned to the EFS file system, used for metadata, cost allocation, or access control.
aws_efs_file_system.lifecycle_policies.transition_to_archive: Specifies when EFS moves files to the Archive storage class (e.g., AFTER_30_DAYS) based on the number of days since last access, as part of the file system's lifecycle policy.
aws_efs_file_system.lifecycle_policies.transition_to_ia: Specifies the number of days (as a string such as 'AFTER_7_DAYS') after which files are transitioned to the Amazon EFS Infrequent Access (IA) storage class within this lifecycle policy.
aws_efs_file_system.lifecycle_policies.transition_to_primary: Specifies when EFS transitions files from the Infrequent Access storage class back to the Standard storage class, with the only valid value being AFTER_1_ACCESS, meaning a file is moved after it is accessed once.
aws_efs_file_system.replication_configuration.destinations.a: Designates the Availability Zone in which the destination file system of the EFS replication configuration is created, allowing a one-zone replicated file system target; if omitted, AWS chooses an AZ for the destination.
