aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.constraints.max_capa: For the EMR instance group's auto scaling policy, this required number defines the maximum allowable number of EC2 instances that the instance group can scale up to.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.constraints.min_capa: The minimum number of EC2 instances that the auto scaling policy for the EMR instance group will maintain, acting as the lower bound in the scaling constraints.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.rules: Defines the list of scaling rules (each containing a name, a CloudWatch metric-based condition, and a scaling action) that the auto scaling policy evaluates to automatically add or remove instances in the EMR instance group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.rules.action: Specifies the scaling action to take when this auto scaling rule is triggered, defining how many instances to add or remove (and optionally the market) for the instance group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.rules.action.market: Specifies the market type (ON_DEMAND or SPOT) of the instances that the auto scaling rule's action adds or removes in the EMR instance group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.rules.action.simple_: Specifies the parameters for a simple scaling action, including the scaling adjustment type (such as CHANGE_IN_CAPACITY), the amount to scale, and an optional cool-down period, used by an EMR instance group auto-scaling rule.

Specifies how the scaling adjustment is interpreted for the simple scaling policy on an EMR instance group, such as an absolute change in instance count (CHANGE_IN_CAPACITY), a percentage change (PERCENT_CHANGE_IN_CAPACITY), or an exact target capacity (EXACT_CAPACITY).
The amount of time, in seconds, after a scaling activity completes before any further trigger-related scaling activities can start.

The amount by which to scale the instance group when this policy is triggered, interpreted according to the adjustment type (such as an absolute change in instance count, a percentage change, or an exact target capacity).
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.rules.description: The description of the scaling rule, used to document the purpose of the rule within the auto scaling policy for the EMR instance group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.rules.name: The name of the auto scaling rule within the EMR instance group's auto scaling policy.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.rules.trigger: Specifies the CloudWatch alarm definition (including metric, comparison operator, threshold, and evaluation periods) that determines when the scaling rule's action is triggered.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.auto_scaling_policy.rules.trigger.cloud_: Defines the CloudWatch alarm that triggers the scaling rule, specifying metric name, namespace, comparison operator, threshold, evaluation periods, period, statistic, unit, and dimensions.

Specifies the arithmetic operation to use when comparing the specified statistic and threshold, such as GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold or LessThanThreshold, for the CloudWatch alarm that triggers the scaling rule.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric dimensions (name/value pairs) that are applied to the alarm metric for this auto scaling rule's trigger.
Specifies the name (key) of a CloudWatch metric dimension included in the alarm definition that triggers the Amazon EMR instance group auto scaling policy.

The value assigned to the CloudWatch alarm dimension (e.g., an EMR instance group ID or cluster ID) that identifies the metric scope for the auto-scaling trigger, such as 'InstanceGroupId' or 'JobFlowId'.
Specifies the number of consecutive evaluation periods during which the monitored metric must breach the specified threshold before the CloudWatch alarm triggers the auto scaling rule.
The name of the CloudWatch metric (e.g., YARNMemoryAvailablePercentage or a custom metric) that the alarm definition monitors to trigger this auto scaling rule for the EMR instance group.
The CloudWatch namespace (e.g., AWS/EMR) that contains the metric being monitored for the auto scaling policy's CloudWatch alarm trigger.
The period is the number of seconds between evaluation periods for the CloudWatch alarm that triggers this scaling rule, determining how often the metric is evaluated.
Specifies the statistic (such as Average, Sum, SampleCount, Minimum, Maximum, or a percentile) to apply when evaluating the CloudWatch metric for the auto scaling alarm.
The numeric value that the CloudWatch metric is compared against (using the comparison operator) to determine when the alarm triggers for the EMR instance group's auto scaling policy.
The unit of measure for the CloudWatch metric (e.g., Percent, Count, Bytes) that the alarm definition uses to evaluate the auto scaling trigger.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.bid_price: Sets the maximum hourly price you are willing to pay for Spot Instances in the EMR instance group; if specified, the group uses Spot Instances with this bid price, otherwise it uses On-Demand instances.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.configurations: Specifies a list of EMR software configurations (classifications and properties) that override the cluster-level configurations for this instance group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.configurations.classification: Specifies the name of the Hadoop configuration group (such as 'core-site' or 'hdfs-site') that this configuration object applies to within the EMR instance group's configuration settings.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.configurations.configuration_properties: Specifies a key-value map of properties for the configuration classification (e.g., Hadoop settings) applied to the EMR instance group's applications.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.configurations.configurations: The list of nested configuration objects under a configuration, allowing hierarchical application of multiple classifications and their properties to the instance group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.custom_ami_id: Specifies a custom Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID to use for the instances in this EMR instance group, overriding the default EMR AMI.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.ebs_configuration: The EbsConfiguration property specifies the Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes to attach to each instance in the Amazon EMR instance group, including whether to use EBS optimization.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.ebs_configuration.ebs_block_device_confi: Specifies the list of EBS block device configurations, each defining a volume specification and the number of volumes per instance, to attach to each instance in the EMR instance group.
Defines the EBS volume configuration, including volume type, size in GB, and optional IOPS, for each EBS block device attached to the instance group.
The IOPS (input/output operations per second) rate for the EBS volume, applicable when the volume type is io1, io2, or gp3.
Specifies the size, in GiB, of each EBS volume defined in the volume specification for the EMR instance group's EBS block device configuration.
Specifies the throughput in MiB/s for a gp3 EBS volume attached to an EMR instance group, used when the volume type is gp3 and VolumeSpecification throughput is provided.
Specifies the EBS volume type (e.g., gp2, gp3, io1, or standard) for each block device in the EMR instance group's EBS configuration.
The number of EBS volumes of the specified volume specification to attach to each instance in the instance group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.ebs_configuration.ebs_optimized: Indicates whether the EC2 instances in this EMR instance group are launched as EBS-optimized, providing dedicated network and disk I/O for Amazon EBS volumes.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.id: The `id` is the AWS-assigned unique identifier for the EMR instance group, used to reference the instance group within the EMR cluster.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.instance_count: The number of EC2 instances to launch in this EMR instance group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.instance_role: Defines the role of this instance group in the EMR cluster, which must be set to MASTER for the primary node group, or CORE or TASK for additional node groups.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.instance_type: Specifies the EC2 instance type (e.g., m5.xlarge) that Amazon EMR will launch for each instance in this instance group, determining the compute and memory resources available to the group.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.job_flow_id: The ID of the EMR cluster (job flow) to which this instance group belongs.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.market: Specifies whether the instance group uses On-Demand or Spot instances, with allowed values ON_DEMAND or SPOT.
aws_emr_instance_group_config.name: Specifies a user-defined name for the EMR instance group, which is used to identify the group within the cluster.

aws_emr_step.hadoop_jar_step: Defines the Hadoop JAR step configuration for the EMR step, including the JAR location, main class, arguments, and custom properties.
aws_emr_step.hadoop_jar_step.args: A list of arguments to pass to the main class of the Hadoop JAR step.
aws_emr_step.hadoop_jar_step.jar: The Amazon S3 location or full path to the JAR file that contains the main code for the EMR step.
aws_emr_step.hadoop_jar_step.main_class: Specifies the name of the main class in the supplied JAR file that the EMR step will execute.
aws_emr_step.hadoop_jar_step.step_properties: This is a list of key-value objects that specify custom properties for the Hadoop JAR step, which are passed to the Hadoop framework during step execution.
aws_emr_step.hadoop_jar_step.step_properties.key: This key specifies a property name to pass to the Hadoop JAR step as part of the step's configuration.
aws_emr_step.hadoop_jar_step.step_properties.value: The value of a property entry in the step_properties map of the Hadoop JAR step, used to pass custom configuration to the JAR when the step executes on the EMR cluster.

aws_emr_studio.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this EMR Studio in AWS.
aws_emr_studio.encryption_key_arn: The ARN of an AWS KMS key used to encrypt data within the EMR Studio workspace, such as notebooks and artifacts.
aws_emr_studio.service_role: The IAM role that EMR Studio assumes to call AWS services on your behalf.
aws_emr_studio.tags: A list of key-value tags to attach to the EMR Studio, used for organizing, managing, and cost allocation of the resource in AWS.
aws_emr_studio.tags.key: Defines a user-defined tag key for the Amazon EMR Studio, which can be used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.
aws_emr_studio.tags.value: The value portion of a tag applied to the EMR Studio, used to categorize, identify, or manage the studio resource.
aws_emr_studio.user_role: The IAM role that EMR Studio users assume, granting permissions for their studio work within the EMR Studio environment.

aws_emr_studio_session_mapping.session_policy_arn: The ARN of the IAM policy that defines the permissions for the EMR Studio session assigned to the mapped user or group.

aws_emr_walworkspace.tags.key: The key (name) of a user-defined tag attached to the EMR WAL workspace, used for resource categorization, cost tracking, and access control.
aws_emr_walworkspace.tags.value: The value component of a tag attached to the EMR WAL workspace, used to store arbitrary metadata for resource identification, organization, and cost allocation.

aws_emrcontainers_endpoint.certificate_authority: The certificate_authority object contains the certificate authority details (such as the certificate ARN) for the EKS cluster backing the EMR Containers endpoint, used to establish TLS trust for the endpoint connection.
aws_emrcontainers_endpoint.certificate_authority.certificate_arn: The ARN of the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to secure the TLS certificate authority for the EMR Containers endpoint.
aws_emrcontainers_endpoint.certificate_authority.certificate_data: The PEM-encoded certificate data from the certificate authority that secures the EMR Containers managed endpoint, used by clients to verify TLS connections.
aws_emrcontainers_endpoint.configuration_overrides: Specifies configuration overrides for the EMR on EKS managed endpoint, including application configurations (e.g., Spark properties) and monitoring configurations (e.g., CloudWatch logging and metrics).
aws_emrcontainers_endpoint.configuration_overrides.application_conf: Specifies application-level configuration overrides (e.g., Spark settings) to apply to workloads using this endpoint, where each list entry is a Configuration object containing a classification and its properties.

The classification for the application configuration override, such as 'spark-defaults', 'hive-site', or 'yarn-site', which identifies the type of configuration properties being applied when the endpoint is created.

Provides a list of application configuration objects, each containing a classification (e.g., spark-defaults) and key-value properties, that override the default EMR on EKS application settings for the endpoint.
Key-value pairs for a configuration classification, used to override application-level settings for the EMR on EKS managed endpoint.
aws_emrcontainers_endpoint.configuration_overrides.monitoring_confi: This object overrides the default monitoring configuration for jobs running through the EMR Containers endpoint, specifying where to send logs (CloudWatch log group and S3 location) and whether to enable the persistent application UI.
This object defines the CloudWatch monitoring configuration for the endpoint, specifying the log group name and optional log stream prefix where EMR Containers delivers application logs.
The name of the CloudWatch log group to which EMR on EKS container logs are delivered when monitoring configuration is enabled for this endpoint.
Specifies the prefix that is prepended to CloudWatch log stream names for monitoring logs emitted by the EMR on EKS managed endpoint.
Specifies the container log rotation settings for the endpoint's monitoring configuration, including the rotation size in megabytes and the maximum number of log files to keep.
The maximum number of rotated container log files to retain for a pod after rotation, after which the oldest logs are deleted.
The size threshold in MB at which container logs are rotated for the Amazon EMR on EKS endpoint's monitoring configuration.
Determines whether persistent Spark UI is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for job runs submitted through this EMR Containers endpoint.
Defines the Amazon S3 configuration for monitoring logs of the EMR containers endpoint, including the destination S3 URI (LogUri) and optional encryption key.
Specifies the S3 URI where logs are stored for monitoring of the EMR on EKS endpoint.
aws_emrcontainers_endpoint.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon EMR on EKS endpoint, used for cost allocation and resource identification.
aws_emrcontainers_endpoint.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the Amazon EMR on EKS endpoint, used for resource identification, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_emrcontainers_security_configuration.tags.key: The key (name) of a user-defined tag attached to the EMR Containers security configuration, used for identifying, categorizing, and managing this AWS resource.
aws_emrcontainers_security_configuration.tags.value: Specifies the value portion of a key-value tag assigned to the EMR Containers security configuration, which can be used to filter and manage the resource.

aws_emrcontainers_virtual_cluster.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the EMR Containers virtual cluster in AWS.
aws_emrcontainers_virtual_cluster.container_provider: The container provider configuration that defines the underlying container platform (e.g., Amazon EKS) on which the virtual cluster runs, including the provider type and the Amazon EKS cluster information.
aws_emrcontainers_virtual_cluster.container_provider.info: The info object inside container_provider contains provider-specific details, specifically the Amazon EKS namespace in which the virtual cluster runs.
aws_emrcontainers_virtual_cluster.container_provider.info.eks_info: Specifies the Amazon EKS cluster information for the container provider, including the Kubernetes namespace where the virtual cluster runs.
aws_emrcontainers_virtual_cluster.container_provider.info.eks_info.namespa: The Kubernetes namespace in the Amazon EKS cluster where the virtual cluster's resources are deployed.
aws_emrcontainers_virtual_cluster.tags.value: The value portion of a tag attached to the EMR Containers virtual cluster.

aws_emrserverless_application.initial_capacity: Configures the initial capacity for each worker type (e.g., driver, executor) of the EMR Serverless application, specifying the worker count and the CPU/memory allocated for that type.
aws_emrserverless_application.initial_capacity.key: Specifies the name of the worker type (for example, driver or executor) for which to define the initial capacity configuration in an AWS EMR Serverless application.
aws_emrserverless_application.initial_capacity.value: Defines the initial capacity configuration for a given worker type (e.g., Driver or Executor) in the serverless application, specifying the number of workers and their CPU/memory resources via the workerCount and workerConfiguration properties.
aws_emrserverless_application.initial_capacity.value.worker_configurat: Specifies the CPU, memory, and disk configuration for workers allocated as the initial capacity of the EMR Serverless application.
The number of vCPUs allocated to each worker in the initial capacity configuration of the EMR Serverless application.
Specifies the disk size in GB for the worker in the initial capacity configuration of the EMR Serverless application.
The disk type (e.g., SSD or HDD) for the storage attached to each worker instance in the initial capacity configuration of the EMR Serverless application.
Defines the memory size (in MB) allocated per worker for the initial capacity of the EMR Serverless application.
aws_emrserverless_application.initial_capacity.value.worker_count: The number of workers of the specified worker type (the key in the initial capacity map) to provision for the EMR Serverless application at startup.
aws_emrserverless_application.interactive_configuration: Configures interactive capabilities for the EMR Serverless application, including enabling the Livy endpoint and EMR Studio integration.
aws_emrserverless_application.maximum_capacity: The maximum capacity limits (CPU, memory, and optional disk) that the EMR Serverless application is allowed to use, defined as a MaximumAllowedResources object that caps the application's total resource usage.
aws_emrserverless_application.monitoring_configuration.cloud_watch_log: Specifies the CloudWatch Logs group, log stream name prefix, and optional encryption key ARN that the EMR Serverless application uses to deliver its runtime logs to Amazon CloudWatch.
aws_emrserverless_application.monitoring_configuration.managed_persist: This field specifies the managed persistence monitoring configuration, controlling whether Spark event logs are persisted and the S3 location where they are stored for the EMR Serverless application.
aws_emrserverless_application.monitoring_configuration.prometheus_moni: Configures the Prometheus monitoring endpoint for the EMR Serverless application by specifying the remote write URL where application metrics are sent.
aws_emrserverless_application.monitoring_configuration.s3_monitoring_c: This nested block configures the S3 monitoring destination for the EMR Serverless application, specifying the S3 URI (log_uri) where logs are delivered and optionally a KMS key ARN (encryption_key_arn) for encrypting the logs.
aws_emrserverless_application.network_configuration: Specifies the VPC subnets and security group IDs that the EMR Serverless application uses to run jobs within a private network.
aws_emrserverless_application.runtime_configuration.classification: Specifies the classification name (e.g., spark-defaults) for the runtime configuration, which defines the set of properties that apply to the EMR Serverless application.
aws_emrserverless_application.runtime_configuration.configurations: Specifies a list of sub-configurations for a given runtime configuration classification, allowing nested engine-specific settings (such as Spark or Hive properties) to be applied to the EMR Serverless application.
aws_emrserverless_application.runtime_configuration.properties: Specifies a map of additional key-value pairs to apply as runtime configuration settings for the EMR Serverless application, extending the configuration defined by the parent runtime configuration's key and value fields.
aws_emrserverless_application.tags.value: The value component of a key-value tag applied to the EMR Serverless application, which can be any string and is used for resource metadata, filtering, and cost allocation.
aws_emrserverless_application.worker_type_specifications: Defines CPU and memory specifications for each worker type (e.g., Driver or Executor) in the EMR Serverless application, allowing per-worker-type resource overrides.

aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.description: Describes the ID mapping workflow, providing a human-readable summary of its purpose and configuration for management and identification in AWS Entity Resolution.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.id_mapping_incremental_run_config: Specifies the incremental run configuration for the ID mapping workflow, defining the interval (and interval type) at which the workflow automatically runs on new data.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.id_mapping_incremental_run_config.increm: Determines whether the incremental run of the ID mapping workflow imports new records (IMPORT) or updates existing record mappings (UPDATE).
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.id_mapping_techniques: Defines the technique (rule-based or machine learning-based) and its configuration for generating unique IDs when matching records in the ID mapping workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.id_mapping_techniques.id_mapping_type: Specifies whether this ID mapping technique uses rule-based matching or a provider-based machine-learning approach, with allowed values RULE_BASED or PROVIDER.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.id_mapping_techniques.normalization_vers: Specifies the version of the normalization rules (e.g., '1.0' or '2.0') applied to standardize input records' attributes during the ID mapping workflow, controlling how data is prepared before matching.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.id_mapping_techniques.provider_propertie: Configuration for the ID mapping provider, including the provider schema ARN and provider-specific parameters, used when the id mapping technique is provider-based.
Specifies the Amazon S3 location of an intermediate source dataset that a provider-based ID mapping workflow can access to improve entity resolution accuracy.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.id_mapping_techniques.rule_based_propert: Specifies the configuration for rule-based ID matching within the workflow, including the matching rules and attribute mappings used to compare records.
Specifies the cardinality of matches for the rule-based ID mapping, either ONE_TO_ONE (each record maps to at most one other record) or MANY_TO_MANY (each record can match multiple records).
Specifies the record matching model (e.g., ONE_TO_ONE or MANY_TO_MANY) that determines how source records are paired with matched records in the rule-based mapping workflow.
Specifies whether the rule-based properties in the ID mapping workflow apply to the source or target side (valid values: SOURCE or TARGET).
Defines the list of matching rules that specify how record attributes are compared (e.g., exact, fuzzy) across source data to link records into an entity.
The list of record attribute names (matching keys) that are compared between records to determine if they refer to the same entity within a rule of the rule-based ID mapping workflow.
Provides an identifying name for the rule that defines how matching keys are combined in the rule-based mapping technique of the AWS Entity Resolution ID mapping workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.input_source_config: Specifies the list of input data sources (each with an ARN and schema name) from which the entity resolution ID mapping workflow reads records for matching and linking.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.input_source_config.input_source_arn: The ARN of the input source (such as an Amazon S3 bucket or AWS Glue table) that provides the data for the ID mapping workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.input_source_config.schema_arn: The ARN of the AWS Entity Resolution schema that defines the attributes and data format for this input source in the ID mapping workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.input_source_config.type: Specifies whether the input source is the source or target dataset in the ID mapping workflow, with allowed values SOURCE or TARGET.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.output_source_config: Configures the destinations where the ID mapping workflow writes its matched record output, specifying the S3 output path and optional KMS key for encryption.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.output_source_config.kmsarn: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the output data written to the S3 output location for this ID mapping workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.output_source_config.output_s3_path: Specifies the S3 bucket and object key prefix where the ID mapping workflow writes its output data files.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that the Entity Resolution ID mapping workflow assumes to access the input data from the source and write results to the output target.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.tags: In an AWS Entity Resolution ID mapping workflow, tags are custom key-value pairs you can attach to the workflow resource to help organize, identify, and manage it, as well as support cost allocation and IAM-based access control.
aws_entity_resolution_id_mapping_workflo.workflow_name: The unique name of the ID mapping workflow, used as a friendly identifier when creating and managing the workflow in AWS Entity Resolution.

aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.description: An optional free-form description that helps identify the purpose or contents of the ID namespace.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.id_mapping_workflow_properties: A list of configurations for ID mapping workflows that define how identifiers are mapped within this namespace, where each item specifies a workflow type (e.g., ID_MAPPING) and its provider properties.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.id_mapping_workflow_properties.id_mappin: Specifies the cardinality of the ID mapping workflow: ONE_TO_ONE for a unique source-to-ID mapping or ONE_TO_MANY for one source record mapping to multiple IDs.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.id_mapping_workflow_properties.provider_: Specifies the provider-specific configuration for an ID mapping workflow, including the provider configuration map and optional intermediate source S3 location.
Map of provider-specific configuration parameters passed to the entity resolution provider for this ID mapping workflow.
The ARN of the AWS Marketplace provider service used to perform the ID mapping workflow for this ID namespace.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.id_mapping_workflow_properties.rule_base: Configures the rule-based matching configuration for this ID namespace mapping workflow, including the attribute matching model and the list of matching rules that define how source and target attributes are compared.

Specifies the matching model for rule-based ID mapping, determining whether a record is considered a match when all attributes in the rule match (ALL_MATCH) or when any single attribute matches (ANY_MATCH).
Specifies the record matching models (e.g., ONE_TO_ONE, ONE_TO_MANY, MANY_TO_MANY) that define the mapping cardinality used by the rule-based matching logic in this ID mapping workflow property.
Specifies the rule definition types (e.g., SOURCE or TARGET) used to categorize the matching rules in the rule-based ID mapping workflow for the ID namespace.

Defines the list of source-to-target attribute mapping rules used by the rule-based ID mapping workflow, where each rule specifies a source attribute and the corresponding target attribute in the ID namespace.
The list of record attribute names (columns) that are compared between source records to determine if they match under this rule in the rule-based mapping workflow.
The name that uniquely identifies this matching rule within the rule-based properties of the ID mapping workflow for the entity resolution ID namespace.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.id_namespace_name: Specifies the name of the ID namespace, which uniquely identifies it within the AWS account and Region.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.input_source_config: Configures the input sources for the ID namespace, specifying each data source's ARN and schema to be used for entity resolution.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.input_source_config.input_source_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the input data source (such as an S3 bucket) from which the entity resolution ID namespace reads its records for matching.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.input_source_config.schema_name: Specifies the name of the schema that describes the structure of the input data, which AWS Entity Resolution uses to interpret the fields for record matching.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Entity Resolution assumes to read from the input sources configured for this ID namespace.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.tags: Assigns key-value metadata tags to this AWS Entity Resolution ID Namespace resource, enabling cost allocation, access control, and organization of the namespace.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Entity Resolution ID namespace, used for metadata organization and cost allocation.
aws_entity_resolution_id_namespace.type: Specifies whether the ID namespace is a SOURCE or TARGET type, determining its role in the entity resolution mapping workflow.

aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.description: An optional human-readable description of the Entity Resolution matching workflow, used to provide additional context about the workflow's purpose or configuration.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.incremental_run_config: Configures how the matching workflow handles incremental runs, specifying the incremental run type (such as IMMEDIATE or SCHEDULED) to process only new or updated records.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.incremental_run_config.incremental_run_t: Specifies whether the incremental run is triggered immediately when new data is added (IMMEDIATE) or on a recurring schedule (SCHEDULED).
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.input_source_config: Defines the list of input data sources for the matching workflow, specifying the ARN of each source and the schema name used to interpret the data.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.input_source_config.apply_normalization: Specifies whether normalization is applied to the input source data before matching.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.input_source_config.input_source_arn: The ARN of the input source (such as an AWS Glue table or S3 bucket) containing the customer records to be used in the matching workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.input_source_config.schema_arn: The ARN of the AWS Entity Resolution schema that defines the attributes and types for interpreting the records from the associated input source.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.output_source_config: Specifies the output destinations for the matching workflow, including the S3 path (OutputS3Path), the IAM role (RoleArn) that grants write access, and an optional KMS key (KMSArn) for encrypting the output.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.output_source_config.apply_normalization: Indicates whether the matching workflow applies data normalization (such as standardizing name and address formats) to the output source records.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.output_source_config.customer_profiles_i: Configures writing the matching workflow's output to an Amazon Connect Customer Profiles domain, including the domain ARN and the object type name to use.
The ARN of the Amazon Connect Customer Profiles domain where the matching workflow's resolved output entities are written.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Connect Customer Profiles object type that stores the output records generated by this matching workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.output_source_config.kmsarn: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the output source data of the matching workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.output_source_config.output: The `output` list within `output_source_config` defines the output columns for the matching workflow's result file, with each item specifying the output attribute name and whether the value should be hashed.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.output_source_config.output.hashed: When true, this output field's value is hashed in the match results, protecting sensitive data like emails or phone numbers.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.output_source_config.output.name: The name of the output attribute that gets written to the output source, corresponding to an attribute from the input schema of the matching workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.output_source_config.output_s3_path: The Amazon S3 bucket and prefix (path) where the matching workflow writes its output files.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.resolution_techniques: Defines the matching method used to resolve entities, specifying whether the workflow uses rule-based matching or machine learning and the associated configuration.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.resolution_techniques.provider_propertie: Specifies the configuration for using an external matching service provider, including the provider's ARN and the input schema mapping required to invoke that provider in the resolution workflow.
Specifies the Amazon S3 location (bucket and path) where intermediate data is stored during the entity resolution workflow, used by the matching provider for processing.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.resolution_techniques.resolution_type: Specifies the matching technique to use in the workflow, either rule-based matching (`RULE_MATCHING`) or machine learning-based matching (`ML_MATCHING`).
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.resolution_techniques.rule_based_propert: Defines the rule-based resolution settings for the workflow, including the list of matching rules and the attribute matching model (ONE_TO_ONE or MANY_TO_MANY) that controls how input records are compared.

Determines whether a match requires all specified attributes to be equivalent (ONE_TO_ONE) or whether any single attribute can suffice for a match (MANY_TO_MANY) when evaluating records under this rule set.

Specifies the purpose of the rule-based matching workflow, which can be set to IDENTIFIER_GENERATION to generate unique identifiers for matched records or INDEXING to index records for efficient match queries.
The list of rule definitions that specify the matching criteria and actions used to match records in the rule-based matching workflow.
Specifies the list of attribute names from the input data that the rule uses as matching keys to compare records and determine whether they represent the same entity.
The name of the rule in the rule-based matching configuration, used to identify and reference the rule within the matching workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.resolution_techniques.rule_condition_pro: Specifies the list of matching rules, each containing the rule name and matching keys, that define how records are compared to determine matches in the entity resolution workflow.
Specifies the condition expression (a SQL-like predicate on record fields) that must be satisfied for this rule to apply during entity resolution matching.
Specifies a unique name for this rule within the rule-based matching configuration of the Entity Resolution workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.role_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the matching workflow assumes to access source data and output locations.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the matching workflow, used to assign metadata for identifying and managing the workflow.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.tags.value: Value of a tag attached to the AWS Entity Resolution matching workflow, used for organization and cost tracking.
aws_entity_resolution_matching_workflow.workflow_name: The name of the matching workflow, which is a unique, human-readable identifier for the workflow within your AWS account and is used in the CreateMatchingWorkflow API request.

aws_entity_resolution_policy_statement.action: The list of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) actions, such as entityresolution:CreateMatchingWorkflow, that this policy statement allows or denies for the specified Entity Resolution resource.
aws_entity_resolution_policy_statement.condition: The condition statement (a JSON-formatted string) that specifies when the policy statement takes effect, using IAM condition operators and keys such as aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn.
aws_entity_resolution_policy_statement.effect: Determines whether the policy statement allows or denies the specified actions on the Entity Resolution resource, typically specified as 'Allow' or 'Deny'.
aws_entity_resolution_policy_statement.principal: Defines the list of AWS principals (such as IAM role ARNs, IAM user ARNs, or AWS account IDs) that the entity resolution policy statement authorizes, controlling which principals can access the associated Entity Resolution resource.

aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.description: An optional description of the schema mapping that provides human-readable context about its purpose or contents.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.mapped_input_fields: Specifies the list of mapped input fields, where each field entry defines the name and type (such as NAME, EMAIL, or ADDRESS) of an attribute from the input source that is used for entity resolution matching.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.mapped_input_fields.field_name: The name of the source data field that is mapped to an attribute in the schema.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.mapped_input_fields.group_name: Specifies the logical group name for an input field in the schema mapping, enabling multiple fields to be grouped together into a composite match key for entity resolution.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.mapped_input_fields.hashed: Specifies whether the input field is hashed before being used in entity resolution matching, so raw values are not stored in plaintext.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.mapped_input_fields.match_key: Specifies a string that groups this input field with other fields sharing the same match key, so that the entity resolution job uses them together as a single matching criterion when comparing records.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.mapped_input_fields.sub_type: Specifies a more granular subtype for the input field's type (such as a name or address component like FIRST_NAME or CITY) when defining a schema mapping in AWS Entity Resolution, allowing finer-grained mapping of source data to the standard schema.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.mapped_input_fields.type: Specifies the semantic type of the mapped input field (for example, name, email, phone, address, or custom), enabling AWS Entity Resolution to interpret the field's value for matching and normalization.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.schema_name: The unique name you assign to this Entity Resolution schema mapping within your AWS account and region, used to identify the mapping when interacting with Entity Resolution APIs and the console.
aws_entity_resolution_schema_mapping.tags: Specifies a list of tag objects (key-value pairs) to attach to the AWS Entity Resolution schema mapping, enabling resource identification, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_event_schemas_discoverer.tags.key: Specifies a tag key to associate with the EventBridge Schema Discoverer, enabling you to categorize, filter, and control access to the resource via resource-level policies or cost allocation tags.
aws_event_schemas_discoverer.tags.value: The tag value for the EventBridge Schema Discoverer, paired with a tag key to assign custom metadata such as environment, project, or cost-allocation labels to the discoverer resource.

aws_event_schemas_registry.tags.key: The tag key associated with the EventBridge Schema Registry, used to assign a custom metadata label that helps organize, identify, and filter the registry by their project, environment, or other criteria.
aws_event_schemas_registry.tags.value: The value of a tag key attached to the EventBridge Schema Registry, used to store arbitrary metadata for resource management and filtering.

aws_event_schemas_registry_policy.id: The unique identifier of the registry policy, equal to the name of the registry to which the policy is attached.
aws_event_schemas_registry_policy.policy: The JSON resource-based policy document that grants or denies permissions to principals for actions on the EventBridge schema registry and its schemas.
aws_event_schemas_registry_policy.registry_name: The name of the EventBridge Schema Registry to which this resource-based policy is attached, identifying the registry whose access permissions the policy controls.
aws_event_schemas_registry_policy.revision_id: The revision ID of the registry policy, used for optimistic concurrency control to prevent conflicting updates (you must provide the current revision when updating the policy).

aws_event_schemas_schema.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to an EventBridge Schema, used to organize and categorize the schema within AWS.
aws_event_schemas_schema.tags.value: The value of a tag key attached to the EventBridge Schema, used to store arbitrary metadata for the schema resource.

aws_events_api_destination.description: A description for the API destination to create.
aws_events_api_destination.http_method: The HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST, PATCH) used when EventBridge invokes the API destination endpoint.
aws_events_api_destination.invocation_rate_limit_per_second: The maximum number of invocations per second that EventBridge allows to the API destination.

aws_events_archive.archive_name: The name of the EventBridge archive, which uniquely identifies the archive within the AWS account and region.
aws_events_archive.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this EventBridge archive in AWS.
aws_events_archive.description: The description of the archive, providing an optional human-readable explanation of the archive's purpose or contents.
aws_events_archive.event_pattern: A JSON object specifying the event pattern that determines which events are captured in the archive.
aws_events_archive.kms_key_identifier: Specifies the AWS KMS key (by ARN or alias) used to encrypt the events stored in this archive; if omitted, EventBridge uses an AWS managed key.
aws_events_archive.retention_days: The number of days that events are retained in the archive before they are automatically deleted.
aws_events_archive.source_arn: The ARN of the event source, such as an EventBridge bus, from which the archive collects events.

aws_events_connection.auth_parameters: The authentication parameters for the event connection, specifying how requests to the destination are authenticated (via API key, basic, or OAuth credentials) along with optional HTTP invocation parameters.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.api_key_auth_parameters: Specifies the API key name and value used for API key authorization when EventBridge invokes the API destination associated with this connection.
The name of the API key for API key authentication, which is used together with the API key value to authenticate requests made through the EventBridge connection.
The value of the API key used for authentication when the EventBridge connection uses API key authorization.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.basic_auth_parameters: Defines the username and password used for basic authentication when the EventBridge connection invokes the API destination.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.basic_auth_parameters.pa: The password to use for basic authentication when connecting to the API destination or endpoint, paired with the username in the same basic auth parameters.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.basic_auth_parameters.us: The username for basic authentication when the EventBridge connection invokes the API destination.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.connectivity_parameters: Defines the private connectivity parameters for an EventBridge connection, including a resource configuration ARN and optional resource-specific settings used to reach endpoints within a VPC or via a PrivateLink resource configuration.
Contains the ARN of the VPC endpoint in the 'ResourceArn' subproperty, defining the private resource target for the EventBridge connection.
The ARN of the resource association used for the connectivity parameters of the EventBridge connection.
The ARN of the AWS resource configuration (such as a VPC endpoint) used by the EventBridge connection to route traffic through a private network to the destination API.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.invocation_http_paramete: Configures the HTTP headers, query string, and path parameters that are passed to the API destination invocation when using this connection.
This list of key-value objects defines the body parameters that are URL-encoded and sent as the HTTP request body when the EventBridge connection invokes the API destination.
Indicates whether the value of this body parameter is a secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager, which EventBridge retrieves and uses when making the HTTP invocation.
The name of the body parameter to include in the HTTP invocation request for the EventBridge connection.
The value to be paired with the key for a body parameter in the HTTP invocation parameters of the EventBridge connection.
A list of key-value pairs (each with `Key` and `Value`) that define the HTTP headers to include in the API invocation request for this EventBridge connection.
Specifies whether the value of this header parameter is a secret that should be retrieved from AWS Secrets Manager.
The name of an HTTP header to include in the API destination invocation request, defined within the connection's invocation HTTP parameters.
The value to be sent as the header value in the HTTP request to the API destination, which can be a static string or a JSONPath expression that extracts data from the event at runtime.
Defines the query string parameters to be sent in the HTTP request for the EventBridge connection, where each item specifies a parameter key, its value, and whether the value is a secret.

Indicates whether the value of this query string parameter is a secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager (true) or a plaintext value (false), where when true the Value field references the secret name to be resolved at invocation time.
The key specifies the name of a query string parameter in the invocation HTTP request, used by the API destination connection's authentication parameters.
Specifies the value of a query string parameter sent in the HTTP request when the EventBridge connection invokes the API destination.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.oauth_parameters: Configuration for OAuth authorization within the connection's authentication parameters, including the authorization endpoint, client application credentials, and HTTP method used to request the token.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.oauth_parameters.authori: The URL of the OAuth authorization server's endpoint where the connection redirects users for authentication and consent during the OAuth authorization code grant flow.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.oauth_parameters.client_: Specifies the OAuth client ID and client secret used to authenticate the connection with the authorization endpoint.
The OAuth client ID used by the EventBridge connection to authenticate with the target API.
The client secret that the EventBridge connection uses to authenticate to the OAuth authorization endpoint.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.oauth_parameters.http_me: The HTTP method (e.g., GET or POST) used for the OAuth authorization request to the specified authorization endpoint for the EventBridge connection.
aws_events_connection.auth_parameters.oauth_parameters.oauth_h: Specifies additional HTTP parameters (header parameters, query string parameters, and body parameters) to include when making the OAuth authorization request to the authorization endpoint.

Specifies a list of key-value pairs to include in the body of the HTTP request used when obtaining an OAuth token for the EventBridge connection, allowing custom data to be sent in the token request body.
Specifies whether the value for this OAuth body parameter is a secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager (true) or a plaintext string (false).
The key that identifies the specific body parameter entry in the OAuth HTTP request body parameters for this EventBridge connection.
The value of a body parameter that is sent in the HTTP request when retrieving the OAuth token, paired with its corresponding key.
Defines the HTTP header key-value pairs to include in the OAuth authorization request for the EventBridge connection.
This boolean flag indicates whether the header parameter's value is a secret (stored and encrypted as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager) rather than a plaintext value.
The name of an HTTP header to include in the OAuth-authenticated request for this EventBridge connection.
The value of the HTTP header parameter that will be included in the OAuth request to the API destination.
Specifies key-value pairs to append as query string parameters to the OAuth HTTP request for an EventBridge connection's authorization flow.
Indicates whether the value of the query string parameter is a secret that is stored in AWS Secrets Manager, allowing EventBridge to reference it securely in the OAuth HTTP request.
The key (name) of a query string parameter to be included in the OAuth HTTP request made by the EventBridge connection when obtaining an OAuth token.
The value of the query-string parameter to be included in the OAuth HTTP request when authorizing the EventBridge connection.
aws_events_connection.authorization_type: Specifies the authorization type for the EventBridge connection, which can be one of BASIC, OAUTH_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS, or API_KEY, determining how the connection authenticates to the API destination.
aws_events_connection.invocation_connectivity_parameters.resou: Specifies the resource parameters used for invocation connectivity, specifically containing the ARN of the private resource (such as a VPC endpoint) that EventBridge uses to route invocations.
The ARN of the resource association (such as a VPC endpoint) that EventBridge uses to route connection invocations to a private resource.
Specifies the ARN of the resource configuration that defines the private VPC endpoint network access used by the EventBridge connection when invoking the target resource.
aws_events_connection.kms_key_identifier: Specifies the AWS KMS key (by ID, ARN, or alias) used to encrypt the connection's credentials and other sensitive parameters, enabling customer-managed encryption instead of the default AWS-owned key.

aws_events_endpoint.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this EventBridge endpoint in AWS.
aws_events_endpoint.description: A user-provided description that identifies the purpose of the EventBridge global endpoint, which routes events between event buses across multiple AWS regions for disaster recovery.
aws_events_endpoint.endpoint_id: The unique identifier assigned by Amazon EventBridge to the endpoint when it is created.
aws_events_endpoint.endpoint_url: The fully qualified DNS URL assigned to this EventBridge global endpoint, used as the ingestion target for events routed to its configured event buses.
aws_events_endpoint.event_buses: Specifies the list of EventBridge event buses to which the endpoint sends events, where each entry includes the ARN of the event bus and optionally an IAM role to use for event delivery.
aws_events_endpoint.event_buses.event_bus_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the EventBridge event bus that the endpoint associates with for routing events.
aws_events_endpoint.name: The unique name you assign to this EventBridge global endpoint, used to identify it when routing events between event buses across regions.
aws_events_endpoint.replication_config: Configures multi-Region replication for this EventBridge endpoint, including whether replication is enabled and the list of AWS Regions to which events are replicated.
aws_events_endpoint.replication_config.state: Determines whether EventBridge replicates events from the primary region to secondary regions for this global endpoint, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.
aws_events_endpoint.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that EventBridge assumes to replicate events between the event buses associated with this global endpoint.
aws_events_endpoint.routing_config: Defines how the EventBridge endpoint routes events to regional event buses, including the routing criteria that determines the primary and secondary event bus targets and the failover configuration for health check-based rerouting.
aws_events_endpoint.routing_config.failover_config: Defines the primary and secondary AWS Regions used by the EventBridge endpoint for failover routing.
aws_events_endpoint.routing_config.failover_config.primary: The primary region configuration for an Amazon EventBridge global endpoint, defined by the HealthCheck ARN that EventBridge monitors to determine if the primary Region is healthy and when to fail over to the secondary Region.
aws_events_endpoint.routing_config.failover_config.primary.h: The ARN of the Route 53 health check that determines whether the primary region is healthy, triggering failover to the secondary region for the EventBridge endpoint.
aws_events_endpoint.routing_config.failover_config.secondary: Defines the secondary failover target for the EventBridge endpoint, containing the ARN of the regional event bus that receives events when the primary is unavailable.
The ARN of the EventBridge event bus in the secondary Region that receives events when the primary Region fails over.
aws_events_endpoint.state: The current lifecycle state of the EventBridge endpoint as reported by the service (e.g., ACTIVE, CREATING, UPDATING, DELETING).
aws_events_endpoint.state_reason: The reason that describes the current state of the EventBridge endpoint, such as error details if the endpoint is in a FAILED state.

aws_events_event_bus.tags.key: The key (name) of a tag attached to the Amazon EventBridge event bus.
aws_events_event_bus.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag attached to an Amazon EventBridge event bus, used for metadata, cost allocation, and resource access control.

aws_events_rule.tags.key: The user-defined key of a tag attached to the EventBridge rule, used to categorize and manage the rule within AWS.
aws_events_rule.tags.value: The value portion of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the EventBridge rule, used to organize, identify, and control access to the rule.
aws_events_rule.targets.app_sync_parameters: For an EventBridge target that invokes an AWS AppSync GraphQL API, this object specifies AppSync-specific parameters such as the GraphQL operation (mutation) to execute with the event payload.
aws_events_rule.targets.app_sync_parameters.graph_qloper: The GraphQL query or mutation (e.g., mutation { ... }) to execute against the AppSync API when this target is triggered by the event rule.
aws_events_rule.targets.arn: The ARN of the target resource (such as a Lambda function, SNS topic, or other AWS service) that the rule invokes or sends events to.
aws_events_rule.targets.batch_parameters: Specifies the parameters for an AWS Batch job that the event rule invokes as a target, including job definition, job name, array properties, and retry strategy.
aws_events_rule.targets.batch_parameters.array_propertie: This object, nested within an EventBridge rule target's Batch parameters, defines the array size of the AWS Batch job, specifying how many child jobs the array job should launch.
The number of child jobs to run when the Batch job is submitted as an array job, controlling how many parallel attempts are launched.
aws_events_rule.targets.batch_parameters.job_definition: The name or ARN of the AWS Batch job definition to run when the event rule matches an event and targets this Batch job.
aws_events_rule.targets.batch_parameters.job_name: The name of the AWS Batch job to run when this target is invoked by the event rule.
aws_events_rule.targets.batch_parameters.retry_strategy: Defines the retry strategy for the Batch job target, including the number of attempts to retry the job submission.
Determines the number of times a failed AWS Batch job is retried (total attempts including the original), where each retry moves the job to RUNNABLE status and a value of 1 (the default) means no retries.
aws_events_rule.targets.dead_letter_config: Configures a dead-letter queue (specified by its SQS queue ARN) to which EventBridge sends events that fail delivery to this target.
aws_events_rule.targets.dead_letter_config.arn: The ARN of the SQS queue to which EventBridge routes events that fail to be delivered to the target, as part of the target's dead-letter configuration.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters: Specifies the ECS task definition and related settings used when the event target invokes an Amazon ECS task.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.capacity_provider: Defines the capacity provider strategy used for ECS tasks launched by this EventBridge rule target, including a list of capacity providers with their weights and base values.
The base value designates how many tasks, at minimum, to run on the specified capacity provider within the capacity provider strategy for the ECS task launched by this EventBridge rule target.
The name of the capacity provider (e.g., FARGATE or a custom capacity provider) used by the ECS task target's capacity provider strategy to determine the infrastructure on which the task runs.

The relative weight of the capacity provider, used to determine the proportion of tasks that are scheduled on it when multiple capacity providers are specified in the ECS task's capacity provider strategy.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.enable_ecsmanaged: Indicates whether to enable Amazon ECS managed tags on the task launched by the EventBridge target.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.enable_execute_co: Enables ECS Exec for the task's containers, allowing you to run interactive commands inside them.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.group: The ECS task group to assign to the tasks launched by this EventBridge target, which overrides the group in the task definition and can be used for task grouping and filtering.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.launch_type: The launch type (EC2 or FARGATE) that specifies how the ECS task is launched when the event rule triggers the target.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.network_configura: Configures the VPC subnets and security groups used by the ECS task or service that the EventBridge rule target runs.
Defines the VPC subnets, security groups, and public IP assignment for the ECS task or service used as the event target.
Indicates whether the ECS task's elastic network interface should be assigned a public IP address (ENABLED) or not (DISABLED) when the task runs with the awsvpc network mode.
Specifies the security group IDs to attach to the ECS task's elastic network interface when this EventBridge rule target launches an ECS task, under the VPC configuration.
The IDs of the subnets in which the ECS task will run when the EventBridge rule triggers it.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.placement_constra: Specifies the placement constraints for the ECS task invoked by the EventBridge rule, controlling which container instances or availability zones the task may be placed on.
The placement constraint expression to apply to the ECS task launched by this rule, supporting attribute-based queries like `attribute:ecs.instance-type =~ t2.*` or `distinctInstance`.
Specifies the type of ECS placement constraint to apply to the task, with valid values `distinctInstance` or `memberOf`.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.placement_strateg: Specifies the placement strategy for ECS tasks started by this EventBridge target, controlling how tasks are distributed across container instances in the cluster (e.g., spread, binpack, or random).
The field to apply the ECS placement strategy against, such as 'attribute:ecs.availability-zone' or 'instanceId', typically used with the 'spread' placement strategy type.
For an EventBridge rule target that runs an ECS task, this specifies the type of placement strategy (random, spread, or binpack) used to determine how tasks are placed across container instances.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.platform_version: The platform version on which the ECS task runs, such as 'LATEST' or a specific version like '1.4.0'.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.propagate_tags: Specifies whether to propagate the tags from the task definition to the Amazon ECS task; valid values are `TASK_DEFINITION` or `NONE`.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.reference_id: Specifies the optional reference ID string that identifies the ECS task started by this EventBridge rule target.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.tag_list: Specifies a list of tags to apply to the ECS task that is launched by the EventBridge rule target.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.tag_list.key: The key of a tag to apply to the ECS task when the event rule triggers the ECS target.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.tag_list.value: In an ECS target for an EventBridge rule, this field specifies the value of one tag applied to the ECS task launched by that target, pairing with the corresponding key in the tag_list entry.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.task_count: Specifies the number of tasks to create when running the ECS task defined in the task definition.
aws_events_rule.targets.ecs_parameters.task_definition_a: The ARN of the ECS task definition that EventBridge invokes to start the ECS task when the rule fires for this target.
aws_events_rule.targets.http_parameters: Specifies the HTTP parameters (headers, path, and query string) to use when the target is an API destination or webhook.
aws_events_rule.targets.http_parameters.header_parameter: Specifies the HTTP headers to include in the request when the event rule target invokes an API destination or HTTP endpoint.
aws_events_rule.targets.http_parameters.path_parameter_v: Specifies the list of concrete values to substitute for each path parameter placeholder (e.g., {id}) in the HTTP request URL when the rule invokes an API destination target.
aws_events_rule.targets.http_parameters.query_string_par: A map of key-value pairs that are appended to the query string of the HTTP request sent to the target when the rule is invoked, allowing you to pass custom query parameters to an API destination or other HTTP target.
aws_events_rule.targets.id: The Id property of a target provides a unique, user-defined name for that target within the rule, and it is required.
aws_events_rule.targets.input: Specifies the literal text or JSON payload delivered to the target, overriding the original event that triggered the rule.
aws_events_rule.targets.input_path: A JSONPath string that selects a portion of the original event to pass as the input to this target, overriding the full event payload.
aws_events_rule.targets.input_transformer: Defines a custom transformation of the incoming event using a set of JSON path mappings and an input template, so the payload delivered to the target is reshaped from the original event.
aws_events_rule.targets.input_transformer.input_paths_ma: A map of user-defined variable names to JSONPath expressions that extract values from the source event, which are then referenced as variables in the input transformer's template.
aws_events_rule.targets.input_transformer.input_template: Defines the template string that specifies how the event input is transformed before being sent to the target, using JSON paths enclosed in angular brackets (e.g., <$.source>) for dynamic values.
aws_events_rule.targets.kinesis_parameters: Defines the parameters for a Kinesis stream target, most notably the partition key that determines which shard the event is delivered to.
aws_events_rule.targets.kinesis_parameters.partition_key: A JSON path expression within the event payload that EventBridge uses to extract the partition key for the Kinesis record, required when the target is a Kinesis stream.
aws_events_rule.targets.redshift_data_parameters: Specifies the parameters for executing an Amazon Redshift Data API statement as the EventBridge rule target, including the database, SQL command, and optional database user or secret manager credentials.
aws_events_rule.targets.redshift_data_parameters.databas: The name of the Amazon Redshift database that the SQL statement is run against when the CloudWatch Events rule triggers the Redshift Data API target.
aws_events_rule.targets.redshift_data_parameters.db_user: The name of the database user that Amazon Redshift Data API uses to access the cluster when executing the SQL statement for this EventBridge target.
aws_events_rule.targets.redshift_data_parameters.secret_: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Redshift cluster credentials used by the Redshift Data API to execute the target's SQL statement.
aws_events_rule.targets.redshift_data_parameters.sql: Specifies the SQL statement text that Amazon EventBridge passes to the Amazon Redshift Data API for execution when the rule triggers this target.
aws_events_rule.targets.redshift_data_parameters.sqls: A list of SQL statements to be executed against the Amazon Redshift cluster when the event rule triggers the Redshift Data API target.
aws_events_rule.targets.redshift_data_parameters.stateme: The name of the Redshift Data API prepared statement to execute when the event rule triggers the target.
aws_events_rule.targets.redshift_data_parameters.with_ev: Whether to pass the original event as an `:event` parameter to the Redshift Data API statement executed by this EventBridge target.
aws_events_rule.targets.retry_policy: Configures the retry policy for the target, specifying the maximum number of retry attempts and the maximum event age for a failed event invocation.
aws_events_rule.targets.retry_policy.maximum_event_age_i: The maximum time in seconds (1-86400) that EventBridge retains an event for a target after a failed invocation, after which the event is discarded and no further retries are made.
aws_events_rule.targets.retry_policy.maximum_retry_attem: The maximum number of times EventBridge retries invoking the target after a failed invocation, as part of the rule's retry policy.
aws_events_rule.targets.role_arn: The ARN of the IAM role that EventBridge assumes to invoke the target.
aws_events_rule.targets.run_command_parameters: Specifies the parameters for an AWS Systems Manager Run Command that is invoked when the rule's target is an EC2 instance via SSM Run Command.
aws_events_rule.targets.run_command_parameters.run_comma: Specifies the AWS Systems Manager Run Command target instances by defining a key (such as an EC2 tag key or resource group) and a list of values used to select which instances the command runs against.
The EC2 tag key used by Systems Manager Run Command to select which instances the command targets.

The list of string values for a RunCommand target, which, together with its key, define the set of EC2 instances (e.g., by tag or resource group) that receive the Systems Manager Run Command invoked by this EventBridge rule.
aws_events_rule.targets.sage_maker_pipeline_parameters: An object that holds the runtime parameters for a SageMaker Pipeline target, including a list of pipeline parameter name-value pairs to pass to the pipeline execution.
aws_events_rule.targets.sage_maker_pipeline_parameters.p: The list of SageMaker pipeline input parameters (name-value pairs) that are passed to the pipeline execution when EventBridge invokes the SageMaker pipeline target.
The name of a SageMaker pipeline parameter to pass as input when the EventBridge rule target invokes the pipeline.
The value of a SageMaker pipeline parameter (Name/Value pair) supplied to a SageMaker pipeline when the EventBridge rule triggers the pipeline execution.
aws_events_rule.targets.sqs_parameters: Configuration for an SQS queue target, containing FIFO-specific settings such as the message group ID and message deduplication ID.
aws_events_rule.targets.sqs_parameters.message_group_id: Specifies the message group ID for messages sent to a FIFO SQS queue as an EventBridge rule target, which groups messages so that they are processed in order and are not interleaved with messages from other groups.

aws_evidently_experiment.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the experiment, which uniquely identifies it in AWS Evidently.
aws_evidently_experiment.description: Provides an optional, human-readable description of the experiment to convey its purpose or context.
aws_evidently_experiment.metric_goals: Metric goals define the success metrics of the experiment, each specifying the metric to monitor (via a metric name or a CloudWatch metric definition), the desired change direction (increase or decrease), and the entity ID and value extraction keys used to evaluate results from event data.
aws_evidently_experiment.metric_goals.desired_change: Specifies whether the experiment aims to increase or decrease the value of the metric, with allowed values of 'INCREASE' or 'DECREASE'.
aws_evidently_experiment.metric_goals.entity_id_key: The key in the experiment event data that identifies the entity (e.g., user or session) for which the metric goal is evaluated.
aws_evidently_experiment.metric_goals.event_pattern: Defines the CloudWatch Events event pattern (as a JSON string) that selects which events Evidently counts for this metric goal in the experiment.
aws_evidently_experiment.metric_goals.metric_name: The name of the metric that this experiment goal tracks, typically the CloudWatch metric name used to evaluate experiment results.
aws_evidently_experiment.metric_goals.unit_label: The unit label is a human-readable label for the units of measurement associated with the metric goal (e.g., 'requests', 'users', 'conversions'), used for display in the Evidently console and experiment analysis.
aws_evidently_experiment.metric_goals.value_key: The name of the field in the event data that Evidently reads to obtain the numeric value for the experiment's metric goal, which is the value the service measures for the goal.
aws_evidently_experiment.name: The name of the experiment, which must be unique within the project.
aws_evidently_experiment.online_ab_config: The online_ab_config object configures the online A/B experiment, specifying the control treatment name and the percentage of traffic allocated to each treatment variant.
aws_evidently_experiment.online_ab_config.control_treatment_name: The name of the treatment that serves as the control group within the online A/B experiment, against which all other treatment variations are compared and measured.
aws_evidently_experiment.online_ab_config.treatment_weights: Defines the traffic allocation percentages for each treatment in the experiment, where each object maps a treatment name to a weight (0-100) representing the percentage of traffic to send to that treatment in the online AB experiment.
aws_evidently_experiment.online_ab_config.treatment_weights.split: In an online AB experiment, split_weight is the proportion of traffic allocated to this treatment, expressed as an integer weight out of 100000 total (e.g., 10000 means 10%), and the weights across all treatments must sum to 100000.
aws_evidently_experiment.online_ab_config.treatment_weights.treat: The name of the treatment in the experiment that this weight applies to, used to allocate traffic among treatments in the online AB configuration.
aws_evidently_experiment.project: The name or ARN of the Evidently project that contains this experiment.
aws_evidently_experiment.randomization_salt: Sets the randomization salt used by Evidently to hash the entity ID, determining the variation assignment for a given user or entity in the experiment.
aws_evidently_experiment.remove_segment: When set to true during an update, removes the segment currently associated with the Evidently experiment, so the experiment no longer targets that audience segment.
aws_evidently_experiment.running_status: RunningStatus is an object that lets you control the experiment's current lifecycle state, such as setting it to RUNNING to start the experiment or COMPLETED to stop it.
aws_evidently_experiment.sampling_rate: The percentage (0-100) of the audience that is randomly allocated to the experiment, determining the proportion of incoming traffic that is subject to the experiment's treatment variants.
aws_evidently_experiment.segment: The name or ARN of an Evidently segment that restricts the experiment to a defined user audience; if omitted, the experiment runs on the full eligible population.
aws_evidently_experiment.tags.key: The key portion of a key-value tag applied to the Evidently experiment, used for metadata and resource categorization.
aws_evidently_experiment.treatments: Defines the list of treatments (variants) for the experiment, each specifying the feature to vary, a treatment name, and an optional description, which the Evidently service uses to split traffic and evaluate results.
aws_evidently_experiment.treatments.description: A human-readable description of the treatment, explaining its purpose or the variation it represents within the Evidently experiment.
aws_evidently_experiment.treatments.feature: The name of the feature that this treatment applies to, which must reference an existing feature in the Evidently project.
aws_evidently_experiment.treatments.treatment_name: The name of a treatment (variation) in the Evidently experiment, used to identify the treatment among the experiment's variations and when viewing analysis results.
aws_evidently_experiment.treatments.variation: The name of the feature variation that this treatment uses in the experiment.

aws_evidently_feature.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this Evidently feature in AWS.
aws_evidently_feature.default_variation: Specifies the variation used as the default for an Evidently feature when no targeting rules match or no other overrides apply.
aws_evidently_feature.description: An optional description of the Evidently feature, used to convey the feature's purpose or intended behavior to viewers in the console.
aws_evidently_feature.entity_overrides: Specifies a list of entity overrides, where each override assigns a specific variation to a given entity (such as a user or session) for this feature.
aws_evidently_feature.entity_overrides.entity_id: The unique identifier of the user or session for which this entity override sets a specific feature variation.
aws_evidently_feature.entity_overrides.variation: The name of the variation to assign to the overridden entity in an entity override.
aws_evidently_feature.evaluation_strategy: Determines whether the feature is evaluated as a feature flag using allocation rules (ALL_RULES) or as an experiment that exposes the feature to a percentage of users (AFFECTED_USERS).
aws_evidently_feature.name: The name of the feature, which must be unique within the Evidently project and can contain only letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens.
aws_evidently_feature.project: The name or ARN of the Evidently project that this feature belongs to.
aws_evidently_feature.tags.key: The key for a tag attached to the Evidently feature, enabling you to categorize and manage the resource.
aws_evidently_feature.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the Evidently feature, used to assign custom metadata for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control in AWS Evidently.
aws_evidently_feature.variations: Specifies the list of variations for the feature, where each variation defines a name and a value that the feature can serve to users, enabling A/B testing and experimentation.
aws_evidently_feature.variations.boolean_value: In a feature variation, when the variation type is boolean, this field specifies the true/false value that is served for that variation.
aws_evidently_feature.variations.double_value: The numeric double value assigned to this variation of the feature, used when the variation's value type is set to double.
aws_evidently_feature.variations.long_value: Sets the numeric (long) value for this feature variation, which Evidently returns as the variation's value when the feature is evaluated for a user or session.
aws_evidently_feature.variations.string_value: For a variation of the Evidently feature, this defines the string-typed value that is returned when the feature is evaluated and this variation is selected.
aws_evidently_feature.variations.variation_name: The user-defined name for a variation of the Evidently feature, used to reference this variation when defining traffic allocation or feature evaluation rules.

aws_evidently_launch.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Evidently launch within AWS.
aws_evidently_launch.description: Provides an optional human-readable description of the launch to help identify its purpose.
aws_evidently_launch.execution_status: Configures the execution state of an Amazon CloudWatch Evidently launch by specifying a target status (such as RUNNING or CANCELLED) and an optional status reason, which is used when updating the launch resource.
aws_evidently_launch.groups: Specifies the launch groups that define how traffic is allocated to feature variations in this Evidently launch.
aws_evidently_launch.groups.description: A human-readable description of the launch group, specifying the purpose or context of the traffic segment in the Evidently launch.
aws_evidently_launch.groups.feature: The name or ARN of the feature that this launch group uses to serve a variation to the assigned traffic.
aws_evidently_launch.groups.group_name: The name of a group in an AWS Evidently launch, which identifies a feature variation and the percentage of traffic allocated to that group.
aws_evidently_launch.groups.variation: The name of the variation that this launch group is allocated, determining which feature variant is served to users in this group.
