aws_evidently_launch.metric_monitors: This list specifies the CloudWatch metrics that Evidently monitors to evaluate the launch's performance, where each monitor defines the metric name, entity ID key, value key, event pattern, and unit label used to measure the launch's success.
aws_evidently_launch.metric_monitors.entity_id_key: For an AWS Evidently launch metric monitor, this specifies the event attribute name (e.g., `userId`) that identifies the entity the metric is measured for.
aws_evidently_launch.metric_monitors.event_pattern: The CloudWatch Events event pattern, specified as a JSON string, that defines which application events are counted for this metric monitor in an Evidently launch, used to extract metric values.
aws_evidently_launch.metric_monitors.metric_name: The metric_name field is the human-readable name of a metric that the Evidently launch monitors, used by Evidently to identify the metric in console views and when reporting metric values.
aws_evidently_launch.metric_monitors.unit_label: The human-readable label that describes the unit of measurement for the metric being monitored by this metric monitor (for example, 'requests' or 'errors').
aws_evidently_launch.metric_monitors.value_key: The JSON path or key in the event payload that holds the numeric value used to evaluate the metric for the AWS Evidently launch's metric monitor.
aws_evidently_launch.name: The name of the Evidently launch.
aws_evidently_launch.project: The name or ARN of the Evidently project in which this launch is created.
aws_evidently_launch.randomization_salt: A string hashing salt that Evidently uses to compute deterministic assignment of evaluation units to variations, allowing you to change the randomization behavior of the launch.
aws_evidently_launch.scheduled_splits_config: A list of scheduled split configurations that define how traffic is allocated to each feature variation at specified start times, enabling a gradual time-based rollout for the launch.
aws_evidently_launch.scheduled_splits_config.group_weights: The group_weights list assigns a traffic weight to each launch group (variation) for the scheduled split, determining what percentage of user traffic that variation receives during that time segment.
aws_evidently_launch.scheduled_splits_config.group_weights.gr: The name of the feature variation (group) to which the corresponding weight is assigned in this scheduled traffic split for the AWS Evidently launch.
aws_evidently_launch.scheduled_splits_config.group_weights.sp: Sets the proportion of traffic allocated to the corresponding variation group for a scheduled split in the Amazon CloudWatch Evidently launch.
aws_evidently_launch.scheduled_splits_config.segment_override: Configures traffic-split overrides for specific audience segments during a scheduled split, letting you direct different proportions of a segment's users to the launch's variations.
The order in which this segment override is evaluated relative to other segment overrides in the same scheduled split, with lower numbers evaluated first.
Specifies the name or ARN of the Evidently segment to which the override applies, enabling different traffic allocation or variation choices for users matching that segment during the launch step.
Specifies the traffic percentage allocated to each feature variation for a given audience segment override in a scheduled split of the Evidently launch.
In a segment override for a scheduled split, this value is the name of an existing launch group whose traffic allocation is being overridden by the associated split weight for that segment.
Sets the percentage of traffic from the segment that is allocated to a feature variation, where the collection of weights across variations determines the split for that segment override.
aws_evidently_launch.scheduled_splits_config.start_time: The UTC timestamp that marks the start of this step in a scheduled split launch, after which the specified group weights apply.
aws_evidently_launch.tags.key: Represents a tag key assigned to the Evidently launch, allowing you to categorize and manage this launch resource with custom metadata.
aws_evidently_launch.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the Evidently launch, used to organize and identify the launch resource.

aws_evidently_project.app_config_resource: Specifies the AWS AppConfig application and configuration profile to associate with this Evidently project, enabling the project to use AppConfig as the source for feature flag variations.
aws_evidently_project.app_config_resource.application_id: The application_id specifies the AWS AppConfig application ID that this Evidently project uses to store and manage its feature flag configuration.
aws_evidently_project.app_config_resource.environment_id: The ID of the AWS AppConfig environment that hosts the configuration used by this Evidently project for feature flag evaluation.
aws_evidently_project.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Evidently project, which uniquely identifies the project in AWS.
aws_evidently_project.data_delivery.log_group: The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where Evidently delivers the project's data, such as evaluation events, for analysis and monitoring.
aws_evidently_project.data_delivery.s3: Configures the S3 bucket and optional prefix where Evidently delivers project data such as events and evaluation results.
aws_evidently_project.data_delivery.s3.bucket_name: The name of the S3 bucket to which Evidently delivers experiment and feature-evaluation data for this project.
aws_evidently_project.data_delivery.s3.prefix: Specifies the S3 key prefix under which AWS Evidently will store evaluation event data for this project when data delivery is configured to an S3 bucket.
aws_evidently_project.description: An optional free-form text field that provides a description for the Evidently project.
aws_evidently_project.name: The name to assign to the Evidently project, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region.
aws_evidently_project.tags.key: The key component of a tag attached to the Amazon Evidently project, allowing you to categorize and filter the project by user-defined labels.
aws_evidently_project.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the Evidently project, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_evidently_segment.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Evidently segment.
aws_evidently_segment.description: A user-supplied text description of the segment, used to clarify its purpose or contents.
aws_evidently_segment.name: The user-defined name of the audience segment, used to identify it within Evidently experiments and launches.
aws_evidently_segment.pattern: The JSON pattern that defines the conditions under which a user matches this segment, used to target audiences for Evidently experiments and launches.
aws_evidently_segment.tags.value: The value of a tag applied to the Evidently segment, used for metadata, resource organization, and cost allocation.

aws_evs_environment.connectivity_info.private_route_server_p: Specifies the private route server peerings that the EVS environment uses to establish private network connectivity to your VPC.
aws_evs_environment.created_at: This read-only string contains the ISO 8601 timestamp of when the EVS environment was created.
aws_evs_environment.environment_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this EVS environment, assigned by AWS when the environment is created.
aws_evs_environment.environment_state: The read-only `environment_state` field reports the current lifecycle status of the AWS Elemental Video System (EVS) environment as tracked by the `AWS::Evs::Environment` resource.
aws_evs_environment.hosts.instance_type: The EC2 instance type of a host in an AWS Elastic Video System (EVS) environment, which determines the compute and memory capacity available for video processing workloads.
aws_evs_environment.hosts.key_name: The name of the EC2 key pair used for SSH access to the host nodes in the EVS environment.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.expansion_vlan2.cidr: The IPv4 CIDR block assigned to the second expansion VLAN (expansion_vlan2) within the initial VLAN configuration of the AWS EVS environment, defining the subnet range for devices on that VLAN.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.hcx_network_acl_id: The ID of the Amazon EC2 network ACL that controls HCX (Hybrid Cloud Extension) traffic on this initial VLAN in the EVS environment.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.is_hcx_public: Indicates whether the initial VLAN is marked as public for VMware HCX, enabling its use for hybrid cloud network extension.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.vm_management: The vm_management object under initial_vlans specifies the VLAN configuration used for managing virtual machines within the AWS EVS environment.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.vm_management.cidr: The IPv4 CIDR block defining the address range for the virtual machine management network within this initial VLAN configuration.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.vmk_management: Configures the VMkernel management interface for the specified initial VLAN, providing networking details for management traffic within the AWS EVS environment.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.vmk_management.cidr: The CIDR block for the VMware management network (vmk_management), defining the IP range used for management traffic in the EVS environment.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.vmotion: Specifies the VLAN configuration used for VMware vMotion traffic in the initial VLAN setup for the environment.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.vmotion.cidr: The CIDR block of the initial vMotion VLAN in the AWS EVS environment, defining the network range for live migration traffic.
aws_evs_environment.initial_vlans.vsan.cidr: The IPv4 CIDR block for the VSAN network within one of the environment's initial VLANs.
aws_evs_environment.state_details: A read-only string that provides supplementary details about the current state of the AWS EVS environment, including error messages if the environment is not in a healthy state.
aws_evs_environment.vcf_hostnames.cloud_builder: The hostname of the Cloud Builder virtual appliance in the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) environment, which is used to deploy and manage the software-defined data center (SDDC) infrastructure.
aws_evs_environment.vcf_hostnames.nsx_manager1: Specifies the fully-qualified domain name (FQDN) for the second NSX Manager node (index 1) in the VMware Cloud Foundation environment's hostname configuration block.
aws_evs_environment.vcf_hostnames.nsx_manager2: The fully qualified hostname of the second NSX Manager node in the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) environment, required by the EVS environment to connect to your VCF management cluster.
aws_evs_environment.vcf_hostnames.nsx_manager3: The hostname to assign to the third NSX Manager node within the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) environment managed by this AWS Elastic VMware Service (EVS) environment.
aws_evs_environment.vcf_hostnames.sddc_manager: The hostname of the SDDC Manager node in the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) environment that this AWS EVS environment is associated with.
aws_evs_environment.vcf_hostnames.vcenter: The hostname or IP address of the vCenter server in the VMware Cloud Foundation environment represented by this resource.

aws_fin_space_environment.federation_parameters.attribute_map.key: This key is an attribute name within the AttributeMap of FederationParameters, which defines custom SAML attributes to be made available during federated sign-in to the FinSpace environment.
aws_fin_space_environment.federation_parameters.attribute_map.valu: Defines the FinSpace user attribute name that the corresponding SAML attribute (key) is mapped to in the federated authentication configuration of the FinSpace environment.
aws_fin_space_environment.tags.value: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to an AWS FinSpace environment, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_fis_experiment_template.experiment_options: Specifies experiment-wide options for the template, such as account targeting (single vs. multi-account) and the empty target resolution mode (fail or skip).
aws_fis_experiment_template.experiment_report_configuration: Configures the delivery of the experiment report for the FIS experiment template, specifying the S3 destination bucket and prefix as well as the report format and schema version for the generated experiment results.
aws_fis_experiment_template.experiment_report_configuration.data_sou: Specifies the CloudWatch dashboards that are included as data sources in the experiment report generated by this FIS experiment template.
Specifies the CloudWatch dashboards to include as data sources in the experiment report generated by the FIS experiment template.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudWatch dashboard to include as a data source in the experiment report.
aws_fis_experiment_template.experiment_report_configuration.outputs: Specifies the output destinations for the experiment report, such as an S3 bucket or a CloudWatch Logs log group, where the FIS experiment report is delivered.
Configures the S3 bucket and optional key prefix where the executed experiment's report output files are delivered.
The name of the S3 bucket to which AWS FIS delivers the experiment report output file.
The key prefix used to store the experiment report output files within the specified S3 bucket.
aws_fis_experiment_template.experiment_report_configuration.post_exp: The duration of time after the experiment ends during which data is collected and included in the experiment report, capturing post-experiment metrics such as recovery or rollback effects.
aws_fis_experiment_template.experiment_report_configuration.pre_expe: The length of time before the experiment's start that is captured in the experiment report, specified as an ISO 8601 duration (for example, PT10M).
aws_fis_experiment_template.log_configuration: Specifies where to deliver experiment logs, including the destination CloudWatch Logs group and/or S3 bucket for storing the FIS experiment's activity and results.
aws_fis_experiment_template.log_configuration.cloud_watch_logs_confi: Specifies the CloudWatch Logs destination for FIS experiment logs, including the ARN of the log group where logs are delivered.
The ARN of the Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group where the experiment template sends its logs.
aws_fis_experiment_template.log_configuration.log_schema_version: Specifies the schema version for the FIS experiment logs, which currently supports only version 1.
aws_fis_experiment_template.log_configuration.s3_configuration: Configures the Amazon S3 destination (bucket and optional prefix) where AWS FIS stores the logs of experiment executions.
aws_fis_experiment_template.log_configuration.s3_configuration.bucke: The name of the S3 bucket that AWS FIS uses to store experiment report and execution logs.
aws_fis_experiment_template.log_configuration.s3_configuration.prefi: Specifies the prefix to prepend to the log file names when experiment logs are delivered to the configured S3 bucket.
aws_fis_experiment_template.stop_conditions.source: The service source type for the stop condition, such as 'aws:cloudwatch:alarm', which defines the CloudWatch alarm that stops the experiment when it enters the ALARM state.
aws_fis_experiment_template.stop_conditions.value: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudWatch alarm that, when in alarm state, stops the experiment.
aws_fis_experiment_template.tags: Specifies a map of key-value pairs to tag the AWS FIS experiment template, enabling you to organize, identify, and control access to the template using resource tags.

aws_flow_log.destination_options: Specifies the destination options for the flow log, such as the file format (plain-text or parquet), whether to enable Hive-compatible partitions, and whether to partition logs by hour, when delivering to an Amazon S3 bucket.
aws_flow_log.destination_options.file_format: Specifies the file format (plain-text or parquet) used to store VPC flow log records in the destination S3 bucket.
aws_flow_log.destination_options.hive_compatible_part: Whether to enable Hive-compatible partitioning (e.g., year=2023/month=01/day=01/hour=00) for the S3 destination of the flow log, instead of the default partition format (e.g., 2023/01/01/00).
aws_flow_log.destination_options.per_hour_partition: Indicates whether to partition flow log records in the S3 destination into separate hourly folders, creating a new partition for each hour.
aws_flow_log.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the VPC flow log, used to organize and identify the log resource.
aws_flow_log.tags.value: The value component of a key-value tag applied to the AWS Flow Log, used for resource identification and management.

aws_fms_policy.delete_all_policy_resources: Indicates whether AWS Firewall Manager deletes all resources managed by this policy (such as AWS WAF rule groups or Shield protections) when the policy itself is deleted.
aws_fms_policy.exclude_map.account: The list of AWS account IDs to exclude from the Firewall Manager policy's scope.
aws_fms_policy.exclude_map.orgunit: The list of AWS Organizations organizational unit (OU) IDs to exclude from this Firewall Manager policy's scope.
aws_fms_policy.exclude_resource_tags: When true, the policy applies only to resources that do not have the tags specified in the associated 'resource_tags' list, thereby excluding tagged resources from the policy's scope; when false, it applies to resources that have those tags.
aws_fms_policy.id: The unique identifier (policy ID) assigned by AWS Firewall Manager to this policy.
aws_fms_policy.include_map.account: The list of AWS account IDs to include in the policy's scope, defining which accounts the Firewall Manager policy applies to.
aws_fms_policy.include_map.orgunit: Specifies the AWS Organizations organizational unit IDs to include in the scope of the AWS Firewall Manager policy.
aws_fms_policy.policy_description: A description of the AWS Firewall Manager policy, used to identify the policy's purpose or scope.
aws_fms_policy.policy_name: The friendly name of the Firewall Manager policy, used to identify it in the AWS console and API operations.
aws_fms_policy.remediation_enabled: Indicates whether Firewall Manager automatically applies the policy's rules to noncompliant resources to remediate them.
aws_fms_policy.resource_set_ids: The list of IDs of the resource sets to which this AWS Firewall Manager policy applies.
aws_fms_policy.resource_tag_logical_operator: Specifies the logical operator (AND or OR) used to combine multiple resource tag conditions in the AWS Firewall Manager policy when determining which resources are included or excluded.
aws_fms_policy.resource_tags: This list of tags identifies the AWS resources to which the Firewall Manager policy applies, allowing the policy to target resources based on their associated tags.
aws_fms_policy.resource_tags.key: The key of a tag used to match resources that this AWS Firewall Manager policy applies to, based on the resource's tags.
aws_fms_policy.resource_tags.value: The tag value, paired with the corresponding key, that Firewall Manager uses to match resources for inclusion in (or exclusion from, depending on the policy's ExcludeResourceTags setting) the policy's scope.
aws_fms_policy.resource_type_list: Specifies the list of AWS resource types (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance, AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer) to which this Firewall Manager policy applies, filtering the resources evaluated and protected by the policy.
aws_fms_policy.security_service_policy_data.policy_opti: The IPv4 CIDR block (e.g., '10.0.0.0/16') that defines the source or destination network to which this network ACL entry applies, used for matching traffic in the Firewall Manager network ACL policy.
Indicates whether this network ACL entry applies to outbound (egress) traffic (true) rather than inbound (ingress) traffic (false).
Defines the ICMP type and code numbers that the Network ACL entry uses to match ICMP traffic, limiting the rule to specific ICMP message types.
The numeric ICMP code value used to match specific ICMP messages in the first network ACL entry set of the common Network ACL policy, where -1 matches all ICMP codes for the given type.
The ICMP type number (e.g., 8 for echo request, 3 for destination unreachable) that the network ACL entry matches for ICMP traffic.
The IPv6 CIDR block that this network ACL entry in the first set of entries applies to for the common network ACL policy.
Defines the inclusive range of destination ports (From and To) that this Firewall Manager network ACL entry uses to match traffic for its associated rule action.
The inclusive lower bound of the port range that this network ACL entry applies to, used by Firewall Manager to define the starting port for allowing or denying traffic in a Network ACL policy.
The upper bound (inclusive) of the port range for this network ACL entry, defining the last port in the range allowed or denied by the entry.
Specifies the IP protocol (e.g., tcp, udp, icmp, or a protocol number) for the network ACL entry in the Firewall Manager policy.
Specifies the action of the network ACL entry, either 'allow' to permit matching traffic or 'deny' to block it.
When set to true, Firewall Manager automatically remediates the first entries in the target network ACL to match the policy's specified first entry, replacing non-compliant entries.
Indicates whether AWS Firewall Manager will automatically remediate the last entries of the network ACL to match the policy-defined entries, such as the default deny-all rule.

Specifies the IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR range that this network ACL entry in the 'last entries' set matches as the source or destination address, used by AWS Firewall Manager to enforce the network ACL policy across accounts.
Specifies whether this network ACL entry applies to egress traffic (true) or ingress traffic (false) in the last set of entries for the Firewall Manager policy's common network ACL configuration.
Defines the ICMP type and code numbers that the network ACL entry applies to, used when the entry's protocol is set to ICMP or ICMPv6.
The ICMP code value that, together with the ICMP type, identifies the specific ICMP message type that the network ACL entry evaluates.
The ICMP type number (e.g., 8 for echo request) that, together with the code, defines the ICMP protocol variant matched by this network ACL entry in the Firewall Manager policy.
Specifies the IPv6 CIDR block that the network ACL entry matches for traffic, within the set of entries that are evaluated last (at the end of the ACL) in the Network ACL common policy.
Defines the inclusive range of transport-layer ports (From and To) that the network ACL entry in the last-entries set uses to match traffic.
The inclusive lower bound (starting port number) of the port range for this network ACL entry, defining where the allowed or denied traffic port range begins.
The upper (inclusive) bound of the destination port range for this network ACL entry in the FMS policy's common network ACL configuration.
Specifies the IP protocol (e.g., tcp, udp, icmp, or -1 for all protocols) for the network ACL entry in the last entries set of the Firewall Manager network ACL common policy.
Specifies whether the network ACL entry allows or denies matching traffic, with valid values `allow` and `deny`.
aws_fms_policy.tags: The tags to assign to the Firewall Manager policy, which are key-value pairs that help you identify, organize, and manage the policy, and can be used for cost allocation and access control.
aws_fms_policy.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Firewall Manager policy, used to organize, identify, and manage the policy within AWS.
aws_fms_policy.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS Firewall Manager policy, used for identifying or categorizing the policy.

aws_fms_resource_set.description: An optional, user-defined text field that describes the purpose or contents of the AWS Firewall Manager resource set, aiding in identification and management.
aws_fms_resource_set.name: The name of the Firewall Manager resource set, which must be unique within the account and is used to identify the resource set in AWS Firewall Manager.
aws_fms_resource_set.resource_type_list: Specifies the list of AWS resource types (such as AWS::S3::Bucket or AWS::EC2::Instance) that are included in the resource set, which Firewall Manager uses to identify the resources to apply policies to.
aws_fms_resource_set.resources: Specifies the list of resource identifiers (such as ARNs) that make up this Firewall Manager resource set, which can then be associated with a Firewall Manager policy.
aws_fms_resource_set.tags: The list of key-value tag objects to attach to the AWS FMS resource set, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource set in AWS Firewall Manager.
aws_fms_resource_set.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to an AWS Firewall Manager resource set, used for organizing, identifying, and filtering the resource set in AWS.
aws_fms_resource_set.tags.value: The value of a tag associated with this AWS Firewall Manager resource set, enabling cost allocation and resource metadata management.

aws_forecast_dataset.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the forecast dataset.
aws_forecast_dataset.encryption_config: If set, this object defines the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the dataset, specified via its KmsKeyArn subfield, enabling server-side encryption of the forecast data.
aws_forecast_dataset.schema: Defines the dataset schema by specifying the list of attributes (each with a name and data type) that determine the columns of the dataset.
aws_forecast_dataset.schema.attributes: Defines the fields of the dataset, where each attribute specifies a name and a data type (such as string, integer, float, or timestamp) for a column in the dataset.
aws_forecast_dataset.schema.attributes.attribute_name: The name of an attribute (column) in the dataset schema, which must match the field name in the source data (e.g., the column header in CSV input).
aws_forecast_dataset.schema.attributes.attribute_type: Specifies the data type of the attribute (column) in the dataset schema, which must be one of string, integer, float, or timestamp, determining how the data is interpreted for forecast training.
aws_forecast_dataset.tags: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the Forecast dataset for cost allocation and resource management.
aws_forecast_dataset.tags.key: The user-defined key of a tag applied to the Amazon Forecast dataset, used to categorize and manage the resource.
aws_forecast_dataset.tags.value: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Forecast dataset, used for metadata, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_forecast_dataset_group.tags.value: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon Forecast dataset group, used to organize, categorize, or identify the resource (e.g., by project or environment).

aws_fraud_detector_detector.associated_models.arn: ARN of the Amazon Fraud Detector model associated with this detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type: The event type configuration for the detector, which defines the event variables, entity types, and labels used to evaluate fraud events.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types: Defines the entity types associated with the event type, which identify the people or things involved in the event (e.g., customer, merchant) for Amazon Fraud Detector analysis.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies an entity type (e.g., customer, merchant) defined in the event type for the detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.created_time: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) set by AWS Fraud Detector when the entity type was created, returned as a computed attribute of the event type's entity types.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.description: Provides a human-readable description of the entity type (e.g., customer, merchant) that is used within the event type in Amazon Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.inline: Indicates whether the entity type is defined inline within the event type resource (true) or references an existing Amazon Fraud Detector entity type (false).
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.last_updated_tim: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when this entity type within the event type was last updated by the AWS Fraud Detector service.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.name: The name of an entity type (e.g., 'customer' or 'merchant') associated with the event type, used to categorize entities in fraud detection models.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.tags: The resource tags (key-value pairs) to attach to this entity type within the detector's event type, used for managing and categorizing the AWS Fraud Detector entity-type resource.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.tags.key: The tag key (e.g., 'environment') attached to an entity type within the detector's event type, used for resource management and identification.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.entity_types.tags.value: The value of a key-value tag attached to an entity type, enabling categorization and management of that entity type within the AWS Fraud Detector detector's event type.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables: Defines the list of event variables (name, type, and default value) that make up the event type's structure and are used by the detector to process incoming events for fraud prediction.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this event variable, automatically assigned by AWS Fraud Detector upon creation.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.created_time: The timestamp in ISO 8601 format indicating when the event variable was created in Amazon Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.data_source: Specifies whether the event variable's value is sourced from the event data ('EVENT') or from a model's output score ('MODEL_SCORE') in the Amazon Fraud Detector detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.data_type: Defines the data type of the event variable (e.g., STRING, INTEGER, FLOAT, BOOLEAN) used to capture event data for fraud detection analysis.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.default_value: The default value assigned to this event variable when it is not provided in the event data, used for model training and fraud prediction.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.description: A description of the event variable, providing context about what data it represents within the detector's event type.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.inline: Specifies whether the event variable is defined inline as part of this detector (true) or references an existing event variable in Amazon Fraud Detector (false).
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.last_updated_: The timestamp, in ISO 8601 format, indicating when this event variable was last updated, automatically maintained by AWS Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.name: The name of an event variable that identifies the input field associated with the detector's event type, used in model training and rules.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.tags: Tags (key-value pairs) applied to this specific event variable for filtering, cost allocation, and access management within AWS Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to an event variable in the event type of the AWS Fraud Detector detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.tags.value: Specifies the value for a tag key-value pair attached to an event variable in the detector's event type.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.event_variables.variable_type: Sets the variable type (e.g., EMAIL_ADDRESS, IP_ADDRESS) for an event variable in the event type, defining the semantic category of the data used by the detector's fraud model.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.inline: Indicates whether the event type is defined inline within the detector resource (created during detector creation) rather than referencing an already existing event type.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels: The labels list defines the possible outcome categories (such as 'fraud' and 'legitimate') that the detector's event type can assign to events for model training and risk classification.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the label within Amazon Fraud Detector, used for referencing the label in detector event type configurations and outcomes.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.created_time: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) when this label was created within the AWS Fraud Detector event type.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.description: The description of the label, providing contextual information about what the label represents in the event type.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.inline: For each label in the detector's event type, a boolean flag indicating whether the label is defined inline within the detector (true) or references an existing label by ARN (false).
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.last_updated_time: For each label defined in the detector's event type, this attribute provides the timestamp (as a string) of when that label was last updated.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.name: The unique name of a label that categorizes events as fraudulent or legitimate within the detector's event type.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.tags: Specifies the list of AWS resource tags (key-value pairs) to attach to this label within the fraud detector's event type, enabling resource-level tracking and management.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.tags.key: The tag key for a tag attached to a label within the event type of an AWS Fraud Detector detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.labels.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to a label within the event type of an AWS Fraud Detector detector, used to provide arbitrary metadata for that label.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.tags.key: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the detector's event type, used to identify, filter, and manage the event type resource in AWS Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.event_type.tags.value: The value of the tag associated with the event type in the Amazon Fraud Detector detector, used to attach metadata for management and organization.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rule_execution_mode: Controls how the detector's rules are evaluated during fraud detection, accepting either ALL_MATCHED (evaluate all rules) or FIRST_MATCHED (stop after the first matching rule).
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules: The list of rules associated with the detector, providing the fully resolved rule configurations (including rule ID, expression, language, and outcomes) as returned by the AWS Fraud Detector service.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.arn: The ARN of the Amazon Fraud Detector rule associated with this detector, used to identify and link the rule to the detector's version.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.created_time: The creation timestamp of the rule, formatted as an ISO 8601 string, which is set by AWS when the rule is created.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.description: The description of a rule in the AWS Fraud Detector detector, a free-form string that explains the rule's purpose or logic for operational clarity.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.detector_id: The ID of the detector to which this rule belongs, which for rules defined within a detector resource is the same as the containing detector's ID.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.expression: The logical expression written in the Fraud Detector rule language that is evaluated against event variables to determine whether the rule is satisfied and triggers its associated outcomes.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.language: The language used for the rule's expression, with the only supported value being DETECTORPY.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.last_updated_time: The timestamp, in ISO 8601 format, indicating when the rule was last updated.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes: Defines the list of outcomes (decision labels such as 'fraud' or 'legitimate') that are associated with a fraud detection rule and are emitted when the rule's conditions match.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the outcome assigned to a rule in the detector, uniquely identifying that outcome resource in AWS Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.created_time: The timestamp for when this outcome was created in AWS Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.description: Provides a human-readable description of an outcome that a rule can produce, clarifying the business meaning or purpose of that outcome within the detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.inline: Indicates whether the outcome is defined inline within the detector resource (true) or references an existing outcome (false).
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.last_updated_time: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the outcome configuration associated with this rule was last updated.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.name: In an AWS Fraud Detector detector, this specifies the name of an outcome associated with a rule, which defines the decision label (e.g., 'approve' or 'decline') returned when the rule's conditions are met.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.tags: The list of tags (key-value pairs) assigned to a rule outcome in an Amazon Fraud Detector detector, used for categorizing and managing the outcome resource.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.tags.key: The tag key for a tag attached to an outcome of a rule in an AWS Fraud Detector detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.outcomes.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to an outcome defined within a rule of the AWS Fraud Detector detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.rule_id: The unique identifier for a rule within the detector's rule set, used to reference and manage the rule's configuration in Amazon Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.rule_version: The version identifier of the rule, which distinguishes this rule's iteration from other versions of the same rule ID within the detector.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.tags: A list of key-value tags assigned to this rule in the AWS Fraud Detector detector, used for identifying, managing, and organizing the rule.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.rules.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to a rule in an AWS Fraud Detector detector, enabling custom metadata for rule identification and management.
aws_fraud_detector_detector.tags.value: The value half of a key-value tag assigned to the Amazon Fraud Detector detector resource, allowing users to attach custom metadata to the detector.

aws_fraud_detector_entity_type.tags.value: Specifies the value portion of a tag attached to the AWS Fraud Detector entity type resource, enabling you to associate metadata for cost allocation, access control, or resource identification.

aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types: This computed field lists the entity types associated with the event type, each defining a named entity (such as a customer or transaction) with an optional description that Amazon Fraud Detector evaluates for fraudulent activity.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.arn: The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an entity type defined within the event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.created_time: The creation timestamp of the entity type within the AWS Fraud Detector event type, returned as a read-only ISO 8601 formatted string.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.description: The description of an entity type (a category of participants in the event, such as a customer or account) that is associated with the AWS Fraud Detector event type, providing additional context about that entity type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.inline: When true, the entity type definition is provided inline within the event type resource rather than referencing an existing entity type by ARN or name.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.last_updated_time: The timestamp, in ISO 8601 format, indicating when this entity type was last updated within the AWS Fraud Detector event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.name: Specifies the name of an entity type (e.g., 'customer', 'account') that is associated with this event type in Amazon Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.tags: A list of key-value tags to assign to this entity type within the event type, enabling resource management and cost tracking.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to an entity type defined within this event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.entity_types.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to an entity type in the AWS Fraud Detector event type, used for categorizing and managing the entity type resource.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables: The list of event variables that define the individual data elements of an event (such as IP address, email, transaction amount, or card number), each specifying its data source, data type, default value, and variable type for Amazon Fraud Detector to use in fraud analysis.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.arn: The ARN of the event variable, which uniquely identifies it in Amazon Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.created_time: The timestamp indicating when this event variable was created in Amazon Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.data_source: The data source of the event variable, indicating whether its value is derived from the event data ('EVENT') or from a model score ('MODEL_SCORE').
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.data_type: Specifies the data type (STRING, INTEGER, FLOAT, or BOOLEAN) for an event variable, determining how the variable value is interpreted in fraud detection event evaluations.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.default_value: The default value for the event variable, used when no value is supplied for the variable in an event.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.description: Specifies a human-readable description for the event variable, clarifying its purpose and usage in the fraud detector event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.inline: Specifies whether the event variable is defined inline in the event type, as opposed to referencing an existing variable from the AWS Fraud Detector variable library.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.last_updated_time: The timestamp, in ISO 8601 format, indicating when this event variable was last updated.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.name: The unique name of an event variable associated with the event type, used to identify the variable in fraud detection rules and model training.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.tags: Specifies the list of AWS tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the event variable, used to organize, manage, and identify the variable within the AWS Fraud Detector event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to an event variable, used to assign metadata for organizing and managing the variable within an AWS Fraud Detector event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to an event variable, paired with its tag key, used to categorize or manage the variable within AWS Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.event_variables.variable_type: Specifies the semantic category or type of the event variable (such as CARD_BIN, EMAIL_ADDRESS, or IP_ADDRESS) so that AWS Fraud Detector can apply the appropriate domain-specific interpretation when evaluating fraud risk.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels: The list of labels that define the possible classifications for events of this fraud detector event type, where each label object includes its name and other metadata, reflecting the labels currently associated with the event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this label within the AWS Fraud Detector event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.created_time: The creation timestamp of the label, returned by the AWS Fraud Detector API as a string (read-only).
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.description: Provides a human-readable description of the label, explaining its meaning or intended use within the event type in Amazon Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.inline: Indicates whether the label is defined inline within the event type (true) or references an existing label by ARN (false).
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.last_updated_time: The timestamp (as a string) of when the label was most recently updated, indicating the last modification time of the label within the event type.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.name: The name of a label (e.g., 'fraud' or 'legitimate') that Amazon Fraud Detector can assign to events of this event type as a possible classification outcome.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.tags: The list of AWS resource tags (key-value pairs) assigned to a specific label in the event type, enabling categorization and management of that label within AWS Fraud Detector.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag assigned to a label within the AWS Fraud Detector event type, used for categorizing the label for resource management and access control.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.labels.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to a label within the event type, used to store metadata alongside the tag key.
aws_fraud_detector_event_type.tags.value: The value portion of a tag attached to the AWS Fraud Detector event type, enabling users to assign custom metadata for resource identification and management.

aws_fraud_detector_label.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to an AWS Fraud Detector label, used for resource organization, filtering, and cost allocation.
aws_fraud_detector_label.tags.value: The value component of a tag attached to an AWS Fraud Detector label, used to store arbitrary metadata for identifying and organizing the label resource.

aws_fraud_detector_outcome.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS Fraud Detector outcome, used to organize and identify the outcome resource.

aws_fraud_detector_variable.tags.key: The tag key for the AWS Fraud Detector variable, used to assign custom metadata for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.
aws_fraud_detector_variable.tags.value: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS Fraud Detector variable, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_fsx_data_repository_association.s3.auto_export_policy.events: Specifies the file system event types (NEW, CHANGED, DELETED) that trigger automatic export of file data from the FSx for Lustre file system to the linked S3 bucket.
aws_fsx_data_repository_association.s3.auto_import_policy.events: Determines which S3 event types (NEW, CHANGED, DELETED) trigger automatic import of object changes from the linked S3 bucket into the FSx file system.
aws_fsx_data_repository_association.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon FSx data repository association, used to identify and categorize the resource.
aws_fsx_data_repository_association.tags.value: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the FSx data repository association, used to assign custom metadata for organizational and identification purposes.

aws_fsx_file_system.backup_id: The ID of an existing FSx backup to use when creating this file system, which restores the file system from that backup instead of creating a new empty one.
aws_fsx_file_system.dnsname: The DNS name assigned to the Amazon FSx file system, used to mount the file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.file_system_type: Specifies the type of Amazon FSx file system to create, such as LUSTRE, WINDOWS, ONTAP, or OPENZFS, determining the underlying storage and feature set.
aws_fsx_file_system.file_system_type_version: Specifies the version of the file system type to use, such as the Lustre version (e.g., 2.10, 2.12) or Windows Server version (e.g., 2012_R2, 2016), for the FSx file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.id: The unique identifier of the Amazon FSx file system, such as fs-0123456789abcdef0.
aws_fsx_file_system.kms_key_id: The ID or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the file system's data at rest, overriding the default service key when specified.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration: The Lustre configuration for an FSx for Lustre file system, specifying deployment type, data repository import/export paths, and other Lustre-specific settings.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.auto_import_policy: Specifies how changes to files in the linked S3 bucket are automatically imported into the Lustre file system, with valid values NONE, NEW, and NEW_CHANGED (default is NONE).
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.automatic_backup_re: Specifies the number of days to retain automatic backups for the FSx for Lustre file system, where a value of 0 disables automatic backups.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.copy_tags_to_backup: Indicates whether tags on the FSx Lustre file system are copied to its automatic and manual backups; defaults to false.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.daily_automatic_bac: The time of day (in UTC, 24-hour HH:MM format) when FSx for Lustre automatically creates a daily backup of the file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.data_compression_ty: Specifies the data compression type for the Amazon FSx for Lustre file system, either LZ4 to enable compression or NONE to disable it.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.data_read_cache_con: This nested object configures the data read cache for the FSx for Lustre file system, specifying the cache size (and optionally its type) used to accelerate read requests by caching frequently accessed data on faster storage.
Specifies the size in GiB of the data read cache for the FSx for Lustre file system, which caches frequently accessed data to improve read latency.

Specifies the sizing mode (AUTOMATIC or USER_PROVISIONED) for the data read cache on an FSx for Lustre file system that uses HDD storage, controlling whether the cache size is automatically managed or manually set via the Size field.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.deployment_type: Determines the Lustre file system's deployment type (e.g., SCRATCH_1, SCRATCH_2, PERSISTENT_1, or PERSISTENT_2), which influences performance, data durability, and cost.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.drive_cache_type: Determines whether the Lustre file system uses an SSD drive cache for read operations, with valid values 'READ' or 'NONE'.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.efa_enabled: Specifies whether to enable Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for the Amazon FSx for Lustre file system, providing low-latency and high-bandwidth networking for HPC workloads.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.export_path: Specifies the Amazon S3 directory (bucket and optional prefix) to which files are exported from the FSx for Lustre file system when linked to a data repository.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.import_path: Specifies the Amazon S3 path (starting with s3://) from which data is imported into the Lustre file system, such as an S3 bucket or bucket prefix used as the data repository.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.imported_file_chunk: Specifies the size in bytes of the chunks that the FSx for Lustre file system uses when importing files from its linked S3 data repository.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.metadata_configurat: Configures the metadata storage for the FSx for Lustre file system, allowing either automatic (AWS-managed) metadata capacity or user-provisioned metadata storage with a specified capacity.
Specifies the provisioned IOPS to use for the FSx for Lustre file system's metadata, required when the metadata configuration mode is set to USER_PROVISIONED.

Controls whether the Lustre file system's metadata configuration is automatically managed (AUTOMATIC) or manually provisioned (USER_PROVISIONED, requiring an Iops value) to determine the IOPS of the metadata storage.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.per_unit_storage_th: Specifies the per-unit storage throughput (in MB/s per TiB) for the Lustre file system, which is required for persistent deployment types (PERSISTENT_1 or PERSISTENT_2) and must be one of the supported values (e.g., 50, 100, 200).
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.throughput_capacity: Specifies the throughput capacity of the FSx for Lustre file system in megabytes per second (MB/s), which for PERSISTENT_2 deployment types must be one of 125, 250, 500, or 1000 MB/s, while PERSISTENT_1 requires a value between 50 and 200 MB/s.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_configuration.weekly_maintenance_: Sets the day and time (in UTC, formatted as d:HH:MM, e.g., '1:04:30') when the weekly maintenance window starts for the FSx for Lustre file system, allowing AWS to perform system maintenance at that scheduled time.
aws_fsx_file_system.lustre_mount_name: The mount name (such as 'lustre') for the Amazon FSx for Lustre file system, used by clients to mount the file system after it is created.
aws_fsx_file_system.network_type: Determines whether the FSx file system is reachable over the internet ('INTERNET') or only within the VPC ('INTERNAL').
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration: Specifies the FSx for ONTAP-specific configuration for the file system, including settings like deployment type, throughput capacity, automatic backup retention and start time, disk I/O configuration, admin password, preferred subnet, route tables, and endpoint IP address range.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.automatic_backup_ret: Specifies the number of days that automatic backups are retained before being deleted, with a range from 0 to 90 days, where 0 disables automatic backups.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.daily_automatic_back: The preferred time in HH:MM UTC format for daily automatic backups of the FSx for ONTAP file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.deployment_type: Specifies the deployment type for the FSx for ONTAP file system, either MULTI_AZ_1 for a multi-AZ deployment or SINGLE_AZ_1 for a single-AZ deployment.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.disk_iops_configurat: Specifies the disk I/O operations per second (IOPS) configuration for the ONTAP file system's SSD storage, defining whether IOPS are automatically set (AUTOMATIC) or manually provisioned (USER_PROVISIONED) via the iops property.
Specifies the initial number of input/output operations per second (IOPS) to provision for the SSD storage of the Amazon FSx for ONTAP file system, determining its baseline performance level.

Specifies the disk I/O configuration mode for the FSx for ONTAP file system, either 'AUTOMATIC' (the system sets IOPs automatically) or 'USER_PROVISIONED' (you specify the IOPs value in the same disk_iops_configuration).
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.endpoint_ip_address_: Specifies the CIDR block from which FSx for ONTAP assigns IP addresses to the file system's management and data endpoints; if omitted, Amazon FSx automatically chooses an available range.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.endpoint_ipv6_addres: The IPv6 CIDR block from which FSx for ONTAP selects IP addresses for the file system's management and intercluster endpoints.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.fsx_admin_password: The fsx_admin_password specifies the password for the NetApp ONTAP administrator (admin) user on the FSx for ONTAP file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.hapairs: Specifies the number of high-availability (HA) pairs for the FSx for ONTAP file system, which determines total SSD storage capacity and compute resources, with allowed values of 1, 2, or 4 and a default of 2.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.preferred_subnet_id: Specifies the ID of the subnet where the FSx for ONTAP file system's primary management endpoint is placed, allowing you to choose the preferred Availability Zone for management traffic (typically used in multi-AZ deployments).
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.route_table_ids: Specifies the list of VPC route table IDs to be associated with the network interfaces (endpoints) of the FSx for ONTAP file system, controlling how traffic is routed between the file system and other resources in your VPC.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.throughput_capacity: Specifies the sustained throughput capacity of the FSx for ONTAP file system in megabytes per second (MB/s).
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.throughput_capacity_: Specifies the throughput capacity in MB/s per high-availability (HA) pair for an FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system, which determines the aggregate performance of the file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.ontap_configuration.weekly_maintenance_s: Specifies the preferred day and time (in `ddd:hh:mm` format, e.g., `SAT:02:00`) for the start of the weekly maintenance window for the FSx for ONTAP file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration: The `open_zfsconfiguration` block configures the OpenZFS-specific settings for an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system, including deployment type, throughput capacity, and associated options.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.automatic_backup_r: The number of days that automatic backups of the OpenZFS file system are retained; a value of 0 disables automatic backups.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.copy_tags_to_backu: Indicates whether to copy the file system's tags to each OpenZFS backup created from it.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.copy_tags_to_volum: Indicates whether to copy tags from the OpenZFS file system to volumes created within it.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.daily_automatic_ba: The preferred local time (in HH:MM format) at which daily automatic backups of the OpenZFS file system are started.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.deployment_type: Specifies the FSx for OpenZFS deployment type (e.g., SINGLE_AZ_1, SINGLE_AZ_2, or MULTI_AZ_1), which determines whether the file system is deployed in a single or multiple Availability Zones and impacts its availability and performance characteristics.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.disk_iops_configur: Specifies the disk IOPS configuration for the OpenZFS file system, including the mode (automatic or user-provisioned) and the number of IOPS to provision.
The number of provisioned input/output operations per second (IOPS) for the storage backing the FSx for OpenZFS file system, required when the disk I/O configuration mode is set to USER_PROVISIONED.
Specifies whether the file system uses automatic disk I/O operations per second (IOPS) provisioning or user-provisioned IOPS, with valid values AUTOMATIC or USER_PROVISIONED.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.endpoint_ip_addres: The IP address range in CIDR notation for the OpenZFS file system's management endpoint, which must be within one of the subnets specified for the file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.endpoint_ipv6_addr: Defines the IPv6 CIDR block from which the OpenZFS file system's endpoint IP addresses are allocated, allowing you to control the address space for service endpoints.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.options: Specifies the list of OpenZFS configuration options for the file system, where the only supported value is DELETE_CHILD_VOLUMES_AND_SNAPSHOTS, which permits the file system to be deleted together with its child volumes and snapshots.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.preferred_subnet_i: The preferred subnet ID where Amazon FSx for OpenZFS provisions the file system's endpoint network interface, allowing you to control the network placement of the endpoint within your VPC.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.read_cache_configu: Specifies the read cache configuration for the FSx for OpenZFS file system, including the memory size (SizeGiB) allocated for the L2 ARC read cache.
Specifies the size of the read cache, in GiB, for the Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system.
Determines how the read cache size is managed for the Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system, with values such as NO_CACHE, USER_PROVISIONED, or PROPORTIONAL_TO_THROUGHPUT_CAPACITY.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.root_volume_config: This object defines the configuration of the root volume for an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system, including settings such as data compression, NFS exports, user and group quotas, and read-only status.
Indicates whether tags on the root volume are copied to snapshots taken from that volume for an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system.
Specifies the data compression type for the OpenZFS root volume, allowed values are NONE, ZSTD, or LZ4.
Specifies the NFS export configuration for the root volume of the OpenZFS file system, defining the clients and mount options allowed to access the volume.
Defines the list of client configurations that specify which clients (IP addresses or CIDR ranges) can access the NFS export and the NFS export options (e.g., rw, ro, sync) granted to them.
Specifies the client IP address, CIDR range, or hostname that is allowed to access the NFS export defined in this client configuration.

Specifies the list of NFS export options (such as `rw`, `ro`, `sync`, `async`, or `no_root_squash`) that are applied to the client or client range identified in the containing `client_configurations` entry of the root volume's NFS export configuration.
Specifies whether the root volume of the FSx for OpenZFS file system is read-only, preventing users from writing to the root volume when set to true.
The size in KiB of the data records (blocks) used for the root volume of the OpenZFS file system, which can be set to 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128 and affects performance and compression efficiency.
Specifies the list of user and group quotas (each with a type, ID, and storage capacity quota in GiB) applied to the root volume of the OpenZFS file system.
Numeric ID of the user or group to which the quota applies.
The maximum storage capacity, in GiB, that the specified user or group can consume on the root volume of the FSx for OpenZFS file system, enforced by this user/group quota.
Specifies whether the quota applies to a user or a group, with allowed values USER or GROUP.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.route_table_ids: Specifies the list of Amazon VPC route table IDs that the FSx for OpenZFS file system uses to route network traffic, allowing it to communicate with resources in other subnets or networks.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.throughput_capacit: Specifies the throughput capacity of the Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system in megabytes per second (MB/s), determining its performance level.
aws_fsx_file_system.open_zfsconfiguration.weekly_maintenance: Specifies the preferred day and time (in the format d:HH:MM, where d is 1-7 for Monday-Sunday) in UTC to start weekly maintenance for the FSx for OpenZFS file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.resource_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the FSx file system in AWS.
aws_fsx_file_system.root_volume_id: The unique identifier of the root volume of the Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.security_group_ids: Specifies the list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the file system's network interfaces, controlling inbound and outbound traffic.
aws_fsx_file_system.storage_capacity: Specifies the storage capacity in gibibytes (GiB) to provision for the Amazon FSx file system, setting the total amount of storage and subject to type-specific limits and increments (e.g., Lustre requires 1,200–100,000 GiB in multiples of 1,200).
aws_fsx_file_system.storage_type: The storage type for the FSx file system, specifying whether it uses SSD or HDD storage, which affects performance and cost.
aws_fsx_file_system.subnet_ids: The IDs of the subnets in which Amazon FSx creates the file system's network endpoints, with one subnet required for Lustre and two subnets (in different Availability Zones) for Windows File Server.
aws_fsx_file_system.tags: Specifies a list of key-value tags to assign to the Amazon FSx file system for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource, including for cost allocation.
aws_fsx_file_system.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the FSx file system, used to identify the tag for resource management and cost allocation.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration: Defines the Windows-specific configuration for an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system, including Active Directory settings, throughput capacity, and maintenance window.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.active_directory_i: The ID of the AWS Managed Microsoft Active Directory that this FSx for Windows file system joins, used when the file system is joined to a Managed AD server rather than a self-managed directory.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.aliases: Specifies additional DNS aliases (CNAME) for the FSx for Windows File Server file system, enabling access via alternate domain names.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.audit_log_configur: Configures the audit log delivery for the Windows file server, specifying the destination for audit logs (e.g., CloudWatch Logs or Amazon S3) and the types of file access events to audit.

Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the destination for Windows File Server audit logs, such as a CloudWatch Logs log group or a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream; when omitted, FSx uses its default destination.

Specifies the level of file-access auditing to record for the Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system, using values such as DISABLED, SUCCESS_ONLY, FAILURE_ONLY, or SUCCESS_AND_FAILURE to control which successful and/or failed file access operations are written to the audit log destination.

Specifies the level of file share access auditing for the FSx for Windows File Server, controlling whether success, failure, both, or no file access events are recorded in the audit log (values: DISABLED, SUCCESS_ONLY, FAILURE_ONLY, SUCCESS_AND_FAILURE).
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.automatic_backup_r: Specifies the number of days to retain automatic backups for the Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system; setting this to 0 disables automatic backups.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.copy_tags_to_backu: If set to true, tags on the Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system are copied to its automatic and user-initiated backups (and when tags are specified at backup creation, only those tags are copied), otherwise no tags are copied to backups.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.daily_automatic_ba: The preferred time of day (in HH:MM format, UTC) to start the automatic daily backup for the Windows file system.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.deployment_type: Specifies the deployment type for the FSx for Windows File Server, such as MULTI_AZ_1 or SINGLE_AZ_1, which determines whether the file system is deployed across multiple Availability Zones for high availability or in a single Availability Zone for cost savings.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.disk_iops_configur: Configures the disk I/O performance (IOPS) for an FSx for Windows File Server file system, specifying either automatic mode or a user-provided number of I/O operations per second.
The number of input/output operations per second (IOPS) to provision for the SSD storage of the FSx Windows file system, used when the disk I/O configuration mode is set to USER_PROVISIONED.
Specifies whether the disk I/O operations for the FSx for Windows file system are automatically managed by Amazon FSx (AUTOMATIC) or user-provided (USER_PROVIDED).
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.fsrm_configuration: File Server Resource Manager (FSRM) settings for an Amazon FSx for Windows file system, including an enable flag, scheduled scan schedule, and aggregate/per-user quota limits.
Enables the File Server Resource Manager (FSRM) service on the FSx for Windows File Server, allowing quota management and file screening.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.preferred_subnet_i: Specifies the ID of the subnet where AWS places the preferred file server for a MULTI_AZ_1 FSx for Windows File Server file system; when omitted, AWS automatically chooses one from the subnets associated with the file system's VPC.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.self_managed_activ: Configures the file system to join a self-managed Microsoft Active Directory domain, specifying the domain name, DNS servers, and service account credentials for directory access.
The DNS IP addresses of the self-managed Active Directory domain controllers that FSx for Windows File Server uses to locate and join the domain.

Specifies the ARN or name of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the user name and password for the service account used to join the FSx for Windows file system to a self-managed Active Directory domain, providing an alternative to directly supplying UserName and Password fields.
The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the self-managed Microsoft Active Directory directory that this FSx Windows File Server will join, for example corp.example.com.
Specifies the name of the group in the self-managed Active Directory that is granted administrative access to the Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system.
The distinguished name of the organizational unit (OU) in the self-managed Active Directory where the FSx for Windows File Server computer account is created.
The password for the service account that Amazon FSx uses to join the self-managed Microsoft Active Directory domain.
The user name of the service account that Amazon FSx uses to join the Windows File Server to your self-managed Microsoft Active Directory domain.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.throughput_capacit: Specifies the sustained throughput of the Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system in megabytes per second (MB/s), determining its performance tier.
aws_fsx_file_system.windows_configuration.weekly_maintenance: Sets the preferred weekly maintenance window start time for the FSx Windows file system, formatted as day-of-week:time (e.g., '2:04:00').

aws_fsx_s3_access_point_attachment.ontap_configuration: The ONTAP-specific settings for the S3 access point, defining the FSx for ONTAP volume to attach, the S3 bucket and read/write settings, and an optional alias used to address the access point.
aws_fsx_s3_access_point_attachment.ontap_configuration.file_system_identity: Identifies the FSx for ONTAP file system and its storage virtual machine (SVM) to which the S3 access point is attached, containing the file system ID and SVM ID.
Configures the Unix user identity (e.g., user name or UID) that the FSx for ONTAP S3 access point uses to map file system access requests to a specific Unix user's permissions.
Specifies the Windows user credentials (domain and password) that define the file system's identity when the FSx for ONTAP file system is joined to an Active Directory domain.
aws_fsx_s3_access_point_attachment.open_zfsconfiguration.file_system_identi: Specifies the POSIX user ID and group ID (file system identity) that the OpenZFS file system uses when accessing the attached S3 access point.
Defines the POSIX user (UID and GID) on the FSx for OpenZFS file system that is used to map operations from the attached S3 access point.
The numeric secondary group ID (GID) that is added to the POSIX user's secondary group list for the file system identity used by the S3 access point attachment.
aws_fsx_s3_access_point_attachment.s3_access_point.vpc_configuration: Specifies the VPC configuration for the S3 access point, including the VPC ID in which the access point is created and which restricts access to requests originating from that VPC only.

aws_fsx_snapshot.id: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this FSx snapshot.
aws_fsx_snapshot.name: The user-assigned name of the FSx snapshot, used to identify it within the volume.
aws_fsx_snapshot.resource_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned by AWS to the FSx snapshot, uniquely identifying it across regions and accounts.
aws_fsx_snapshot.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon FSx snapshot, used to organize and identify the snapshot within AWS.
aws_fsx_snapshot.tags.value: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the FSx snapshot, used for organizing and identifying the resource.
aws_fsx_snapshot.volume_id: The ID of the Amazon FSx volume (file system) from which this snapshot is created.

aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.active_directory_configuration: Specifies the Active Directory configuration for the storage virtual machine to join a domain, including the NetBIOS name and self-managed Active Directory settings such as domain name, organizational unit, and administrator credentials.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.active_directory_configuration.net_bios_: Specifies the NetBIOS name of the Active Directory computer object that the FSx storage virtual machine will use when it is joined to a Microsoft Active Directory domain.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.active_directory_configuration.self_mana: Specifies the self-managed Microsoft Active Directory configuration for joining the storage virtual machine to the domain, including DNS server IP addresses, domain name, service account username and password, and optional organizational unit and administrator group settings.
Specifies the IPv4 addresses of the domain controllers in your self-managed Active Directory, which Amazon FSx uses for DNS resolution when joining the storage virtual machine to the directory.
The password for the service account that FSx uses to join the storage virtual machine to the self-managed Active Directory domain.
The fully qualified domain name of the self-managed Active Directory that the storage virtual machine (SVM) will join.
Specifies the name of the self-managed Active Directory group that is granted administrative privileges on the FSx for Windows File Server file system associated with this storage virtual machine.
The distinguished name of the organizational unit (OU) in the self-managed Active Directory where the FSx for ONTAP storage virtual machine's computer account is created.
The password for the service account user used to join the storage virtual machine to the self-managed Active Directory domain.
The user name of a service account with privileges to join the storage virtual machine to the self-managed Active Directory domain.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.file_system_id: The unique identifier of the Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system on which the storage virtual machine is created.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.name: The name of the storage virtual machine (SVM), which must be unique within the file system.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.resource_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this FSx storage virtual machine.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.root_volume_security_style: Specifies the security style (UNIX, NTFS, or MIXED) for the storage virtual machine's root volume, determining how file permissions are evaluated for files and directories.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.storage_virtual_machine_id: The unique identifier of the Amazon FSx storage virtual machine.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.svm_admin_password: Sets the password for the storage virtual machine's administrator (vsadmin) account, which must be at least 8 characters and cannot contain '/', '\', or '@'.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.tags: Specifies a list of key-value pairs to attach to this FSx storage virtual machine for resource organization, cost tracking, and access control.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.tags.key: Defines the key portion of a user-defined tag attached to the FSx Storage Virtual Machine, enabling logical grouping, cost tracking, and access control for the resource.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.tags.value: The value part of a key-value tag attached to the FSx Storage Virtual Machine, used to label and categorize the resource for management and cost tracking.
aws_fsx_storage_virtual_machine.uuid: The universally unique identifier assigned to the storage virtual machine by the FSx service, used to uniquely identify it across all FSx resources.

aws_fsx_volume.backup_id: The ID of the backup from which the volume is created, used to restore a volume from an existing backup.
aws_fsx_volume.name: Specifies the name of the Amazon FSx volume, which must be unique within the file system and is used to identify the volume.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration: Specifies the ONTAP-specific configuration for an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP volume, including settings such as the junction path, security style, size, and storage efficiency.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.aggregate_configurat: Configures the ONTAP storage aggregate name and size for the FSx volume, determining which aggregate hosts the volume's data and its allocated storage capacity.
Specifies the list of ONTAP aggregates (storage pools) to which the volume's data is assigned within the aggregate configuration of an FSx for ONTAP volume.

For an FSx for ONTAP volume, specifies the number of constituent volumes to create within each aggregate that is selected by the aggregate configuration, controlling the volume's data distribution and performance across aggregates.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.copy_tags_to_backups: Indicates whether tags on the volume are copied to backups created from it.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.junction_path: The junction path where the ONTAP volume is mounted within the file system, such as /vol1.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.ontap_volume_type: Specifies the ONTAP volume type for the volume, with valid values RW (read/write), DP (data-protection), or LS (load-sharing).
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.security_style: Specifies the security style for the FSx for ONTAP volume, which can be UNIX, NTFS, or MIXED, controlling how file and directory permissions are applied.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.size_in_bytes: The size of the FSx for ONTAP volume, specified in bytes.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.size_in_megabytes: Specifies the storage capacity of the FSx for ONTAP volume in megabytes (MB), used to set the volume's size.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.snaplock_configurati: Specifies the SnapLock (write-once, read-many) compliance settings for the FSx for ONTAP volume, including retention periods, autocommit interval, privileged delete behavior, and whether the volume is a SnapLock audit log volume.
