The name or ID of the ONTAP volume used to store audit logs for this SnapLock configuration.
Specifies the duration after which a file on the FSx for ONTAP SnapLock volume is automatically committed to the WORM state, using a predefined interval such as 5 minutes, 1 hour, or 1 day.

Specifies the unit of time (DAYS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used with the accompanying value to determine how long after creation a file on a SnapLock volume is automatically committed to a write-once-read-many (WORM) state.

The numeric value of the autocommit period, used with the unit type to define how long after file modification or creation files are automatically committed to the WORM state in the SnapLock configuration of the FSx for ONTAP volume.
Specifies whether privileged delete is enabled or disabled for the SnapLock volume, controlling whether an administrator can permanently delete files before their retention period expires.
Defines the default and maximum retention periods for WORM-protected files in this ONTAP SnapLock volume.
Sets the default retention period applied to files on this SnapLock volume when no explicit retention period is specified at file creation.
The type of the default retention period for the SnapLock configuration, specifying the time unit (e.g., SECONDS, DAYS, YEARS, INFINITE) applied to the volume's default retention duration.
The numeric value of the default SnapLock retention period for the FSx for ONTAP volume, paired with the sibling `unit` field to set how long files are locked by default.
Specifies the maximum length of time that a file can remain locked in the SnapLock (WORM) volume, expressed as a value and unit (e.g., years, days).

Specifies the unit of time (e.g., SECONDS, MINUTES, HOURS, DAYS, MONTHS, YEARS, or INFINITE) for the maximum retention period of the SnapLock volume, paired with the value field to define how long files are locked.
The numeric value of the maximum Snaplock retention period for the FSx for ONTAP volume, paired with the unit to define the upper bound of the WORM retention window.
Specifies the minimum retention period for files in an FSx for ONTAP SnapLock volume, determining how long a file must remain locked before it can be modified or deleted.
The unit of time (e.g., DAYS, MONTHS, YEARS) used to interpret the numeric value of the minimum retention period for this volume's SnapLock configuration.

The numeric duration of the minimum SnapLock retention period, expressed in the time unit specified by the sibling 'unit' attribute (e.g., days, years), for files on this FSx for ONTAP SnapLock volume.
Specifies the SnapLock immutability mode for the volume, either 'COMPLIANCE' or 'ENTERPRISE', determining the WORM (write-once-read-many) protection behavior.
Turns on volume append mode for the SnapLock volume, allowing existing WORM-protected files to be appended to without modifying or deleting their content.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.snapshot_policy: The snapshot policy to apply to the FSx for ONTAP volume, controlling automatic snapshot creation schedules.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.storage_efficiency_e: Indicates whether storage efficiency, which includes data compression, deduplication, and compaction, is enabled for the FSx for ONTAP volume.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.storage_virtual_mach: The unique identifier of the storage virtual machine (SVM) that will host this FSx for ONTAP volume.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.tiering_policy: Defines the tiering policy for the ONTAP volume, specifying how cold data is moved from the SSD tier to the capacity pool storage, including the tiering policy name and optional cooling period.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.tiering_policy.cooli: The number of days data must remain in the standard (hot) storage tier before being automatically moved to the cold capacity pool storage tier for this FSx for ONTAP volume's tiering policy.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.tiering_policy.name: Specifies the tiering policy name that controls how data is tiered from SSD to cold storage for the ONTAP volume, with allowed values like AUTO, ALL, SNAPSHOT_ONLY, or NONE.
aws_fsx_volume.ontap_configuration.volume_style: Specifies whether the ONTAP volume is a FlexVol (standard flexible volume) or a FlexGroup (a scalable collection of FlexVols), with valid values FLEXVOL and FLEXGROUP.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration: Configures the OpenZFS-specific properties of this FSx volume, such as the parent volume ID, data compression type, NFS export settings, and storage capacity quotas.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.copy_tags_to_snaps: Controls whether tags from this FSx for OpenZFS volume are copied to any snapshots created from it, as specified by CopyTagsToSnapshots.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.data_compression_t: Specifies the data compression algorithm for the OpenZFS volume, with valid values of NONE, ZSTD, or LZ4.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.nfs_exports: This field specifies the NFS export configuration for the OpenZFS volume, including client access rules and transit encryption settings for each export.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.nfs_exports.client: Specifies the list of client configurations that define which client IP addresses or ranges can access the NFS export and the access options (such as read/write permissions) applied to them.
Specifies the clients that can access the NFS export, such as a single IP address, an IP address range in CIDR notation, or a hostname.
The list of NFS protocol options (for example, 'nfsvers=4.1' or 'sec=sys') that are applied to the client configuration for this OpenZFS volume export.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.options: A list of options for the FSx for OpenZFS volume, where the only supported value is DELETE_CHILD_VOLUMES_AND_SNAPSHOTS, which causes the volume's child volumes and snapshots to be deleted when the volume is deleted.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.origin_snapshot: Specifies the source snapshot and copy strategy (full or incremental) used to create the OpenZFS volume from an existing FSx for OpenZFS snapshot.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.origin_snapshot.co: Specifies the copy strategy to use when creating the OpenZFS volume from the origin snapshot, with allowed values FULL_COPY, INCREMENTAL_COPY, or NONE.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.origin_snapshot.sn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the OpenZFS snapshot to use as the origin when creating the volume.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.parent_volume_id: Specifies the ID of the parent volume in the OpenZFS file system that this volume is a child of, using 'root' to create a root volume.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.read_only: When set to true, makes the FSx for OpenZFS volume read-only; when false (default), the volume is writable.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.record_size_ki_b: Specifies the record size of the OpenZFS volume in kibibytes (KiB), which controls the block size for file data and must be one of the valid values 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, or 1024 (default 128).
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.storage_capacity_q: Specifies the maximum storage capacity in GiB that the OpenZFS volume can use, acting as a quota; when omitted, the volume may consume all of the file system's available storage.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.storage_capacity_r: The amount of storage capacity in GiB to reserve for the OpenZFS volume, guaranteeing that this space is available for the volume's data and snapshots.
aws_fsx_volume.open_zfsconfiguration.user_and_group_quo: Defines storage capacity quotas for specific users or groups on the OpenZFS volume, with each entry specifying the quota type (user or group), the user or group ID, and the maximum storage capacity in GiB.
The numeric UID or GID that identifies the user or group for which this OpenZFS volume quota is set.
Defines the storage capacity quota in GiB for a user or group on the FSx for OpenZFS volume, limiting how much space that user or group can consume.
The type of quota, either USER or GROUP, determines whether the quota applies to a specific user or group by ID.
aws_fsx_volume.resource_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the FSx volume.
aws_fsx_volume.tags.key: The tag key portion of a tag attached to the FSx volume, used to organize and identify the volume, support cost allocation, and enable IAM-based access control, with uniqueness required among tags on the volume.
aws_fsx_volume.tags.value: The value portion of a user-defined tag associated with the FSx volume, enabling customization of metadata for resource tracking, cost allocation, and access control policies.
aws_fsx_volume.uuid: The system-assigned UUID for an FSx for OpenZFS volume, which serves as the unique mount name that clients use to access the volume and is distinct from the volume's resource ID.
aws_fsx_volume.volume_id: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the FSx volume, formatted as `fsvol-` followed by a 17-character hexadecimal string, which is populated after the volume is created.
aws_fsx_volume.volume_type: Specifies the type of FSx volume being created, either ONTAP or OPENZFS, which determines the applicable file system and volume configuration.

aws_game_lift_alias.routing_strategy: The routing strategy defines how a GameLift alias directs game session requests to fleets, either by specifying a fleet ID for simple routing or by providing a terminal message to stop routing.

aws_game_lift_build.storage_location: The S3 bucket and object key where the build's game build files are stored, along with the IAM role ARN that GameLift assumes to access the files.

aws_game_lift_container_fleet.instance_inbound_permissions.from_port: Specifies the starting port number of the range of inbound ports that are allowed on the container fleet's instances.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.instance_inbound_permissions.ip_range: Specifies the CIDR IP address range allowed to connect to the container fleet's game server ports.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.instance_inbound_permissions.protocol: Specifies the IP protocol (TCP or UDP) for the inbound traffic that is allowed to reach the container fleet's instances.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.instance_inbound_permissions.to_port: The upper bound of the port range that is allowed for inbound traffic to the container fleet's instances, used together with the from_port value to define a contiguous range.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations: A list of objects, each representing a GameLift location (AWS Region) where the container fleet has active instances, including the location name and its operational status and capacity, as computed and returned by the service.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.location: The name of an AWS Region or Local Zone location to add to the container fleet's set of enabled locations.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.location_capacity: Specifies the scaling limits for the number of EC2 instances hosting container groups in the corresponding location, including desired, minimum, and maximum counts.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.location_capacity.desired_ec2_: Sets the desired number of EC2 instances to run in this location for the container fleet, used by GameLift to scale capacity toward that target.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.location_capacity.managed_capa: Specifies the managed capacity configuration for the container fleet at this location, defining settings like the desired number of instances for that location.
Determines the number of minutes of idle time (no active game sessions) that must elapse before Amazon GameLift scales in (removes) an instance in the container fleet.
Controls whether the managed container fleet maintains a warm pool of instances or scales to zero when there are no active game sessions in that location.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.location_capacity.max_size: The `max_size` property under a location's `location_capacity` specifies the upper bound of container instances that can run in that location for this GameLift container fleet.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.location_capacity.min_size: The minimum number of container instances that GameLift maintains in the corresponding fleet location, defining the lower bound for auto scaling capacity for that location.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.player_gateway_status: Indicates the current operational status of the player gateway in the fleet's location, such as ACTIVE or ERROR.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.stopped_actions: Specifies the fleet actions to stop in a particular location (e.g., AUTO_SCALING, CUSTOM_GAME_SERVER_ACTIONS, or CUSTOM_GAME_SERVER_SHUTDOWN) to prevent them from running there for the container fleet.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.comparison_operator: The comparison operator used to evaluate the scaling metric against the threshold in the container fleet scaling policy, such as GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold or LessThanThreshold.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.evaluation_periods: The number of consecutive 1-minute evaluation periods that the fleet's metric must breach the policy's threshold before the target tracking scaling policy triggers an adjustment.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.metric_name: The name of the CloudWatch metric (e.g., CPUUtilization, PlayerCount) that this scaling policy watches to determine when to trigger scaling actions for the container fleet.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.name: The name string that uniquely identifies this scaling policy within the container fleet, used to reference the policy in metrics and API calls.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.policy_type: The type of scaling policy for the container fleet, either 'TargetTracking' to adjust capacity based on a target metric value or 'RuleBased' to scale based on custom conditions.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.scaling_adjustment: The number of instances by which the GameLift Container Fleet's desired capacity is increased or decreased when a CHANGE_IN_CAPACITY scaling policy is triggered.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.scaling_adjustment_type: Specifies whether the scaling adjustment is an absolute change in capacity, an exact capacity value, or a percentage change in capacity (ChangeInCapacity, ExactCapacity, or PercentChangeInCapacity).
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.target_configuration: The target tracking configuration for a scaling policy, specifying the metric and target value (e.g., a target fleet utilization or instance count) that the GameLift container fleet automatically adjusts capacity to maintain.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.target_configuration.ta: The target value for the metric used by the target-based scaling policy; GameLift adjusts the fleet's desired capacity to keep the metric near this value.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_policies.threshold: The target value of the specified metric that, when crossed, triggers the scaling adjustment for the container fleet's autoscaling policy.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.tags.key: The case-sensitive key of a tag attached to the Amazon GameLift container fleet, which serves as the tag's identifier for categorization and cost tracking.
aws_game_lift_container_fleet.tags.value: The value part of a key-value tag attached to the GameLift container fleet, used for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.game_server_container_definition.depends: Determines the condition (such as START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, or HEALTHY) that the referenced dependency container must satisfy before the game server container is allowed to start.
The name of the container that the game server container depends on, used to define the startup order between containers in the container group.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.game_server_container_definition.environ: The name of the environment variable whose value is being overridden for the game server container defined in this GameLift container group.
Specifies the value for an environment variable override applied to the game server container at runtime, replacing any default value defined in the container image.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.game_server_container_definition.mount_p: Specifies whether the mounted volume is read-only or read-write, using values like READ_ONLY or READ_WRITE.
The file path inside the game server container where the mounted volume is accessible, as specified in the mount point configuration for the container group definition.
Specifies the file path on the underlying EC2 instance that the container mount point references, allowing the container to access data stored on the instance's filesystem.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.game_server_container_definition.port_co: Specifies the starting port in a contiguous range of ports that the game server container uses for incoming game traffic, as part of a container port range for the container group definition.
The network protocol (TCP or UDP) for the container port range, used for routing traffic to the game server container.

The ending port number in the inclusive range of ports that the game server container uses for inbound game traffic, as part of the container port configuration for the GameLift container group definition.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.container_: The name assigned to the support container, which serves as a unique identifier within the container group definition.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.depends_on: Defines which other containers in the same container group must reach a specified condition (e.g., START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, HEALTHY) before this support container is started.

Defines the required condition (e.g., START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, HEALTHY) on the referenced container that must be met before the support container in the GameLift container group definition is started.
The name of a container in the same container group that this support container depends on, used to define startup order.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.environmen: A list of environment variable overrides applied to the support container when it runs, each specifying the variable name and value to replace any value defined in the container image, for a GameLift container group definition.
Specifies the name of the environment variable to override in the support container's runtime configuration.
The value portion of an environment variable override applied to a support container in the GameLift container group definition, replacing the container image's default environment variable value.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.essential: Indicates whether the support container is essential, meaning that if an essential support container stops or fails, the entire container group is stopped.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.health_che: Specifies the container health check configuration, including the command to run, interval, timeout, retries, and start period, used by Amazon GameLift to determine whether the support container is healthy.
The command to run inside the support container to perform a health check, specified as a list of strings representing the executable and its arguments.
Specifies the time interval (in seconds) between successive health check runs for this support container in the GameLift container group definition.
The retries field specifies the number of consecutive failed health checks after which the container is considered unhealthy in the GameLift container group definition.
The number of seconds that the health check waits after the support container starts before beginning its health checks in a GameLift container group definition.
The amount of time (in seconds) that GameLift waits for the container health check command to return before considering the health check failed and marking the container unhealthy.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.image_uri: The URI of the container image that this support container in the GameLift container group definition will pull and run.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.linux_capa: Configures the Linux kernel capabilities (additional or dropped) for the support container, controlling which privileged operations the container is allowed to perform.
Specifies the list of Linux capabilities to add (include) for the support container, granting the container these additional Linux privileges on top of its default capabilities.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.memory_har: Sets the maximum memory (in mebibytes) that the support container is allowed to use, enforcing a hard limit on its memory consumption.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.mount_poin: Defines the mount points for the support container, specifying the container path and the source volume to attach for shared storage within the GameLift container group.
Specifies whether the mounted container path is accessible as read-only (READ_ONLY) or read-write (READ_WRITE) to the support container.
Specifies the path inside the support container where a mounted volume is accessible, used to define the container's mount point for persistent storage.

Specifies the absolute file system path on the host EC2 instance that serves as the source volume for a mount point in a support container definition within an AWS GameLift container group definition.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.port_confi: Defines the port range and protocol (e.g., TCP or UDP) that the support container exposes for inbound traffic in the GameLift container group definition.

Specifies an inclusive range of container ports (from a starting port to an ending port) that a support container in an Amazon GameLift container group definition exposes for game traffic or other networking purposes.
Specifies the starting (lower) port number in a contiguous range of ports that this support container is configured to use within its port configuration.
The network protocol (TCP or UDP) used by the container port range in the GameLift container group.
Specifies the upper (inclusive) bound of the port range that this support container can use for its network traffic.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.resolved_i: The resolved image digest for the support container, computed from the image URI to uniquely identify the exact container image version used by the container group definition.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.support_container_definitions.vcpu: The number of vCPU units allocated to this support container in the GameLift container group definition, which sets the CPU resource limit for that container.
aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.tags.key: The key of a tag applied to an Amazon GameLift container group definition, enabling resource organization and cost allocation.

aws_game_lift_fleet.certificate_configuration.certificate_ty: Determines whether an AWS GameLift fleet uses a generated TLS certificate, with valid values DISABLED (no certificate) or CERTIFICATE_GENERATED (automatically generated by GameLift).
aws_game_lift_fleet.ec2_inbound_permissions.from_port: The lower bound of the port range for inbound traffic allowed to the fleet's EC2 instances from the specified IP range.
aws_game_lift_fleet.ec2_inbound_permissions.ip_range: The IP address range, in CIDR notation, that is allowed to connect to the fleet's EC2 instances for the specified protocol and port.
aws_game_lift_fleet.ec2_inbound_permissions.protocol: The IP protocol (TCP or UDP) allowed for inbound traffic on the specified port range for the fleet's EC2 instances.
aws_game_lift_fleet.ec2_inbound_permissions.to_port: The upper bound of the port range that is allowed for inbound traffic to the fleet's EC2 instances, used with `from_port` to define the permitted range.
aws_game_lift_fleet.locations: The locations attribute lists the AWS Regions (locations) where the GameLift fleet has deployed instances, returned as a computed list of location objects.
aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.location: The AWS Region code (e.g., 'us-east-1') that identifies where this GameLift fleet location is deployed for hosting game servers.
aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.location_capacity: Defines the desired, minimum, and maximum instance counts for the fleet in a specific location (region).
aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.location_capacity.desired_ec2_: Sets the desired number of EC2 instances for a given fleet location, which GameLift uses as the scaling target for that location's capacity within its configured minimum and maximum limits.
aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.location_capacity.managed_capa: Determines the managed capacity strategy for a GameLift fleet location when there is no demand, specifying whether the fleet can scale down to zero instances or must maintain a minimum capacity.
aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.location_capacity.max_size: The maximum number of EC2 instances that can be active for this fleet location, setting the upper bound for auto-scaling capacity.
aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.location_capacity.min_size: Specifies the minimum number of EC2 instances that must be maintained for the fleet in the associated location as part of its capacity configuration.
aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.player_gateway_status: The player gateway status for each fleet location, representing the operational state of the gateway that routes player connections to game sessions in that location.
aws_game_lift_fleet.runtime_configuration.server_processes.c: The number of game server processes to launch concurrently on each instance for this server process configuration.
aws_game_lift_fleet.runtime_configuration.server_processes.l: Specifies the file path to the server executable within the game build that GameLift launches to host game sessions for this fleet.
aws_game_lift_fleet.runtime_configuration.server_processes.p: The parameters string supplies command-line arguments that Amazon GameLift passes to the server executable when launching the server process, as defined within the runtime configuration's server process definition.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.comparison_operator: Specifies the comparison operator used to evaluate the scaling metric against the threshold in a GameLift fleet scaling policy, such as GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold, GreaterThanThreshold, LessThanThreshold, or LessThanOrEqualToThreshold.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.evaluation_periods: Determines how many recent metric evaluation periods are considered when deciding whether to trigger a scaling adjustment for the fleet based on the associated CloudWatch metric.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.location: Specifies the name of the location (such as an AWS Region or custom location) where this scaling policy is applied, enabling per-location autoscaling in a multi-location GameLift fleet.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.metric_name: The name of the GameLift metric (such as ActivatingGameSessions, ActiveInstances, or IdleInstances) that this scaling policy uses to trigger scaling actions.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.name: The unique, descriptive name that identifies this scaling policy within the fleet.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.policy_type: Determines the type of scaling policy for the GameLift fleet, either 'TargetTracking' for dynamic scaling based on a target metric value or 'RuleBased' for policies defined by custom scaling rules.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.scaling_adjustment: The numeric value applied to the fleet's desired instance count when the scaling policy's conditions are met, interpreted as a change, exact capacity, or percentage according to the ScalingAdjustmentType property.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.scaling_adjustment_type: Specifies how the scaling adjustment value in the policy is applied, with valid values including ChangeInCapacity (adjust by a set number of instances), ExactCapacity (set capacity to an exact number), and PercentChangeInCapacity (adjust by a percentage of current capacity).
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.status: The current lifecycle state of the scaling policy, such as ACTIVE, UPDATE_REQUESTED, UPDATING, DELETE_REQUESTED, DELETING, DELETED, or ERROR.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.target_configuration: Provides the target value for the metric used in a target-based scaling policy, determining the desired instance capacity for the GameLift fleet.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.target_configuration.ta: Specifies the target value of the metric used by a target-based scaling policy to decide when to adjust fleet capacity for an Amazon GameLift fleet.
aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.threshold: The numeric value that the scaling policy's specified metric is compared against using the comparison operator to trigger a fleet capacity adjustment.

aws_game_lift_game_server_group.instance_definitions.instance_type: The EC2 instance type (e.g., c5.large, m5.large) that GameLift uses to launch instances in this game server group's underlying fleet.
aws_game_lift_game_server_group.instance_definitions.weighted_capacity: Sets the relative weighting that this instance type contributes to the game server group's total capacity, used by Amazon GameLift to determine how many instances of each type are needed to meet the group's target capacity.
aws_game_lift_game_server_group.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to this GameLift game server group.
aws_game_lift_game_server_group.tags.value: The value of an arbitrary tag key assigned to the GameLift GameServerGroup, used for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.destinations.destination_arn: The ARN of a GameLift fleet or alias that this game session queue uses as a destination for game session placement requests.
aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.filter_configuration: Filters the locations where the queue can place new game sessions by specifying a list of allowed AWS region codes.
aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.player_latency_policies.maximum_individu: Sets the maximum acceptable latency in milliseconds for an individual player to a game location; if the player's latency exceeds this threshold, that location is excluded from consideration for the player's game session placement.
aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.player_latency_policies.policy_duration_: The length of time in seconds that this player latency policy remains in effect for the game session placement.
aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.priority_configuration: Specifies the priority settings for the GameLift session queue, including the order in which locations are used and the order in which placement criteria like latency and cost are prioritized.
aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to this GameLift game session queue, used to organize and identify the queue for cost and access management.
aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.tags.value: The value component of a tag key-value pair applied to the GameLift game session queue for resource organization and management.

aws_game_lift_location.location_arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the GameLift location, returned after the location is created and used for referencing it in IAM policies and other resources.
aws_game_lift_location.location_name: Specifies the name of the GameLift location, which is typically an AWS Region code (e.g., 'us-east-1') or a custom location name used to identify the location for game hosting.
aws_game_lift_location.tags.key: The key of a tag assigned to the GameLift location, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_game_lift_matchmaking_configuration.game_properties.key: The identifying key of a custom game property (a key-value pair) that is passed to a matchmade game session to provide custom configuration data.
aws_game_lift_matchmaking_configuration.game_properties.value: The string value of a game property key-value pair that is passed to GameLift matchmaking to filter or customize game sessions.
aws_game_lift_matchmaking_configuration.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to a GameLift matchmaking configuration, used to identify, organize, and manage the resource.

aws_game_lift_matchmaking_rule_set.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the GameLift matchmaking rule set, used to identify and categorize the rule set for resource management and cost allocation.
aws_game_lift_matchmaking_rule_set.tags.value: The value portion of a tag attached to the GameLift matchmaking rule set, used to organize and identify the rule set within AWS.

aws_game_lift_script.storage_location: The Amazon S3 bucket and key that store the zipped script file, along with the IAM role that allows GameLift to access that location.
aws_game_lift_script.tags.key: The key of a tag attached to the GameLift script, used to identify and categorize the resource.
aws_game_lift_script.tags.value: The string value paired with a tag key on the GameLift script, used to label and categorize the resource for cost allocation and identity-based policies.

aws_global_accelerator_accelerator.tags: Specifies custom tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the AWS Global Accelerator accelerator for resource categorization and management.
aws_global_accelerator_accelerator.tags.value: The value of a tag attached to the accelerator, used to categorize and manage the resource as a user-defined string.

aws_global_accelerator_cross_account_att.resources.cidr: Specifies the IP address range in CIDR notation (e.g., '10.0.0.0/8') for a resource being attached, used when the resource is an IP range rather than an endpoint ID in this cross-account attachment.
aws_global_accelerator_cross_account_att.resources.endpoint_id: The ARN or resource identifier of the AWS resource (such as a Network Load Balancer, Application Load Balancer, or Elastic IP) that is attached to the accelerator from a different AWS account.
aws_global_accelerator_cross_account_att.resources.region: The AWS Region where the resource being added to the cross-account attachment is located, such as when the resource is a regional endpoint group.
aws_global_accelerator_cross_account_att.tags: Specifies a list of key-value tags to attach to the cross-account attachment, which can be used for resource identification, cost allocation, and tag-based access control in AWS Global Accelerator.
aws_global_accelerator_cross_account_att.tags.key: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Global Accelerator cross-account attachment, allowing you to attach custom metadata such as cost center or environment for identification and management.
aws_global_accelerator_cross_account_att.tags.value: The value component of a tag key-value pair that you attach to an AWS Global Accelerator cross-account attachment for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.endpoint_configurations.attachment_arn: The ARN of the AWS resource (such as an Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance) that is attached as an endpoint in this endpoint group.
aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.endpoint_configurations.client_ippreserv: Indicates whether client IP address preservation is enabled for this endpoint, which keeps the original client IP address in the packet headers forwarded by Global Accelerator to the endpoint.
aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.endpoint_configurations.endpoint_id: The ARN of the endpoint resource (such as an Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, EC2 instance, or Elastic IP address) that Global Accelerator routes traffic to for this endpoint configuration.
aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.endpoint_configurations.weight: The weight assigned to the endpoint, controlling the proportion of traffic routed to it relative to other endpoints in the group (values 0-255, higher means more traffic).
aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.health_check_path: The URI path that AWS Global Accelerator uses to perform health checks against endpoints in the endpoint group, such as '/health' or '/'.
aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.port_overrides: A list of port overrides that map a listener port to a different endpoint port for the endpoint group, allowing traffic to be redirected to a custom port on the endpoint.
aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.port_overrides.endpoint_port: The actual port on the endpoint that receives traffic when this port override is applied, replacing the listener port for the mapped endpoint.
aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.port_overrides.listener_port: Specifies the original port on the accelerator listener that this port override maps to the endpoint port, redirecting traffic received on that listener port to the endpoint's configured port.

aws_global_accelerator_listener.port_ranges: Defines the list of port ranges (each with a `from` and `to` port) that the listener forwards traffic on.
aws_global_accelerator_listener.port_ranges.from_port: The first port in the inclusive range of ports (from_port to to_port) that the AWS Global Accelerator listener accepts and forwards traffic on.
aws_global_accelerator_listener.port_ranges.to_port: The inclusive ending port number of the range for the listener.

aws_glue_blueprint.tags.key: A user-defined tag key attached to the AWS Glue Blueprint resource within the tags map, used for organizing and managing the blueprint.
aws_glue_blueprint.tags.value: The value component of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS Glue Blueprint, used for organizing, tracking, and allocating costs for the blueprint.

aws_glue_catalog.create_database_default_permissions.perm: The list of AWS Glue permissions (e.g., 'ALL' or 'CREATE_TABLE') granted by default to the specified principal on newly created databases in the Data Catalog.
aws_glue_catalog.create_database_default_permissions.prin: Defines the principal (IAM user, role, or all users) that the Glue database's default permissions are granted to, via its Data Lake principal identifier.
The unique identifier (such as an IAM role ARN, IAM user ARN, or AWS account ID) of the Data Lake principal that receives the default permissions for databases created in the Glue catalog.
aws_glue_catalog.create_table_default_permissions.permiss: The list of permissions (e.g., ALL, SELECT, INSERT) to be granted to the principal in the default permissions for tables created in this Glue catalog database.
aws_glue_catalog.create_table_default_permissions.princip: Specifies the principal (such as an IAM role, user, or AWS account) that receives the configured default permissions on newly created tables in the Glue data catalog.

aws_glue_classifier.csv_classifier: Defines the configuration for an AWS Glue classifier that parses CSV files, including the delimiter, quote symbol, header detection, and whether to treat a single column as a valid CSV format.
aws_glue_classifier.grok_classifier: Configures a Grok classifier in AWS Glue, specifying the grok pattern used to parse log or unstructured data, custom pattern definitions, and the classification name applied to matched data.
aws_glue_classifier.json_classifier: Specifies a JSON classifier for AWS Glue that uses a JSON path to identify the JSON data structure within input records.
aws_glue_classifier.xmlclassifier: Defines the row tag and optional classification for an XML classifier, used by AWS Glue to parse XML data and infer its schema.

aws_glue_connection.catalog_id: The identifier of the AWS Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) in which the Glue connection is stored or referenced.
aws_glue_connection.connection_input: Configuration object that defines the properties of an AWS Glue connection, including connection type, connection properties, and physical connection requirements for the target data store.
aws_glue_connection.connection_input.authentication_configur: Configures OAuth-based authentication details (such as client credentials and token endpoint) for Glue connection types that require OAuth, like Salesforce or ServiceNow.
Specifies the username and password used for basic authentication when connecting to the data source for this AWS Glue connection.
The password component of the basic authentication credentials used to authenticate to the data source for this AWS Glue connection.
Specifies the username for basic authentication when connecting to the data source using this AWS Glue connection.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the credentials or secret associated with this Glue connection's authentication configuration.

In an AWS Glue connection's OAuth2 authentication configuration for the authorization code grant flow, this field supplies the authorization code returned by the identity provider, which Glue exchanges for access and refresh tokens.
The redirect URI to which the OAuth2 authorization server sends the user after authorization, used in the authorization code flow for the Glue connection's authentication configuration.

aws_sqs_queue.attributes: The queue's read-only attributes as returned by the SQS API (for example ApproximateNumberOfMessages, QueueArn), keyed by attribute name.
aws_sqs_queue.queue_url: The URL identifying the created SQS queue.
